What Austen parodies in Sense and Sensibility she raises to an apotheosis in Persuasion: the sublimity of a particular, inwardly isolated sensibility. Anne Elliot is hardly the only figure in Austen who has an understanding heart. Her difference is in her almost preternatural acuteness of perception of others and of the self, which are surely the qualities that most distinguish Austen as a novelist. Anne Elliot is to Austen’s work what Rosalind of As You Like It is to Shakespeare’s: the character who almost reaches the mastery of perspective that can be available to the novelist or playwright, lest all dramatic quality be lost from the novel or play.

罗莎琳德和安妮·艾略特比哈姆雷特、福斯塔夫、伊丽莎白·班纳特，甚至比《曼斯菲尔德庄园》中的范妮·普莱斯都更加沉着冷静，几乎能够洞察戏剧和小说的全貌。她们的沉着冷静无法完全超越视角转换，但罗莎琳德的机智和安妮的敏感——两者都平衡得恰到好处，既不咄咄逼人也不过度防备——使她们比我们更能体会到创作者们所拥有的那种沉着冷静。

More even than Hamlet or Falstaff, or than Elizabeth Bennet, or than Fanny Price in Mansfield Park, Rosalind and Anne Elliot are almost completely poised, nearly able to see all around the play and the novel. Their poise cannot transcend perspectivizing completely, but Rosalind’s wit and Anne’s sensibility, both balanced and free of either excessive aggressivity or defensiveness, enable them to share more of their creators’ poise than we ever come to do.

奥斯汀的笔触始终保持着戏剧张力；直到小说结尾，我们都能感同身受地体会到安妮对温特沃斯重燃旧情的焦虑。我们对安妮的信任，正如我们对罗莎琳德的信任一样；如果评论家们能更相信罗莎琳德对剧中其他人物以及她自身的反应，他们就能像看清雅克的虚荣一样，清晰地看到试金石的腐朽。安妮·艾略特的反应同样具有说服力；我们必须努力赋予她的话语以分量，而小说中除了温特沃斯之外的其他人物则没有这种分量。

Austen never loses dramatic intensity; we share Anne’s anxiety concerning Wentworth’s renewed intentions until the novel’s conclusion. But we rely upon Anne as we should rely upon Rosalind; critics would see the rancidity of Touchstone as clearly as they see the vanity of Jaques if they placed more confidence in Rosalind’s reactions to everyone else in the play, as well as to herself. Anne Elliot’s reactions have the same winning authority; we must try to give the weight to her words that is not extended by the other persons in the novel, except for Wentworth.

即使是读者，也难免会犯最初低估安妮·艾略特的错误。伊丽莎白·班纳特或罗莎琳德的机智比安妮·艾略特的敏锐感受更容易被人欣赏。她性格的秘密在于，她融合了奥斯汀式的反讽和华兹华斯式的对希望的期盼。奥斯汀颇具莎士比亚的功力，能够塑造出众多性格鲜明的人物，无论主角还是配角，他们的言谈举止都自成一体，却又彼此迥然不同。安妮·艾略特是奥斯汀笔下最后一位秉持新教意志的女主角，但这种意志在她身上得到了修正，或许可以说是完善，受到了其后裔——浪漫主义的同情想象的影响，而华兹华斯正是这种想象的先驱。正是这一点，造就了安妮如此复杂而敏感的性格。

Even the reader must fall into the initial error of undervaluing Anne Elliot. The wit of Elizabeth Bennet or of Rosalind is easier to appreciate than Anne Elliot’s accurate sensibility. The secret of her character combines Austenian irony with a Wordsworthian sense of deferred hope. Austen has a good measure of Shakespeare’s unmatched ability to give us persons, both major and minor, who are all utterly consistent in their separate modes of speech, and yet completely different from one another. Anne Elliot is the last of Austen’s heroines of what I think we must call the Protestant will, but in her the will is modified, perhaps perfected, by its descendant, the Romantic sympathetic imagination, of which Wordsworth was the prophet. That is what helps to make Anne so complex and sensitive a character.

简·奥斯汀早期的女主人公，以伊丽莎白·班纳特为代表，她们体现了新教意志，是塞缪尔·理查森笔下克拉丽莎·哈洛的直接继承者，而塞缪尔·约翰逊则作为道德权威在一旁徘徊。马克思主义批评不可避免地将新教意志，即便在其文学表现形式中，也视为一种商业行为。如今，人们热衷于谈论简·奥斯汀所忽略的社会经济现实，例如西印度群岛的奴隶制——这构成了她笔下大多数人物享有经济保障的根本基础。然而，所有成功的文学作品都建立在某种程度的排除之上，而且没有人能够证明，提高对文化与帝国主义之间关系的认识，对理解《曼斯菲尔德庄园》有任何丝毫益处。《劝导》的结尾是对英国海军的致敬，而温特沃斯则回到陆地上，与安妮·艾略特温柔地享受着爱情的甜蜜。但奥斯汀的伟大艺术再次体现在对现实的排除上，英国海上霸权的丑陋现实与《劝导》的关系，正如西印度群岛的奴隶制与《曼斯菲尔德庄园》的关系一样。然而，奥斯汀对新教意志的务实和世俗后果却极为关注，在我看来，这些后果对于我们理解她小说中的女主人公至关重要。

Jane Austen’s earlier heroines, of whom Elizabeth Bennet is the exemplar, manifested the Protestant will as direct descendants of Samuel Richardson’s Clarissa Harlowe, with Samuel Johnson hovering nearby as moral authority. Marxist criticism inevitably views the Protestant will, even in its literary manifestations, as a mercantile matter, and it has become fashionable to talk about the socioeconomic realities that Jane Austen excludes, such as the West Indian slavery that is part of the ultimate basis for the financial security most of her characters enjoy. But all achieved literary works are founded upon exclusions, and no one has demonstrated that increased consciousness of the relation between culture and imperialism is of the slightest benefit whatsoever in learning to read Mansfield Park. Persuasion ends with a tribute to the British navy, and with Wentworth on land, gently appreciating the joys of affection with Anne Elliot. But once again, Austen’s is a great art founded upon exclusions, and the sordid realities of British sea power are no more relevant to Persuasion than West Indian bondage is to Mansfield Park. Austen was, however, immensely interested in the pragmatic and secular consequences of the Protestant will, and they seem to me a crucial element in helping us appreciate the heroines of her novels.

奥斯汀笔下莎士比亚式的内省，在安妮·艾略特身上达到了顶峰，她修正了克拉丽莎·哈洛世俗化的新教殉道——被洛夫莱斯强奸后缓慢死去——的道德强度。真正剥夺克拉丽莎求生意志的，是她维护自身完整性的更强烈的意志。如果屈从于忏悔的洛夫莱斯，嫁给他，就等于损害了她存在的本质，损害了她被践踏的意志的尊严。奥斯汀将《克拉丽莎》中的悲剧转化为讽刺喜剧，但这种转变中，她维护自身意志的驱动力几乎没有改变。在《劝导》中，重点在于一种自愿的尊重交换，男女双方都高度认可对方的价值。显然，财富、财产和社会地位等外在因素至关重要，但常识、和蔼可亲、文化修养、机智和爱意等内在因素也同样重要。

Austen’s Shakespearean inwardness, culminating in Anne Elliot, revises the moral intensities of Clarissa Harlowe’s secularized Protestant martyrdom, her slow dying after being raped by Lovelace. What removes Clarissa’s will to live is her stronger will to maintain the integrity of her being. To yield to the repentant Lovelace by marrying him would compromise the essence of her being, the exaltation of her violated will. What is tragedy in Clarissa is converted by Austen into ironic comedy, but the will’s drive to maintain itself scarcely alters in this conversion. In Persuasion the emphasis is on a willed exchange of esteems, where both the woman and the man estimate the value of the other to be high. Obviously, outward considerations of wealth, property, and social standing are crucial elements here, but so are the inward considerations of common sense, amiability, culture, wit, and affection.

奥斯汀笔下的主要女主人公——伊丽莎白、爱玛、范妮和安妮——都拥有如此强烈的内在自由，以至于她们的个性无法被压抑。奥斯汀作为小说家的艺术在于，她并不过多关注这种内在自由的社会经济根源，尽管在《曼斯菲尔德庄园》和《劝导》中，这种焦虑感有所增强。在奥斯汀的作品中，反讽成为一种创造性的工具，而约翰逊博士将这种创造性定义为诗歌的本质。一种以拒绝接受除自己所尊重的人之外的任何人的尊重为核心的内在自由观念，本身就是一种最高层次的反讽。奥斯汀所有作品中最精彩的喜剧场景或许是伊丽莎白拒绝达西的第一次求婚，在这个场景中，意志与尊重之间的辩证关系所蕴含的反讽几乎达到了令人瞠目结舌的地步。在《爱玛》中延续的那种高级喜剧风格，在《曼斯菲尔德庄园》中有所收敛，然后在《劝导》中变成了另一种东西，虽然难以辨认，但又难以命名。在《劝导》中，奥斯汀已经是一位如此自觉的大师，她似乎改变了“意愿”的本质，仿佛“意愿”也可以被说服，成为一种更罕见、更无私的自我行为。

Austen’s major heroines—Elizabeth, Emma, Fanny, and Anne—possess such inward freedom that their individualities cannot be repressed. Austen’s art as a novelist is not to worry much about the socioeconomic genesis of that inner freedom, though the anxiety level does rise in Mansfield Park and Persuasion. In Austen, irony becomes the instrument for invention, which Dr. Johnson defined as the essence of poetry. A conception of inward freedom that centers upon a refusal to accept esteem except from one upon whom one has conferred esteem, is a conception of the highest degree of irony. The supreme comic scene in all of Austen might be Elizabeth’s rejection of Darcy’s first marriage proposal, where the ironies of the dialectic of will and esteem become very nearly outrageous. That high comedy, which continued in Emma, is somewhat chastened in Mansfield Park, and then becomes something else, unmistakable but difficult to name, in Persuasion, where Austen has become so conscious a master that she seems to have changed the nature of willing, as though it, too, could be persuaded to become a rarer, more disinterested act of the self.

没有人认为简·奥斯汀在《劝导》中变成了一位浪漫主义作家；她钟爱的诗人依然是威廉·考珀，而非华兹华斯，她最喜欢的散文作家也一直是约翰逊博士。然而，在她早期小说中普遍存在的对想象力和“浪漫爱情”的强烈怀疑，在《劝导》中却不再存在。安妮和温特沃斯在长达八年的绝望分离中始终保持着彼此的爱意，而且两人都拥有丰富的想象力，能够构想出一个圆满和解的结局。这才是浪漫小说的素材，而非讽刺小说的素材。《劝导》中的讽刺手法常常辛辣讽刺，但几乎从未指向安妮·艾略特，也极少指向温特沃斯上校。

No one has suggested that Jane Austen becomes a High Romantic in Persuasion; her poet remained William Cowper, not Wordsworth, and her favorite prose writer was always Dr. Johnson. But her severe distrust of imagination and of “romantic love,” so prevalent in the earlier novels, is not a factor in Persuasion. Anne and Wentworth maintain their affection for each other throughout eight years of hopeless separation, and each has the power of imagination to conceive of a triumphant reconciliation. This is the material for a romance, not for an ironical novel. The ironies of Persuasion are frequently pungent, but they are almost never directed at Anne Elliot and only rarely at Captain Wentworth.

奥斯汀压抑了她笔下主人公们特有的讽刺，这与《劝导》中弥漫的某种此前从未出现过的哀怨之间存在着一种微妙的联系。尽管安妮对自己充满信心，但她却极易受到一种焦虑的侵扰——这种焦虑她从未允许自己表达出来，这种焦虑源于一种未曾体验过的人生，其中潜在的损失超越了性方面的缺失，却又包含其中。我只记得一位评论家，澳大利亚的安·莫兰，强调了奥斯汀强烈暗示的内容：“安妮……是一个充满激情的女人。违背她的意愿，她的内心不断地渴望得到满足。”由于安妮在八年前拒绝了温特沃斯的尊重，她感到有必要压抑自己的意志，因此她成为了奥斯汀笔下第一个意志与想象力截然相反的女主人公。

There is a difficult relation between Austen’s repression of her characteristic irony about her protagonists and a certain previously unheard plangency that hovers throughout Persuasion. Despite Anne’s faith in herself, she is very vulnerable to the anxiety, which she never allows herself to express, of an unlived life, in which the potential loss transcends yet includes sexual unfulfillment. I can recall only one critic, the Australian Ann Molan, who emphasizes what Austen strongly implies: “Anne…is a passionate woman. And against her will, her heart keeps asserting its demand for fulfillment.” Since Anne had refused Wentworth her esteem eight years before, she feels a necessity to withhold her will, and thus becomes the first Austen heroine whose will and imagination are antithetical.

安妮·艾略特的内心世界，以及奥斯汀的内心世界，都不存在内战；但自我分裂带来的悲伤却逐渐显现，记忆与想象结盟，对抗着意志。吉恩·鲁奥夫注意到，安妮和温特沃斯身上都蕴含着近乎华兹华斯式的记忆力量。既然奥斯汀绝非偶然成为小说家，我们或许会问，她为何选择以共同的怀旧之情为《劝导》的基调。毕竟，被抛弃的温特沃斯比安妮更不愿重燃旧情，然而记忆与想象的融合最终也战胜了他的意志。这是否意味着简·奥斯汀自身意志的某种放松？鉴于她在《劝导》完成后开始创作的未完成小说《桑迪顿》中回归了早期的创作风格，或许安妮·艾略特的故事对这位小说家而言只是一次探索或放纵。华兹华斯与《劝导》之间的相似之处虽有限，却真实存在。英国的浪漫主义盛期小说，无论是拜伦式的《简·爱》和《呼啸山庄》，还是华兹华斯式的《亚当·比德》，都明显是后世发展起来的。奥斯汀笔下的女主人公在《劝导》中并没有改变，但她无疑变得更加复杂，带着一种对生命局限的新的忧伤。或许，《劝导》中偶尔流露出的那种优雅的悲情，与简·奥斯汀自身的健康状况以及她对早逝的预感有关。

There is no civil war within Anne Elliot’s psyche, or within Austen’s; but there is the emergent sadness of a schism in the self, with memory taking the side of imagination in an alliance against the will. The almost Wordsworthian power of memory in both Anne and Wentworth has been noted by Gene Ruoff. Since Austen was anything but an accidental novelist, we might ask why she chose to found Persuasion upon a mutual nostalgia. After all, the rejected Wentworth is even less inclined to will a renewed affection than Anne is, and yet the fusion of memory and imagination triumphs over his will also. Was this a relaxation of the will in Jane Austen herself? Since she returns to her earlier mode in Sanditon, her unfinished novel begun after Persuasion was completed, it may be that the story of Anne Elliot was an excursion or indulgence for the novelist. The parallels between Wordsworth and Persuasion are limited but real. High Romantic novels in England, whether of a Byronic kind like Jane Eyre and Wuthering Heights or of a Wordsworthian sort like Adam Bede, are a distinctly later development. The ethos of the Austen heroine does not change in Persuasion, but she is certainly a more problematic being, tinged with a new sadness concerning life’s limits. It may be that the elegant pathos Persuasion sometimes courts has a connection to Jane Austen’s own ill health, her intimations of her early death.

斯图尔特·塔夫在比较华兹华斯和奥斯汀时，敏锐地指出，两人都是“婚姻诗人”，并且都拥有“一种责任感，这种责任感被那些将自身生活的完整性和宁静与他人的生活紧密相连，并将自身和所有人的生活置于超越社会秩序的更高层次的人所理解和深刻体会”。苏珊·摩根进一步拓展了塔夫的洞见，指出奥斯汀的《爱玛》与华兹华斯伟大的《颂歌：童年回忆中的不朽感悟》之间存在着特殊的关联。个体意识的成长是两部作品的共同主题，华兹华斯的成长既包含得失，而奥斯汀的成长则只有得失。爱玛的意识确实在发展，她经历了一种近似华兹华斯式的转变，从近乎唯我论的快乐走向了对他人同情的更为艰难的快乐。安妮·艾略特从一开始就更加成熟，几乎不需要在意识上成长。她对温特沃斯长久以来的拒绝，使她免受希望的毁灭性影响。奥斯汀用她一贯的娴熟技巧，将其中蕴含的复杂情感表达了出来，而非希望：

Stuart Tave, comparing Wordsworth and Austen, shrewdly noted that both were “poets of marriage” and both also possessed “a sense of duty understood and deeply felt by those who see the integrity and peace of their own lives as essentially bound to the lives of others and see their lives of all in a more than merely social order.” Expanding Tave’s insight, Susan Morgan pointed to the particular affinity between Austen’s Emma and Wordsworth’s great “Ode: Intimations of Immortality from Recollections of Early Childhood.” The growth of the individual consciousness, involving both gain and loss for Wordsworth but only gain for Austen, is the shared subject. Emma’s consciousness certainly does develop, and she undergoes a quasi-Wordsworthian transformation from the pleasure of near solipsism to the more difficult pleasures of sympathy for others. Anne Elliot, far more mature from the beginning, scarcely needs to grow in consciousness. Her long-lamented rejection of Wentworth insulates her against the destructiveness of hope. Instead of hope, there is a complex of emotions, expressed by Austen with her customary skill:

安妮·艾略特的文采该有多么雄辩啊！——至少，她对早早萌生的热烈情愫和对未来的乐观自信是多么的渴望啊！她反对那种过度焦虑的谨慎，那种谨慎似乎侮辱了努力，也怀疑了天意！——她年轻时被迫变得谨慎，随着年龄的增长，她才学会了浪漫——这是不自然的开始之后的自然结果。

How eloquent could Anne Elliot have been,—how eloquent, at least, were her wishes on the side of early warm attachment, and a cheerful confidence in futurity, against that over-anxious caution which seems to insult exertion and distrust Providence!—She had been forced into prudence in her youth, she learned romance as she grew older—the natural sequel of an unnatural beginning.

在这里，对爱情的理解完全是回顾性的；安妮不再认为爱情对她来说是唾手可得的。的确，温特沃斯回来了，八年后依然心怀怨恨，他意识到安妮对他的影响力已永远消失。他之所以能成为一位杰出的海军指挥官，正是因为他拥有果断和自信的品质，而这些品质恰恰是他谴责安妮所缺乏的。奥斯汀以近乎苛刻的笔触，描绘了他逐渐放弃这种地位的过程：记忆的力量日益占据主导，他逐渐意识到自己之前认为安妮无能为力的想法完全是错误的。讽刺的是，他需要经历一个自我说服的过程，而安妮却在等待，甚至不知道自己也在等待，也不知道有什么能重新燃起她的希望。这种喜剧效果中带着一丝淡淡的忧伤，因为读者也在等待，思考着偶然性在这件事中扮演了多么重要的角色。

Here learning romance is wholly retrospective; Anne no longer regards it as being available to her. And, indeed, Wentworth returns, still resentful after eight years, and reflects that Anne’s power with him is gone forever. The qualities of decision and confidence that make him a superb naval commander are precisely what he condemns her for lacking. With almost too meticulous a craft, Austen traces his gradual retreat from this position, as the power of memory increases its dominance over him and as he learns that his jilted sense of her as being unable to act is quite mistaken. It is a beautiful irony that he needs to undergo a process of self-persuasion while Anne waits, without even knowing that she is waiting or that there is anything that could rekindle her hope. The comedy of this is gently sad, as the reader waits also, reflecting upon how large a part contingency plays in the matter.

尽管前苏格拉底哲学家和弗洛伊德都认为世间万物皆非偶然，但奥斯汀却持不同观点。对她而言，性格亦是命运，但命运一旦启动，在奥斯汀所处的那个社会环境如此复杂多变的情况下，往往会凌驾于性格之上。重读《劝导》，即便我仍记得那令人欣慰的结局，但温特沃斯和安妮却不由自主地渐行渐远，这依然令我感到焦虑。直到安妮读到温特沃斯写给她的那封饱含痛苦的信，读者才能完全相信他们最终会达成和解。

While the pre-Socratics and Freud agree that there are no accidents, Austen thinks differently. Character is fate for her also, but fate, once activated, tends to evade character in so overdetermined a social context as Austen’s world. In rereading Persuasion, though I remember the happy conclusion, I nevertheless feel anxiety as Wentworth and Anne circle away from each other in spite of themselves. The reader is not totally persuaded of a satisfactory interview until Anne reads Wentworth’s quite agonized letter to her:

“我再也无法默默聆听。我必须用我力所能及的方式与你交谈。你刺穿了我的灵魂。我一半痛苦，一半希望。不要告诉我一切都太迟了，不要告诉我如此珍贵的感情已永远消逝。我再次将自己献给你，我的心比八年半前你几乎将它击碎时更加属于你。不要说男人比女人更容易遗忘，不要说男人的爱更早消逝。我只爱过你。我或许不义，或许软弱，或许怨恨，但我从未动摇过。只有你把我带到巴斯。我的思绪和计划都只为你。——你难道没有看到这一切吗？你难道不明白我的心意吗？——如果我能读懂你的心意，就像我想你一定也读懂了我的心意一样，我甚至不会等这十天。我几乎无法写作。我每时每刻都听到一些令我难以承受的声音。你压低了声音，但我能分辨出你声音中的细微差别，而其他人却听不出来。——太好了，太完美了！”你确实公正无私。你相信人与人之间存在真挚的感情和忠贞。相信这种感情在FW中最为炽烈，最为坚定。

“我必须走了，生死未卜；但我会尽快回来，或者跟随你们一行人。只需一句话，一个眼神，就能决定我今晚是能进你父亲的家，还是永远都进不去。”

“I can listen no longer in silence. I must speak to you by such means as are within my reach. You pierce my soul. I am half agony, half hope. Tell me not that I am too late, that such precious feelings are gone for ever. I offer myself to you again with a heart even more your own, than when you almost broke it eight years and a half ago. Dare not say that man forgets sooner than woman, that his love has an earlier death. I have loved none but you. Unjust I may have been, weak and resentful I have been, but never inconstant. You alone have brought me to Bath. For you alone I think and plan.—Have you not seen this? Can you fail to have understood my wishes?—I had not waited even these ten days, could I have read your feelings, as I think you must have penetrated mine. I can hardly write. I am every instant hearing something which overpowers me. You sink your voice, but I can distinguish the tones of that voice, when they would be lost on others.—Too good, too excellent creature! You do us justice indeed. You do believe that there is true attachment and constancy among men. Believe it to be most fervent, most undeviating, in F.W.

“I must go, uncertain of my fate; but I shall return hither, or follow your party, as soon as possible. A word, a look will be enough to decide whether I enter your father’s house this evening, or never.”

我无法想象《傲慢与偏见》中会出现这样一封信，甚至《爱玛》或《曼斯菲尔德庄园》中也未曾出现过。敏锐的读者或许从小说伊始就已察觉到安妮的热情，但在此之前，温特沃斯身上丝毫没有流露出同等的热情。他的信，正如一位海军指挥官应有的风格，文笔拙劣，并不完全符合奥斯汀的笔法，但这反而更显其魅力。我们逐渐意识到，此前我们之所以相信他，仅仅是因为安妮对他的爱激起了我们的兴趣。奥斯汀明智地没有让他本身就足够引人入胜。然而，本书的部分效果在于，它让读者相信自身拥有敏锐的洞察力和自我说服力；安妮·艾略特对读者来说几乎完美得有些过分，正如她对奥斯汀本人而言也过于完美一样，但细心的读者最终会获得足够的自信，以正确的视角看待安妮。这部小说最微妙之处在于，它唤起读者自身的记忆力，以匹配安妮·艾略特过于坚忍而无法直接表达的那种持久而强烈的渴望。

I cannot imagine such a letter in Pride and Prejudice, or even in Emma or Mansfield Park. The perceptive reader might have realized how passionate Anne was, almost from the start of the novel, but until this there was no indication of equal passion in Wentworth. His letter, as befits a naval commander, is badly written and not exactly Austenian, but is all the more effective thereby. We come to realize that we have believed in him until now only because Anne’s love for him provokes our interest. Austen wisely has declined to make him interesting enough on his own. Yet part of the book’s effect is to persuade the reader of the reader’s own powers of discernment and self-persuasion; Anne Elliot is almost too good for the reader, as she is for Austen herself, but the attentive reader gains the confidence to perceive Anne as she should be perceived. The subtlest element in this subtlest of novels is the call upon the reader’s own power of memory to match the persistence and intensity of the yearning that Anne Elliot is too stoical to express directly.

书中始终萦绕着一种渴望，它影响着安妮的感知，也影响着我们自身的感知。我们对安妮存在的感知，与我们自身对逝去爱情的记忆紧密相连，无论这种爱情是虚构的还是理想化的。一段八年前破裂的感情能够成功修复，这本身就显得不太可能，这本应会削弱奥斯汀这部最“现实主义”小说的质感，但她却巧妙地避免了这种情况的发生。如同作者一样，读者也被说服，开始为安妮祈祷，希望她也能拥有自己渴望的东西。安·莫兰敏锐地指出，奥斯汀“在安妮对自己最不满的时候，对安妮也最满意”。读者跟随奥斯汀的笔触，逐渐地，安妮也被说服，最终与读者产生共鸣，让她的渴望得以更充分地表达出来。

The yearning hovers throughout the book, coloring Anne’s perceptions and our own. Our sense of Anne’s existence becomes identified with our own consciousness of lost love, however fictive or idealized that may be. There is an improbability in the successful renewal of a relationship devastated eight years before which ought to work against the texture of this most “realistic” of Austen’s novels, but she is very careful to see that it does not. Like the author, the reader becomes persuaded to wish for Anne what she still wishes for herself. Ann Molan has the fine observation that Austen “is most satisfied with Anne when Anne is most dissatisfied with herself.” The reader is carried along with Austen, and gradually Anne is also persuaded and catches up with the reader, allowing her yearning a fuller expression.

约翰逊博士在《漫步者》杂志第29期“预见不幸的愚蠢之处”一文中警告人们不要抱有任何焦虑的预期，无论是恐惧的还是充满希望的：

Dr. Johnson, in The Rambler, Number 29, on “The Folly of Anticipating Misfortunes,” warned against anxious expectations of any kind, whether fearful or hopeful:

因为恐惧和希望的对象都尚不确定，所以我们不应偏袒任何一方，因为它们都同样具有谬误；希望能增加幸福，恐惧则会加剧灾难。人们普遍认为，没有人能从拥有中获得与其渴望和追求相匹配的幸福；也没有人能从现实中感受到生活之苦如其想象中那般可怕。

because the objects both of fear and hope are yet uncertain, so we ought not to trust the representations of one more than the other, because they are both equally fallacious; as hope enlarges happiness, fear aggravates calamity. It is generally allowed, that no man ever found the happiness of possession proportionate to that expectation which incited his desire, and invigorated his pursuit; nor has any man found the evils of life so formidable in reality, as they were described to him by his own imagination.

这是约翰逊一系列反对想象力泛滥的论断之一，他的门徒奥斯汀肯定读过其中一些。如果按照这位伟大评论家的建议，排除掉这类表现形式，那么华兹华斯就根本无法写作，奥斯汀也无法写出《劝导》。然而，对于这位西方小说中精通排除艺术的大师来说，写出这样一部作品却十分怪异。简·奥斯汀的任何一部小说都可以被称为一种精妙的省略，所有可能干扰她那讽刺却又令人愉悦的结局的事物都被省略了。《劝导》是她四部经典小说中最不受欢迎的一部，因为它最为怪异。她站在感伤主义时代的尾声，与华兹华斯一样，她的艺术依赖于一种分裂：一方面是日渐衰落的新教意志，另一方面是新近活跃起来的同情性想象力，而记忆则被赋予了弥合这种分裂的重任。

This is one of a series of Johnsonian pronouncements against the dangerous prevalence of the imagination, some of which his disciple Austen had certainly read. If you excluded such representations, on the great critic’s advice, then Wordsworth could not have written at all, and Austen could not have written Persuasion. Yet it was a very strange book for her to write, this master of the highest art of exclusion that we have known in the Western novel. Any novel by Jane Austen could be called an achieved ellipsis, with everything omitted that could disturb her ironic though happy conclusions. Persuasion remains the least popular of her four canonical novels because it is the strangest. Poised as she is at the final border of the Age of Sensibility, she shares with Wordsworth an art dependent upon a split between a waning Protestant will and a newly active sympathetic imagination, with memory assigned the labor of healing the divide.

第七章

CHAPTER 7

I Promessi Sposi（未婚夫）（1827、1840）

I Promessi Sposi (The Betrothed) (1827, 1840)

莱桑德罗· M ·安佐尼

ALESSANDRO MANZONI

任何在意大利长期居住过的人都会感受到亚历山德罗·曼佐尼的影响力。尽管他只创作过一部小说《订婚者：十七世纪米兰的故事》和几首令人难忘的诗歌，但在有文化修养的意大利人眼中，他却是一位堪比但丁、威尔第、莱奥帕尔迪和翁加雷蒂的文化巨匠。

ANYONE WHO HAS LIVED in Italy for protracted stays will encounter the aura of Alessandro Manzoni. Though he wrote only a single novel, The Betrothed: A Tale of XVII Century Milan, and a few memorable poems, he is for literate Italians a cultural titan akin to Dante, Verdi, Leopardi, Ungaretti.

1873年5月22日，亚历山德罗·曼佐尼逝世，享年88岁，意大利举国哀悼。在美国，沃尔特·惠特曼和赫尔曼·梅尔维尔——至今仍是我们最不朽的作家——的逝世，恐怕不会举行哀悼日。曼佐尼的地位远不及但丁，但除了莎士比亚、塞万提斯和蒙田，又有谁能与但丁比肩呢？然而在意大利，如今读但丁的人寥寥无几，曼佐尼的作品依然拥有读者。

When Alessandro Manzoni died at the age of eighty-eight on May 22, 1873, Italy observed a day of mourning. In the United States, it is inconceivable that there should have been a day of mourning for Walt Whitman or Herman Melville, to this moment our most enduring writers. Manzoni is hardly of Dante’s eminence, but, then, who is, except for Shakespeare, Cervantes, and Montaigne? Yet in Italy, where alas so few now read Dante, Manzoni still finds an audience.

尽管曼佐尼将《订婚者》的故事背景设定在十七世纪，但他的写作却是针对他所处的那个浪漫化基督教时代，以及他所期盼的未来。他从维吉尔和但丁的作品中找到了理想的先驱，但实际上，如果没有沃尔特·斯科特爵士的范例和创作方法，他根本无法完成这部小说。曼佐尼从1828年到1850年潜心创作的论文《论历史小说》实际上是对他的小说的辩护，而他直到1840年仍在不断修改这部小说。他从未直接提及《订婚者》，而是暗示读者可以自行领会他隐藏的主题：历史小说能否存续？

Though he sets The Betrothed in the seventeenth century, Manzoni writes for his own era of romanticized Christianity and for what he hoped would be the future. He found his desired precursors in Virgil and in Dante, but actually he could not have composed his novel without the example and procedures of Sir Walter Scott. His essay On the Historical Novel, on which Manzoni labored from 1828 to 1850, was an apologia for his novel, which he kept revising until 1840. He never mentions The Betrothed but relies implicitly on his readers to know his hidden theme: can the historical novel survive?

伟大的诗人与伟大的历史学家可以同时存在于同一个人身上而不致混淆，但不能同时存在于同一部作品中。事实上，构成历史小说审判论据的两种截然相反的批评，早在历史小说诞生之初及其鼎盛时期就已出现，如同看似健康的婴儿体内潜藏着致命疾病的病菌。

历史小说如今还流行吗？人们创作历史小说的热情和阅读历史小说的热情是否依旧？我不得而知，但我忍不住想象，如果这篇文章发表于三十年前，那时世人正翘首以盼、如饥似渴地阅读沃尔特·斯科特的小说，那么它对历史小说的论述或许会显得古怪而鲁莽。我也不禁想象，即便现在有人愿意费心思给它贴上这样的标签，其原因也必然截然不同。而对于一种注定长存的艺术体裁而言，三十年本不该是一段漫长的岁月。

（译者：桑德拉·伯曼）

A great poet and a great historian may be found in the same man without creating confusion, but not in the same work. In fact, the two opposite criticisms that furnished the lines of argument for the trial of the historical novel had already showed up in the first moments of the genre and at the height of its popularity, like germs of an eventually mortal illness in a healthy-looking baby.

And is the historical novel still popular? Is there the same desire to write historical novels and the same desire to read those that are already written? I don’t know, but I can not help imagining that, if this essay had come out some thirty years ago, when the world was eagerly awaiting and avidly devouring the novels of Walter Scott, it would have seemed eccentric and brash in its treatment of the historical novel. Nor can I help imagining that, if anyone now were willing to trouble himself enough to call it these names, it would be for an altogether different reason. And thirty years ought to be no time at all for a genre of art that was destined to live on.

(trans. Sandra Bermann)

我记得1984年我曾思考过这个问题，当时我评论了戈尔·维达尔的《林肯》，认为它几乎可以算得上是历史小说的一次真正复兴。多年后，我在罗马附近拜访了维达尔和他的伴侣，并饶有兴致地听他谈起曼佐尼和卡尔维诺。曼佐尼的预言似乎很准确；如今，即使是最优秀的历史小说，似乎也难免缺乏新鲜感。

I remember pondering this matter in 1984, when I reviewed Gore Vidal’s Lincoln and judged it to be something close to a legitimate revival of the historical novel. Years later, I visited Vidal and his partner near Rome and enjoyed his reaction to Manzoni and to Calvino. It seems likely that Manzoni was an accurate prophet; even the most talented historical novels now seem tainted by a lack of freshness whenever they appear.

我重读曼佐尼的《订婚夫妇》时，感觉它不像是一部历史小说。曼佐尼本人就是这本书的灵魂。字里行间流露出的，是作者的温情、基督教式的怜悯、辛辣的幽默，以及一种温柔却又令人惊叹的力量，他以生动的笔触描绘了瘟疫、饥荒、暴乱、无端暴力等种种恐怖，以及年轻的农家恋人露西亚和伦佐痛苦的分离。他们受到可怕的西班牙贵族唐·罗德里戈的威胁，罗德里戈垂涎露西亚的美色，并恐吓教区神父唐·阿邦迪奥，迫使他拒绝为这对未婚夫妇主持婚礼。

Manzoni’s The Betrothed, as I reread it, does not seem like a historical novel. The man is the book. What comes through on every page is the warmth, Christian compassion, wry humor, and gentle yet surprising strength to deal vividly with horrors like the plague, famine, riots, random violence, and the painful separation of the young peasant lovers Lucia and Renzo, who are menaced by the dreadful Don Rodrigo, a Spanish nobleman who lusts after Lucia and who has frightened the parish priest Don Abbondio into refusing to perform the marriage of the betrothed couple.

唐·阿邦迪奥是个滑稽的弱者，这在小说中显得格外独特，因为其他所有神职人员都睿智、仁慈，甚至英勇无畏。有时我觉得曼佐尼最令人惊讶的成就，就是他成功地消除了我在这方面的怀疑。嘉布遣会修士克里斯托弗罗在与唐·罗德里戈对峙时，展现出了非凡的英雄气概：

Don Abbondio is a comic weakling, unique in this novel because all the rest of the clergy are wise, benign, and even heroic. Sometimes I think that the most surprising achievement of Manzoni is to overcome my skepticism in this regard. The Capuchin monk Fra Cristoforo is superbly heroic as he confronts Don Rodrigo:

“那就劝她过来，让她接受我的保护。她想要什么我都会满足，而且没人敢骚扰她，否则我就不是绅士了。”

听到这个提议，修士原本竭力压抑的愤慨瞬间爆发。他所有谨慎和耐心的决心都烟消云散；旧我与新我融为一体：在这种情况下，克里斯托弗修士实际上拥有了两个人的精力。

“你的保护！”他喊道，后退了几步，骄傲地踮起右脚，右手叉腰，左手伸出食指指向唐·罗德里戈，目光如炬地盯着他——“你的保护！幸好你说了那句话；幸好你提出了这样的建议。你太过分了：我再也不怕你了。”

“你竟敢这样跟我说话，修士！”

“我仿佛在和一个被上帝遗弃的人说话，一个再也无法吓唬人的人说话。你的庇护！我当然知道那个无辜的女孩受到上帝的庇护；但是你——你让我对此如此确信，以至于我不再需要小心翼翼地对你说话了。露西亚，我说——你看我是如何昂首挺胸、目光坚定地念出她的名字的。”

“什么！在这房子里……！”

“我怜悯这房子。诅咒笼罩着它。你们等着瞧，几块石头能挡住上帝的审判，两个哨兵就能吓退它。你们以为上帝按照自己的形象创造了一个生命，是为了让你们享受折磨她的乐趣吗？你们以为上帝不会保护她吗？你们藐视了他的警告。你们必将为此受审判！法老的心和你们一样刚硬，但上帝找到了办法将它击碎。露西娅不会伤害你们；我——一个贫穷的修士——都这样告诉你们；至于你们自己，听听我对你们的预言。总有一天……”

直到此刻，唐·罗德里戈都呆立在那里，愤怒和惊讶让他说不出话来；但当他听到这预言的开头被吟诵出来时，他的愤怒中又增添了一种模糊而神秘的恐惧。

他迅速抓住那只举起的、带有威胁意味的手，提高嗓门盖过这个不祥预言家的声音，喊道：“滚出我的视线，你这个厚颜无耻的乡巴佬，你这个戴着兜帽的粗人！”

‘Well, advise her to come and put herself under my protection. She’ll have everything she wants, and no one’ll dare molest her, or I’m no gentleman.’

At this suggestion the friar’s indignation, which he had held in check with difficulty till then, burst out. All his resolutions of prudence and patience went to the winds; his old self joined up with the new: in such cases, in fact, Fra Cristoforo really had the energy of two men.

‘Your protection!’ exclaimed he, recoiling a couple of paces, leaning proudly on his right foot, putting his right hand to his hip, pointing the other with outstretched forefinger towards Don Rodrigo, and fixing on him a pair of blazing eyes—‘your protection! It’s a good thing you said that; it’s a good thing you made such a suggestion. You’ve gone over the limit: and I’m not afraid of you any more.’

‘How dare you talk to me like that, friar!’

‘I’m talking as one talks to one abandoned by God, who cannot frighten any longer. Your protection! I well knew that innocent girl was under God’s protection; but you—you’ve filled me with such a certainty of it now that I no longer need to take care what I say to you. Lucia, I say—see how I pronounce her name with head high and steady eyes.’

‘What! In this house…!’

‘I pity this house. A curse hangs over it. You will see if the justice of God can be kept out by a few stones, or frightened off by a pair of sentries. You think God made a creature in His own image in order to give you the pleasure of tormenting her! You think God won’t be able to defend her! You’ve spurned His warning. You are judged for it! Pharaoh’s heart was as hard as yours, and God found a way to crush it. Lucia is safe from you; I—a poor friar—I tell you that; and as for yourself, listen to what I foretell for you. A day will come…’

Up to now Don Rodrigo had been standing rooted there, speechless with rage and amazement; but when he heard this beginning of a prophecy being intoned, a vague, mysterious dread was added to his rage.

Quickly he seized that lifted, threatening hand, and, raising his voice to drown that of this prophet of ill-omen, shouted: ‘Get out of my sight, you impudent peasant, you lout in a cowl.’

唐·罗德里戈虽然已经够邪恶了，但与书中真正的大反派——“无名氏”相比，却显得相形见绌。这个反派的原型是历史上一个真实的恶棍：米兰公爵的后裔弗朗切斯科·贝尔纳迪诺·维斯康蒂，他因被仁慈的红衣主教费德里戈·博罗梅奥感化而改邪归正，而博罗梅奥正是曼佐尼笔下真正的英雄。在转变之前，“无名氏”的邪恶简直令人啼笑皆非：

Don Rodrigo, though more than nasty enough, is dwarfed by the book’s grand villain, known only as the Unnamed. He is based upon an actual historical monster, Francesco Bernardino Visconti, a scion of the Dukes of Milan, famous for being converted from iniquity to goodness by the benevolent Cardinal Federigo Borromeo, Manzoni’s authentic hero. Until that transformation, the Unnamed is all but hilariously wicked:

然而，我们这位暴君的名声早已传遍米兰各省。他的生平事迹在各地都成了民间传说的素材，他的名字本身就带有某种引人入胜、离奇古怪、充满传奇色彩的意味。人们怀疑他到处都有爪牙和雇佣杀手，这也使得他的事迹在各地广为流传。这些仅仅是猜测——毕竟谁会公开承认自己受人摆布呢？——但每一个小暴君都可能是他的同伙，每一个小恶棍都可能是他的爪牙。正是这种不确定性，使得人们对他的认知更加宏大，对他的恐惧也更加深重。每当一群身份不明、面目狰狞的暴徒出现在某个地方，每当发生骇人听闻的罪行，而凶手又无法立即被指认或猜测时，人们就会低声议论那个人的名字——多亏了当局的谨慎，我们不得不称他为“无名氏”。

The fame of our tyrant, however, had long been diffused throughout the whole of the Milanese provinces. Everywhere his life was a subject for popular tales, and his name bore with it the idea of something compelling, strange, and fabulous. The suspicion that he had his agents and hired assassins everywhere also contributed to keeping his memory alive everywhere. These were only suspicions—for who would openly avow such a dependence? —but every petty tyrant might be his colleague, every little malefactor one of his men. And this very uncertainty made the conception of it vaster, and the fear of it deeper. Whenever a set of unknown and unusually savage-looking bravoes put in an appearance anywhere, whenever some appalling crime was committed whose author could not be pointed out or guessed at once, people muttered the name of the man whom, thanks to that blessed circumspection of our authorities, we shall be constrained to call the Unnamed.

《未婚妻》的任何情节梗概听起来都可能相当荒谬，因为其中的戏剧性元素可能会让人感到不适。然而，瘟疫的威胁和恐怖却弥补了小说中那些令人不忍直视的情节。可怜的露西娅承受着巨大的精神和道德折磨，以至于她向圣母玛利亚许愿，如果神明能让她免于遭受比死亡更可怕的命运——被唐·罗德里戈强奸，她将放弃与伦佐或其他任何人的婚姻。最终，还是弗拉·克里斯托弗罗说服了她，让她相信上帝和圣母玛利亚希望她嫁给伦佐。

Any plot summary of The Betrothed can sound quite silly, since the melodramatic elements can make one wince a bit. Still, menace and the horror of the plague work to redeem the Perils of Pauline aspects of the novel. Poor Lucia suffers intensely mental and moral anguish, to the point where she promises the Virgin Mary that she will renounce marriage to Renzo or anyone else if the divine powers rescue her from the well-known fate worse than death, rape by Don Rodrigo. It will take Fra Cristoforo to persuade her that God and the Virgin Mother want her to marry Renzo.

重读《订婚夫妇》，尽管我对天主教的虔诚毫无兴趣，却依然兴致盎然。曼佐尼之所以能够触及普世情感，是因为他笔下人物和个性的原始力量，以及他在这部杰作中驾驭多种叙事声音的卓越能力。尽管一切最终都如愿以偿：露西亚和伦佐幸福地结婚生子，唐·罗德里戈不幸死于瘟疫，无名氏成为穷人的庇护者，克里斯托弗修士成为瘟疫受害者的殉道者，曼佐尼的声音抚慰并提升了读者的精神境界，但总感觉还缺少些什么。或许是因为意大利语原著——一部以托斯卡纳方言写成的语言实验作品——即便在阿奇博尔德·科尔昆（他同时也是《曼佐尼及其时代》（1954）一书的作者）的精彩翻译下，也难免有所缺失。

Rereading The Betrothed, I enjoy myself greatly despite my lack of interest in Catholic piety. Manzoni is able to touch the universal because of the primordial strength of his character and personality, and his considerable ability to play with an assortment of narrative voices throughout his masterwork. Though everything ends as it should, with Lucia and Renzo happily married with many children, Don Rodrigo miserably dead from the plague, the Unnamed a patron of the poor, Fra Cristoforo a living martyr to the victims of the plague, and Manzoni a voice that comforts and elevates the reader, something is still lacking. Perhaps the Italian original, a language experiment in the Tuscan vernacular, loses too much even in the eloquent translation of Archibald Colquhoun, who also wrote a very useful study, Manzoni and His Times (1954).

我发现自己的保留意见令我感到遗憾，因为曼佐尼的作品带给我如此多的愉悦。我们不能要求每一部小说都像《堂吉诃德》、《克拉丽莎》或《追忆似水年华》那样伟大。 《未婚妻》与沃尔特·斯科特爵士的杰作，如《米德洛锡安之心》、约瑟夫·康拉德的《诺斯特罗莫》和菲尔丁的《汤姆·琼斯》等，属于同一类作品。这的确是一个星光熠熠的群体，但它与《悲惨世界》或《战争与和平》相比，仍略逊一筹。

I find that my reservations sadden me, since Manzoni has given me so much pleasure. One cannot ask every novel to be Don Quixote or Clarissa or In Search of Lost Time. The Betrothed finds its place in a group that includes the best of Sir Walter Scott, such as The Heart of Midlothian, Joseph Conrad’s Nostromo, and Fielding’s Tom Jones. That is an illustrious galaxy but not quite Les Misérables or War and Peace.

第八章

CHAPTER 8

红与黑（1830）

The Red and the Black (1830)

S·滕达尔

STENDHAL

司汤达（笔名，真名玛丽-亨利·贝勒）于1842年在巴黎去世，享年59岁。他死于当时荒谬的梅毒疗法，而他已患梅毒多年。鲜有著名小说家拥有像司汤达那样迷人的个性。他对生活的看法如同假面舞会或嘉年华表演一般。他笔下如潮水般涌来的书信，既诙谐又充满怀旧之情，常常流露出情欲的怀旧之情。

STENDHAL, a pseudonym for Marie-Henri Beyle, died in Paris in 1842 at the age of fifty-nine. His death was caused by the absurd treatments for syphilis, a disease he had suffered for some time. Few major novelists have had a personality so winsome as Stendhal’s. His vision of life is rather like a masked ball or a carnival performance. His torrent of letters are playful, wistful, and frequently a study in erotic nostalgia.

二十世纪法国最重要的诗人、文学家保罗·瓦雷里曾赞扬司汤达文笔生动活泼。在我看来，这正是司汤达的首要成就，他的才思妙想无穷无尽，极具感染力，正如他形容自己理想的读者那样，这种天赋只属于“少数幸运儿”。

Paul Valéry, the major French poet and person-of-letters of the twentieth century, praised Stendhal for his gift of liveliness. That seems to me the first accomplishment of Stendhal, whose wit was endless and infectious, a gift given to “the happy few,” as he characterized his ideal readers.

我非常欣赏瓦雷里的这番话：司汤达的作品让读者为成为他的读者而感到自豪。瓦雷里对司汤达的评价道，他最喜爱的这位小说家既感受到文学虚荣心的驱使，更深层次上又有一种绝对的骄傲，这种骄傲让他明白，他的作品只能依靠自身。

I love Valéry’s observation that Stendhal makes the reader proud to be his reader. The heart of Stendhal is in Valéry’s reflection that his favorite novelist felt the spur of literary vanity but more deeply an absolute pride that knew it had to depend on nothing but itself.

瓦雷里的最终结论是，司汤达的个性如此鲜明，以至于他无法被简单地定义为一位作家。

Valéry’s final judgment is that Stendhal was so radically himself that he could not be reduced to a writer.

不过，我对司汤达的了解主要还是停留在小说家这一身份上。在我看来，他最优秀的作品是未完成的《吕西安·勒文》，但这部作品对普通读者来说过于零散。《红与黑》和《帕尔马修道院》经久不衰的受欢迎程度实至名归。我自己在这两部作品之间摇摆不定，因为《帕尔马修道院》中的于连·索雷尔比《帕尔马修道院》中的任何人物都更加丰满，但司汤达笔下生动鲜活的意大利，在经历了他晦涩的法国之后，又给人一种耳目一新的感觉。

Still, I know Stendhal primarily as a novelist. His strongest work to me is the unfinished Lucien Leuwen, yet it is too fragmentary for the common reader. The perpetual popularity of The Red and the Black and The Charterhouse of Parma is more than deserved. I myself vacillate between the two, since Julien Sorel is a richer character than anyone in The Charterhouse yet the liveliness of Stendhal’s Italy is a relief after his occluded France.

尽管充满讽刺意味，我还是很难不把于连·索雷尔视为司汤达的化身。于连的想象力就是司汤达的，也就是说，它带有拿破仑和拜伦式的色彩。司汤达是否是莎士比亚式的作家尚有争议。于连几乎算不上莎士比亚式的主人公，但叙述者却是。司汤达赋予于连一种不可思议的能力，让他能够凭借意志力开启或关闭自己的情欲。小说结尾，脱胎换骨的于连再次深深地爱上了雷纳尔夫人，对玛蒂尔德·德·拉莫尔几乎漠不关心，除非她怀着他相信会是他们儿子的孩子。我们永远不会知道孩子的性别，也不知道玛蒂尔德是否会再婚。最终，我们看到的是一个有自杀倾向的于连。你可以把他的态度看作是认命，但其中也包含着令人不安的病态因素。即使是迷人的疯狂，也终究是疯狂，这对于精力充沛、活力四射、雄心勃勃的于连·索雷尔来说，是一个悲哀的命运。

Despite all ironies, I find it difficult not to see Julien Sorel as Stendhal’s surrogate. Julien’s imagination is Stendhal’s, which is to say that it is Napoleonic and Byronic. Whether Stendhal is a Shakespearean writer is open to dispute. Julien is hardly a Shakespearean protagonist, yet the narrator is. Stendhal gives Julien the uncanny ability to turn his erotic preferences on or off by acts of will. At the novel’s close, a transfigured Julien is again fiercely in love with Madame De Rênal and all but indifferent to Mathilde de La Mole, except insofar as she carries what he trusts will be their son. We never will find out the gender of the baby or whether Mathilde will or will not marry again. What we confront at the end is a suicidal Julien. You can regard his attitude as resignation, but there is a troubling element of pathology. Even an attractive craziness remains madness, a sad fate for the energetic, vital, and ambitious Julien Sorel.

如同塞万提斯一样，司汤达最能体现其“游戏人”的本质，正如约翰·赫伊津哈1938年出版的巨著《游戏人》所言，该书对艺术和历史中的游戏元素进行了深刻的研究。读了赫伊津哈的著作，我得出了一个结论：一切皆为游戏，唯独游戏除外。那么，在《于连·索雷尔》中，究竟还保留了多少堂吉诃德式的元素呢？

Like Cervantes, Stendhal is most himself as Homo Ludens, to cite the great book of 1938 by Johan Huizinga, a profound study of the play element in the arts and in history. Reading Huizinga, I arrive at the formula: all is play except in games. How much of the quixotic element remains in Julien Sorel?

司汤达的情史颇为坎坷。他七岁时母亲去世，与父亲关系恶劣。二十一岁时，他与女演员梅拉妮·吉尔伯特在马赛同居，但到了1806年，他已在不伦瑞克担任拿破仑军队的副官。 1800年，他在米兰服役期间爱上了安吉丽娜·皮特拉格鲁阿，十一年后，在他返回米兰时，安吉丽娜成为了他的情妇。然而，他一生中最主要的感情始于1818年，当时他爱上了玛蒂尔德·维斯孔蒂尼·登博夫斯卡，但遭到了她的断然拒绝。他终身未婚，情史也屡遭挫折。1824年，他与克莱芒蒂娜·库里亚尔伯爵夫人有过一段恋情，但三年后两人分手。1829年，他再次尝试，这次的对象是阿尔贝特·德·鲁本普雷，但这段感情也只是昙花一现。最后，他向朱莉娅·里涅里求婚。尽管遭到她的监护人拒绝，八年后他与她再次交往，但这段关系逐渐淡漠。到了1841年，他主要靠两条狗维持生计，或许还经历了另一段失败的恋情。由于梅毒以及当时治疗梅毒的特殊疗法，他身体虚弱，于1842年去世。

Stendhal’s own erotic career was rather vexed. His mother died when he was seven. His relations with his father were hostile. At twenty-one, he lived in Marseilles with the actress Mélanie Guilbert, but by 1806 he had taken up a post as a Napoleonic intendant in Brunswick. When in the army in 1800 in Milan, he had fallen in love with Angelina Pietragrua, who became his mistress eleven years later, on his return to Milan. Yet the major attachment of his life began in 1818, when he fell in love with Matilde Viscontini Dembowska, who totally rejected him. He never married, and went from debacle to debacle. In 1824, there was a love affair with Comtesse Clémentine Curial, but she broke with him three years later. In 1829, he tried again, this time with Alberthe de Rubempre, but it proved ephemeral. Finally, he proposed marriage to Giulia Rinieri. Though he was refused by her guardian, eight years later he became involved with her, but the relationship waned. By 1841, he was sustained mostly by his two dogs and perhaps had another failed affair. Weakened by syphilis and the peculiar remedies then used for it, he died in 1842.

作为爱欲理论家，司汤达堪称大师，尽管他在追求爱欲的过程中显然并不务实。他超凡的智慧和对快乐的感知力支撑着他，无论是在生活中还是在艺术创作中。近几周来，我一直在重读《红与黑》，先是读原著，后来又读了罗杰·加德的译本，读得津津有味，却丝毫没有厌倦。有时我会放下它，过几天再重新拿起来。我不禁思考，我为何如此被它吸引。

As a theorist of Eros, Stendhal was a master, though clearly not very pragmatic in his quest for it. His transcendent wit and sense of delight kept him going in life as in art. I have been rereading The Red and the Black, first in the original and also in the useful translation by Roger Gard, for some weeks now and cannot seem to get weary of it. Sometimes I put it down and come back to it a few days later. I find myself wondering why I am so held by it.

这部小说最初是一个名为《朱利安》的故事，取材于安托万·贝尔泰的真实经历。贝尔泰枪杀了米舒德·德·拉图尔夫人，最终被送上断头台。我记得曾在1988年我编辑的《红与黑》一书中重印过卡罗尔·A·莫斯曼的一篇精彩文章。莫斯曼女士清晰地阐述了构成这部小说——既可以称之为朱利安的小说，也可以称之为玛蒂尔德的小说——的各种线索。当朱利安战胜玛蒂尔德时，他过早地宣称自己的小说已经完成。玛蒂尔德的原型是玛格丽特·德·瓦卢瓦，她是仲马小说中的女主角，历史上她是凯瑟琳·德·美第奇的女儿。凯瑟琳·德·美第奇通过她的儿子们统治法国，直到她的王朝终结。纳瓦拉的亨利，即波旁王朝的第一位国王亨利四世，娶了玛格丽特·德·瓦卢瓦为妻。这是一场政治联姻，以友谊为主，但缺乏激情。玛格丽特王后情人众多，其中就包括约瑟夫·博尼法斯·雅辛托，即拉莫尔勋爵。这位大胆的胡格诺派教徒拉莫尔参与了营救纳瓦拉的亨利的阴谋后被斩首。传说玛格丽特王后命人将拉莫尔的头颅进行防腐处理，之后将其保存在一个镶满珠宝的匣子里。玛蒂尔德的小说以及司汤达的小说都以这样的结尾作结：

The novel began as a tale called “Julien,” based on one Antoine Berthet, who shot a Madame Michoud de la Tour and was guillotined. I recall reprinting a strong essay by Carol A. Mossman in a volume I edited on The Red and the Black in 1988. Ms. Mossman articulates the various strands that come together in what could be called Julien’s novel and also Mathilde’s novel. When he triumphs over Mathilde, Julien prematurely says that his novel is completed. Mathilde models herself upon Marguerite de Valois, heroine of a Dumas novel, and historically the daughter of Catherine de’ Medici, who ruled France through her sons until the line came to an end. Henry of Navarre, first of the Bourbon kings as Henry IV, married Marguerite de Valois, a political match marked by friendship but little passion. Queen Marguerite had many lovers, among them Joseph Boniface Hyacinth, Lord La Mole. A Huguenot, the audacious La Mole was beheaded after he joined in a plot to free Henry of Navarre. The legend is that Marguerite caused La Mole’s head to be embalmed and kept afterward in a casket bedecked by jewels. Mathilde’s novel, and Stendhal’s, concludes:

“我想见他，”她说。

福凯决心既不说话也不起身。他用手指着地板上的一件蓝色大斗篷；朱利安的遗骸就裹在里面。

她跪倒在地。毫无疑问，博尼法斯·德·拉莫尔和玛格丽特·德·纳瓦尔的记忆赋予了她超乎常人的决心。她颤抖着双手解开了斗篷。富凯别过脸去。

他听见玛蒂尔德在房间里快速走动。她点燃了许多蜡烛。当福凯鼓起勇气看向她时，她已将朱利安的头放在面前的一张小大理石桌上，正亲吻着他的额头……

玛蒂尔德跟随她的爱人来到他选定的墓地。一大群神父护送着灵柩，而所有人都不知道，她独自一人坐在蒙着面纱的灵车里，膝上抱着她深爱之人的头颅。

就这样，在夜深人静之时，队伍几乎抵达了汝拉山脉最高峰之一的顶峰。在那个被无数蜡烛照亮的幽暗小洞穴里，二十位祭司正在举行亡灵祭祀仪式。队伍途经的所有山村村民都被这奇特的仪式所吸引，纷纷跟随队伍前来。

玛蒂尔德身穿长长的丧服出现在人群中，仪式结束后，成千上万枚五法郎的硬币散落在人群中。

她独自一人与福凯待在一起时，坚持要亲手埋下爱人的头。福凯几乎因悲痛而精神崩溃。

在玛蒂尔德的安排下，这个荒凉的洞穴被装饰上了在意大利耗费巨资雕刻的大理石浮雕。

雷纳尔夫人信守了她的诺言。她绝无自杀之意；但在朱利安去世三天后，她也离开了人世，孩子们就在她的怀里。

剧终

致少数幸运儿

—I want to see him, she said.

Fouqué had the resolution neither to speak nor to rise. He pointed with his finger at a large blue cloak on the floorboards; in that was wrapped what remained of Julien.

She threw herself on her knees. The memory of Boniface de La Mole and Marguerite de Navarre inspired her, no doubt, with superhuman resolve. Her trembling hands opened the cloak. Fouqué turned away his eyes.

He heard Mathilde walking about rapidly in the room. She lit a large number of candles. When Fouqué summoned up the strength to look at her, she had placed Julien’s head on a little marble table in front of her, and was kissing its brow…

Mathilde followed her lover to the tomb he had chosen. A large band of priests escorted the bier and, unknown to all, alone in her veiled carriage, she carried on her knees the head of the man she had so dearly loved.

Coming in this way almost to the summit of one of the highest mountains in the Jura, in the depths of the night, and in that little cave now magnificently lit up by innumerable tapers, twenty priests celebrated the service for the dead. All the inhabitants of the little mountain villages that the convoy had crossed followed it, attracted by the singularity of this strange rite.

Mathilde appeared in the midst of them in long mourning robes and, at the end of the service, had many thousand five-franc pieces scattered in the crowd.

Left alone with Fouqué, she insisted on burying her lover’s head with her own hands. Fouqué narrowly avoided losing his mind with grief.

By Mathilde’s agency this wild cavern was decorated with marble carvings sculpted in Italy at great expense.

Mme de Rênal was faithful to her promise. In no way did she seek to take her own life; but three days after Julien, she died, her children in her arms.

The End

To The Happy Few

司汤达对结局持一种漫不经心的态度。雷纳尔夫人虔诚得不像话，不可能自杀。我们并不知道她三天后究竟是什么夺走了她的生命。除非她期待着尤利安复活，否则很难想象有人会独自因悲伤而死。玛蒂尔德比尤利安还要疯狂，或许她扮演纳瓦拉王后玛格丽特的角色能给她带来慰藉。卡罗尔·莫斯曼巧妙地梳理了司汤达的叙事脉络，将罗马皇帝尤利安、施洗约翰、拿破仑以及舞女莎乐美交织在一起。莎乐美在被人用银盘端来施洗约翰的头颅后，亲吻并充满欲望地抚摸着它。

Stendhal takes a throwaway attitude toward endings. Madame de Rênal is too pious for suicide. We are not told what kills her after three days. Unless she had expected a resurrected Julien, it is rather difficult to see anyone dying of grief alone. Mathilde, crazier even than Julien, perhaps finds comfort in acting the part of Queen Marguerite of Navarre. Carol Mossman shrewdly retraces Stendhal’s web that weaves together the Roman Emperor Julian the Apostate, Saint John the Baptist, Napoleon, and the dancer Salome, who kisses and lustfully caresses the severed head of John after it has been brought to her on a silver platter.

那么于连·索雷尔呢？当司汤达将他从我们身边带走时，他又是怎样的呢？他既令人钦佩，又令人厌恶。他对玛蒂尔德极其冷漠。玛蒂尔德为他付出了那么多，却被他视作一个闯入者。他几乎懒得假装对她有任何爱意。然而，对于他曾试图谋杀的雷纳尔夫人，他却达到了前所未有的爱的狂喜，而雷纳尔夫人也完全沉浸其中。除了戏剧性的反讽之外，司汤达的笔触摒弃了讽刺挖苦。

And what of Julien Sorel? How is he when Stendhal takes him away from us? He is and he is not admirable. Toward Mathilde he is dreadful. Having gone through so much for him, she is made to feel like an intruder. He scarcely bothers to pretend any love for her. But toward Madame de Rênal, whose murder he has attempted, he mounts to an ecstasy of love beyond anything he has ever known, and in which she fully shares. Except for dramatic irony, Stendhal’s stance eschews sardonicism.

于连为何选择死亡？他审视自身，审视社会，审视基督教，也审视司汤达的小说——这部小说剥夺了他其他出路。一部原本是喜剧的作品，无法容纳悲剧的结局。你不可能不喜欢司汤达。你很难对于连产生任何好感，事实上，也很难对小说中的其他任何人物产生好感。或许仅仅是因为，拿破仑的神话——尽管对司汤达、巴尔扎克、维克多·雨果来说依然如此强大——已经失去了往日的魅力。没有拿破仑，就没有于连·索雷尔。

Why does Julien choose death? He passes judgment on himself, on society, on Christianity, and on Stendhal’s novel that denies him any other exit. A book that has been comedy cannot accommodate a tragic conclusion. It is impossible not to like Stendhal. It is very difficult to have any affection for Julien, or indeed for anyone else in the novel. Perhaps it is simply that the myth of Napoleon, still so potent for Stendhal, Balzac, Victor Hugo, has worn itself out. Without Napoleon, no Julien Sorel.

瑟米斯对司汤达不愿完成作品感到十分困惑。我确信，他对于连·索雷尔的喜爱几乎不亚于塞万提斯对堂吉诃德的喜爱。《悲伤的骑士》以优雅的结局收尾，因为他接受了失败。我不认为于连·索雷尔被打败了，尽管他最终选择了优雅的结局。想想于连在整部小说中经历了多少。无论她或他自身有何局限，他都赢得了两位杰出女性的爱。在一个鄙视试图跻身上流社会的农民的社会里，他几乎已经战胜了自己的出身。

Surmise is rather baffled by Stendhal’s aversion to completion. I am persuaded that he loves Julien Sorel almost as much as Cervantes loved Don Quixote. The Sorrowful Knight graciously ends because he accepts defeat. I do not think that Julien Sorel has been defeated, though he chooses to end graciously anyway. Consider how far Julien has come in the course of the novel. He has achieved the love of two remarkable women, whatever their limitations or his. He has come within a notch of triumphing over his origins, in a society that despises peasants who seek to rise into the world of aristocrats.

司汤达赋予于连几乎所有自然所能赋予的特质。他英俊潇洒，勇敢无畏，才智过人，是位领袖而非追随者，却又孤苦伶仃，缺乏父爱。即便在故事的结尾，他也只是偶尔流露出些许阴郁的沉闷。他如同他的创造者司汤达一样，在清醒与激情之间摇摆不定。

Stendhal endows Julien with almost all that nature can give. He is very handsome, courageous, capable of intellectual brilliance, a leader, not a follower, yet motherless, pragmatically unfathered. Even at the close he has only sporadic moments of dark inertia. He eddies between lucidity and passion, as does his creator, Stendhal.

朱利安（Julien）之所以能得救（纯粹从世俗意义上来说），是因为他拥有深厚的情感。尽管他的处境迫使他做出种种虚伪之事，但他始终追求的是爱和精神的自由。

Julien is saved (in a purely secular way) by his capacity for deep feeling. Despite all the hypocrisies forced upon him by his situation, his quest is for love and for the spirit’s freedom.

第九章

CHAPTER 9

帕尔马修道院（1839 年）

The Charterhouse of Parma (1839)

S·滕达尔

STENDHAL

尽管司汤达称这部小说为短篇小说，但无论篇幅还是构思，它都相当厚重。然而，他却在1838年末不到两个月的时间内就完成了这部作品。故事发生在意大利北部——他最喜爱的地区——以及拿破仑战败之后，拿破仑曾是他的偶像。司汤达幻想自己有一半意大利血统，并暗示小说中迷人的男主人公法布里齐奥·德尔·东戈（Fabrizio del Dongo）——他是美艳动人的吉娜·桑塞维里娜公爵夫人（Gina Sanseverina）的姻亲侄子，而公爵夫人也爱慕着他——是罗伯特中尉的私生子。罗伯特中尉后来出现在滑铁卢战场上。当他再次出现时，他已是罗伯特伯爵将军，法布里齐奥根本认不出他。然而，正如司汤达所说：“他要是能找到法布里齐奥·德尔·东戈该有多高兴啊！”父亲以司汤达式的讽刺手法偷走了儿子的马。

THOUGH STENDHAL CALLED this a short novel, it is quite substantial, in length as in design. And yet he wrote it in less than two months, in late 1838. It is set in the north of Italy, his favorite region, in the aftermath of Napoleon, his sometime hero. Stendhal had a fantasy that he was half Italian and hints that Fabrizio del Dongo, the delightful male protagonist and nephew-by-marriage of the marvelous Duchess Gina Sanseverina, who is in love with him, was the illegitimate son of Lieutenant Robert, who turns up later in the novel on the battlefield of Waterloo. When he reappears, he is General Count d’A*** Robert, whom Fabrizio has no way of recognizing, yet, as Stendhal remarks, “How happy he would have been to find Fabrizio del Dongo!” With Stendhalian irony, the father steals the son’s horse.

法布里齐奥在滑铁卢的经历是司汤达笔下著名的场景。他为法军而战，目睹并听到炮火轰鸣，甚至远远地看到了拿破仑皇帝。然而，此时这位年轻的意大利贵族已是醉酒，神志不清，无法确定自己所见究竟是什么。法军溃败，普鲁士骑兵的胜利在法军阵营中引发了恐慌，可怜的法布里齐奥奉命行事，却被法国逃兵重伤。这位贵族最终还是回到了家乡，而司汤达的故事也继续向前推进。

Fabrizio’s experience of Waterloo is a famous set-piece. He fights on the side of the French, sees and hears cannon fire and gunfire and even, at a distance, the Emperor Napoleon, though by then the young Italian nobleman is so high on brandy he cannot be sure what he sees. The French army breaks up, and the victorious Prussian cavalry causes such hysteria in the ranks that poor Fabrizio, obeying orders, is severely wounded by French deserters. The noble scamp finds his way back home eventually, and Stendhal charges on.

司汤达是莎士比亚的忠实拥趸，他在《帕尔马修道院》中创作了自己的《罗密欧与朱丽叶》版本。法布里齐奥比罗密欧更胜一筹，但朱丽叶却是莎士比亚笔下最伟大的角色之一，无人能超越。法布里齐奥笔下的朱丽叶是虔诚的克莱莉娅，我觉得她平淡无奇，难以配得上司汤达笔下那种热情洋溢的魅力。然而，和所有读者一样，我被魅力四射的吉娜·德尔·东戈深深吸引。她是一位年轻的寡妇，比法布里齐奥年长十五岁，化名吉娜·皮特拉内拉，即圣塞维里娜公爵夫人。吉娜深深爱着她的姻亲侄子，因此不存在乱伦的障碍。但法布里齐奥，这位日后将成为教会高官的人物，对与姑姑发生任何实质性的性关系都十分谨慎，尽管他们之间关系暧昧。他并不爱她，尽管他看重她胜过世上任何人。

Stendhal, a lover of Shakespeare, composes his own version of Romeo and Juliet in The Charterhouse of Parma. Fabrizio is an improvement upon Romeo, but no one could improve upon Juliet, who is one of Shakespeare’s triumphs. The Juliet of Fabrizio is the pious Clelia, whom I find rather colorless and hardly worthy of the Stendhalian gusto. However, like all readers, I am fascinated by the magnificent Gina del Dongo, who is a young widow, fifteen years older than Fabrizio, and is known under the name of Gina Pietranera, the Duchess Sanseverina. Gina is totally in love with her nephew by marriage, and so there is no incest barrier, but Fabrizio, who will become a high dignitary of the Church, is very wary of any actual consummation with his aunt, though they come close. He is not in love with her, though he regards her more highly than anyone else alive.

莫斯卡伯爵已步入中年，他深爱着吉娜，但吉娜的座右铭是：如果法布里齐奥不快乐，我也无法快乐。莫斯卡伯爵是一位和蔼可亲的权谋家，他辗转于帕尔马王子之间，先后担任首席大臣，先是效力于专横跋扈的父亲，后又效力于年仅二十二岁、刚刚掌权的儿子。年长的帕尔马王子对吉娜垂涎已久，却始终无果；而年轻的王子则更加渴望，最终，他不顾宫廷的死寂（没有了圣塞维里娜），短暂地占有了吉娜。这位高尚的公爵夫人懊悔不已，为了拯救法布里齐奥的性命而牺牲了自己，之后永远地离开了帕尔马。

Count Mosca, who is in his later middle age, is fiercely in love with Gina, but her motto is: If Fabrizio is not happy, then I cannot be happy. An amiable Machiavel, Mosca shuttles in and out as first minister to the Princes of Parma, initially to the despotic father and then to the twenty-two-year-old son, when he comes into power. The older Prince of Parma lusts after Gina, to no effect, and the younger one lusts even more fiercely and at last, to the great detriment of his court, which is lifeless without the Sanseverina, enjoys her very briefly. Chagrined, the high-minded Duchess sacrifices herself to save Fabrizio’s life, and then departs Parma for good.

《帕尔马修道院》的情节错综复杂，充满了冒险、阴谋、突如其来的暴力、意想不到的善意，以及最重要的——那种热情洋溢的“sprezzatura”（不经意的优雅），这种看似漫不经心实则高尚的艺术，在圣塞维里娜、法布里齐奥和亡命诗人费兰特·帕拉身上体现得淋漓尽致。如果说《帕尔马修道院》有什么缺点，除了司汤达在结尾处理上的一贯粗糙之外，那就是情节过于繁杂。法布里齐奥如此冲动，以至于他无法停止四处奔波，辗转于不同的女人之间，经历一场又一场的决斗，一次又一次的擦伤，一次又一次的伤口。但以司汤达的风格来看，法布里齐奥最终会成为虔诚、受人尊敬且雄辩的帕尔马大主教。

The plot of The Charterhouse of Parma is a labyrinth of escapades, intrigues, sudden outbursts of violence, unexpected kindnesses, above all the passionate sprezzatura, the art of throwaway high-mindedness exemplified by the Sanseverina, Fabrizio, and the outlaw poet Ferrante Palla. If The Charterhouse has a fault, aside from Stendhal’s slapdash weakness at endings, it would be the profusion of plot. Fabrizio is so impulsive that he cannot stop moving from place to place, woman to woman, duel to duel, scrape to scrape, wound to wound. Stendhal being Stendhal, Fabrizio will end as the pious, revered, and eloquent Archbishop of Parma.

法布里齐奥的原型是十六世纪的亚历山德罗·法尔内塞，他是教皇保罗三世的孙子，也是一位红衣主教和著名的艺术收藏家。他的姑姑吉娜也更像十六世纪的人物，她的鲁莽、慷慨大方以及对爱和生活的热爱都体现了这一点。十六世纪的影子也出现在费兰特·帕拉身上，他既是诗人、强盗，又是自封的人民代言人。帕拉是一名医生，但由于他激进地反抗帕尔马的统治政权，已被宣布为非法，禁止行医，并被判处死刑。和小说中几乎所有其他男性一样，他深爱着吉娜，尽管他与另一个被他从丈夫身边夺走的女人育有五个孩子。

The model for Fabrizio is the sixteenth-century Alessandro Farnese, the grandson of Pope Paul III and himself a cardinal and famous collector of the arts. His aunt Gina also seems to be more sixteenth than nineteenth century in her recklessness, lavish generosity, and high sense of love and life. The sixteenth-century throwbacks include the poet, bandit, and self-styled tribune of the people Ferrante Palla, who is a medical doctor but has been outlawed and forbidden to practice his profession since he is a radical rebel against the regime that governs Parma, and is under sentence of death. Like almost every other male in the novel, he is passionately in love with Gina, though he has five children by a woman he has reft away from her husband:

“可是，你们是如何生存下去的呢？”公爵夫人动情地问道。

“孩子们的母亲靠纺纱为生。最大的女儿寄宿在某个自由派人士的农场里，负责放羊。至于我，我在从皮亚琴察到热那亚的路上拦路抢劫。”

“你如何调和抢劫行为与你的自由主义原则？”

“我会记下我抢劫过的人，如果我有什么所得，我会把偷来的钱还给他们。我认为像我这样的人民保民官所从事的工作，考虑到其危险性，每月至少值一百法郎。所以我非常谨慎，每年偷的钱不超过一千二百法郎。其实，这样说也不对，我还会多偷一点，因为这样我才能支付印刷作品的费用。”

“什么方法有效？”

“……她最终能有自己的房间和预算吗？”

“什么？”公爵夫人惊讶地说，“那是您，先生，本世纪最伟大的诗人之一，著名的费兰特·帕拉？”

“或许很有名，但肯定很不幸。”

“像您这样有才华的人，先生，为了生存，不得不靠偷窃为生！”

“或许正因如此，我才有点天赋。直到现在，我们所有成名的作家都是受政府或他们试图颠覆的宗教资助的。我，首先，冒着生命危险；其次，夫人，想想我出去偷东西时那些令人不安的想法吧！我这样做对吗？我问自己。保民官这个职位真的值每月一百法郎吗？我只有两件衬衫，你看到的这件外套，几件破烂的武器，我肯定最终会被绳子勒死。我敢说我是无私的。如果不是那段致命的爱情，让我只能在与孩子母亲的相处中感受到痛苦，我会很幸福的。贫穷压得我喘不过气，它丑陋不堪。我喜欢漂亮的衣服，白皙的双手……”

（译者：约翰·斯特罗克）

‘But how do you survive?’ asked the duchess, much moved.

‘The children’s mother spins. The oldest girl gets her board at the farm of some liberal or other, where she watches over the sheep. As for me, I hold people up along the road from Piacenza to Genoa.’

‘How do you reconcile robbery with your liberal principles?’

‘I keep a note of the people I rob, and if ever I have anything, I shall give them back the sums I’ve stolen. I adjudge that a tribune of the people such as myself is performing a task which, on account of the danger, is worth a good hundred francs a month. So I’m very careful not to take more than twelve hundred francs a year. Actually, that’s wrong, I steal a small amount over and above that, because that way I can meet the costs of getting my works printed.’

‘What works?’

‘…will she ever have a room and a budget?’

‘What,’ said the duchess, in astonishment, ‘that’s you, signore, one of the greatest poets of the century, the famous Ferrante Palla?’

‘Famous perhaps, but very unfortunate, that’s for sure.’

‘And a man with your talent, signore, is obliged to steal in order to live!’

‘It’s for that reason that I have some talent perhaps. Up until now, all our authors who have become known were people paid by the government or by the religion they were trying to undermine. I, primo, risk my life; secundo, signora, imagine the disturbing thoughts I have when I go out stealing! Am I in the right? I ask myself. Does the position of tribune perform a service truly worth a hundred francs a month? I have two shirts, the coat that you see, a few poor weapons and I’m sure to finish by the rope. I dare to think I’m disinterested. I would be happy were it not for the fatal love which lets me find only unhappiness with the mother of my children. Poverty weighs on me, it’s ugly. I love fine clothes, white hands…’

(trans. John Sturrock)

小说结尾前，费兰特·帕拉在暴君父亲去世后，领导了一场反对帕尔马年轻王子的起义。这场叛乱由圣塞维里纳家族资助，莫斯卡伯爵对此毫不知情，他以必要的流血手段强行镇压了起义。费兰特·帕拉逃脱后，对公爵夫人说，没有共和主义者，就不可能有共和国，帕尔马的改变需要一个世纪。

Before the novel concludes, Ferrante Palla has led an insurrection against the young Prince of Parma, after the death of the tyrannical father. The rebellion is financed by the Sanseverina, an act unknown to Count Mosca, who quells the uprising quite firmly with some necessary bloodshed. Ferrante Palla escapes and remarks later to the duchess that you cannot have a republic without republicans and that it will take a century to change Parma.

这出戏码持续了五百页，一路欢愉不断，最终却以悲伤收场。法布里齐奥如今已是帕尔马大主教，他无可救药地爱上了已婚的克莱莉娅。法布里齐奥坚持要绑架他和克莱莉娅所生的幼子桑德里诺，好让他与亲生父亲团聚。不出所料，一切都出了差错：

The whirligig goes on spinning for five hundred pages, one delight after another, only to end in sadness. Fabrizio, now the Archbishop of Parma and hopelessly in love with Clelia, who is married to someone else, insists that his son by her, the young child Sandrino, be abducted so as to unite him with his actual father. Everything goes wrong, as could be expected:

这次精心策划的绑架，最终却以悲剧收场。桑德里诺被秘密安置在一栋宽敞华丽的宅邸中，侯爵夫人几乎每天都来探望他。几个月后，桑德里诺便去世了。克莱莉娅认为，这是她违背对圣母玛利亚的誓言后应得的惩罚。在桑德里诺生病期间，她曾多次在光天化日之下见到法布里齐奥，甚至两次是在大白天，每次都带着无比温柔的神情。她只比心爱的儿子多活了几个月，但她也得到了安慰——她是在爱人的怀抱中离世的。

法布里齐奥深爱着克莱莉娅，也笃信不疑，他绝不会选择自杀。他希望能在一个更好的世界里与克莱莉娅重逢，但他如此聪慧，自然不会对自己的过错不感到愧疚。

This abduction, very neatly carried out, had a most unhappy outcome. Having been installed secretly in a large and beautiful house where the marchesa came to see him almost every day, Sandrino died at the end of a few months. Clelia imagined that she had been struck by a just punishment for having been unfaithful to her vow to the Madonna. She had seen Fabrizio so often in the light, twice even in broad daylight, and with such transports of tenderness, during Sandrino’s illness. She survived this beloved son for only a few months, but she had the comfort of dying in the arms of her lover.

Fabrizio was too much in love and too much of a believer to resort to suicide. He hoped to find Clelia again in a better world, but he was too intelligent not to feel that he had much to atone for.

司汤达一定意识到自己不知道该如何收尾。克莱莉娅究竟死于何事？我们不得而知。法布里齐奥，一个虔诚的基督徒，或许相信来世，但鲜有读者会认同他需要赎罪。一旦司汤达开始着手收尾，便无法自拔：

Stendhal must have realized he did not know how to end anything. What kills Clelia? We are not told. Fabrizio, a totally sincere Christian, may believe in an afterlife, but few readers will agree that he needs to atone. Once Stendhal starts to end, he cannot stop himself:

莫斯卡伯爵夫人最终强烈赞成丈夫重返内阁，但她始终不愿返回恩斯特五世统治下的奥地利王国。她在波河左岸的维尼亚诺设府，距离卡萨尔马焦雷仅四分之一里格，因此也属于奥地利王国境内。在伯爵为她建造的维尼亚诺宏伟宫殿里，她每周四都会接待帕尔马的上流社会人士，每天都会接待众多好友。法布里齐奥总有一天会来维尼亚诺。总之，伯爵夫人营造了幸福的假象，但她与她深爱的法布里齐奥相处的时间却很短暂，而法布里齐奥只在修道院住了短短一年。

帕尔马的监狱空无一人，伯爵极其富有，恩斯特五世深受臣民爱戴，臣民们将他的统治与托斯卡纳大公的统治相提并论。

致少数幸运儿

Countess Mosca had strongly approved, with time, that her husband should resume the ministry, but she had never been willing to return to the States of Ernest V. She held court in Vignano, a quarter league from Casal-Maggiore, on the left bank of the Po and consequently within the States of Austria. In the magnificent palazzo of Vignano, which the count had had built for her, she received the whole of Parma’s high society every Thursday, and her numerous friends every day. Fabrizio would not fail to come to Vignano one day. In a word, the countess had conjoined all the appearances of happiness, but she survived Fabrizio for only a very short time, the Fabrizio whom she had adored and who spent only one year in his charterhouse.

The prisons of Parma were empty, the count was immensely rich and Ernest V was adored by his subjects, who compared his government to that of the grand dukes of Tuscany.

TO THE HAPPY FEW

老生常谈的问题又出现了。法布里齐奥究竟是怎么死的？反过来，吉娜嫁给了莫斯卡，为何也突然离去？司汤达不知道，我们也不知道。我们并不为莫斯卡的富有而感到高兴；他失去吉娜又作何感想？我感激司汤达，但也不禁希望他能活得更久一些，以便采纳巴尔扎克的建议进行修改。巴尔扎克曾被《帕尔马修道院》深深吸引。

The usual questions return. What kills Fabrizio? In turn, why does Gina, now married to Mosca, also depart so abruptly? Stendhal doesn’t know, nor do we. We are not moved to rejoicing that Mosca is so wealthy; how does he feel about losing Gina? I am grateful to Stendhal but find myself wishing he had lived long enough to revise, following the suggestions of Balzac, who was intoxicated by The Charterhouse of Parma.

第十章

CHAPTER 10

伏脱冷传奇：

The Vautrin Saga:

《老高老》（1835年），《幻灭》（1837年）

Old Goriot (1835), Lost Illusions (1837),

《妓女的辉煌与苦难》（1838）

The Splendor and Misery of the Courtesans (1838)

奥诺雷·德·巴尔扎克

HONORÉ DE BALZAC

巴尔扎克的《人间喜剧》中充满了形形色色的人物，他们都精力充沛、个性鲜明，其中许多人甚至带有几分魔性，而这一切都由一位极具个人风格的天才人物所引领。我并未完全沉浸在巴尔扎克的文学漩涡中，因为我只读过他的十二部长篇小说和几篇短篇小说。因此，我无法评判在这场天才风暴中，谁才是真正鹤立鸡群的人物。然而，我却对伏脱冷这个人物着迷不已。伏脱冷曾是黑道之王，最终却成为了巴黎警察局长。他的真名是雅克·科林，他也曾以卡洛斯·埃雷拉神父的身份出现，一个自称西班牙神职人员的人。在黑道和当局眼中，他被称为“死神道奇”，他的手下则称他为“达布”。

THE HUMAN COMEDY OF BALZAC overflows with fabulous persons, all of them fiercely energetic and many of them daemonic, guided by a highly individual genius. I am not fully immersed in the maelstrom of Balzac, since I have read only twelve of the full-length novels and a handful of the stories. I am not therefore in a position to judge who in this storm of genius stands on an eminence far above the others. Still, I am obsessed by Vautrin, the master of the criminal world who at last changes into the head of the Paris police. His real name is Jacques Collin, and he also appears as Abbé Carlos Herrera, a supposed Spanish cleric. To the underworld and to the authorities, he is known as Dodge-Death, called the Dab by his underlings.

伏脱冷体魄强健，才智超群。他与社会抗争，与其说是像雨果《悲惨世界》中那些英勇的青年那样，以受侮辱和伤害者的名义，不如说是以他自己的各种化名，尤其是“道奇·死神”的身份。他以一种微妙的方式对抗着十九世纪法国社会公开的异性恋基础。巴尔扎克明确指出，伏脱冷是同性恋，并且鄙视所有女性。从这个意义上讲，他几乎不能算是巴尔扎克的化身。巴尔扎克或许压抑着欲望，但他仍然是个风流成性的花花公子，即便在他爱上并最终娶了波兰贵族女子埃韦利娜·汉斯卡之后也是如此。埃韦利娜比他多活了近三分之一世纪，并且有过许多情人。

Vautrin is physically powerful and intellectually overwhelming. He wars against society not so much in the name of the insulted and injured, as Victor Hugo’s heroic young men fight in Les Misérables, as in his own various names, particularly in that of Dodge-Death. In a subtle way he battles the overt heterosexual basis of nineteenth-century French society. Balzac makes clear that Vautrin is homoerotic and scorns all womankind. To that degree he is scarcely a surrogate for Balzac, who may have had repressed desires, but was a fierce womanizer even after he fell in love with and eventually married Ewelina Hańska, a Polish noblewoman, who survived him by almost a third of a century and took many lovers.

我一直对小说大师亨利·詹姆斯的评论感到困惑。他写的评论有时糟糕得令人难以置信。如果我引用他对沃尔特·惠特曼的《鼓声》（1865）的评论，那就太不公平了。因为《鼓声》不必与詹姆斯后来深爱的、献给亚伯拉罕·林肯的伟大挽歌《当紫丁香最后一次在庭院里盛开》正面交锋，而《当紫丁香最后一次在庭院里盛开》的版本是在六个月后出版的，其中还收录了《鼓声》的续篇。无论如何，詹姆斯在写这篇评论时年仅二十二岁，后来他回忆起这篇评论时，不禁感到一阵战栗，称之为“那件小丑事”。

I have always been puzzled by the criticism composed by Henry James, master of the art of fiction. At its worst, it can be astonishingly bad. I would be unfair if I cited his review of Walt Whitman’s Drum-Taps (1865), which did not have to confront “When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom’d,” the great elegy for Abraham Lincoln that the mature James came to love, since that was printed in an edition six months later that also contained “The Sequel to Drum-Taps.” In any case, James, who was only twenty-two when he wrote the review, later referred to it with a shudder as that “little atrocity.”

亨利·詹姆斯真正奇特的评论体现在他对霍桑、狄更斯和乔治·艾略特的矛盾评价上。他深受霍桑的影响，却又无法承认这一点。而他对狄更斯的评价则糟糕透顶。

The really peculiar criticism written by Henry James is in his ambivalent accounts of Hawthorne, Dickens, and George Eliot. He owed too much to Hawthorne and could not acknowledge it. On Dickens he is just dreadful.

综上所述，我很高兴地承认亨利·詹姆斯作为莎士比亚（尤其是《 暴风雨》）、屠格涅夫，尤其是巴尔扎克的评论家所取得的非凡成就：

After all this, I am happy to grant Henry James his extraordinary distinction as a critic of Shakespeare, particularly of The Tempest, of Turgenev, and most of all of Balzac:

从这个角度来看，巴尔扎克的教诲极其丰富，若要一一列举他所揭示的真理，那将是一项过于艰巨的任务。我必须从中有所取舍，而我选择了最重要的三四点，它们或多或少地包含了其他真理。如今，无论翻开他的作品，几乎任何一页，最先映入眼帘的都是他笔下人物的境遇，无论在何种描绘中，他都赋予了人物如此重要的地位。与他相比，其他以散文描绘生活的作家似乎几乎完全忽略了人物的境遇。他显然认为，除非在精神和意图上真正做到完全再现，否则虚假的描绘毫无意义，甚至比虚无更甚，是一种极其虚妄的行为。

（《巴尔扎克的教训》，载于《我们言语的问题》）

The lesson of Balzac, under this comparison, is extremely various, and I should prepare myself much too large a task were I to attempt a list of the separate truths he brings home. I have to choose among them, and I choose the most important; the three or four that more or less include the others. In reading him over, in opening him almost anywhere to-day, what immediately strikes us is the part assigned by him, in any picture, to the conditions of the creatures with whom he is concerned. Contrasted with him other prose painters of life scarce seem to see the conditions at all. He clearly held pretended portrayal as nothing, as less than nothing, as a most vain thing, unless it should be, in spirit and intention, the art of complete representation.

(“The Lesson of Balzac,” in The Question of Our Speech)

这无疑是一个重要的洞见，但它适用于伏脱冷吗？如同伊阿古和弥尔顿笔下的撒旦，伏脱冷似乎能够创造完全属于他自己的境遇。可以说，伏脱冷并不完全代表《 人间喜剧》中的人物，然而巴尔扎克的密友们却习惯称他为伏脱冷。巴尔扎克笔下的许多人物或许都试图改变自己的生活境遇，但除了伏脱冷之外，又有谁真正成功了呢？拉斯蒂涅，一个永无止境的向上攀爬者，尽管他内心深处仍有一丝温情，但他欣然接受了自己所达到的地位。

That is certainly a major insight, but does it apply to Vautrin? Like Iago and Milton’s Satan, Vautrin seems able to create conditions all his own. You could say that Vautrin is not altogether representative of The Human Comedy, and yet Balzac’s close friends habitually called him Vautrin. Many of Balzac’s people may try to change their condition of life, but who succeeds fully except Vautrin? There is Rastignac, endless social climber though redeemed by some warmth of heart, but he happily accepts the condition to which he has risen.

我们在《高老头》 （1835 年）中首次见到伏脱冷，其中一个高潮是他被巴黎警察逮捕：

We are introduced to Vautrin in Old Goriot (1835), where one of the climaxes is his arrest by the Paris police:

房间里一片寂静。房客们让开路，三个男人走了进来，他们每人一只手都摸着插在侧袋里的上膛手枪。两个跟在侦探后面的警察守在客厅门口，另外两个人出现在通往楼梯的门口。花园里传来脚步声，几名士兵的步枪再次在窗下的鹅卵石路上响起。特罗姆普尔-拉-莫尔逃跑的希望彻底破灭了，所有人的目光都本能地转向了他。警长径直走到他面前，开始行动，狠狠地击打他的头部，假发掉了下来，科林丑陋的脸庞暴露无遗。他那短短的砖红色头发中透着一股可怕的力量和狡诈，整个头部与他强壮的身躯相得益彰，那一刻，他的双眼仿佛燃烧着地狱之火。在那一瞬间，真正的伏脱冷显露无疑，瞬间展现在众人面前；他们明白了他的过去、现在和未来，他冷酷无情的教义、他的所作所为、他那自私自利的宗教、他那愤世嫉俗和对人类的蔑视所赋予他的威严，以及他那坚不可摧的组织力量。鲜血涌上他的脸颊，他的双眼如同野猫般闪闪发光。他猛地后退，发出一声凶狠的咆哮，引得房客们惊叫起来。随着他这狮子般的惊吓，警察趁着众人的喧闹声，拔出了手枪。柯林看到了闪亮的枪口，意识到了危险，立刻展现出惊人的力量。他脸上突然的变化，既可怕又威严；他就像一口沸腾的蒸汽锅，蒸汽足以撼动山岳，一股可怕的力量却被一滴冷水瞬间化解。这滴冷却他怒火的水滴，如同闪电般掠过他的脑海。他嘴角露出一丝微笑，低头看了看自己的假发。

“你今天心情不太好啊，”他对警长说道，同时猛地向警察们伸出手，扬了扬头。

“先生们，”他说，“戴上手铐或脚镣。我请在场的人作证，我没有反抗。”

（译为：婚姻）

Silence fell on the room. The lodgers made way for three of the men, who had each a hand on a cocked pistol in a side pocket. Two policemen, who followed the detectives, kept the entrance to the sitting-room, and two more men appeared in the doorway that gave access to the staircase. A sound of footsteps came from the garden, and again the rifles of several soldiers rang on the cobblestones under the window. All chance of salvation by flight was cut off for Trompe-la-Mort, to whom all eyes instinctively turned. The chief walked straight up to him, and commenced operations by giving him a sharp blow on the head, so that the wig fell off, and Collin’s face was revealed in all its ugliness. There was a terrible suggestion of strength mingled with cunning in the short, brick-red crop of hair, the whole head was in harmony with his powerful frame, and at that moment the fires of hell seemed to gleam from his eyes. In that flash the real Vautrin shone forth, revealed at once before them all; they understood his past, his present, and future, his pitiless doctrines, his actions, the religion of his own good pleasure, the majesty with which his cynicism and contempt for mankind invested him, the physical strength of an organization proof against all trials. The blood flew to his face, and his eyes glared like the eyes of a wild cat. He started back with savage energy and a fierce growl that drew exclamations of alarm from the lodgers. At that leonine start the police caught at their pistols under cover of the general clamor. Collin saw the gleaming muzzles of the weapons, saw his danger, and instantly gave proof of a power of the highest order. There was something horrible and majestic in the spectacle of the sudden transformation in his face; he could only be compared to a cauldron full of the steam that can send mountains flying, a terrific force dispelled in a moment by a drop of cold water. The drop of water that cooled his wrathful fury was a reflection that flashed across his brain like lightning. He began to smile, and looked down at his wig.

“You are not in the politest of humors to-day,” he remarked to the chief, and he held out his hands to the policemen with a jerk of his head.

“Gentlemen,” he said, “put on the bracelets or the handcuffs. I call on those present to witness that I make no resistance.”

(trans. Marriage)

这是伏脱冷展现其撒旦般威严的时刻。他凭借惊人的自制力保住了性命，阻止了警察开枪射杀他。他又一次死里逃生。

This is Vautrin in his moment of Satanic magnificence. He saves his life by an astonishing act of self-control that prevents the police from shooting him down. Again he dodges death.

“这些人会把这事拖到天荒地老，好让我闲着。就算他们把我直接送进监狱，我很快就能重操旧业，尽管奥尔夫弗尔码头的那些蠢货们根本不听我的。他们肯定会竭尽全力帮助他们的将军——他们那位伟大的‘假死者’——脱身。你们当中有谁能像我一样，说自己有上万个兄弟愿意为他做任何事？”他骄傲地问道。“这其中也有可取之处，”他拍了拍胸口说，“我从未背叛过任何人！——瞧瞧你，你这贱货，”他对老处女说，“他们都怕我，明白吗？但你一出现，他们就恶心。好好捞钱吧。”

他沉默了一会儿，环顾四周，看着房客们的脸。

“你们这些蠢货！难道你们以前没见过罪犯吗？你们眼前这位科林式的罪犯，可比其他人更有骨气；他像让·雅克一样，敢于发声反对社会契约的巨大骗局，他自豪地宣称自己是让·雅克的学生。简而言之，我孤身一人对抗政府和一整套由政府资助的法庭和警察机构，而我足以与他们匹敌。”

“These folks will amuse themselves by dragging out this business till the end of time to keep me idle. If they were to send me straight to jail, I should soon be back at my old tricks in spite of the duffers at the Quai des Orfèvres. Down yonder they will all turn themselves inside out to help their general—their good Trompe-la-Mort—to get clear away. Is there a single one among you that can say, as I can, that he has ten thousand brothers ready to do anything for him?” he asked proudly. “There is some good there,” he said tapping his heart; “I have never betrayed any one!—Look you here, you slut,” he said to the old maid, “they are all afraid of me, do you see? but the sight of you turns them sick. Rake in your gains.”

He was silent for a moment, and looked round at the lodgers’ faces.

“What dolts you are, all of you! Have you never seen a convict before? A convict of Collin’s stamp, whom you see before you, is a man less weak-kneed than others; he lifts up his voice against the colossal fraud of the Social Contract, as Jean Jacques did, whose pupil he is proud to declare himself. In short, I stand here single-handed against a Government and a whole subsidized machinery of tribunals and police, and I am a match for them all.”

此时此刻，很难抵挡伏脱冷的魅力。的确，他从未背叛过任何人，完全可以自诩为卢梭的忠实信徒。巴尔扎克笔下的人物既挑战又肯定了社会契约。伏脱冷并非如此矛盾，但既然他是巴尔扎克笔下的人物，我们将在《妓女的荣光与苦难》第四部——巧妙地命名为“伏脱冷的最后化身”——中见证他惊人的转变。

It is very difficult to resist Vautrin at this moment. Indeed, he has never betrayed anyone and can assert that he is an authentic disciple of Rousseau. Something in Balzac both defies the Social Contract and affirms it. Vautrin is not so ambivalent, but since he is Balzac’s creation, we will see him undergo an astonishing transformation in Part IV of The Splendor and Misery of the Courtesans, shrewdly titled “The Last Incarnation of Vautrin.”

我们需要从更早的时期说起，从英俊的青年吕西安·夏尔东说起，他是巴尔扎克小说《幻灭》（1837）的主人公。吕西安的母系出身于古老的鲁邦普雷家族，他渴望跻身贵族之列。更重要的是，这位俊美得有些怪异的年轻人自诩为诗人（巴尔扎克笔下的吕西安其实诗才平庸），他离开外省前往巴黎，追寻荣耀与财富。尽管我们逐渐对他产生了好感，但他的弱点远不止于诗歌，他的幻想也最终破灭。小说结尾，他正要自杀时，伏脱冷化身为卡洛斯·埃雷拉神父的伏脱冷救了他。两人达成协议：伏脱冷将资助并指导吕西安，助他第二次征服巴黎。至于伏脱冷究竟要确保什么，巴尔扎克并未明确交代。尽管伏脱冷在狱中有过同性恋经历，并且爱上了吕西安，但他们的关系似乎并非公开的性关系。相反，伏脱冷渴望向社会复仇，并将吕西安视为实现这一目标的工具。

We need to start further back, with the handsome young Lucien Chardon, protagonist of Balzac’s novel Lost Illusions (1837). Lucien is descended on the maternal side from the old family de Rubempré, and aspires to join the nobility. More important, this strangely beautiful young man regards himself as a poet (the evidence given us by Balzac shows Lucien to be a very weak poet indeed) and departs the provinces for Paris seeking glory and fortune. Though we come to like him well enough, his weakness extends to more than his verses, and his illusions are devastated. At the novel’s close he is about to commit suicide when he is taken up by Vautrin in his disguise as the Abbé Carlos Herrera. They make a pact by which Vautrin will assume the role of financing and guiding Lucien so that this second time he will conquer Paris. Precisely what Vautrin is to secure is left rather ambiguous by Balzac. Though Vautrin has homosexual experience in prison, and is in love with Lucien, it seems doubtful that their relationship is overtly sexual. Rather, Vautrin desires to revenge himself upon society and sees Lucien as his instrument in that enterprise.

在1838年至1847年分四部分出版的《宫廷女郎的辉煌与悲惨》（Splendeurs et misères des courtisanes，雷纳·赫彭斯托尔1970年的精彩译本名为《高贵与卑贱的妓女》）中，焕然一新的吕西安在一场化装舞会上凯旋而归，伏脱冷也戴着面具出现。只有拉斯蒂涅——伏脱冷在《高老头》中未能勾引他的人——被“闪灵死神”允许认出他。

In Splendeurs et misères des courtisanes, published in four parts from 1838 to 1847, and titled A Harlot High and Low in the splendid translation of Rayner Heppenstall (1970), a newly resplendent Lucien is triumphant at a masked revelry where Vautrin also appears masked. Only Rastignac, whom Vautrin failed to seduce in Old Goriot, is allowed by Dodge-Death to recognize him.

为了打造新吕西安，伏脱冷设计了一个计谋：让他的得意门生去追求并娶一位极其富有却相貌平平的年轻女子。吕西安与绰号“鱼雷”的妓女埃丝特坠入爱河后，伏脱冷便指使吕西安去劝说不幸的埃丝特嫁给贪婪的努辛根男爵。这位男爵是一位极富的金融家，对埃丝特垂涎已久。埃丝特在犹豫许久后，最终只屈服了一次。她感到无比厌恶，最终自杀身亡。

The expenses of creating the new Lucien compel Vautrin to a scheme in which his protégé is to woo and marry an enormously wealthy and sadly rather ugly young woman. When Lucien and Esther, a remarkable whore known as the Torpedo, fall in love with one another, the undaunted Vautrin employs Lucien to persuade the unfortunate Esther to give herself to the horrible Baron Nucingen. He is an immensely rich financier who lusts after her. Esther yields just once, after a long delay. She is disgusted and commits suicide.

巴尔扎克的笔法如此精妙，竟能将这桩荒诞的阴谋巧妙地编织成一个引人入胜的故事，尽管任何概括都会让人觉得冗长乏味。巴黎警方怀疑吕西安和伏脱冷，以他们可能与此案有关为由将他们逮捕。吕西安在审讯中崩溃，供出了伏脱冷的真实身份。悔恨交加之下，伏脱冷在牢房中自缢身亡。伏脱冷，这位真正的“死里逃生者”，一度让警方相信他就是卡洛斯·埃雷拉神父。尽管他因吕西安的死而悲痛欲绝，但他却凭借着过人的智慧，巧妙地利用了自己独特的优势。他手中握有克洛蒂尔德·德·格朗利厄写给吕西安的大量情书，克洛蒂尔德曾希望嫁给吕西安；还有塞里西伯爵夫人和莫弗里涅斯公爵夫人，她们曾是吕西安的情妇。三大与国王和政府关系密切的显赫家族将因此丑闻而遭殃，整个​​政权也岌岌可危。

Balzac is so adroit that he makes this outrageous plot work, though any summary would seem to find it tiresome. The Paris police, suspicious of Lucien and Vautrin, arrest them on the possibility that they were complicit. Lucien breaks under testimony and reveals Vautrin’s true identity. In remorse, he hangs himself in his cell. Vautrin, true Dodge-Death, momentarily persuades the police that he is the Abbé Carlos Herrera. Though ravaged by grief for Lucien, he has the wit to exploit his unique advantage. In his possession are the profuse love letters sent to Lucien by Clotilde de Grandlieu, who had hoped to marry him, and by the Comtesse de Sérisy and the Duchesse de Maufrigneuse, who had been Lucien’s mistresses. Three great houses closely aligned with the king and the government will be victimized by scandal, and the regime could well be compromised.

伏脱冷与法国总检察长格朗维尔伯爵之间展开了一场惊心动魄的决斗。巴尔扎克在描写这场决斗时，将笔触发挥到了极致。伏脱冷被格朗维尔的慷慨和高尚品德所深深折服。而总检察长则领悟到对手身上那令人敬畏的负面特质。

A remarkable duel takes place between Vautrin and the Comte de Granville, who is the attorney general of France. Balzac is at his most sublime as this duel works itself through. Vautrin is overwhelmed by the generosity and high moral nature of Granville. The attorney general in turn recognizes the negative greatness of his adversary.

经格朗维尔允许，伏脱冷参加了吕西安的葬礼。葬礼上，身手不凡的“死亡闪避者”悲痛欲绝，昏厥过去。醒来后，他发现自己坐在出租车里，被两名警察夹在中间。他们把他带到格朗维尔面前。格朗维尔恳求伏脱冷去拯救塞里西伯爵夫人，因为她也因悲痛而崩溃。伏脱冷手里拿着吕西安写给塞里西伯爵夫人却从未寄出的一封情书，他成了塞里西伯爵夫人的心灵医生，用这封信和吕西安只爱她一人的虚假保证，使她恢复了平静。

With Granville’s permission, Vautrin attends the burial of Lucien, where the extraordinary Dodge-Death faints in his grief. When he comes out of it, he is in a cab between two police agents. They bring him to Granville, who urges him to save the Comtesse de Sérisy from madness, since she, too, has collapsed in grief. Vautrin, who possesses a final love letter that Lucien had addressed to the Comtesse de Sérisy but never sent, becomes a doctor of the soul and, with the letter and the false assurances that Lucien had loved only her, restores her to composure.

在巴尔扎克式的最后一次政变中，格朗维尔赦免了伏脱冷的前情人，并任命雅克·科林为巴黎警察局副局长，半年后让他升任局长。结局既讽刺又直白：雅克·科林执掌巴黎警察局十五年后退休。

In a final Balzacian coup, Granville reprieves a former lover of Vautrin, and appoints Jacques Collin to the position of deputy head of the Paris police, to become the head of that august body after another half year. The conclusion is wry and direct: Jacques Collin directs the Paris police force for fifteen years and then retires.

我承认，我非常遗憾地希望巴尔扎克能以截然不同的方式结束伏脱冷的故事。从美学角度来看，这类似于弥尔顿笔下撒旦屈服并重返天使合唱团。另一个阴暗的类比是伊阿古忏悔，并为苔丝狄蒙娜和奥赛罗的幸存以及他们最终的结合而感到欣慰。巴尔扎克是一位杰出的小说家，但他既不是莎士比亚，也不是弥尔顿。伏脱冷的故事值得他赋予更精彩的结局。

I confess to considerable sadness that I wish Balzac had ended the saga of Vautrin in a very different way. Aesthetically, this is akin to Milton’s Satan yielding and rejoining the angelic chorus. Another dark analogue would be Iago repenting and taking pleasure in the survival of Desdemona and Othello and their ongoing union. Balzac is an amazing novelist, but he is neither Shakespeare nor Milton. Vautrin deserved more from him.

第十一章

CHAPTER 11

船长的女儿（1836）

The Captain’s Daughter (1836)

亚历山大· P·普希金

ALEXANDER PUSHKIN

像我这样不懂俄语的读者，只能凭着信念去理解普希金诗歌的伟大，因为即便国际象棋大师纳博科夫也难以将其翻译成其他语言。然而，他的散文小说已被理查德·佩维尔和拉里萨·沃洛霍斯基翻译成一部巨著—— 《小说、故事、旅程：亚历山大·普希金散文全集》（2016）。这本书的亮点在于中篇小说《上尉的女儿》（1836），这是一部以普加乔夫起义（1773-1774）为背景的历史小说。普希金曾有机会查阅沙皇档案，并撰写了《普加乔夫传》，这部作品为他创作《上尉的女儿》提供了素材。叶梅利扬·普加乔夫，1775年被处决，年仅33岁，是一位顿河哥萨克，他曾觊觎叶卡捷琳娜大帝的皇位。他自称是遇刺身亡的沙皇彼得三世，展现出高超的技巧和残忍的手段，集结了一大批哥萨克骑兵和农民。他攻占了喀山，但随后被俄军击败，被其追随者关进笼子押送至俄军手中。在那里，他被公开处决，先是被斩首，然后被肢解。

A READER LIKE MYSELF who has no Russian has to take the greatness of Pushkin’s poetry on faith, since it seems untranslatable, even by the chess master V. Nabokov. But the prose fiction has been translated by Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky in one large volume, Novels, Tales, Journeys: The Complete Prose of Alexander Pushkin (2016). The wonder of the book is the novella The Captain’s Daughter (1836), a historical fiction founded on the Pugachev Rebellion (1773–74). Pushkin had access to the tsarist archives and initially wrote The History of Pugachev, which gave him the materia poetica for The Captain’s Daughter. Yemelyan Pugachev, executed in 1775 at the age of thirty-three, was a Don Cossack who became a pretender to the throne occupied by Catherine the Great. Claiming he was the murdered Emperor Peter III, he manifested considerable skill and appropriate viciousness while gathering a large force of Cossacks and peasants. He captured Kazan but then was defeated by the Russian army and delivered by his followers in a cage, where he was kept until his public execution, in which he was drawn and quartered after decapitation.

我很难描述普希金朴实无华、看似直白的叙事风格。俄罗斯评论家们认为这种风格回归了民间故事。在我看来，托尔斯泰对普希金的借鉴，正如这位俄罗斯主要诗人从莎士比亚那里汲取人物塑造手法一样。普希金小说中的普加乔夫性格复杂。我不知道该称他为幽默的野蛮，还是野蛮的幽默。

It is difficult for me to describe Pushkin’s unassuming and apparently straightforward style of narration. Russian critics speak of its return to folktales. Tolstoy owed as much to Pushkin as the major Russian poet seems, to me at least, to quarry Shakespeare for modes of characterization. Pugachev in Pushkin’s novella has a complicated nature.
