尼古拉一世于1855年克里米亚战争期间去世。他可能是死于肺炎，也可能是自杀。无论如何，他的死对饱受战火蹂躏的祖国来说都是一种解脱。托尔斯泰曾多次修改他书中篇幅最长的章节——关于尼古拉的章节，力求做到尽善尽美。在他看来，这一章并不完整，但很难想象还有什么比这更令人痛心的了。尼古拉非常喜欢判处一些罪行较轻的罪犯“跑鞭刑”，让他们遭受数千鞭的折磨，这必然会导致极其痛苦的死亡，尽管如此，他仍然得意洋洋地宣称俄罗斯没有死刑。沙米尔带着一名手持斧头的刽子手四处巡游，随意执行伊斯兰教法，为了真主的荣耀，砍下别人的手或头颅。至少沙米尔本人是勇敢的，而尼古拉则是一个假装成战士的懦夫。

Nicholas I died in 1855, during the Crimean War. He may have caught pneumonia, or it may have been suicide. Either way, his death was a blessing for his ruined country. Tolstoy wrote many versions of the longest chapter in his book, the one on Nicholas, attempting to get it right. He left it, in his judgment, incomplete, but it is difficult to see how it could be more devastating. Nicholas was very fond of sentencing relatively minor offenders to running the gauntlet, thus receiving thousands of lashes, inevitably a very painful death, though he continued to exult that Russia had no death penalty. Shamil traveled around with an executioner armed with an ax, and freely administered Sharia justice by whim, hands or heads sliced off for the glory of Allah. At least Shamil was personally courageous, whereas Nicholas was a coward pretending to be a warrior.

哈吉·穆拉特堪称完美，他是一位英勇无畏的战士，一位睿智谨慎的谈判者，一位孝顺的儿子，一位深爱妻子的丈夫，尤其对长子优素福关爱有加。他的母亲、妻子和孩子们被沙米尔囚禁，沙米尔威胁要处死优素福或弄瞎他的双眼。

Hadji Murat achieves perfection as personality, most heroic of warriors, wise and wary negotiator, loving son of his mother, devoted husband to his wives, and profoundly caring father of his eldest son, Yusuf, in particular. His mother, wives, and children are held captive by Shamil, who threatens either to execute or to blind Yusuf.

托尔斯泰笔下的哈吉·穆拉特是史诗的终极英雄，超越了阿喀琉斯、赫克托耳、奥德修斯和埃涅阿斯。这位阿瓦尔战士只在必要时才杀人，他并不为暴力本身而欢欣鼓舞。阿喀琉斯内心深处仍保留着孩童般的纯真，他滥杀无辜，仿佛是在抗议自己的必死性。赫克托耳在与阿喀琉斯的最终决战中，表现得异常被动。奥德修斯足智多谋、狡猾奸诈，而且绝非诚实之人。哈吉·穆拉特超越了他。两人都渴望与妻儿团聚，但奥德修斯却在途中拈花惹草，而托尔斯泰的英雄则始终忠贞不渝。埃涅阿斯背叛了狄多，他无疑是个伪君子，并且在实力悬殊的战斗中屠杀了图尔努斯，因为图尔努斯在朱庇特与朱诺和解后，被朱庇特派来的狄拉伊（狄拉伊的侍女）逼入绝境。

Tolstoy creates Hadji Murat as the ultimate hero of epic, transcending Achilles, Hector, Odysseus, Aeneas. The Avar warrior kills only when he has to; he does not rejoice in violence for its own sake. Achilles partly remains a child. He kills indiscriminately, as if to protest his own mortality. Hector, in his final battle against Achilles, is strangely passive. Odysseus is endlessly resourceful and sly and decidedly is not a truth teller. Hadji Murat surpasses him. Both long for their wife and son, but Odysseus dallies by the way, whereas Tolstoy’s hero remains faithful. Aeneas betrays Dido, decidedly is a prig, and butchers Turnus in an unequal contest, since Turnus has been driven desperate by the Dirae sent against him by Jupiter, after the high god’s reconciliation with Juno.

哈吉·穆拉特是一位纯粹的战士，他激励着他那群追随者对他无比忠诚，而他自己也至死不渝。他的一生都在与极其强大的敌人作战：

Hadji Murat is the pure warrior, who inspires loyalty in his little knot of followers, and himself is loyal unto the death. His entire career has been a battle against dreadful odds:

哈吉·穆拉特停顿了一下，深吸了一口气。

“一切都还好，”他继续说道，“后来就变糟了。沙米尔取代了哈姆扎特。他派使者来找我，让我跟他一起对抗俄国人；如果我拒绝，他就威胁要摧毁昆扎克，杀了我。我说我不会跟他走，也不会让他来找我。”

“你为什么不去找他？”洛里斯-梅利科夫问道。

哈吉·穆拉特皱了皱眉，没有立即回答。

“这不可能。沙米尔身上沾满了我的兄弟奥斯曼和阿布努萨尔汗的鲜血。我没有投奔他。罗森将军给我晋升了军官军衔，让我担任阿瓦里亚的指挥官。一切本来都会很顺利，但此前罗森先后任命了卡齐库梅赫的汗穆罕默德·米尔扎和阿赫迈特汗来管理阿瓦里亚。阿赫迈特汗恨我。他想让他的儿子娶汗沙的女儿萨尔塔内特。萨尔塔内特没有嫁给他，他认为是我的错。他恨我，派核弹来杀我，但我逃脱了。之后，他向克鲁格瑙将军告发我，说我不让阿瓦尔人给士兵提供柴火。他还告诉克鲁格瑙将军，我戴上了头巾——就是这个，”哈吉·穆拉特指着他头巾上的头巾说，“这意味着我投奔了沙米尔。将军我不相信他，命令他不许碰我。但将军前往第比利斯后，阿赫迈特汗还是按自己的方式来：他派了一队士兵抓住我，给我戴上镣铐，把我绑在一门大炮上。他们就这样把我关了六天。第七天，他们解开我的绳子，把我带到帖木儿汗的舒拉面前。四十个士兵拿着上了膛的火枪押着我。我的双手被绑着，他们奉命如果我试图逃跑就杀了我。我知道这一点。当我们走到莫克索赫附近一个地方时，那里的小路很窄，右边是大约一百码的陡峭悬崖，我绕到士兵的右边，走到悬崖边。士兵想拦住我，但我从悬崖上跳了下去，还把士兵也拖了下去。士兵被打死了，但我活了下来。肋骨、头、胳膊、腿——浑身上下都断了。我试图爬行，但动弹不得。我的头晕目眩，然后就睡着了。醒来时，我浑身湿透。我浑身是血。一个牧羊人看见了我。他叫来人，他们把我送到了医生那里。肋骨和头部都痊愈了，腿也痊愈了，只是腿长得短了一些。

哈吉·穆拉特伸出了他那条弯曲的腿。

“这对我很有利，这就足够了，”他说。“人们知道了我的情况后开始来找我。我康复后，搬到了特塞尔梅斯。阿瓦尔人再次邀请我统治他们，”哈吉·穆拉特平静而自信地说道。“我同意了。”

Hadji Murat paused and took a deep breath.

“That was all very well,” he went on, “then it all went bad. Shamil stood in place of Hamzat. He sent envoys to me to tell me to go with him against the Russians; if I refused, he threatened to lay waste to Khunzakh and kill me. I said I wouldn’t go with him and wouldn’t let him come to me.”

“Why didn’t you go to him?” asked Loris-Melikov.

Hadji Murat frowned and did not answer at once.

“It was impossible. There was the blood of my brother Osman and of Abununtsal Khan upon Shamil. I didn’t go to him. Rosen, the general, sent me an officer’s rank and told me to be the commander of Avaria. All would have been well, but earlier Rosen had appointed over Avaria, first, the khan of Kazikumykh, Mahomet Mirza, and then Akhmet Khan. That one hated me. He wanted to marry his son to the khansha’s daughter Saltanet. She was not given to him, and he thought it was my fault. He hated me and sent his nukers to kill me, but I escaped from them. Then he spoke against me to General Klugenau, said that I wouldn’t let the Avars give firewood to the soldiers. He also told him that I had put on the turban—this one,” said Hadji Murat, pointing to the turban over his papakha, “and that it meant I had gone over to Shamil. The general did not believe him and ordered him not to touch me. But when the general left for Tiflis, Akhmet Khan did it his way: he had me seized by a company of soldiers, put me in chains, and tied me to a cannon. They kept me like that for six days. On the seventh day they untied me and led me to Temir Khan Shura. I was led by forty soldiers with loaded muskets. My hands were bound, and they had orders to kill me if I tried to escape. I knew that. When we began to approach a place near Moksokh where the path was narrow and to the right there was a steep drop of about a hundred yards, I moved to the right of the soldier, to the edge of the cliff. The soldier wanted to stop me, but I jumped from the cliff and dragged the soldier with me. The soldier was battered to death, but I stayed alive. Ribs, head, arms, legs—everything was broken. I tried to crawl but couldn’t. My head whirled around and I fell asleep. I woke up soaked in blood. A shepherd saw me. He called people, they took me to the aoul. Ribs and head healed, the leg healed, too, only it came out short.”

And Hadji Murat stretched out his crooked leg.

“It serves me, and that’s good enough,” he said. “People found out and started coming to me. I recovered, moved to Tselmes. The Avars again invited me to rule over them,” Hadji Murat said with a calm, assured pride. “And I agreed.”

托尔斯泰似乎在告诉我们，如果英雄想要成就自我，那么所有能被打破的东西都应该被打破。哈吉·穆拉特，一个完全成就自我的人，一路前行，直到被阻止，即便被阻止，他仍然继续前进。

It is almost as though Tolstoy is telling us that what can be broken should be broken if the hero is to achieve himself. Hadji Murat, fully achieved, goes on until he is stopped, and even then keeps going:

然后他彻底从洞里爬了出来，一瘸一拐地拿着匕首径直走向敌人。几声枪响划破夜空，他踉跄倒地。几个民兵得意地尖叫着冲向倒地的他。然而，在他们看来已经死去的尸体突然动了起来。先是血淋淋的剃光头，没有戴头巾，抬起了头，然后整个身体也抬起了，接着他抓住一棵树，完全站了起来。他看起来如此可怕，以至于追赶他的人都停下了脚步。但他突然颤抖了一下，踉跄着离开树干，像被割倒的蓟草一样，脸朝下重重地摔倒在地，再也没有动弹。

Then he got out of the hole altogether and, limping badly, walked straight ahead with his dagger to meet his enemies. Several shots rang out, he staggered and fell. Several militiamen, with a triumphant shriek, rushed to the fallen body. But what had seemed to them a dead body suddenly stirred. First the bloodied, shaven head, without a papakha, rose, then the body rose, and then, catching hold of a tree, he rose up entirely. He looked so terrible that the men running at him stopped. But he suddenly shuddered, staggered away from the tree, and, like a mowed-down thistle, fell full length on his face and no longer moved.

这一点非常值得重申。我想起了库丘林，盖尔语中的阿喀琉斯，或者哈吉·穆拉特，叶芝在他那首意味深长的悼念诗《库丘林的慰藉》中写道：

This more than merits repeating. I think of Cuchulain, the Gaelic Achilles or Hadji Murat, in Yeats’s inevitably phrased death poem “Cuchulain Comforted”:

一个身负六处致命伤的男人，一个男人

暴力而又声名显赫，大步走过死者之中；

树枝间探出一双双眼睛，然后就消失了。

A MAN that had six mortal wounds, a man

Violent and famous, strode among the dead;

Eyes stared out of the branches and were gone.

然后某些裹尸布低声交谈着

Then certain Shrouds that muttered head to head

来过又走了。他倚靠在一棵树上。

仿佛在冥想伤口和鲜血。

Came and were gone. He leant upon a tree

As though to meditate on wounds and blood.

这位伴随叶芝一生的英雄开始冥想，但就像哈吉·穆拉特一样，他需要那棵树。诗人将库丘林安置在来世，不是与他的同伴在一起，而是与懦夫们在一起：

The hero who had been with Yeats throughout his career begins his meditation but, like Hadji Murat, needs the tree. Cuchulain is placed by his poet in the afterlife, not with his peers, but with the cowards:

“现在我们必须放声歌唱，尽我们所能地唱好歌。”

但首先您必须了解我们的性格：

都是被定罪的懦夫，被同胞杀害

“Now must we sing and sing the best we can,

But first you must be told our character:

Convicted cowards all, by kindred slain

“或者被迫离开家园，在恐惧中死去。”

“Or driven from home and left to die in fear.”

他们唱歌，但既没有人类的曲调，也没有人类的歌词。

虽然一切都像以前一样按常规方式进行；

They sang, but had nor human tunes nor words,

Though all was done in common as before;

他们的喉咙变了，变成了鸟类的喉咙。

They had changed their throats and had the throats of birds.

叶芝将此视为他晚期剧作《库丘林之死》的续篇，在《库丘林之死》中，垂死的英雄看到了幻象：

Yeats regarded this as a sequel to his late play The Death of Cuchulain, where the dying hero has a vision:

外面有漂浮物

我死后将呈现的形态，

我灵魂最初的形状，是一个柔软如羽毛的形状，

那难道不是一种奇特的灵魂形态吗？

一位伟大的战士？

There floats out there

The shape that I shall take when I am dead,

My soul’s first shape, a soft feathery shape,

And is not that a strange shape for the soul

Of a great fighting-man?

对于那位摸索着他脖子并询问他是否准备好的盲人，他肯定地回答：

And, to the Blind Man who is groping at his neck and asking if he is ready, he affirms:

我说它马上就要唱歌了。

I say it is about to sing.

诗歌和戏剧都巧妙地引用了但丁在《地狱篇》第十五歌第 118-124 行中对他的老师布鲁内托·拉蒂尼的描述：

Both poem and play deftly allude to Dante’s vision of his teacher Brunetto Latini in the Inferno, Canto XV, lines 118–24:

“……一群我可能无法融入的人来了；

我的宝物已托付给你，

我依然生活在其中，我别无所求。

“…A people comes with whom I may not be;

Commended unto thee be my Tesoro,

In which I still live, and no more I ask.”

然后他转过身，看起来像是那些人中的一员。

Then he turned round, and seemed to be of those

谁在维罗纳为绿斗篷而战

穿过平原；似乎就在他们之中。

Who at Verona run for the Green Mantle

Across the plain; and seemed to be among them

是获胜者，而不是失败者。

The one who wins, and not the one who loses.

（朗费罗译）

(trans. Longfellow)

但丁为何将他敬爱的老师与同性恋者相提并论，至今仍是个谜。重要的是，正如库丘林和哈吉·穆拉特一样，失败者最终会蜕变为胜利者。托尔斯泰以被压倒却依然顽强的蓟（被称为“鞑靼人”）为开篇和结尾，他并没有将自己的英雄变成一只超自然的鸟，而是赋予了他夜莺的挽歌：

Why Dante places his revered teacher among the sodomites is an enigma. What matters, here as with Cuchulain and with Hadji Murat, is that the defeated transmute into the victorious. Tolstoy, who begins and ends with the crushed but still-resistant thistle (called “the Tartar”), does not mutate his hero into a supernatural bird but gives him the threnody of the nightingales:

夜莺在枪声中停止了鸣叫，但随后又开始鸣唱，先是近处的一只，然后是远处的其他几只。

The nightingales, who had fallen silent during the shooting, again started trilling, first one close by and then others further off.

第25章

CHAPTER 25

《还乡》（1878）

The Return of the Native (1878)

托马斯·哈迪​

THOMAS HARDY

我从十五岁左右就开始读托马斯·哈代的作品。我最先沉浸其中的两部小说是《还乡》（1878）和《林中居民》（1887）。但它们远非他最好的小说：他最好的作品包括《远离尘嚣》（1874）、《卡斯特桥市长》（1886）、《德伯家的苔丝》（1891）以及《无名的裘德》（1895）。《无名的裘德》的评价极其恶劣，以至于哈代愤然放弃小说创作，转而重拾诗歌创作——诗歌才是他创作生涯的起点。哈代于1928年去世，享年八十七岁。二十世纪能与哈代比肩的英国诗人不多：撇开爱尔兰诗人叶芝和谢默斯·希尼，以及美国诗人艾略特不谈，他们或许包括D·H·劳伦斯、爱德华·托马斯、威尔弗雷德·欧文、早期的W·H·奥登、基思·道格拉斯和杰弗里·希尔。

I HAVE BEEN READING Thomas Hardy since I was about fifteen. The first two of his novels I sank into were The Return of the Native (1878) and The Woodlanders (1887). They are far from being the best of his fictions: those would have to include Far from the Madding Crowd (1874), The Mayor of Casterbridge (1886), Tess of the d’Urbervilles (1891), and Jude the Obscure (1895), which was so viciously received that Hardy, in revulsion, turned back from writing novels to composing poetry, which had started his career. Hardy died in 1928, at the age of eighty-seven. There are not many English poets of the twentieth century who are Hardy’s equals: setting aside Yeats and Seamus Heaney as Irish, and Eliot as American, they might include D. H. Lawrence, Edward Thomas, Wilfred Owen, the early W. H. Auden, Keith Douglas, and Geoffrey Hill.

作为小说家，哈代深受乔治·艾略特的影响，但他真正的先驱是浪漫主义盛期抒情诗人珀西·比希·雪莱，后者对爱欲有着悲剧性的理解。这种悲剧性贯穿于哈代的创作，尤其体现在他笔下那些栩栩如生的女主人公身上：芭丝谢芭·埃弗丁、尤斯塔西亚·维、玛蒂·索斯、苔丝·德比菲尔德、苏·布莱德海德。在雪莱的作品中，自我的阴影始终笼罩在欲望与满足之间。对他而言，爱与爱的手段、善与善的手段，是无法调和的。

As a novelist Hardy was influenced by George Eliot, but his authentic precursor was the High Romantic lyric poet Percy Bysshe Shelley, who had a tragic vision of Eros. This prevails throughout Hardy and is felt particularly in his most vivid heroines: Bathsheba Everdene, Eustacia Vye, Marty South, Tess Durbeyfield, Sue Bridehead. In Shelley the shadow of selfhood always falls between desire and its fulfillment. For him love and the means of love, good and the means of good, were irreconcilable.

亨利·詹姆斯认为哈代是乔治·艾略特的乏味模仿者，并在他的《异端邪说之后：现代异端入门》（1934 年）中称托马斯·哈代是“一个个性鲜明、不受任何制度束缚或任何客观信仰约束的人”。

Henry James dismissed Hardy as a tedious imitator of George Eliot, and in his After Strange Gods: A Primer of Modern Heresy (1934) called Thomas Hardy “a powerful personality uncurbed by any institutional attachment or by submission to any objective beliefs.”

D·H·劳伦斯在其著作《托马斯·哈代研究》（作于1914-1915年，遗作于1932-1933年出版）中，实际上写的是D·H·劳伦斯本人的研究，因为该书隐含地记录了他修改《虹》的艰辛历程。然而，该书对哈代的解读却展现出非凡的洞察力。

D. H. Lawrence, in his Study of Thomas Hardy (composed 1914–15, published posthumously, 1932–33), essentially wrote a Study of D. H. Lawrence since the book implicitly records his struggle to revise The Rainbow. However, it does manifest remarkable acuity in regard to Hardy.

《还乡》是第一部悲剧性的重要小说。尤斯塔西亚，一个阴郁、狂野、热情奔放的女孩，对自己的欲望了如指掌，又没有继承任何令她羞于承认的传统——毕竟她出身于一个充满小说气息的意大利家庭。她先是爱上了性情不定的威尔德夫，但威尔德夫无法满足她；之后，她又抛弃了他，转而嫁给了刚刚归来的克莱姆。她究竟想要什么？她自己也不清楚，但显然是某种形式的自我实现；她渴望成为真正的自己，成就真正的自己。然而，她却不知该如何实现，又该通过何种途径——浪漫的想象如此描绘：巴黎和上流社会。仿佛这些就能消除她内心的不满。

[The Return of the Native] is the first tragic and important novel. Eustacia, dark, wild, passionate, quite conscious of her desires and inheriting no tradition which would make her ashamed of them, since she is of a novelistic Italian birth, loves, first, the unstable Wildeve, who does not satisfy her, then casts him aside for the newly returned Clym, whom she marries. What does she want? She does not know, but it is evidently some form of self-realization; she wants to be herself, to attain herself. But she does not know how, by what means, so romantic imagination says, Paris and the beau monde. As if that would have stayed her unsatisfaction.

—

书中真正的悲剧是什么？是荒原。是原始的、未经雕琢的土地，本能的生命在那里涌动。在那里，在深沉而粗犷的本能涌动中，蕴藏着促成悲剧的现实。在万物的核心附近，可以听到那造就我们、毁灭我们的悸动。荒原涌动着原始的本能。埃格登，它那黝黑的土壤强壮、粗犷、充满生机，如同野兽的躯体。尤斯塔西亚、威尔德夫、约布莱特夫人、克莱姆以及所有其他的人，都诞生于这片粗犷的土地之中。他们是某一年的意外收获。有些人倒下或死去，有些人去传教或结婚，这又有什么关系呢？这难道不比埃格登一个秋天里枯萎的荒原、泛红的浆果、带籽的荆豆和枯死的蕨类植物更重要吗？荒原依然存在。它的身体强壮而肥沃，它还会结出更多的果实。这里蕴藏着一种阴郁而潜在的力量，无论产品最终如何，它都会持续产出。这里是深邃而黑暗的源泉，所有这些微小的生命都源于此。而这些微小的生命却被倾泻而出，白白浪费。其中蕴含着一种野蛮的满足感：因为还有更多的东西等待着我们，如此强大而深邃的创造力正在那里运作，所以这一切又有什么关系呢？

What is the real stuff of tragedy in the book? It is the heath. It is the primitive, primal earth, where the instinctive life heaves up. There, in the deep, rude stirring of the instincts, there was the reality that worked the tragedy. Close to the body of things, there can be heard the stir that makes us and destroys us. The heath heaved with raw instinct. Egdon, whose dark soil was strong and crude and organic as the body of a beast. Out of the body of this crude earth are born Eustacia, Wildeve, Mistress Yeobright, Clym, and all the others. They are one year’s accidental crop. What matters if some are downed or dead, and others preaching or married: what matter, any more than the withering heath, the reddening berries, the seedy furze, and the dead fern of one autumn of Egdon? The heath persists. Its body is strong and fecund, it will bear many more crops besides this. Here is the somber, latent power that will go on producing no matter what happens to the product. Here is the deep, black source whence all these little contents of lives are drawn. And the contents of the small lives are spilled and wasted. There is savage satisfaction in it: for so much more remains to come, such black, powerful fecundity is working there, that what does it matter?

· · ·

在哈代的小说中，一个反复出现的启示是：存在着一个宏大的背景，它鲜活而充满活力，远比生活在其中的人物本身更为重要。在阴郁而充满激情的埃格登小镇、绿意盎然、饱含深情的林地、以及深不可测的星辰的映衬下，勾勒出一幅幅渺小的人生图景：《还乡》、 《林中人》或《塔上二人组》。在这幅宏大而难以理解的、远超人类心智所能理解的原始死亡图景之上，描绘出人类道德生活和斗争的渺小而悲惨的片段，悲惨得近乎可笑。法律和秩序的小小庇护所，人类用来抵御自然荒芜浩瀚的城墙之内的小小堡垒，总是显得过于狭小，那些带着城墙法则冒险前行的先驱者，最终死于这法则的束缚之中，他们自由却又不自由，一边宣扬着城墙法则，一边眺望着荒芜的自然。

That is a constant revelation in Hardy’s novels: that there exists a great background, vital and vivid, which matters more than the people who move upon it. Against the background of dark, passionate Egdon, of the leafy, sappy passion and sentiment of the woodlands, of the unfathomed stars, is drawn the lesser scheme of lives: The Return of the Native, The Woodlanders, or Two on a Tower. Upon the vast, incomprehensible pattern of some primal mortality greater than ever the human mind can grasp, is drawn the little, pathetic patter of man’s moral life and struggle, pathetic, almost ridiculous. The little fold of law and order, the little walled city within which man has to defend himself from the waste enormity of nature, becomes always too small, and the pioneers venturing out with the code of the walled city upon them die in the bonds of that code, free and yet unfree, preaching the walled city and looking to the waste.

可以说，劳伦斯对埃格登荒原的热情有些过头了。他似乎将埃格登荒原与哈代的内在意志（源于叔本华的生存意志）混为一谈，正如劳伦斯“绿意盎然、汁液充沛的热情”源自尼采的《想想大地》一样。劳伦斯真正提出的，是《还乡》中那个令人深思的问题：尤斯塔西亚·维耶的愿望为何无法实现？

You can say that Lawrence is rather too ecstatic about Egdon Heath. He seems to mix it up with Hardy’s Immanent Will, which stems from Schopenhauer’s Will to Live, just as Lawrence’s “leafy, sappy passion” derives from Nietzsche’s “Think of the Earth.” What Lawrence truly raises is the dark question of The Return of the Native: why cannot Eustacia Vye be fulfilled?

当我太久没读哈代的作品时，我对《还乡》的记忆就只剩下尤斯塔西亚、红人文恩和埃格登荒原了。克莱姆是哈代在人物塑造上的败笔之一，几乎毁了整部小说。这本书最大的亮点是性感迷人的尤斯塔西亚·维，她最终自杀了。我当时觉得，现在依然觉得这令人痛心，但哈代本人也和任何读者一样感到痛苦。以下是哈代在开篇章节“夜之女王”中对她的描述：

When I have stayed away too long from Hardy, all I can remember about The Return of the Native are Eustacia, the red man Venn, and Egdon Heath. Clym is one of Hardy’s failures in characterization and comes close to ruining the novel. The great glory of the book is the sexually enchanting Eustacia Vye, who finally kills herself. I found and still find this dreadful, but Hardy suffered quite as much as any reader could. Here is the description of her that Hardy gives in the early chapter “Queen of Night”:

她本人体态丰满，略显丰腴；既不泛红，也不苍白；触感如云般柔软。她的头发仿佛整个冬天都不足以构成它的影子。它像夜幕降临般笼罩着她的额头，熄灭了西方的余晖。

她的神经仿佛延伸到了那一头秀发里，只要轻轻抚摸她的头发，就能让她的脾气平静下来。每次梳头，她都会立刻安静下来，像个斯芬克斯。如果她从埃格登河岸下走过时，浓密的发丝像有时那样被欧洲金雀花（Ulex Europæus）的刺毛缠住——这种刺毛就像一把梳子——她就会后退几步，再从那刺毛处走过一遍。

她有一双异教徒般的眼睛，充满了夜幕的神秘。那光芒忽明忽暗，时隐时现，被厚重的眼睑和睫毛遮蔽了一部分；而且她的下眼睑比一般英国女性要浓密得多。这使她能够沉浸在遐想中而不显露痕迹：人们或许会认为她可以不闭眼睡觉。假设男女的灵魂是可见的本质，你可以想象尤斯塔西亚的灵魂如同火焰般炽热。从她深邃的瞳孔中迸发的火花，也给人同样的印象。

She was in person full-limbed and somewhat heavy; without ruddiness, as without pallor; and soft to the touch as a cloud. To see her hair was to fancy that a whole winter did not contain darkness enough to form its shadow. It closed over her forehead like nightfall extinguishing the western glow.

Her nerves extended into those tresses, and her temper could always be softened by stroking them down. When her hair was brushed she would instantly sink into stillness and look like the Sphinx. If, in passing under one of the Egdon banks, any of its thick skeins were caught, as they sometimes were, by a prickly tuft of the large Ulex Europæus—which will act as a sort of hairbrush—she would go back a few steps, and pass against it a second time.

She had pagan eyes, full of nocturnal mysteries. Their light, as it came and went, and came again, was partially hampered by their oppressive lids and lashes; and of these the under lid was much fuller than it usually is with English women. This enabled her to indulge in reverie without seeming to do so: she might have been believed capable of sleeping without closing them up. Assuming that the souls of men and women were visible essences, you could fancy the colour of Eustacia’s soul to be flame-like. The sparks from it that rose into her dark pupils gave the same impression.

哈代的尤斯塔西亚或许借鉴了沃尔特·佩特的《文艺复兴》，该书出版于《还乡》五年前。在某种程度上，尤斯塔西亚与佩特笔下波提切利的维纳斯和达芬奇的蒙娜丽莎——两种截然相反的女性性欲的象征——有着某种共通之处。尤斯塔西亚如火焰般炽热的特质，恰好呼应了佩特在《文艺复兴》“结论”中对激情狂喜的描绘，《还乡》的题词或许可以这样写：“至少我们的生命如火焰般炽热，它不过是各种力量的交汇，每时每刻都在更新，而这些力量迟早都会分道扬镳。”

Hardy’s Eustacia may owe something to Walter Pater’s The Renaissance, published five years before The Return of the Native, since in some ways she makes a third with Pater’s evocations of the Botticelli Venus and Leonardo’s Mona Lisa, visions of antithetical female sexuality. Eustacia’s flame-like quality precisely recalls Pater’s ecstasy of passion in the “Conclusion” to The Renaissance, and the epigraph to The Return of the Native could well have been: “This at least of flame-like our life has, that it is but the concurrence, renewed from moment to moment, of forces parting sooner or later on their ways.”

至少尤斯塔西亚如火焰般炽烈的生命有一点可以肯定：各种力量的交汇终将导致分离。然而，哈代笔下这位最美的女性，也是最渴望厄运降临的，因为她的灵魂如同火焰般炽热。荒原只给她带来了威尔德夫和克莱姆，但巴黎或许也难以给她带来更好的归宿，因为作为夜之女王，她吸引着悲伤的恒久与温柔。

This at least of flame-like Eustacia’s life has, that the concurrence of forces parts sooner rather than later. But, then, this most beautiful of Hardy’s women is also the most doom-eager, the color of her soul being flame-like. The heath brings her only Wildeve and Clym, but Paris doubtless would have brought her scarce better, since as Queen of Night she attracts the constancy and the kindness of sorrow.

十五岁时我爱上了尤斯塔西亚·维，八十八岁时，这份激情再次燃起。托马斯·哈代的两段婚姻都存在着矛盾之处，包括膝下无子。然而，他曾一度对他的第一任妻子爱得如痴如醉。每当他描写尤斯塔西亚，笔下的她都仿佛燃烧着火焰。七十多年过去了，我依然记得第一次读到哈代对尤斯塔西亚的描写时，她那蓬乱的头发被轻轻抚摸时的神态，即便那抚摸她的只是普通的金雀花，也让我感到无比惊叹：

At fifteen I fell in love with Eustacia Vye, and at eighty-eight the passion returns. Both of Thomas Hardy’s marriages had equivocal elements, including childlessness. And yet, for a while, he was fiercely in love with his first wife. When he writes of Eustacia he catches fire. Across more than seventy years, I remember my first wonder at Hardy’s description of Eustacia’s conduct when her wild hair was stroked down, even when common gorse performed the caress:

她的神经仿佛延伸到了那一头秀发里，只要轻轻抚摸她的头发，就能让她的脾气平静下来。每次梳头，她都会立刻安静下来，像个斯芬克斯。如果她从埃格登河岸下走过时，浓密的发丝像有时那样被欧洲金雀花（Ulex Europæus）的刺毛缠住——这种刺毛就像一把梳子——她就会后退几步，再从那刺毛处走过一遍。

Her nerves extended into those tresses, and her temper could always be softened by stroking them down. When her hair was brushed she would instantly sink into stillness and look like the Sphinx. If, in passing under one of the Egdon banks, any of its thick skeins were caught, as they sometimes were, by a prickly tuft of the large Ulex Europæus—which will act as a sort of hairbrush—she would go back a few steps, and pass against it a second time.

谁能抵挡住一个如此热情奔放的女人，她甚至会回到金雀花丛中，再次感受它的轻抚？哈代笔下的女性拓展并丰富了他的想象力。除了《卡斯特桥市长》中的迈克尔·亨查德之外，他笔下的男性角色始终缺乏鲜活的生命力。然而，他笔下的女性如此迷人，以至于读者几乎不会在意这一点。我找不到尤斯塔西亚·维耶的任何缺陷；她的悲剧源于她所处的环境和境遇。她的丈夫克莱姆和情人威尔德夫，都无法与她那强烈的性魅力和耀眼光芒相提并论。在《还乡》的序言中，哈代特意告诉我们，莎士比亚笔下的李尔王在埃格登荒原上饱受折磨。尤斯塔西亚的痛苦表现得不那么淋漓尽致，毕竟哈代不是莎士比亚，但她被荒原上的大多数居民所憎恨，他们视她为女巫。她有一个来自科孚岛的意大利父亲，然而，引发这种憎恨的远不止她那异域风情的美貌。在一个狭小的世界里，她的性魅力如同霍桑《红字》中十七世纪马萨诸塞湾殖民地的海丝特·白兰一样，孤立无援。可惜的是，她缺乏海丝特·白兰那般坚韧不拔的毅力，而海丝特的这种毅力又因抚养亲生女儿珀尔的需要而更加强大。海丝特和珀尔活了下来。尤斯塔西亚溺水身亡，很可能是蓄意而为。威尔德夫也溺水身亡，徒劳地试图救她。克莱姆失去了妻子和母亲，成了一名业余传教士，向所有愿意倾听的人布道。

Who can resist a woman who lives at so high a frequency that she backtracks to have the gorse stroke her again? Hardy’s women enlarge and attune his imagination. His men, except for Michael Henchard in The Mayor of Casterbridge, never quite come alive. Yet so marvelous are his women that the reader scarcely cares. I find no flaws in Eustacia Vye; her tragedy stems from context and circumstance. Her husband and her lover, Clym and Wildeve, are hopelessly inadequate to her sexual intensity and splendor. In a preface to The Return of the Native, Hardy takes care to tell us that Shakespeare’s King Lear suffered his agonies on Egdon Heath. Eustacia suffers less expressively, Hardy not being Shakespeare, but she is hated by most of the natives of the heath, who regard her as a witch. She had an Italian father from Corfu, yet much more than her exotic beauty stimulates the hatred. In a minimized world, she is as isolated in her sexual strength as Hester Prynne is in the seventeenth-century Massachusetts Bay Colony of Hawthorne’s The Scarlet Letter. Alas, she lacks Hester Prynne’s stubborn strength of endurance, enhanced by Hester’s need to nurture her natural daughter, Pearl. Hester and Pearl survive. Eustacia suffers death by water, probably with deliberation. Wildeve also drowns, vainly attempting to save her. Clym, wifeless and motherless, becomes a lay preacher speaking to whoever will listen.

有时我真希望哈代把这部小说命名为《夜之女王》，因为这是尤斯塔西亚的故事，而不是克莱姆的故事。或许哈代对她的爱，就像福楼拜对《包法利夫人》中的爱玛·艾玛，或者托尔斯泰对《安娜·卡列尼娜》倾注了全部心血一样。福楼拜在爱玛自杀时痛哭流涕，托尔斯泰也一定为他心爱的安娜感到悲痛。这三位女性的离世都是巨大的损失。哈代虽然拥有原始的力量，但他当然不是福楼拜那样的艺术家，只有托尔斯泰才能让我们感受到，透过他，大地在呐喊。

Sometimes I wish that Hardy had titled the novel Queen of Night, since it is Eustacia’s book and not Clym’s. It may be that Hardy loved her as Flaubert loved Emma Bovary or Tolstoy invested so heavily in Anna Karenina. Flaubert wept as he murdered Emma through her suicide. Tolstoy must have grieved for his wonderful Anna. All three women were great losses. Hardy, despite his primeval power, is not of course the artist that Flaubert was, and only Tolstoy can give us the sense that through him the earth cries out.

第26章

CHAPTER 26

《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》（1880）

The Brothers Karamazov (1880)

F·约多尔· D ·奥斯托耶夫斯基

FYODOR DOSTOEVSKY

我之前曾写过关于陀思妥耶夫斯基最后一部也是最伟大的作品的文章，但我现在不再认同我之前的评论。父亲离开敖德萨后就拒绝说俄语，我从小只说意第绪语。我在康奈尔大学和耶鲁大学学习过其他语言，之后在教书期间又掌握了一些语言。没能学会俄语是我最大的遗憾之一。这意味着我对普希金、果戈理、托尔斯泰、契诃夫、屠格涅夫、冈察洛夫、莱蒙托夫、陀思妥耶夫斯基以及其他十九世纪俄罗斯经典作家的阅读都受限于译本。我年轻时读过康斯坦斯·加内特的早期译本，虽然译文堪称壮举，但用词生硬，而且我感觉译文不够准确，尤其在传达语气方面有所欠缺。

I HAVE WRITTEN about Dostoevsky’s final and greatest work before, but I no longer agree with my earlier critique. My father refused to speak Russian after he left Odessa, and I grew up speaking only Yiddish. I studied other languages at Cornell and Yale, and since then, during my teaching years, I have mastered others. It is one of my regrets that I never learned Russian. That means my reading of Pushkin, Gogol, Tolstoy, Chekhov, Turgenev, Goncharov, Lermontov, Dostoevsky, and the other classic authors of nineteenth-century Russia has been enslaved to translations. The earlier ones by Constance Garnett that I read in my youth were a heroic enterprise yet stilted in diction and, I gather, inaccurate and particularly poor in conveying tone.

然而，自1990年以来，杰出的译者夫妇理查德·佩维尔和拉里萨·沃洛霍斯基将许多俄罗斯经典作品翻译成了引人入胜的英文版本，而我正是他们成千上万感激不尽的读者之一。尽管我多次重读他们的《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》，这部气势磅礴的小说依然未能让我彻底爱上它，但我开始对它有了更深的理解，也逐渐厘清了我对陀思妥耶夫斯基作品的复杂情感。

However, since 1990, the remarkable married team of Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky have translated many of the Russian classics into persuasive English versions, and I am among their thousands of grateful debtors. Several rereadings of their The Brothers Karamazov have not made me love that overpowering novel, but I begin to understand it better, and to clarify my ambivalences concerning Dostoevsky.

圣伯夫，在我看来，除了保罗·瓦雷里之外，是最有趣的法国评论家。他教会我们，在深入阅读任何一位作家的作品时，都要问自己一个至关重要的问题：作者会如何看待我们？陀思妥耶夫斯基对我的反应，加深了我对已故父亲终生的感激之情，感谢他让我离开敖德萨，从而给了我过上美好生活的机会。尽管陀思妥耶夫斯基有时否认自己是反犹主义者，但还是让他自己来作证吧：

Sainte-Beuve, to me the most interesting of French critics except for Paul Valéry, taught us to ask a crucial question of any writer whom we read deeply: what would the author think of us? Dostoevsky’s reaction to me would intensify my lifelong gratitude to my late father for getting out of Odessa and thus giving me a chance to live a good life. Though Dostoevsky sometimes denied he was an anti-Semite, let him testify for himself:

犹太人在欧洲掌控所有证券交易所绝非偶然；他们控制资本、主宰信贷绝非偶然；他们主宰国际政治也绝非偶然——我再说一遍——未来将会发生什么，犹太人自己也心知肚明：他们的统治，他们的完全统治即将到来！即将到来的是思想的彻底胜利，届时，人类的情感、对真理的渴望、基督教的信仰、欧洲各国人民的民族自豪感和民众自豪感都将臣服于他们。

我有时会想：如果俄罗斯不是三百万犹太人，而是三百万俄罗斯人，而犹太人有八千万，那会怎样？他们会如何对待俄罗斯人？他们会如何统治俄罗斯人？犹太人会给予俄罗斯人什么权利？……他们会不会像古代对待异族那样，将他们屠杀殆尽，直至彻底灭绝？

我重申：没有上帝，犹太人是不可想象的。而且，我甚至不相信受过教育的犹太人中存在无神论者：他们的本质都是一样的……他们都坚定不移地等待着弥赛亚的到来，从最卑微的犹太人到最高贵、最博学的哲学家和卡巴拉拉比，无一例外：他们都相信弥赛亚将再次在耶路撒冷团结他们，并用他的剑使万国臣服于他。

（作家日记）

It is not for nothing that over there [in Europe] the Jews rule all the stock-exchanges; it is not for nothing that they control capital, that they are the masters of credit, and it is not for nothing—I repeat—that they are also the masters of international politics, and what is going to happen in the future is known to the Jews themselves: their reign, their complete reign is approaching! What is coming is the complete triumph of ideas before which sentiments of humanity, the thirst for truth, Christian feelings, the national and popular pride of European peoples, must bow.

I sometimes imagine: what if there were not three million Jews, but three million Russians in Russia, and there were eighty million Jews? Well, how would they treat Russians, and how would they lord it over them? What rights would Jews give Russians?…Wouldn’t they slaughter them to the last man, to the point of complete extermination, as they used to do with alien peoples in ancient times?

I repeat: it is impossible to conceive of a Jew without God. Moreover, I do not believe in the existence of atheists even among educated Jews: they are all of the same essence….They are all…undeviatingly awaiting the Messiah, all of them, from the very lowest Kike to the highest and most learned philosopher and rabbi-Kabalist: they all believe that the Messiah will again unite them in Jerusalem and bring by his sword all nations to their feet.

(Diary of a Writer)

读到这段话，我的第一反应是想起那句犹太教经典《塔木德》的格言：若有人欲取你性命，先下手为强。然而，我如今已是垂暮之年，不再是年轻时那个在布朗克斯街头不由自主地打架斗殴的人。陀思妥耶夫斯基拥有一群坚定的拥护者，他们对他的种种批评置之不理。其中一些人，如今已离世，曾是我的挚友。《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》的审美力量丝毫未减，但当人们称赞这部小说对道德和宗教的深刻见解时，我却感到不安。人们或许会更喜欢列夫·托尔斯泰的作品，这无可厚非：

When I read this, my initial response is to remember the Talmudic adage: If someone seeks to take your life, rise up and slay him first. Still, I am now a very old man, and not the involuntary Bronx street-fighter of my early youth. Dostoevsky has a coven of stalwart defenders who brush his hatreds aside. Some of them, now departed, were my good friends. Nothing diminishes the aesthetic power of The Brothers Karamazov, but I am uneasy when the novel is praised for its insights into morality and religion. One can be pardoned for preferring Leo Tolstoy:

犹太人是神圣的存在，他从天上带来了永恒之火，并用它照亮了整个世界。他是宗教的源泉、泉源和精神支柱，其他所有民族的信仰和宗教都源于他。犹太人是自由的先驱……犹太人是文明的先驱……犹太人是永恒的象征。

The Jew is that sacred being who has brought down from heaven the everlasting fire, and has illuminated with it the entire world. He is the religious source, spring, and fountain out of which all the rest of the peoples have drawn their beliefs and their religions. The Jew is the pioneer of liberty….The Jew is the pioneer of civilization….The Jew is the emblem of eternity.

由于不懂俄语，我本人无法在美学上更偏爱托尔斯泰而非陀思妥耶夫斯基。但最伟大的俄罗斯评论家们将托尔斯泰与荷马、但丁和莎士比亚相提并论。读过佩维尔和沃洛霍斯基翻译的托尔斯泰作品后，我深信不疑。陀思妥耶夫斯基，即便在《群魔》和《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》中，也达到了另一个境界。

Lacking Russian, I myself cannot give Tolstoy the aesthetic preference over Dostoevsky. But the greatest Russian critics speak of Tolstoy as being of the eminence of Homer, Dante, Shakespeare. Reading Tolstoy rendered by Pevear and Volokhonsky, I am persuaded. Dostoevsky, even in The Demons and The Brothers Karamazov, is of another order.

陀思妥耶夫斯基的这部巅峰之作有很多优点，但我认为他塑造的人物形象最吸引人，几乎堪比莎士比亚笔下的人物：卡拉马佐夫三兄弟，阿廖沙、米佳和伊万。年仅十九岁的阿廖沙和伊万是同父同母的兄弟；长兄米佳是他们的同父异母兄弟。他们的父亲费奥多尔是个五十五岁、性情恶劣、贪婪成性、嗜酒如命的酒鬼。费奥多尔的私生子斯麦尔佳科夫则是个脾气暴躁、心怀怨恨的厨子。

There are many strengths in Dostoevsky’s culminating novel, but I find Dostoevsky’s almost Shakespearean invention of characters most appealing: the three Karamazov brothers, Alyosha, Mitya, Ivan. Alyosha, who is just nineteen, and Ivan are full brothers; the oldest, Mitya, is their half-brother. Their father is the rancid, lustful, gluttonous drunkard Fyodor, who is fifty-five. Smerdyakov, the bastard son of Fyodor, is a surly and resentful cook.

阿廖沙简直像个圣人：开朗、慈爱、虔诚。对陀思妥耶夫斯基来说，阿廖沙是这部小说的主人公。实际上，这部小说的主角是米佳：他热情奔放、挥霍无度、行动冲动，却也拥有同情心、克制和慷慨的精神，并且可能对俄罗斯这片土地抱有信仰。或许是出于我个人的偏好，我更喜欢伊万：他才智过人、充满怀疑精神，悲剧性地徘徊在西方对认知的重视和他那俄罗斯灵魂（无论那灵魂究竟是什么）之间。斯麦尔佳科夫是个怪人，但也是个有趣的怪人。

Alyosha is a kind of saint: cheerful, loving, deeply religious. For Dostoevsky, Alyosha is the book’s hero. Actually, it is Mitya’s novel: he is passionate, spendthrift, an impulsive man of action, yet capable of compassion, restraint, generosity of spirit, and a potential believer in the Russian earth. Doubtless because of my own peculiarities, I prefer Ivan: enormously intelligent, skeptical, tragically caught between a Western regard for cognition and his own Russian soul, whatever that is. Smerdyakov is a beast, but an interesting one.

格鲁申卡和卡捷琳娜是小说中的主要女性角色。与托尔斯泰不同，陀思妥耶夫斯基似乎不太擅长刻画女性。格鲁申卡美丽、骄傲、风情万种，但绝非放荡不羁，老卡拉马佐夫和米佳都对她展开了同样热烈的追求。她与阿廖沙的友谊使她变得温柔。卡捷琳娜则更加骄傲，性格内向，虽然与米佳订婚，却被米佳抛弃，转而与格鲁申卡在一起。弗洛伊德所说的“道德受虐倾向”是她的弱点，即使读者开始猜测她和伊万已经坠入爱河，她仍然对米佳忠贞不渝。

Grushenka and Katerina are the principal women characters. Unlike Tolstoy, Dostoevsky seems to me uneasy in representing women. Grushenka is beautiful, proud, flirtatious, in no way promiscuous, and is pursued with equal ferocity by old Karamazov and Mitya. She is gentled by a friendship with Alyosha. Katerina is even prouder, essentially withdrawn, and, though betrothed to Mitya, is abandoned by him for Grushenka. What Freud once called moral masochism is her weakness, and she remains loyal to Mitya even after the reader begins to surmise that she and Ivan have fallen in love.

佐西玛是一位资深僧侣，是阿廖沙的道德和宗教导师，和阿廖沙一样，他代表了陀思妥耶夫斯基的理想。他宣扬宽恕和对大地的敬畏，他会亲吻大地，用泪水浇灌它，并且拥有洞察一切的超凡洞察力，能够看透他遇到的每一个灵魂。

Zosima, a senior monk, is Alyosha’s moral and religious guide, and, like Alyosha, represents the Dostoevskian ideal. He preaches forgiveness, and reverence for the earth, which he kisses and waters with his tears, and is endowed with a clairvoyant understanding of every soul he encounters.

《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》的仰慕者包括爱因斯坦、弗洛伊德、维特根斯坦、海德格尔、乔伊斯、卡夫卡和科马克·麦卡锡。他们中也包括弗拉基米尔·普京和约瑟夫·斯大林。西格蒙德·弗洛伊德认为它是史上最伟大的小说，但毕竟，他也写过一篇关于陀思妥耶夫斯基和弑父的文章。他自己的奇幻小说《图腾与禁忌》（1913）是陀思妥耶夫斯基奇幻作品的怪诞版本。在弗洛伊德的笔下，部落之父坚持要独占所有女性，最终被一群敌对兄弟杀死，这些兄弟吞噬了图腾之父。斯大林和普京与沙皇亚历山大二世一样，都对《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》推崇备至，后者在《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》出版后的第二年遇刺身亡。一些历史学家认为，斯大林是奉斯大林的亲信希姆莱——拉夫连季·贝利亚的命令被毒死的，贝利亚本人已于1953年被处决。可悲的是，普京至今仍然健在。

The admirers of The Brothers Karamazov include Einstein, Freud, Wittgenstein, Heidegger, Joyce, Kafka, and Cormac McCarthy. They also include Vladimir Putin and Joseph Stalin. Sigmund Freud considered it the greatest novel ever written, but, after all, he wrote an essay on Dostoevsky and parricide. His own fantasy Totem and Taboo (1913) is a lurid version of Dostoevsky’s phantasmagoria. In Freud, the tribal father insists on possessing all women for himself, and then is murdered by the horde of enemy brothers, who devour the totem father. Stalin and Putin join Tsar Alexander II, who was assassinated the year after The Brothers Karamazov was published. Some historians believe Stalin was poisoned at the order of Lavrentiy Beria, Stalin’s Himmler, himself executed in 1953. Putin, alas, is still very much with us.

—

经过这段令人不安的插曲之后，我又回到了卡拉马佐夫家族，以及他们与那些性格迥异的女性之间的纠葛，这些女性彼此之间截然不同，但每一个都让人难以爱上，或者难以抗拒地爱上。

After this uneasy excursus, I return to the Karamazov family and their entanglements with women who are very different from one another, yet each difficult to love or to avoid loving.

我们必须从老卡拉马佐夫说起，记住他才五十五岁：

One has to begin with old Karamazov, and remember that he is just fifty-five:

“别生我哥哥的气！别再伤害他了！”阿廖沙突然坚定地说。

“哎呀，也许吧。哎哟，头疼死了！伊万，把白兰地拿走，我都跟你说了三遍了。”他陷入沉思，突然露出一个意味深长的狡黠笑容：“别生我这种老家伙的气，伊万。我知道你不爱我，但还是别生气。我没什么值得你爱的。你去切尔马什尼亚，我会去看你，我会带礼物。我会给你介绍一个姑娘，我早就看上她了。她还光着脚呢。别害怕光脚的姑娘，别瞧不起她们，她们可是宝贝……！”

他啪的一声亲吻了自己的手。

“对我来说，”他突然变得兴致勃勃，仿佛一时清醒过来，谈到他最喜欢的话题时，“对我来说……啊，你们这些孩子！我的宝贝们，我的小猪崽们，对我来说……我这辈子都没见过丑女人，这是我的原则！你们能理解吗？可你们怎么可能理解呢？你们血管里流的还是奶而不是血，还没孵化呢！按照我的原则，每个女人身上都能找到极其有趣的东西，一些其他女人身上找不到的东西——关键在于如何找到它，这就是诀窍！……”

“Don’t be angry with my brother! Stop hurting him,” Alyosha all of a sudden said insistently.

“Well, well, maybe I will. Oof, what a headache! Take away the cognac, Ivan, it’s the third time I’m telling you.” He lapsed into thought and suddenly smiled a long and cunning smile: “Don’t be angry with an old runt like me, Ivan. I know you don’t love me, but still don’t be angry. There’s nothing to love me for. You go to Chermashnya, and I’ll visit you there, I’ll bring presents. I’ll show you a young wench there, I’ve had my eye on her for a long time. She’s still barefoot. Don’t be afraid of the barefoot ones, don’t despise them, they’re pearls…!”

And he kissed his hand with a smack.

“For me,” he suddenly became all animated, as if sobering up for a moment, once he hit on his favorite subject, “for me…Ah, you children! My babes, my little piglets, for me…even in the whole of my life there has never been an ugly woman, that’s my rule! Can you understand that? But how could you understand it? You’ve still got milk in your veins instead of blood, you’re not hatched yet! According to my rule, one can damn well find something extremely interesting in every woman, something that’s not to be found in any other—one just has to know how to find it, that’s the trick!…”

老卡拉马佐夫除了自己谁也不爱。他和米佳互相鄙视。他需要阿廖沙的爱，而他也确实得到了这份爱，但他既不理解这种需要，也不理解阿廖沙。归根结底，他害怕伊万，并且极力希望阿廖沙不要爱上他的亲兄弟，但这根本不可能。他是个守财奴，也是个精明的土地投机者，被谋杀后会留下十万卢布的遗产。他的活力与福斯塔夫不同，是盲目的、愚钝的、没有智慧的。他就像一台吃喝玩乐的机器，而人工智能无疑终有一天会把这种机器带给我们。

Old Karamazov loves no one except himself. He and Mitya despise one another. He needs Alyosha’s love, which he has, but understands neither the need nor Alyosha. At bottom he fears Ivan and desperately wants Alyosha not to love his full brother, which is impossible. A miser and a shrewd speculator in land, he will leave behind him an estate of a hundred thousand rubles when he is murdered. His vitalism, unlike that of Falstaff, is mindless, without wit, and blind. He might as well be an eating, drinking, sleeping, and whoring machine, which doubtless artificial intelligence will yet bring to us.

出于诸多原因，其中一些相当私人，我对纳博科夫这个人以及他的写作风格都抱有诸多保留意见。我竟然会引用他对陀思妥耶夫斯基的评价，这让我感到很奇怪，因为他认为陀思妥耶夫斯基只是拙劣地模仿了果戈理。以下摘自他曾经在我中途离场的讲座，是他对陀思妥耶夫斯基的一些看法：

For many reasons, some of them quite personal, I have many reservations about Nabokov, both as person and as author. I find it odd that I should cite him on Dostoevsky, whom he regarded as a bad imitator of Gogol. Here, from the lectures I once walked out upon, are his reflections on Dostoevsky:

从艺术视野的历史发展来看，陀思妥耶夫斯基是一个非常引人入胜的现象。如果你仔细研读他的任何一部作品，比如《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》，你会发现自然背景以及所有与感官感知相关的事物几乎都不存在。他笔下的风景是思想的风景，是道德的风景。天气在他的世界里并不存在，所以人们的穿着打扮也无关紧要。陀思妥耶夫斯基通过情境、伦理问题、心理反应以及内心的波澜来刻画人物。在描写完人物的外貌之后，他会采用一种古老的手法，在接下来的场景中不再提及人物的具体外貌特征。这与托尔斯泰等艺术家截然不同，托尔斯泰总是能在脑海中清晰地描绘出人物的形象，并准确地预判人物在特定时刻的姿态。但陀思妥耶夫斯基身上还有更令人惊讶之处。他似乎被俄罗斯文学的命运选中，注定要成为俄罗斯最伟大的剧作家，但他却走错了方向，转而创作小说。在我看来，小说《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》一直像是一部零散的戏剧，舞台上摆放的家具和其他道具恰好满足了各个演员的需求：一张圆桌上留着玻璃杯湿漉漉的圆形痕迹，一扇漆成黄色的窗户，让外面看起来像是有阳光，或者一丛灌木被舞台工作人员匆匆搬进来，并被压扁了……

我们必须始终记住，陀思妥耶夫斯基本质上是一位推理小说作家，他笔下的每一个人物，一旦出场，便始终如一，直至故事的结尾，其独特的性格特征和个人习惯都未曾改变。在整部作品中，他们就像复杂棋局中的棋子一样，在作者的笔下周旋。陀思妥耶夫斯基是一位布局精巧的作家，他成功地吸引了读者的注意力；他以炉火纯青的技艺层层推进，营造出高潮迭起的氛围，并始终保持着悬念。但是，如果你重读他之前读过的作品，熟悉了其中的情节转折和复杂之处，你就会立刻意识到，初读时那种紧张刺激的感觉已经荡然无存……

陀思妥耶夫斯基最钟爱的主题——人类尊严的种种遭遇——既与闹剧紧密相连，也与戏剧密不可分。然而，由于沉溺于这种闹剧式的元素，同时又缺乏真正的幽默感，陀思妥耶夫斯基有时几乎就要滑向喋喋不休、庸俗不堪的胡言乱语……

如同陀思妥耶夫斯基的所有小说一样，这部作品也是文字的奔涌和翻滚，无休止的重复，撇开低语不谈，语言的泛滥令人震惊，尤其是在读过莱蒙托夫那种清澈而优美的散文之后。我们知道，陀思妥耶夫斯基是一位伟大的真理追寻者，一位精神病态的天才，但我们也知道，他并非托尔斯泰、普希金和契诃夫意义上的伟大作家。我再次强调，这并非因为他创造的世界不真实——所有作家的世界都是不真实的——而是因为他创造的世界过于仓促，缺乏那种最不理性的杰作（为了成为杰作）所必须具备的和谐与简洁。的确，从某种意义上说，陀思妥耶夫斯基的粗犷手法过于理性，虽然他的事实只是精神事实，他的人物只是以人为原型的观念，但他们的互动和发展却是由十八世纪末十九世纪初世俗的、传统的长篇小说的机械手法推动的。

In the light of the historical development of artistic vision, Dostoevski is a very fascinating phenomenon. If you examine closely any of his works, say The Brothers Karamazov, you will note that the natural background and all things relevant to the perception of the senses hardly exist. What landscape there is is a landscape of ideas, a moral landscape. The weather does not exist in his world, so it does not much matter how people dress. Dostoevski characterizes his people through situation, through ethical matters, their psychological reactions, their inside ripples. After describing the looks of a character, he uses the old-fashioned device of not referring to his specific physical appearance any more in the scenes with him. This is not the way of an artist, say Tolstoy, who sees his character in his mind all the time and knows exactly the specific gesture he will employ at this or that moment. But there is something more striking still about Dostoevski. He seems to have been chosen by the destiny of Russian letters to become Russia’s greatest playwright, but he took the wrong turning and wrote novels. The novel The Brothers Karamazov has always seemed to me a straggling play, with just that amount of furniture and other implements needed for the various actors: a round table with the wet, round trace of a glass, a window painted yellow to make it look as if there were sunlight outside, or a shrub hastily brought in and plumped down by a stagehand….

Let us always remember that basically Dostoevski is a writer of mystery stories where every character, once introduced to us, remains the same to the bitter end, complete with his special features and personal habits, and that they all are treated throughout the book they happen to be in like chessmen in a complicated chess problem. Being an intricate plotter, Dostoevski succeeds in holding the reader’s attention; he builds up his climaxes and keeps up his suspenses with consummate mastery. But if you re-read a book of his you have already read once so that you are familiar with the surprises and complications of the plot, you will at once realize that the suspense you experienced during the first reading is simply not there any more….

The misadventures of human dignity which form Dostoevski’s favorite theme are as much allied to the farce as to the drama. In indulging this farcical side and being at the same time deprived of any real sense of humor, Dostoevski is sometimes dangerously near to sinking into garrulous and vulgar nonsense….

It is, as in all Dostoevski’s novels, a rush and tumble of words with endless repetitions, mutterings aside, a verbal overflow which shocks the reader after, say, Lermontov’s transparent and beautifully poised prose. Dostoevski as we know is a great seeker after truth, a genius of spiritual morbidity, but as we also know he is not a great writer in the sense Tolstoy, Pushkin, and Chekhov are. And, I repeat, not because the world he creates is unreal—all the worlds of writers are unreal—but because it is created too hastily without any sense of that harmony and economy which the most irrational masterpiece is bound to comply with (in order to be a masterpiece). Indeed, in a sense Dostoevski is much too rational in his crude methods, and though his facts are but spiritual facts and his characters mere ideas in the likeness of people, their interplay and development are actuated by the mechanical methods of the earthbound and conventional novels of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.

如果这一切都被接受，《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》在重读时就会荡然无存。纳博科夫尽管有些矫揉造作，但他仍然是一位伟大的文学艺术家，正如《微暗的火》所展现的那样。而且，他无疑精通并热爱俄语。然而，这只是一种夸张的解读，而非批评。随着小说的推进，米佳、伊万和阿廖沙经历了真实的转变。而年老的卡拉马佐夫、格鲁申卡和卡捷琳娜则没有。或许斯麦尔佳科夫的性格有所恶化，尽管他本就已堕落。格鲁申卡和卡捷琳娜反复无常，但话说回来，我认为没有人会称赞陀思妥耶夫斯基是一位研究女性（甚至男性）的心理学家。纳博科夫或许敏锐地指出，陀思妥耶夫斯基应该成为一名剧作家。

If all this were to be accepted, The Brothers Karamazov would vaporize upon rereading. Nabokov, despite his preciosity, could be a great literary artist, as in Pale Fire. And most certainly he knew and loved the Russian language. Yet this is caricature, not criticism. Mitya, Ivan, and Alyosha undergo authentic change as the novel proceeds. Old Karamazov, Grushenka, Katerina do not. Perhaps Smerdyakov changes for the worse, though he had not far to go. Grushenka and Katerina keep changing their minds and then changing back again, but, then, I do not think that anyone extols Dostoevsky as a psychologist in regard to women, or indeed even to men. Nabokov may have been acute in suggesting that Dostoevsky should have been a playwright.

陀思妥耶夫斯基的小儿子阿廖沙于1878年去世，年仅三岁。如果陀思妥耶夫斯基还活着，这部小说就会有第二卷，几乎完全以完全成熟的阿廖沙为中心展开。我并不确定自己是否会想读它，因为我时不时会对阿廖沙感到厌倦。他有时也会让人感到不安，比如这位圣洁的主人公和他心爱的丽莎之间的这段对话：

Dostoevsky’s youngest son, Alyosha, had died at the age of three in 1878. Had Dostoevsky lived, there would have been a second volume of the novel, centering almost wholly upon the fully mature Alyosha. I am by no means certain that I would have wanted to read it, as I weary of Alyosha from time to time. He can also be disconcerting, as in this exchange between the saintly hero and his beloved Liza:

“我这辈子都会来看你，”阿廖沙坚定地回答道。

“我只跟你说这些，”莉莎再次开口，“只跟我自己说，也只跟你说。这世上只有你一个人。我宁愿跟你说，也不愿跟我自己说。我一点也不觉得羞耻。阿廖沙，为什么我一点也不觉得羞耻，一点也不？阿廖沙，犹太人真的会在逾越节偷走孩子并杀害他们吗？”

“我不知道。”

“我这儿有本书。我在里面读到过某个审判，说有个犹太人先砍掉了一个四岁男孩的所有手指，然后把他钉在墙上，用钉子钉死，最后在审判中说男孩死得很快，四个小时就死了。很快！他说男孩一直在呻吟，不停地呻吟，他就站在那里欣赏。真好！”

“好的？”

“好。有时候我会幻想是我把他钉在十字架上。他吊在那里呻吟，我坐在他对面，吃着菠萝蜜饯。我很喜欢菠萝蜜饯。你喜欢吗？”

“I’ll always come to see you, all my life,” Alyosha answered firmly.

“I tell this to you alone,” Liza began again. “Only to myself, and also to you. You alone in the whole world. And rather to you than to myself. And I’m not at all ashamed with you. Alyosha, why am I not at all ashamed with you, not at all? Alyosha, is it true that Jews steal children on Passover and kill them?”

“I don’t know.”

“I have a book here. I read in it about some trial somewhere, and that a Jew first cut off all the fingers of a four-year-old boy, and then crucified him on the wall, nailed him with nails and crucified him, and then said at his trial that the boy died quickly, in four hours. Quickly! He said the boy was moaning, that he kept moaning, and he stood and admired it. That’s good!”

“Good?”

“Good. Sometimes I imagine that it was I who crucified him. He hangs there moaning, and I sit down facing him, eating pineapple compote. I like pineapple compote very much. Do you?”

我很少在阅读时感到如此困惑，以至于无法继续读下去。读者该如何理解阿廖沙的“我不知道”？无论你是谁，又该如何理解丽莎对菠萝蜜饯和被钉在十字架上的男孩的偏爱？查阅那些公认的陀思妥耶夫斯基学术批评并不能让我感到快乐。他们闪烁其词，避而不谈，最终还是回到了《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》的伟大之处。

It is not often that I am so discombobulated as I read that I am just stopped. What is the reader to do with Alyosha’s “I don’t know”? What are you, whoever you are, to do with Liza’s taste for pineapple compote and crucified boys? Consulting the going and accepted scholarly criticism of Dostoevsky does not make me happy. They dodge and they duck, they dance in and out of the question, and finally fall back on the greatness of The Brothers Karamazov.

他们有时会提及弗拉基米尔·索洛维约夫，这位俄罗斯东正教的神秘主义倡导者，因贫困导致肾衰竭，47岁便英年早逝。索洛维约夫是陀思妥耶夫斯基的朋友，有些人认为他是阿廖沙的原型。尽管索洛维约夫晚年痴迷于“黄祸”论，即亚洲人对俄罗斯的入侵，但他一生致力于宣扬一种真正普世的爱。尤其值得一提的是，他捍卫了俄罗斯犹太人的公民权利，努力驳斥血祭诽谤，并期盼犹太教与基督教最终能够和解。索洛维约夫是一位伟人。至于陀思妥耶夫斯基，或许是一位伟大的作家，或许不是一位，这取决于你的审美判断，但在我看来，他是一个令人厌恶的人。

They do sometimes invoke Vladimir Solovyov, a mystical exponent of Russian Orthodox Christianity who died at forty-seven of kidney failure, brought on by destitution. Solovyov was a friend of Dostoevsky, and some find in him a model for Alyosha. Though in his final years Solovyov became obsessed with the Yellow Peril, or Asiatic encroachment upon Russia, at his apex he preached a love authentically universal. In particular, he defended Jewish civil rights in Russia, worked hard to refute the blood libel, and hoped for an eventual reconciliation between Judaism and Christianity. Solovyov was a great man. Dostoevsky, depending upon your aesthetic judgments, may or may not have been a great writer, but to my mind he was a dreadful human being.

仅仅从小说体裁的角度来解读《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》并无太大帮助。我们或许可以称之为圣经，但这未免过于宽泛，因为陀思妥耶夫斯基似乎将《约伯记》与《启示录》融为一体。佐西马神父对《约伯记》的独特解读——加上结尾处虔诚的补充，即上帝赐予约伯全新的儿女和牲畜，与那些被毁灭的一样美好——被奉为《启示录》本身。

To invoke the genre of the novel does not help much in reading The Brothers Karamazov. We might call it Scripture, though that would be too broad a designation, since Dostoevsky seems to combine the book of Job with the Revelation of Saint John the Divine. Father Zosima’s peculiar reading of the book of Job—with the pious padding added to the end, that God gives Job an entirely new set of sons, daughters, and livestock, just as good as those that were destroyed—is exalted as Revelation itself.

这是米佳的小说，但陀思妥耶夫斯基却把自己的名字赋予了老卡拉马佐夫，这位最糟糕的父亲身上那种感官上的放纵，让我们在他被斯麦尔佳科夫谋杀后，倍感他的缺席。陀思妥耶夫斯基在《笔记》中宣称：“我们每个人，无一例外，都是费奥多尔·帕夫洛维奇”，因为我们都是感官主义者和虚无主义者，无论我们如何试图伪装。陀思妥耶夫斯基强迫自己信奉宗教，但他绝非神秘主义者，他正是卡夫卡那句激情澎湃的格言“不再搞心理学！”的先驱。陀思妥耶夫斯基笔下的人物几乎没有符合规范的性格：他们随心所欲，而他们的意志又变幻莫测。陀思妥耶夫斯基本人亦是如此。他对伊万的不公令人恼火，但陀思妥耶夫斯基的目的正是要激怒我们。

It is Mitya’s novel, but Dostoevsky gave his own first name to old Karamazov, and the sensual exuberance of this worst of fathers makes us feel his absence after he is murdered by Smerdyakov. Dostoevsky, in his Notebooks, declared, “We are all, to the last man, Fyodor Pavloviches,” since we are all sensualists and nihilists, however we attempt to be otherwise. Dostoevsky, who compelled himself to religious belief, was anything but a mystic, and was the ancestor of Kafka’s passionate motto: “No more psychology!” There are almost no normative personalities among Dostoevsky’s characters: they are what they will to be, and their wills are inconstant. And so is Dostoevsky’s. His unfairness to Ivan is exasperating, but Dostoevsky intends to exasperate us.

他激烈地讽刺西方化，并坚信俄罗斯人是上帝的选民，基督是俄罗斯的基督。热情奔放、言辞激烈是一回事，而为了世界末日而宣扬对非俄罗斯人的仇恨则是另一回事。西方文学传统对陀思妥耶夫斯基而言并非像对托尔斯泰那样构成噩梦，但我并不确定陀思妥耶夫斯基是否能理解莎士比亚和维克多·雨果的小说之间的区别，因为雨果笔下世间苦难者的形象与陀思妥耶夫斯基的视角颇为相似。

He was a vehement parodist of Westernization, and firmly believed that Russians were the Chosen People and that Christ was the Russian Christ. It is one thing to be passionate and provocative, and quite another to preach hatred of non-Russians in anticipation of the End of the World. Western literary tradition was not for Dostoevsky the nightmare it constituted for Tolstoy, but I am uncertain that Dostoevsky could see the differences between Shakespeare and the novels of Victor Hugo, whose vision of the wretched of the earth was not far from Dostoevsky’s own.

剩下的只有伊万那首臭名昭著的散文诗《大审判官》，以及陀思妥耶夫斯基笔下伊万与西方文学中最乏味的魔鬼相遇时所遭受的谵妄。我承认，作者为了证明没有上帝的生活是不可能的，竟然如此牺牲伊万的正直，这让我感到愤慨。如今，大审判官已经变得索然无味：与其说是令人厌恶，不如说是令人厌烦。陀思妥耶夫斯基自己也配得上他赋予伊万的那个空洞乏味的魔鬼。如果你想要一个真正的魔鬼，那就去看看伊阿古，或者弥尔顿笔下的撒旦，或者威廉·布莱克的《天堂与地狱的婚姻》，或者拜伦和雪莱之间的争论，或者霍桑的《奇灵沃思》，再从那里去看看纳撒尼尔·韦斯特的《伯劳鸟》，最后去看看科马克·麦卡锡的《霍尔顿法官》。

What is left is Ivan’s notorious prose poem “The Grand Inquisitor” and the delirium with which Dostoevsky afflicts Ivan in the encounter with the most insipid devil in Western literature. I confess to a sense of indignation that his author so sacrifices Ivan’s integrity in order to demonstrate that life without God is impossible. By now the Grand Inquisitor has staled: he is not so much nasty as dreary. Dostoevsky himself deserved the vapid devil he bestows upon Ivan. If you want a devil, go to Iago or to Milton’s Satan, or to William Blake’s The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, or to the agon between Byron and Shelley, or to Hawthorne’s Chillingworth, and from there to Nathanael West’s Shrike, and on to Cormac McCarthy’s Judge Holden.

带着些许沮丧告别《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》。理查德·佩维尔温和地辩称，这是一部充满欢乐的作品，因为它以阿廖沙和一群年轻人彼此宣告爱意的喜悦结尾。但我始终对这个结尾不太满意，因为它带有一种欢呼式的成分。不过，一个疲惫不堪的八十八岁诺斯替犹太人，或许是陀思妥耶夫斯基最不希望的读者。

I am a little dejected in departing from The Brothers Karamazov on this note. Richard Pevear gently argues that it is a joyful book, because it ends in the joy of Alyosha and a group of youngsters proclaiming love for one another. I have never been happy with that final scene, as there is an element of cheerleading in it. Still, an exhausted eighty-eight-year-old Gnostic Jew is perhaps the very last person Dostoevsky would have wanted as his reader.

第27章

CHAPTER 27

卡萨马西玛公主(1886)

The Princess Casamassima (1886)

亨利·詹姆斯​

HENRY JAMES

亨利·詹姆斯创作的政治小说《卡萨马西玛公主》描绘了伦敦无政府主义者的景象，其时间远早于约瑟夫·康拉德的《秘密特工》和《在西方的注视下》，这一点令人惊讶。大约在同一时期，他还创作了同样具有政治色彩的小说《波士顿人》，但这部小说中的冲突发生在男女之间。我更喜欢《波士顿人》 ，但我在《恶魔知晓》 （2015）一书中对此进行了深入探讨。

IT IS STRIKING that Henry James composed his political novel The Princess Casamassima, with its vista of London anarchists, well in advance of Joseph Conrad’s The Secret Agent and Under Western Eyes. At about the same time, he wrote The Bostonians, also political, but there the war is between women and men. I prefer The Bostonians but have considered it at length in a book called The Daemon Knows (2015).

《卡萨玛西玛公主》虽然情节引人入胜，但其问题在于主人公海辛斯·罗宾逊。詹姆斯大胆地将他与哈姆雷特和李尔王相提并论。我必须承认，我无法理解詹姆斯为何会这样想。可怜的海辛斯是社会、经济和文化力量的受害者，而这些力量远远超出了他的理解范围。哈姆雷特的意识甚至比亨利·詹姆斯本人还要广阔。丹麦王子最大的敌人是他自己。李尔王的情感深度超越了亨利·詹姆斯，也超越了任何其他作家，无论是荷马、但丁、塞万提斯还是蒙田。

The problem of The Princess Casamassima, though compelling as it unfolds, is Hyacinth Robinson, the protagonist. James audaciously compared him to Hamlet and to Lear. I must admit that I do not understand how James could think that. Poor Hyacinth is a victim of social, economic, and cultural forces far beyond his ken. Hamlet’s consciousness is more capacious even than that of Henry James. The Prince of Denmark is his own worst enemy. King Lear’s range of affect transcends anything in the world of Henry James or of any other writer, be it Homer or Dante, Cervantes or Montaigne.

海辛斯是法国交际花弗洛伦蒂娜·维维耶与一位不知名的英国贵族私通所生的孩子。弗洛伦蒂娜巧妙地刺死了她的情人，情人当场毙命，弗洛伦蒂娜被判入米尔班克监狱。临死前，海辛斯的养母平妮（平森特小姐，维维耶的密友）将他带进了监狱。多年以后，海辛斯才得知弗洛伦蒂娜是他的生母，而那位被杀的贵族是他的生父。

Hyacinth is the child of an affair between Florentine Vivier, a French courtesan, and an unnamed English lord. Florentine deftly stabs her lover, who expires, and she is sentenced to Millbank prison. As she dies, Hyacinth’s adoptive mother, Pinnie (Miss Pynsent, a close friend of Vivier), brings him into the prison. Much later, Hyacinth will learn that Florentine was his mother and the slain lord his father.

从很多方面来看，《卡萨马西玛公主》都是一部关于受害者的小说。海辛斯敏感而聪颖，却因教育不足而受限，他颇具艺术天赋，这一点在他成为一名技艺超群的装订师后可见一斑。伦敦社会的不公令他困惑不已，于是他加入了无政府主义运动，并自愿执行一项暗杀任务。这与他的人格如此格格不入，在我看来，这无疑是小说的一个缺陷。小说最大的成功之处在于詹姆斯对克里斯蒂娜·莱特——卡萨马西玛公主——的刻画。她抛弃了乏味的丈夫，在无政府主义阴谋中扮演了重要角色。这不禁让人回想起詹姆斯早期的小说《罗德里克·哈德逊》（1875），小说中年轻的克里斯蒂娜以其美貌、活泼的性格、任性的任性和无穷无尽的恶作剧能力深深吸引了我们。

In many ways, The Princess Casamassima is a study in victimage. Hyacinth is sensitive, intelligent though held back by insufficient education, and is something of an artist, as he demonstrates by becoming an unusually skilled bookbinder. Bewildered by the inequities of London society, Hyacinth joins the anarchist movement, and volunteers to carry out an assassination. This is so clearly incommensurate with his personality that it seems to me a flaw in the novel. The great success is James’s representation of Christina Light, the Princess Casamassima, who has abandoned her boring husband and taken on a leading role in the anarchist conspiracy. This sends the reader back to James’s early novel Roderick Hudson (1875), where the young Christina enchants us with her beauty, high spirits, capriciousness, and endless capacity for mischief making.

多年后重读《罗德里克·哈德森》，感觉这部作品褒贬不一。问题出在罗德里克本人身上。他永远像个青少年，是个颇有才华的雕塑家，却脾气暴躁、自私自利，对未婚妻玛丽·加兰朝三暮四。而罗德里克的慷慨赞助人罗兰·马莱特却无可救药地爱上了玛丽。马莱特最终斥责了罗德里克，因为他索要了一大笔钱（他一直是个寄生虫），仅仅是为了去和克里斯蒂娜公主幽会。受到某种程度的自我反省后，罗德里克·哈德森迷失在阿尔卑斯山的暴风雪中，最终丧命，与其说是意外，不如说是自杀。

Roderick Hudson, which I have just reread after many years, is a mixed performance. Roderick himself is the trouble. He is a perpetual adolescent, a sculptor of some talent but given to tantrums, selfish, egoistic, inconstant to his betrothed Mary Garland, with whom Rowland Mallet, Roderick’s generous patron, is hopelessly in love. Mallet at last reproves Roderick, who has requested a large sum of money (he is a perpetual sponger) merely for the purpose of going off to keep an amorous rendezvous with the Princess Christina. Hurt and dazed by some minimal self-recognition, Roderick Hudson wanders off in an Alpine snowstorm and perishes, in what seems more suicide than an accident.

我不知道D·H·劳伦斯是否读过《罗德里克·哈德森》。罗德里克的命运似乎预示了《恋爱中的女人》中杰拉尔德·克里奇冷酷的自杀结局。亨利·詹姆斯和劳伦斯彼此鄙夷，但劳伦斯的一些短篇小说却明显受到了詹姆斯的影响。

I do not know whether D. H. Lawrence ever read Roderick Hudson. There is a foreshadowing of the icy suicidal death of Gerald Crich of Women in Love in Roderick’s fate. Henry James and Lawrence shared a mutual disdain, yet there are a number of shorter fictions by Lawrence that betray James’s influence.

与巴尔扎克不同，亨利·詹姆斯不会将小说中的人物延续到另一部作品中。克里斯蒂娜·莱特是个例外。他看到了她身上尚未被他完全发掘的潜力。而《卡萨马西玛公主》的诞生，正是这一潜力的完美体现。

Henry James, unlike Balzac, did not carry over characters from one novel to another. Christina Light is the large exception. He saw that she had potential that he had not fully realized. The happy consequence was The Princess Casamassima.

克里斯蒂娜对海辛斯颇为赏识，但当她遇到保罗·穆尼门特时，却对他避而远之。穆尼门特虽是化学家，却是无政府主义组织中的高层人物。穆尼门特和克里斯蒂娜坠入爱河，可怜的卡萨马西马王子一路尾随，仍对背叛他的妻子念念不忘。温柔体贴的海辛斯试图安慰王子，但他却无法释怀。

Christina patronizes Hyacinth but turns away when she meets Paul Muniment, chemist by profession, but high in the anarchist hierarchy. Muniment and Christina become lovers, followed from house to house by the wretched Prince Casamassima, still infatuated with his faithless wife. Hyacinth, gentle and caring, attempts to comfort the Prince but he is inconsolable.

海辛斯的养母阿曼达·平森特临终之际，海辛斯悉心照料，并为她哀悼，这给了她莫大的安慰。凭借着她留下的适度遗产，海辛斯前往法国和意大利，开始寻找真正的自我。他沉醉于风景如画、充满意境的美景，曾经的无政府主义热情也随之消散。回到伦敦后，他无法摆脱刺杀公爵的誓言，却又无力付诸行动。最终，他饮弹自尽，结束了自己的生命。

When Amanda Pynsent, Hyacinth’s foster mother, is dying, she has the comfort of Hyacinth’s care and grief for her. On the moderate legacy she has provided, Hyacinth goes to France and Italy and begins to find his authentic self. He falls in love with scenic and atmospheric beauty, and his anarchist zeal vanishes. On his return to London, he cannot evade his pledge to assassinate a duke, and yet it is not possible for him to carry it out. He shoots himself through the heart.

—

公主和一位名叫申克尔的德国无政府主义者破门而入，闯入了海辛斯的家门：

The Princess and a German anarchist, Schinkel, break down Hyacinth’s door:

壁炉架上只有一根蜡烛的微弱光线，昏暗得她一时什么也看不清。然而，就在那一刻到来之前，她的目光便落在了那张小床上。床上有什么东西——黑色的，模糊的，伸展开来的东西。辛克尔试图阻止她，但只是一瞬间；她看清了一切，随即跪倒在床边。海辛斯躺在那里，仿佛睡着了一般，但床上、他的肋部、他的心脏上，却有一团可怕的血迹。他的手臂无力地垂在身旁，垂在狭窄的床沿外；他的脸色苍白，双眼紧闭。

The light was that of a single candle on the mantel; it was so poor that for a moment she made out nothing definite. Before that moment was over, however, her eyes had attached themselves to the small bed. There was something on it—something black, something ambiguous, something out-stretched. Schinkel held her back, but only for an instant; she saw everything, and with the very act she flung herself beside the bed, upon her knees. Hyacinth lay there as if he were asleep, but there was a horrible thing, a mess of blood, on the bed, in his side, in his heart. His arm hung limp beside him, downwards, off the narrow couch; his face was white and his eyes were closed.

人们或许会理解克里斯蒂娜的震惊，但也会怀疑她是否真的感到悲痛。如果海辛斯刺杀了公爵，那他岂不是犯下了弑父之罪？他岂不是会认同自己那杀人如麻的母亲？这显然是不可能的。或许哈姆雷特之所以没有杀死克劳狄斯，是因为他无法得知格特鲁德和克劳狄斯的通奸始于何时。他会不会是克劳狄斯的儿子？如果莎士比亚知道答案，他也不会告诉我们。

One grants Christina shock but wonders if there is any true grief. Hyacinth would have committed a kind of patricide had he assassinated the Duke. He would also have identified with his murderous mother, an impossibility. It may be that Hamlet held back from slaughtering Claudius because he could not know when the adultery between Gertrude and Claudius had begun. Could he be the son of Claudius? If Shakespeare knows, he will not tell us.

海辛斯太过优秀，太过罕见，与《卡萨玛西玛公主》中狄更斯笔下的伦敦格格不入。亨利·詹姆斯的笔法如此精妙，迫使我们去揣测海辛斯为何不选择逃离困境。作为一名技艺精湛的装订工，他本可以在意大利或法国生存下去。然而，他的宿命却深藏于心。他懂得太多，却又太过匮乏，以至于无法摆脱困境。或许，他才是亨利·詹姆斯所有作品中最具莎士比亚式风格的人物。

Hyacinth is too good, too rare a growth, for the Dickensian London of The Princess Casamassima. Henry James is so subtle that he obliges us to surmise why Hyacinth simply did not walk away from his dilemma. As a skilled bookbinder, he could have survived in Italy or France. The fatality is within him. He knows too much and also too little to work out of entrapment. He may after all be the most Shakespearean figure in all of Henry James.

第28章

CHAPTER 28

《大使们》（1903）

The Ambassadors (1903)

亨利·詹姆斯​

HENRY JAMES

亨利·詹姆斯认为《大使》是他作品的巅峰之作。这本书在资深评论家眼中褒贬不一，问题出在主人公路易斯·兰伯特·斯特雷瑟身上。我曾一度思考，斯特雷瑟是否配得上与伊莎贝尔·阿切尔、米莉·西尔和玛吉·弗弗相提并论。我认为，尽管他令人深感同情和钦佩，但他带给我们的痛苦却不足以真正令人难忘，因为他的遭遇并没有让我们感到痛苦。尼采曾坚持认为，记忆依赖于痛苦。

HENRY JAMES considered The Ambassadors the crown of his work. The book has divided qualified critics, the problem being the protagonist, Lewis Lambert Strether. Once, I wondered if Strether deserved to be compared to Isabel Archer, Milly Theale, and Maggie Verver. I thought that, though he is profoundly sympathetic and admirable, he does not give us enough grief to be truly memorable, since his saga is not painful to us. Nietzsche insisted that memory depends upon pain.

五十五岁的斯特雷瑟觉得自己已年迈。他显然已与令人畏惧的寡妇纽瑟姆夫人订婚。纽瑟姆夫人希望儿子查德结束在巴黎的逗留。查德在巴黎与玛丽·德·维奥内相恋，玛丽是一位美丽、机智、敏感的女子，她已与令人厌恶的丈夫分居。这段恋情极大地改善了查德的为人。《大使》一书表面上展现了斯特雷瑟逐渐改过自新的过程，这主要体现在他与玛丽·德·维奥内以及一位名叫玛丽亚·戈斯特雷的美国女子的对话中。玛丽亚·戈斯特雷爱上了斯特雷瑟，她魅力四射、坦率真诚。

At fifty-five, Strether considers himself elderly. He is evidently betrothed to the fearsome and widowed Mrs. Newsome, who wishes her son, Chad, to break off his sojourn in Paris, where he has been greatly improved by his affair with Marie de Vionnet, a beautiful woman alive with tact and sensibility, who has separated from her unpleasant husband. On its surface The Ambassadors manifests the progressive re-education of Strether, largely by his conversations with Marie de Vionnet and with an American, Maria Gostrey, who falls in love with Strether and is in every way winsome and open.

在阅读并推荐谢尔顿·M·诺维克的传记《亨利·詹姆斯：青年大师》（1996）和《亨利·詹姆斯：成熟大师》（2007）之前，我对亨利·詹姆斯的同性恋倾向一无所知。后来，我又读了詹姆斯写给雕塑家亨德里克·安德森、达德利·乔斯林·珀斯以及霍华德·奥弗林·斯特吉斯和休·沃尔波尔的信件，后两位作家如今都已名声扫地。显然，这四人都是詹姆斯的男宠，而且还有其他人。由于《兰伯特·斯特雷瑟》某种程度上是亨利·詹姆斯的自画像，这或许可以解释他为何放弃了玛丽亚·戈斯特雷给予他的爱，以及玛丽·德·维奥内对他的暗示。

I knew nothing about the homoeroticism of Henry James until I read and endorsed Sheldon M. Novick’s biographies Henry James: The Young Master (1996) and Henry James: The Mature Master (2007). Later, I read the letters of James to the sculptor Hendrik Andersen, to Dudley Jocelyn Persse, and to Howard Overing Sturgis and Hugh Walpole, both writers whose reputations have vanished. Clearly all four were James’s catamites, and there were others. Since Lambert Strether is a kind of self-portrait of Henry James, this may or may not illuminate his renunciation of the love offered to him by Maria Gostrey and implicitly suggested by Marie de Vionnet.

这并非暗示斯特雷瑟有同性恋倾向，因为他几乎同时爱上了玛丽亚和玛丽。然而，他已是中年丧偶之人，詹姆斯也从未暗示斯特雷瑟在妻子和儿子去世后有过任何性经历。难以想象像斯特雷瑟这样细腻的情感竟会与可怕的纽瑟姆太太结合。然而，詹姆斯并没有充分解释，至少在我看来，为什么斯特雷瑟（他经济独立）不留在巴黎，周旋于两位爱慕他的绝世佳人之间。我指的并非性方面，因为斯特雷瑟如今是否对任何人怀有欲望尚不明确，尽管他确实欣赏查德在玛丽·德·维奥内的影响下变得多么英俊。

This is hardly to imply that Strether is homoerotic, since he all but falls in love with both Maria and Marie. Still, he is a widower in late middle age, and James never suggests that Strether has had any sexual experience since the death of his wife and then of his son. It is grotesque to think that so fine a sensibility as Strether’s could ever have united itself with the dreadful Mrs. Newsome. Yet James does not adequately explain, at least to me, why Strether (who has independent means) does not stay in Paris and shuttle between his two adoring and marvelous women. I do not mean sexually, since it is not at all clear that Strether now lusts for anyone, though he does admire how handsome Chad has become under the influence of Marie de Vionnet.

归根结底，问题在于我们能否将路易斯·兰伯特·斯特雷瑟与亨利·詹姆斯这位大师区分开来。我很难做到这一点。我曾疑惑，喜爱巴尔扎克的詹姆斯为何似乎在暗示《路易斯·兰伯特》（1832）这部带有斯威登堡式幻想色彩的作品：书中主人公路易斯·兰伯特拥有超凡的天赋，却英年早逝于爱人宝琳的怀抱，以便他真正的天使之身能够升入天堂。这至今仍是詹姆斯式的谜团。不过，亨利和他的父亲以及才华横溢的哥哥威廉一样，对超感官知觉和我们存在的幽灵般的本质抱有奇特的想法。他们既相信死后的生命，又不相信。

It comes down to whether we can detach Lewis Lambert Strether from the Master Henry James. I can do so only with difficulty. I wondered once why James, who loved Balzac, seems to have alluded to Louis Lambert (1832), a kind of Swedenborgian fantasy in which the young man of the title has preternatural gifts, and expires all too soon in the arms of his beloved Pauline, so that his true angel-self can rise up to heaven. This remains a Jamesian mystery, but, then, Henry, like his father and his gifted brother, William, entertained curious ideas about extrasensory perception and the ghostliness of our condition. They did and did not believe in life after death.

我又回到斯特雷瑟身上。 《大使》的最佳评论家包括萨莉·西尔斯和托尼·坦纳。他们笔下的斯特雷瑟是一位超然的印象派画家，几乎可以称得上是帕特里式的感知典范。他的天赋在于观察。与路易·兰伯特不同，他并非先知。视觉、听觉、嗅觉、味觉、触觉：这些构成了他的世界。而巴黎的伟大将这一切提升到了一种世俗的狂喜之中。

I return to Strether. The best critics of The Ambassadors include Sallie Sears and Tony Tanner. Their Strether is a detached impressionist, an all but Paterian paragon of perception. His genius is to see. Unlike Louis Lambert, he is not a seer. Sights, sounds, odors, tastes, touches: these are his world. And all this is raised to a kind of secular ecstasy by the greatness of Paris.

亨利·詹姆斯和他的化身斯特雷瑟与卡莱尔、罗斯金和纽曼等维多利亚时代的智者有着复杂的关系，他们都强调“观察”是通往智慧殿堂的道路。詹姆斯和斯特雷瑟并不追求智慧或全知全能，他们想要将感知本身提升到艺术的高度。

Henry James and his surrogate Strether have a complex relation to such Victorian sages as Carlyle, Ruskin, and Newman, with their emphasis upon seeing as the road to the palace of wisdom. James and Strether do not seek for wisdom or for complete knowledge. They want to raise perception itself to the status of an art.

我想我真的无法完全区分亨利·詹姆斯和兰伯特·斯特雷瑟。也许这反而是件好事。当我再次重读这本书时，我必须努力克制自己，不让自己变得更像斯特雷瑟，尽管我和他一点也不像。我希望詹姆斯能让斯特雷瑟无限期地留在巴黎，享受与玛丽亚和玛丽之间纯洁的爱恋。但詹姆斯是一位伟大的艺术家，他不会这么做。斯特雷瑟坚持认为，他不能从巴黎的经历中获得任何私利。

I suppose that I really cannot fully distinguish between Henry James and Lambert Strether. That may be all to the good. As I reread yet once more, I have to resist becoming more like Strether, though I do not resemble him in the least. I wish that James had allowed himself to end the book with Strether staying on in Paris indefinitely, allowing himself to enjoy the chaste delights of loving and being loved by Maria and Marie. But James is too great the artist for that. Strether insists that he must gain nothing for himself from his Parisian experience.

他回到了马萨诸塞州的伍利特，但并未投入纽瑟姆太太那令人怀疑的怀抱。他会在那里做什么呢？我愿意相信，他的良心会让他幡然悔悟，允许他重返巴黎，回到玛丽亚·戈斯特雷和玛丽·德·维奥内身边。在现实生活中，这或许是有可能的，但在亨利·詹姆斯大师的喜剧构想中，却并非如此。

Back to Woollett, Massachusetts, he goes, but not to the dubious embrace of Mrs. Newsome. What will he do there? I like to believe that his conscience will relent and allow him to return to Paris, and so to Maria Gostrey and Marie de Vionnet. In mere life, it would be probable, but not in the comedic vision of the Master Henry James.

第29章

CHAPTER 29

诺斯特罗莫号（1904）

Nostromo (1904)

约瑟夫· C·康拉德

JOSEPH CONRAD

约瑟夫·康拉德（ Joseph C. Conrad）原名约瑟夫·特奥多尔·康拉德·科热尼奥夫斯基（Józef Teodor Konrad Korzeniowski），出生于乌克兰，当时乌克兰是俄罗斯帝国的一部分，此前是波兰的一部分。他从小说波兰语，后来学习了法语，英语则成为他的第三语言。

JOSEPH CONRAD was born Józef Teodor Konrad Korzeniowski in the Ukraine, then part of the Russian Empire, and before that of Poland. He grew up speaking Polish, learned French, and turned to English as a third language.

即使对于一位年轻的波兰文人来说，康拉德的早年生活也堪称离奇，更何况是一位英国作家。27岁时，他曾协助西班牙卡洛斯派叛军进行军火走私活动。在此之前，他险些丧命，试图自杀，爱上了一位致命的美人，还挥霍无度地赌博。四年后，他开始在英国商船上从事更为传统的职业，直至1894年。在此期间，他曾担任船长，并获得了英国国籍。在接下来的三十年里，他成为了一位杰出的小说家，创作了《吉姆爷》、《诺斯特罗莫》、《秘密特工》、《在西方的注视下》和《胜利》等杰作。

Conrad’s early life was outrageous enough even for a young Polish person of letters, let alone for an English writer. At twenty-seven, he helped run a munitions-smuggling operation for the Carlist rebels in Spain. Before it was over, he came close to being killed, attempted suicide, fell in love with a fatal beauty, and gambled on a grand scale. Four years later, he began a more conventional career in the British merchant marine, which continued until 1894, during which time he commanded his own vessel, and was granted English citizenship. For his remaining thirty years, he was a superb and successful novelist, bringing forth such masterworks as Lord Jim, Nostromo, The Secret Agent, Under Western Eyes, and Victory.

他的早期故事和小说反映了福楼拜和莫泊桑的影响。亨利·詹姆斯后来成为他的挚友，并将康拉德的文学风格转变为我们现在所认为的詹姆斯的中期风格：《波因顿的战利品》、《梅茜的世界》、 《尴尬的年纪》。

His early stories and novels reflect the influence of Flaubert and of Maupassant. Henry James, who became a close friend, changed Conrad’s literary mode to what we now think of as James’s middle style: The Spoils of Poynton, What Maisie Knew, The Awkward Age.

康拉德与詹姆斯风格迥异的标志之一便是马洛这个人物，这已是老生常谈。马洛赋予了康拉德一种流畅而富有张力的叙事视角。亨利·詹姆斯曾轻蔑地称马洛为“那个荒诞的魔法水手”，这固然有趣，但却无关紧要。马洛在一段时间内区分了亨利·詹姆斯和约瑟夫·康拉德的印象主义风格。认为康拉德远不如詹姆斯那样具有形而上学的理想主义倾向，并非暗示康拉德是更伟大的小说家。但这有助于解释为何康拉德而非亨利·詹姆斯对欧内斯特·海明威、F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德和威廉·福克纳等美国作家产生了更为深远的影响。《太阳照常升起》、 《了不起的盖茨比》和《我弥留之际》的氛围更能体现《黑暗之心》和《诺斯特罗莫》的精髓，而非《卡萨马西玛公主》和《大使们》。

It is a truism to see Conrad’s swerve away from James in the figure of Marlow, who allowed Conrad an effectively sinuous narrative perspective. Henry James dismissed Marlow as “that preposterous magic mariner,” which was good fun, but rather beside the point. Marlow makes the difference, for a while, between the impressionism of Henry James and Joseph Conrad. To judge that Conrad was much less a metaphysical idealist than James is not to suggest that Conrad was the greater novelist. But it helps explain why Conrad, and not Henry James, was the major influence upon the American generation of Ernest Hemingway, F. Scott Fitzgerald, and William Faulkner. The milieu of The Sun Also Rises, The Great Gatsby, and As I Lay Dying evidences the saliences of Heart of Darkness and Nostromo, and not of The Princess Casamassima and The Ambassadors.

我第一次读《诺斯特罗莫》是在1948年，当时参加了一个由一位杰出的老师——小威廉·梅里特·塞尔——主持的小说研讨班。塞尔老师和M·H·艾布拉姆斯一起指导了我在康奈尔大学的本科学习。塞尔老师还向我介绍了塞缪尔·理查森的《克拉丽莎》，这部小说与《堂吉诃德》和《追忆似水年华》一起，至今仍是我最喜欢的几部小说之一。

I first read Nostromo in 1948, for a seminar on the novel conducted by a remarkable teacher, William Merritt Sale, Jr., who, together with M. H. Abrams, guided my undergraduate studies at Cornell University. Sale also introduced me to Samuel Richardson’s Clarissa, which, with Don Quixote and In Search of Lost Time, is still one of my favorite novels.

晚年我在耶鲁大学任教时，对小说的了解主要来自马丁·普莱斯，他于2010年去世，享年90岁。1983年，普莱斯出版了一部杰出的著作：《生命的形式：小说中的人物与道德想象》。在论述康拉德的章节中，普莱斯巧妙地探讨了他所谓的康拉德作品中“反讽的局限性”。

In my later years, teaching at Yale, I learned most about the novel from Martin Price, who died at the age of ninety in 2010. In 1983, Price published a remarkable book: Forms of Life: Character and Moral Imagination in the Novel. In the chapter on Conrad, Price subtly traced what he called “the limits of irony” in the novelist’s work.

然而，康拉德在《诺斯特罗莫》中讽刺的界限究竟在哪里？这位英勇的诺斯特罗莫沉迷于自身的辉煌，尽管他是人民的英雄，但本质上却是空洞的。除了少数例外，康拉德笔下的所有主人公都是空洞之人。康拉德作品中诸多悖论之一在于，大海这面镜子让我们得以窥见一种英雄理想，而这种理想在康拉德的伟大虚构作品中却并不存在。

And yet where are the limits of Conrad’s irony in Nostromo? The magnificent Nostromo is in love with his own magnificence, and though he is a hero of the people, he is essentially hollow. With few exceptions, all of Conrad’s protagonists are hollow men. One of the many paradoxes of Conrad is that the mirror of the sea allows us to perceive a heroic ideal, one that is not available in Conrad’s great fictions.

康拉德作品中讽刺的界限在哪里？对于深受康拉德影响的讽刺家马丁·普莱斯来说，讽刺没有界限。普莱斯既看到了《吉姆爷》中的怀疑主义和讽刺，也看到了其中不屈不挠的浪漫主义。两者都得到了充分的展现，彼此互不平衡，互不否定。普莱斯将《诺斯特罗莫》的排名较低，因为他认为其中的讽刺达到了极致。康拉德是一位杰出的艺术家，他把评判权留给了读者。随着年龄的增长，我放弃了讽刺，转而与诺斯特罗莫一同沉浸在他那如同加里波第般的浪漫主义之中。在《诺斯特罗莫》中，这种浪漫主义是有缺陷的，甚至是堕落的，但这又有什么关系呢？在康拉德的作品中，重要的不是你是否背叛了自己：你当然必须背叛自己，而且你终将背叛自己。你要么背叛他人，要么背叛自己。这就是康拉德式的选择。当然，他人也会背叛你，但这并不重要，这不过是另一种讽刺罢了。诺斯特罗莫为了金钱出卖自己，但他背叛的只有他自身真实的光辉。

What are the limits of irony in Conrad? For Martin Price, a profoundly Conradian ironist, there are no limits. Price sees both the skepticism and the irony of Lord Jim and yet also perceives its unrelenting romanticism. Both are allowed their full eloquence, and neither can balance or negate the other. Price ranks Nostromo lower, because he sees the irony as triumphant there. Conrad, an astonishing artist, allows the reader to decide. As I age, I abandon my ironies and join Nostromo in his Garibaldi-like romanticism. In Nostromo, it is flawed and corrupt, but what matter? What matters in Conrad is not whether you betray yourself: of course you must and will. Either you betray others or yourself. Those are the Conradian options. Of course, others betray you, but that is of minor interest, another mere irony. Nostromo sells himself for silver and yet betrays nothing except his own authentic splendor.

在康拉德的作品中，你屈服于毁灭的元素，死亡之海：康拉德笔下的所有人物，除了《黑暗之心》中的库尔茨之外，没有一个拥有哈姆雷特那样强大的精神力量，而从实用主义的角度来看，库尔茨最终也走向了自我毁灭。爱德华·萨义德敏锐地指出，康拉德令人信服地坚持认为，我们作为人，作为作家，只有依靠自身的怪癖才能生存下去。在康拉德对人性的看法中，最重要的是我们每个人都是不可预测的。

In Conrad, you submit to the destructive element, the sea of death: no character in all of Conrad has a Hamlet-like power of mind, unless it be Kurtz, in Heart of Darkness, and he is self-obliterated, pragmatically speaking. Edward Said shrewdly noted Conrad’s persuasive insistence that we can survive, as persons and as writers, only through the agency of our eccentricities. What matters most in Conrad’s view of the human is that each of us is unpredictable.

康拉德的仰慕者最喜爱的莫过于他的五部伟大作品：《吉姆爷》（1900）、《诺斯特罗莫》（1904）、《秘密特工》（1907）、《在西方的注视下》（1911）和《胜利》（1915）。这些小说叙事细腻而饱含痛苦，构成了一部风格迥异却又无比精彩的杰作。尽管它们有着共同的特征，却也常常让读者怀疑它们是否出自同一位作家之手。康拉德本人及其作品都充满了神秘感，他那令人敬畏的道德形象贯穿始终，他的存在感不容忽视。他是一位难以捉摸的叙事者，却仿佛在书写一部连贯的精神自传。对我而言，康拉德的巅峰之作是《诺斯特罗莫》，这部作品中他的视野最为开阔，他对人类盲点及其所引发的情感的刻画也最为独到。如同所有震撼人心的原创性作品一样，康拉德的原创性也带来了一种难以理解的复杂性，这种复杂性需要读者慢慢体会，甚至可能永远无法完全理解。反复阅读后，我逐渐确信，《诺斯特罗莫》绝非康拉德式的对所谓“忠诚”美德的颂歌。尽管康拉德对尼采极度蔑视，但这部小说却是一部后尼采式的悲剧。马丁·德库德失去了所有幻想，最终因无法忍受孤独而自我毁灭。诺斯特罗莫或许是二十世纪小说英雄中唯一一个令人信服地展现自然崇高之美的人物，正如康拉德所说，他“被背叛，却不知被何人或何物背叛”。但这正是康拉德最深刻的洞察，小说精准地向我们揭示了诺斯特罗莫是如何被他自己，以及他内心深处的某种东西所背叛的。

An admirer of Conrad is happiest with his five great novels: Lord Jim (1900), Nostromo (1904), The Secret Agent (1907), Under Western Eyes (1911), and Victory (1915). Subtle and tormented narratives, they form an extraordinarily varied achievement, and despite their common features they can make a reader wonder that they all have been composed by the same artist. Endlessly enigmatic as a personality and as a formidable moral character, Conrad pervades his own books, a presence not to be put by, an elusive storyteller who yet seems to write a continuous spiritual autobiography. For me, Conrad’s masterwork is Nostromo, where his perspectives are largest and where his essential originality in the representation of human blindnesses and consequent human affections is at its strongest. Like all overwhelming originalities, Conrad’s ensues in an authentic difficulty, which can be assimilated only very slowly, if at all. Repeated rereadings gradually convince me that Nostromo is anything but a Conradian litany to the virtue he liked to call “fidelity.” The book is tragedy, of a post-Nietzschean sort, despite Conrad’s strong contempt for Nietzsche. Martin Decoud, emptied of all illusions, is self-destroyed because he cannot sustain solitude. Nostromo, perhaps the only persuasive instance of the natural sublime in a twentieth-century hero of fiction, dies “betrayed he hardly knows by what or by whom,” as Conrad says. But this is Conrad at his most knowing, and the novel shows us precisely how Nostromo is betrayed, by himself, and by what is in himself.

作者将这位中心人物描述为“伟大的卡帕塔兹，人民的领袖”，字里行间流露出作家对笔下最令人惊叹的想象力的热爱。康拉德在初版十三年后添加的序言“作者注”中，也有一段关键的文字表达了同样的情感：

His creator’s description of this central figure as “the Magnificent Capataz, the Man of the People,” breathes a writer’s love for his most surprising act of the imagination. So does a crucial paragraph from the same source, the “Author’s Note” that Conrad added as a preface thirteen years after the initial publication:

他牢牢掌控着继承的土地，挥霍无度却又慷慨大方，慷慨馈赠，男子气概十足，自尊心极强，隐隐觉得自己无比伟大，并且忠心耿耿地奉献着某种既绝望又无可救药的冲动。他是一位人民的领袖，是人民自身不带任何嫉妒的力量，不屑于领导，却在人民内部掌控着一切。多年以后，他已是名震四方的菲丹萨上尉，在国家中拥有了稳固的地位。在苏拉科现代化的街道上，他忙于处理各种事务，人们投来敬意的目光。他拜访搬运工的遗孀，参加兄弟会，在集会上静静地聆听无政府主义者的演讲。他是新革命运动中神秘的赞助人，是值得信赖的富裕同志菲丹萨，尽管他内心深处深知自己道德的沦丧，但他本质上仍然是一位人民的领袖。在他对生活的热爱与鄙夷交织中，在被背叛的困惑信念中，在被背叛而死的信念中（他几乎不知道被什么人或什么事背叛），他仍然是人民的一员，是他们无可争议的伟人——拥有他自己的私人历史。

In his firm grip on the earth he inherits, in his improvidence and generosity, in his lavishness with his gifts, in his manly vanity, in the obscure sense of his greatness, and in his faithful devotion with something despairing as well as desperate in its impulses, he is a Man of the People, their very own unenvious force, disdaining to lead but ruling from within. Years afterwards, grown older as the famous Captain Fidanza, with a stake in the country, going about his many affairs followed by respectful glances in the modernized streets of Sulaco, calling on the widow of the cargador, attending the Lodge, listening in unmoved silence to anarchist speeches at the meeting, the enigmatical patron of the new revolutionary agitation, the trusted, the wealthy comrade Fidanza with the knowledge of his moral ruin locked up in his breast, he remains essentially a Man of the People. In his mingled love and scorn of life and in the bewildered conviction of having been betrayed, of dying betrayed he hardly knows by what or by whom, he is still of the People, their undoubted Great Man—with a private history of his own.

只有当诺斯特罗莫能够完全真诚地说出“我的名字从苏拉科岛的一端到另一端都知道了。你们还能为我做些什么呢？”时，他才是真正的自己。

Nostromo is only himself when he can say, with perfect truth: “My name is known from one end of Sulaco to the other. What more can you do for me?”

康拉德虚构了一个名为科斯塔瓜纳的南美国家，其最富裕的省份名为奥克西登塔尔，并拥有一座港口城市苏拉科。我们可以推测，康拉德的灵感来源于哥伦比亚。查尔斯·古尔德出生于科斯塔瓜纳，虽有英国血统，却是苏拉科附近银矿的所有者。他厌倦了国内的动荡，转而支持独裁者里维埃拉，但银矿引发了一系列叛乱，其中一场由蒙特罗将军领导，兵临苏拉科城下。古尔德急于保住自己的银矿，命令码头总管诺斯特罗莫将银锭运往国外出售。

Conrad invents a South American country, Costaguana, whose richest province is called Occidental and which has a port city, Sulaco. We can surmise that Conrad had Colombia in mind. Charles Gould, born in Costaguana though of English descent, is the owner of the silver mine near Sulaco. Weary of the country’s turmoil, he backs the dictator Ribiera, but the silver provokes a series of rebellions, including one led by a General Montero, who closes in on Sulaco. Gould, anxious to save his silver, orders the “Capataz de Cargadores” (chief longshoreman) Nostromo to rescue the ingots by taking them upon the water for eventual sale abroad.

乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·菲丹扎，也就是诺斯特罗莫的真名（在意大利语中，“诺斯特罗莫”意为水手长，但也有人认为它是意大利语“nostro uomo ”（意为“我们的人”）的谐音），深受苏拉科所有人的信任。诺斯特罗莫与记者兼漫游者马丁·德库德一同驾驶一艘驳船驶出港口，但当晚驳船与一艘载有叛军的船只相撞。他们将驳船搁浅在无人居住的大伊莎贝尔岛上，才得以打捞起船上的银子。英勇的船长卡帕塔兹游回岸边，留下德库德守卫银子。诺斯特罗莫超越自我，翻山越岭去召集军队，拯救了刚刚独立的苏拉科王国。可怜的德库德无法忍受孤独，乘救生艇出海，用四块金条沉入水中，饮弹自尽，沉入海底。

Giovanni Battista Fidanza, Nostromo’s actual name (in Italian “Nostromo” signifies a boatswain, yet some think it is a play upon the Italian nostro uomo or “our man”), is trusted by everyone in Sulaco. Accompanied by Martin Decoud, journalist and flâneur, Nostromo sails a lighter out of the harbor, but that night it collides with a vessel carrying rebel forces. The silver is salvaged by grounding the lighter on the island of Great Isabel, which is uninhabited. The magnificent Capataz swims back to shore, abandoning Decoud to guard the silver. Surpassing himself, Nostromo rides over mountains to bring in the army that will save the newly independent state of Sulaco. Poor Decoud, unable to bear solitude, rides a lifeboat to sea, weighs his body down with four ingots, shoots himself, and goes down into the water.

诺斯特罗莫独自一人，心中充满着关于宝藏下落的秘密。他开始怀疑自己的英勇事迹是否徒劳，德库德和四块银锭的消失更是让他百思不得其解。大伊莎贝尔岛上修建灯塔后，诺斯特罗莫利用自己的影响力，安排他的朋友，鳏夫加里波第诺·乔治·维奥拉担任灯塔管理员。英俊潇洒的卡帕塔兹爱上了维奥拉的小女儿吉赛尔，而他的未婚妻琳达也爱慕着他的大女儿吉赛尔。不幸的是，在一个漆黑的夜晚，诺斯特罗莫试图偷走更多的银锭时，被年迈的维奥拉误认为是陌生人，开枪射杀。

Nostromo is left alone with his guilty secret as to the fate of the treasure. He begins to believe that his heroic exploits have been for nothing, and he is baffled by the disappearance of Decoud and the four ingots of silver. When a lighthouse is constructed on Great Isabel, Nostromo employs his influence to have his friend, the widowed Garibaldino Giorgio Viola, made the lighthouse keeper. In love with Giselle, Viola’s younger daughter, the magnificent Capataz in turn is loved by the older daughter, Linda, to whom he is betrothed. Unfortunately, one dark night, as Nostromo attempts to nab more ingots, he is shot and killed by old Viola, under the impression that the interloper is a stranger.

诺斯特罗莫的胜利，尽管他自己可能并不知情，在于他真实的形象得以留存，这形象如此强大，以至于康拉德和敏锐的读者都相信，即使是自我背叛的英雄，也保留着一种审美尊严，这使得他的死亡带有悲剧色彩，而非卑劣可耻。可怜的德库，尽管才华横溢，却死于虚无主义，消失得“不留一丝痕迹，被万物的巨大冷漠所吞噬”。诺斯特罗莫死后，在小说精彩绝伦的结尾中，得到了超越一切讽刺的审美致敬：
