Nostromo’s triumph, though he cannot know it, is that an image of his authenticity survives, an image so powerful as to persuade both Conrad and the perceptive reader that even the self-betrayed hero retains an aesthetic dignity that renders his death partly tragic rather than sordid. Poor Decoud, for all his brilliance, dies a nihilistic death, disappearing “without a trace, swallowed up in the immense indifference of things.” Nostromo, after his death, receives an aesthetic tribute beyond all irony, in the superb close of the novel:

琳达的黑色身影在灯笼的光芒下直立起来，双臂高举过头，仿佛要纵身跃下。

“是我爱你，”她低声说道，脸色僵硬，月光下像大理石般洁白。“是我！只有我！她会忘记你，就因为她那张漂亮的脸蛋，惨遭杀害。我无法理解。我无法理解。但我永远不会忘记你。永远不会！”

她静静地站着，一动不动，积蓄力量，将她所有的忠诚、痛苦、困惑和绝望都倾注到一声巨大的呐喊中。

“绝不！吉安·巴蒂斯塔！”

莫尼汉姆博士在警局的巡逻车里转过身，听到这个名字从他头顶掠过。这是诺斯特罗莫的又一次胜利，一次最伟大、最令人艳羡、也最阴险的胜利。在那声仿佛从蓬塔马拉响彻到阿苏埃拉，再到地平线那明亮的线条，被一团闪耀着银光的大白云笼罩的壮丽呐喊中，这位才华横溢的船长在征服财富和爱情的黑暗深渊中，展现出他非凡的天赋。

Linda’s black figure detached itself upright on the light of the lantern with her arms raised above her head as though she were going to throw herself over.

“It is I who loved you,” she whispered, with a face as set and white as marble in the moonlight. “I! Only I! She will forget thee, killed miserably for her pretty face. I cannot understand. I cannot understand. But I shall never forget thee. Never!”

She stood silent and still, collecting her strength to throw all her fidelity, her pain, bewilderment, and despair into one great cry.

“Never! Gian’ Battista!”

Dr. Monygham, pulling round in the police-galley, heard the name pass over his head. It was another of Nostromo’s triumphs, the greatest, the most enviable, the most sinister of all. In that true cry of undying passion that seemed to ring aloud from Punta Mala to Azuera and away to the bright line of the horizon, overhung by a big white cloud shining like a mass of solid silver, the genius of the magnificent Capataz de Cargadores dominated the dark gulf containing his conquests of treasure and love.

正如马丁·普莱斯所指出的，约瑟夫·康拉德的讽刺的界限是无法捉摸的。那“辉煌”究竟是讽刺还是浪漫？我们该如何理解这种演变：最伟大、最令人艳羡、最阴险？“阴险”是指“令人不安”，还是指某种预兆，正如厄休拉·勒奎恩所说的“黑暗的左手”？康拉德将这个问题留给了读者。当我重读《黑暗之心》时，我感到困惑，因为我无法解读马洛或康拉德的晦涩之处。那颗心中似乎存在着一个真空，一片迷雾笼罩的中间地带，我抗拒着继承它。我记得诗人亚伦·福格尔的著作《被迫开口：康拉德的对话诗学》（1985）中，在关于诺斯特罗莫的章节结尾处有一段话：

The limits of Joseph Conrad’s irony, as Martin Price indicated, cannot be known. Is that “magnificent” ironic or romantic? What are we to make of the progression: the greatest, the most enviable, the most sinister of all? Does “sinister” mean “disturbing,” or is it heraldic, what Ursula K. Le Guin called “the left hand of darkness”? Conrad abandons the question to the reader’s share. I am troubled when I reread Heart of Darkness and cannot decipher Marlow’s or Conrad’s obscurantism. There seems a vacuum in that heart, a misty mid-region I rebel against inheriting. I remember a paragraph at the close of the chapter on Nostromo in the poet Aaron Fogel’s book Coercion to Speak: Conrad’s Poetics of Dialogue (1985):

这种将所有权视为强制占有、违背自身意愿继承的观念，如同存在本身，既与哈罗德·布鲁姆的诗歌“影响”概念相似，又与之相悖。在《序曲》中，华兹华斯用“审问”一词来描述他对自身寻找可能主题的审视。正如博尔赫斯将文学比作“另一种审问”一样，其中的讽刺意味无穷无尽。然而，随着康拉德作品的推进，他似乎已经转向，或者说试图转向，部分地摆脱了自我审问的无限讽刺浪漫（由受浪漫主义驱使的叙述者马洛所代表），转而转向在政治小说时期对有限的、外在的、粗糙的、被迫的现实世界对话的描绘。这其中隐隐透露出一种怀疑：总是将强制的表达方式内化为诗歌意志，或许是一种糟糕的辩护，一种糟糕的无限。在布鲁姆式的浪漫主义中，诗学或许是通过内化来否定俄狄浦斯情结中那种被迫与外部世界对话的秩序——将审问转化为一种内在的、与先辈或自身争辩的冲动。无论如何，康拉德从无休止的自我审视转向强调“客观”的政治场景，在这些场景中，被奴役、被殖民或依附的个体被迫发声、拥有、回应。用布鲁姆极具感染力的个人视角来看，古尔德从战败的父亲那里继承的银矿象征着康拉德从他自己的父亲以及他的“先辈们”那里继承的波兰诗歌依附性、波兰悲剧性的“沉默”以及波兰诗歌在更广阔世界中的少数地位。这至少是一种合理的解读。但康拉德对历史上通过依附手段争取独立的斗争的描述，无疑也意在展现殖民者对抗外部影响的实际政治斗争。这是康拉德后期政治小说中向其早期作品提出的自我批判性问题之一，尽管并非总是成功。他逐渐确信，说话的冲动并非总是源于内心，而强迫说话的政治层面有时会被内心的痛苦所掩盖。

This idea of ownership as forced possession, something inherited against one’s will, like existence itself, both resembles and diverges from Harold Bloom’s concept of poetic “influence.” In The Prelude Wordsworth uses the term inquisition to describe his examination of himself for possible themes. As in Borges’ reference to literature as “other inquisitions,” the irony is infinite. Conrad, as his own work progressed, seems however to have turned, or to have tried to turn, partly away from the infinite ironic romance of self-inquisition (represented by the romantically compelled speaker Marlow) toward the representation, during the period of the political novels, of limited, external, crude forced dialogues in the world. There is the hint of a suspicion that it might be a bad defense, a bad infinity, to always internalize the format of coercion to speak as poetic will. Poetics, in Bloomian romanticism, may be the denial, by internalization, of the Oedipal order of forced dialogue in the outside world—the translation of inquisition into an inner feeling of compulsion to quarrel with a forebear or with oneself. In any case, Conrad turned from infinite self-inquisition to emphasize “objective” political scenes in which the enslaved, colonized, or dependent individual is made to speak, to own, to respond. In Bloom’s signally moving personal terms, Gould’s inheritance of the silver mine from his defeated father symbolizes Conrad’s inheritance, from his own father and his “fathers,” of Polish poetic dependency, Polish tragic “silence,” Polish poetic minority in the greater world. And this is, to say the least, a viable reading. But Conrad’s description of historical struggles for independence via dependent means is certainly also meant as a representation of actual political struggle by colonials against outside influences. This is one of the self-critical questions Conrad’s later political novels direct, not always successfully, against his early work. He becomes convinced that the compulsion to speak does not always come from within, and that the political aspect of coercion to speak is at times disguised by inner agony.

在我看来，与前人或与自己争论似乎是更大审判的前奏：作家的思想对自身的影响。在康拉德的政治小说—— 《诺斯特罗莫》、 《秘密特工》、 《西方之眼》——中，他越来越不给笔下人物任何自由，除了他们自身的怪癖。他们的命运不仅受制于他们在经济和社会秩序中的地位，也受制于他们最终走向毁灭的性格。乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·菲丹扎，尽管声名显赫，却始终缺乏安全感，最终为了追求自己的荣耀而牺牲。马丁·德库德则因内心的空虚而无法忍受孤独，最终自杀身亡。

Quarreling with a precursor or with oneself to me seems a prelude to the greater inquisition: the influence of a writer’s mind upon itself. In his political novels—Nostromo, The Secret Agent, Under Western Eyes—Conrad increasingly will not allow his characters any freedom except their own eccentricities. They are overdetermined not only by their place in the economic and social order, but by their personalities that become fatalities. Giovanni Battista Fidanza, perpetually insecure despite his renown, dies as a sacrifice to his own sense of glory. Martin Decoud slays himself because solitude is made unbearable by his inward vacuity.

第三十章

CHAPTER 30

《秘密特工》（1907）

The Secret Agent (1907)

约瑟夫· C·康拉德

JOSEPH CONRAD

三年后，在《秘密特工》中，一个全新的康拉德形象诞生了，他以近乎隐形的叙述者视角，描绘了一个令人想起狄更斯《我们共同的朋友》（1865）中黑暗苦难的伦敦。一代人的时间足以改变伦敦。康拉德对狄更斯十分敬仰。表面上看，他们之间并无太多共同之处，但他们却都饱受着都市噩梦的折磨。在狄更斯笔下，伦敦的犯罪是暴力的，有时甚至是家族内部的。而康拉德则生活在一个无政府主义者对压迫和剥削政权充满愤怒的时代。

THREE YEARS LATER, in The Secret Agent, something like a new Conrad came into being, an almost invisible narrator of a London recalling the dark agonies of Charles Dickens’s Our Mutual Friend (1865). A generation had greatly altered London. Conrad deeply admired Dickens. On the surface they have little in common, but they dream some of the same metropolitan nightmares. London crime, for Dickens, was violent and sometimes familial. Conrad lived in an age of anarchist outrage against repressive and exploiting regimes.

如同许多政治术语一样，无政府主义往往被其敌人赋予负面色彩。希腊语“ anarchos”意为“无政府状态”，而这一概念最初源于罗马，汉娜·阿伦特对其含义的解读是，它旨在增强公民社会的基础。

As with so many political terms, anarchism tended to have a negative aura, as used by its enemies. The Greek anarchos means the absence of authority, which in itself was initially a Roman concept with the meaning, as interpreted by Hannah Arendt, of augmenting the foundations of civil society.

世纪之交，无政府主义者的暗杀事件变得频繁且轰动一时。1894年，法国总统卡诺遇刺身亡；1901年，美国总统威廉·麦金莱遭枪击身亡。此类事件层出不穷，但约瑟夫·康拉德创作《秘密特工》的灵感却源于1894年格林威治皇家天文台遭遇的离奇炸弹袭击。那名企图实施炸弹袭击的法国无政府主义者最终引爆了自己。

Anarchist assassinations became frequent and sensational around the turn of the century. President Carnot of France was slain in 1894; in 1901, President William McKinley of the United States was shot to death. There were other such events, but Joseph Conrad’s inspiration for The Secret Agent came from the weird attempt to bomb the Royal Observatory at Greenwich in 1894. The would-be bomber, a French anarchist, merely blew himself up.

康拉德终其一生都对大多数俄罗斯事物抱有反感，这对于一个波兰流亡者来说完全可以理解。和亨利·詹姆斯一样，他对屠格涅夫另眼相看，而且也和詹姆斯一样，他严重低估了托尔斯泰。尽管他对饱受折磨的陀思妥耶夫斯基抱有敌意，但他却无法完全摆脱《罪与罚》和《群魔》的影响。

Conrad had a lifelong aversion to most things Russian, highly understandable in a Polish exile. Like Henry James, he made an exception for Turgenev, and, again like James, enormously undervalued Tolstoy. Though hostile to the tormented Dostoevsky, he could not quite escape the effect of Crime and Punishment and Demons.

《秘密特工》的副标题是“一个简单的故事”。这或许带有讽刺意味，也或许并非如此。温妮·弗洛克的一生，乃至她的死亡，都绝非简单。她是一位出身工人阶级、容貌姣好的年轻女子，父亲经营着一家酒吧。为了年迈的母亲和患有自闭症的弟弟史蒂夫，她嫁给了年长肥胖的阿道夫·弗洛克。史蒂夫对动物的痛苦极其敏感，除了姐姐的爱，他与世隔绝。

The Secret Agent has the subtitle A Simple Tale. That may or may not be ironic. Winnie Verloc’s life and death are hardly simple. An attractive working-class young woman whose father kept a pub, she married the older and grossly obese Adolf Verloc for the sake of her old mother and for her younger brother, Stevie, who appears to be autistic. He is immensely sensitive to the suffering of animals and, except for the love of his sister, is totally isolated.

弗洛克是俄罗斯的秘密特工，奉俄罗斯大使馆弗拉基米尔先生之命，对格林尼治天文台实施炸弹袭击，以此震慑英国政府和民众，促使其对无政府主义者采取更严厉的镇压措施。弗洛克领导的伦敦小组成员包括：迈克尔斯；靠勾引下层女性为生的亚历山大·奥西蓬同志；资深恐怖分子卡尔·云特；以及最引人注目的，被称为“教授”的可怕人物，他精通爆炸技术。教授在伦敦街头游荡，充满仇恨，却刀枪不入，因为警方意识到他就是一颗行走的炸弹，随时可能引爆自身，殃及众多路人。

Verloc is a secret agent for the Russians and is ordered by Mr. Vladimir of their embassy to carry out a bombing of the Greenwich Observatory, in order to shock the English government and people into a more severe crackdown upon anarchists. The London group headed by Verloc includes Michaelis; Comrade Alexander Ossipon, who lives by seducing lower-class women; the veteran terrorist Karl Yundt; and, most remarkably, the quite scary creature known as “the Professor,” who is gifted at explosives. The Professor walks around London, fierce with hatred, and invulnerable, because the police realize that he is a walking bomb and can at any time explode himself and take with him a number of passing citizens.

维洛克从教授那里得到一枚炸弹，把它交给史蒂维，并指引他前往天文台。爆炸后，人们只能用铲子清理史蒂维的残骸。当温妮意识到维洛克的所作所为极其可怕时，她不假思索地采取了行动：

Verloc receives a bomb from the Professor, gives it to Stevie, and points him toward the Observatory. After the explosion, the remnants of Stevie have to be gathered by shovels. When Winnie realizes Verloc’s enormity, she takes action without reflection:

她立刻向前走去，仿佛她仍然是那个男人的忠贞妻子，与他之间有着牢不可破的契约。她的右手轻轻掠过桌沿，当她走向沙发时，切肉刀已悄无声息地从盘子边消失了。弗洛克先生听到地板吱呀作响，便心满意足地等着。弗洛克太太来了。仿佛史蒂夫无家可归的灵魂径直飞向他姐姐——他的守护者和保护者——的怀抱寻求庇护，她与哥哥的容貌每走一步都越来越像，就连下唇的下垂，甚至连眼睛的细微分叉都如出一辙。但弗洛克先生并没有看到这些。他仰面躺着，目光呆滞地望着上方。他看到天花板和墙壁上，一只紧握着切肉刀的手臂的影子在移动。它上下闪烁，动作悠闲自在。他们动作足够慢，以至于弗洛克先生能够认出肢体和武器。

他们有足够的时间让他完全理解这预兆的含义，并品尝到死亡的滋味涌上心头。他的妻子已经疯了——疯得要杀人。他们有足够的时间让他从最初的麻痹感中恢复过来，转而下定决心，要从与那个持枪疯子的可怕搏斗中取得胜利。他们有足够的时间让弗洛克先生制定一个防御计划：躲到桌子后面，用一把沉重的木椅把那个女人击倒在地。但他们没有足够的时间让弗洛克先生腾出手脚。刀子已经刺入了他的胸膛。它一路畅通无阻。危险就是如此精准。弗洛克太太越过沙发边缘，狠狠地给了弗洛克先生一击，将她那古老而隐秘的血脉传承、洞穴时代的野蛮凶狠，以及酒吧时代失控的神经质狂怒，全都倾注在了这记重击之中。弗洛克先生，这位秘密特工，被这一击的力量微微侧身，一动不动地咽了气，只发出了一声低低的“别这样”作为抗议。

弗洛克太太松开了刀，她与已故哥哥惊人的相似之处也已消失，如今变得十分普通。她深吸了一口气，这是自希特督察向她展示那块贴着标签的史蒂维大衣碎片以来，她第一次轻松地呼吸。她双臂交叉，倚在沙发边，身体前倾。她摆出这副轻松的姿势，并非为了观看或幸灾乐祸地欣赏弗洛克先生的尸体，而是因为客厅里一阵阵地摇晃，仿佛置身于暴风雨中的大海。她感到一阵眩晕，却又平静。她成了一个自由的女人，一种完美的自由让她无所牵挂，也无所事事，因为史蒂维对她而言不再是迫切的牵绊。弗洛克太太习惯于用图像思考，如今却不再受幻象的困扰，因为她什么也不想了。她也一动不动。她像一具尸体般，享受着完全的无忧无虑和无尽的闲暇。她一动不动，一言不发。躺在沙发上的已故弗洛克先生的遗体也同样如此。若非弗洛克太太还活着，这两人本该完美契合：那种谨慎的矜持，不多言，谨慎的举止，曾是他们体面家庭生活的基石。因为他们的生活原本体面，用一种得体的沉默掩盖了从事秘密职业和进行不正当交易可能带来的种种问题。直到生命的最后一刻，他们的体面都未曾被不合时宜的尖叫和其他不合时宜的真诚所扰乱。而在这致命一击之后，这份体面也以静止和沉默的形式延续了下来。

She started forward at once, as if she were still a loyal woman bound to that man by an unbroken contract. Her right hand skimmed slightly the end of the table, and when she had passed on towards the sofa the carving knife had vanished without the slightest sound from the side of the dish. Mr. Verloc heard the creaky plank in the floor, and was content. He waited. Mrs. Verloc was coming. As if the homeless soul of Stevie had flown for shelter straight to the breast of his sister, guardian and protector, the resemblance of her face with that of her brother grew at every step, even to the droop of the lower lip, even to the slight divergence of the eyes. But Mr. Verloc did not see that. He was lying on his back and staring upwards. He saw partly on the ceiling and partly on the wall the moving shadow of an arm with a clenched hand holding a carving knife. It flickered up and down. Its movements were leisurely. They were leisurely enough for Mr. Verloc to recognise the limb and the weapon.

They were leisurely enough for him to take in the full meaning of the portent, and to taste the flavour of death rising in his gorge. His wife had gone raving mad—murdering mad. They were leisurely enough for the first paralysing effect of this discovery to pass away before a resolute determination to come out victorious from the ghastly struggle with that armed lunatic. They were leisurely enough for Mr. Verloc to elaborate a plan of defence involving a dash behind the table, and the felling of the woman to the ground with a heavy wooden chair. But they were not leisurely enough to allow Mr. Verloc the time to move either hand or foot. The knife was already planted in his breast. It met no resistance on its way. Hazard has such accuracies. Into that plunging blow, delivered over the side of the couch, Mrs. Verloc had put all the inheritance of her immemorial and obscure descent, the simple ferocity of the age of caverns, and the unbalanced nervous fury of the age of bar-rooms. Mr. Verloc, the Secret Agent, turning slightly on his side with the force of the blow, expired without stirring a limb, in the muttered sound of the word ‘Don’t’ by way of protest.

Mrs. Verloc had let go the knife, and her extraordinary resemblance to her late brother had faded, had become very ordinary now. She drew a deep breath, the first easy breath since Chief Inspector Heat had exhibited to her the labelled piece of Stevie’s overcoat. She leaned forward on her folded arms over the side of the sofa. She adopted that easy attitude not in order to watch or gloat over the body of Mr. Verloc, but because of the undulatory and swinging movements of the parlour, which for some time behaved as though it were at sea in a tempest. She was giddy but calm. She had become a free woman with a perfection of freedom which left her nothing to desire and absolutely nothing to do, since Stevie’s urgent claim on her devotion no longer existed. Mrs. Verloc, who thought in images, was not troubled now by visions, because she did not think at all. And she did not move. She was a woman enjoying her complete irresponsibility and endless leisure, almost in the manner of a corpse. She did not move, she did not think. Neither did the mortal envelope of the late Mr. Verloc reposing on the sofa. Except for the fact that Mrs. Verloc breathed these two would have been perfectly in accord: that accord of prudent reserve without superfluous words, and sparing of signs, which had been the foundation of their respectable home life. For it had been respectable, covering by a decent reticence the problems that may arise in the practice of a secret profession and the commerce of shady wares. To the last its decorum had remained undisturbed by unseemly shrieks and other misplaced sincerities of conduct. And after the striking of the blow, this respectability was continued in immobility and silence.

即使对康拉德而言，这亦是非凡之作。温妮化身为阿特洛波斯，命运三女神中最古老、最不可避免的那一位。文风变得冷酷无情：“危险竟有如此精准之处。”如果这真是约瑟夫·康拉德的声音，那么它已然像莎士比亚那样，退隐到一种神秘莫测的缥缈之中。

Even for Conrad, this is remarkable writing. Winnie transmutes into Atropos, oldest and most inevitable of the Three Fates. Style becomes implacable: “Hazard has such accuracies.” If this is the voice of Joseph Conrad, it has undergone a Shakespearean withdrawal into an enigmatic reserve.

奥西蓬同志来​​了，像往常一样试图勾引温妮，想以带她逃往法国为诱饵，骗取弗洛克的银行账户。拿到钱后，他被温妮的行为和举止吓坏了，把她丢在了海峡渡轮上。温妮显然害怕被绞死，摘下结婚戒指，投海自尽。

Comrade Ossipon arrives, tries for his customary seduction, hoping to secure Verloc’s bank account on the promise of fleeing to France with Winnie. Taking the cash, he takes fright at Winnie’s deed and demeanor, and abandons her on the channel ferry. Evidently fearing the gallows, Winnie takes off her wedding ring, and drowns herself in the channel.

究竟是康拉德的创作灵感或天赋驱使他写出了这篇“简单的故事”？在我们这个恐怖的时代，《秘密特工》对许多读者而言具有迫切的现实意义。康拉德的妻子杰西·乔治是一位英国工人阶级女性，她在回忆录中提到，丈夫在创作《秘密特工》期间是多么沮丧。无政府主义既令康拉德着迷，又令他感到沮丧。他所有的小说都力图构建一种秩序，而这种秩序与二十世纪初英国的道德观念几乎格格不入。尽管他生活在一个讲究礼仪的环境中，但他的内心始终存在着一种反讽与浪漫（即浪漫主义意义上的浪漫）之间的挣扎。

What was it in Conrad’s daemon or genius that impelled him to compose this “simple tale”? In our Age of Terror, The Secret Agent for many readers has an urgent relevancy. Conrad’s wife, Jessie George, a working-class Englishwoman, in her memoir mentions how depressed her husband was as he labored on The Secret Agent. Anarchism both obsessed and dismayed Conrad. All of his fiction drives toward an idea of order that is hardly to be identified with the morality of the English nation in the early twentieth century. Though he lived in an atmosphere of correctness, there was in him always an agon between irony and romance, in the sense of romanticism.

重读《秘密特工》，我常常有一种莫名的感觉，康拉德似乎刻意将他笔下的人物与自身保持着距离。他并不完全喜欢自己正在做的事情。我想不出他其他任何一部小说或故事像这部一样如此依赖形容词。仿佛他想要修饰许多名词，让它们不那么令他反感。

Rereading The Secret Agent, I frequently have the uncanny sense that Conrad holds his ongoing narrative as far away from himself as he can. He does not altogether like what he finds himself doing. I cannot think of any other novel or story by him in which he relies so much upon adjectives. It is as though he wants to modify many substantives so as to make them less unpleasant to him.

放下《秘密特工》这本书时，我感到更多的是如释重负，而非沮丧。但随即我意识到，明天早晨的《纽约时报》只会让我更加沮丧。国内外的恐怖和暴政已成常态。在我余下的四五年里，总有一天我会重读《秘密特工》，带着敬佩和些许不满。

When I put down my copy of The Secret Agent, I am more relieved than depressed. But then I realize that tomorrow morning’s New York Times will bring me only depression. Terror and tyranny abroad and at home is the way things are. A time will come in my remaining four or five years when I will reread The Secret Agent with admiration and some ingratitude.

第31章

CHAPTER 31

在西方人的注视下（1911）

Under Western Eyes (1911)

约瑟夫· C·康拉德

JOSEPH CONRAD

得知康拉德在创作《西方之眼》期间是多么紧张和痛苦，令人深感痛心。对他而言，这部小说是他创作生涯中最痛苦的。1910年1月，他的精神和身体都崩溃了，这或许是由于他与忠实的经纪人J·B·平克发生争执所致，平克一直资助着康拉德一家。

IT IS SOBERING to learn how tense and unhappy Conrad was as he worked at Under Western Eyes, for him the most excruciating of his novels. Mental and physical breakdown in January 1910 may have been provoked by a quarrel with his faithful agent, J. B. Pinker, who had been financing the Conrad family.

直到1913年小说《机遇》出版，康拉德的经济困境才开始得到缓解。这本书在1914年销量极佳，最终使这位小说家名利双收。我个人觉得《机遇》读起来并不十分流畅，但他最终找到自己的读者群，这着实令人欣慰。

It was not until the publication of the novel Chance in 1913 that Conrad’s financial problems began to be solved. The book sold heavily throughout 1914 and finally made the novelist both prosperous and famous. I cannot say that I find Chance very readable, but it is gratifying that he at last found his public.

康拉德的伟大才华最终在小说《胜利》（1915）中得以展现，这部小说销量不错，但却令许多读者感到困惑。我个人觉得它引人入胜，尽管也令人无比悲伤。小说结尾，舞台空无一人，因为所有主人公都已死去，或死于谋杀，或死于自杀，或死于意外。

The final flickering of Conrad’s greatness came in the novel Victory (1915), which sold well but baffled much of the public. I myself find it rewarding, though hopelessly sad. At its close the stage is bare, since all the protagonists have died, whether by murder, suicide, or accident.

在《西方目光下》出版八年后，康拉德添加了一篇作者注，内容充满反思，略带好斗，与他对所有俄罗斯事物的阴暗看法一致：

Eight years after the publication of Under Western Eyes, Conrad added an author’s note that is reflective, a little pugnacious, and consistent with his dark vista of all things Russian:

我最大的焦虑在于能否保持绝对公正。这种绝对公正的义务，既源于历史渊源，也源于种族和家庭的特殊经历，更源于我根深蒂固的信念：唯有真理，才能为任何虚构作品提供正当性，使其哪怕是最微不足道的艺术价值，或是在当代男女文化中占有一席之地。我从未被要求如此超脱世俗……

My greatest anxiety was in being able to strike and sustain the note of scrupulous impartiality. The obligation of absolute fairness was imposed on me historically and hereditarily, by the peculiar experience of race and family, in addition to my primary conviction that truth alone is the justification of any fiction which makes the least claim to the quality of art or may hope to take its place in the culture of men and women of its time. I had never been called before to a greater effort of detachment….

这里的“种族”指的是波兰人。康拉德在《西方之眼》中始终保持着惊人的超脱，尽管其中始终暗藏着压抑的愤怒。“家庭”指的是康拉德的父亲阿波罗·科热尼奥夫斯基（1820-1869），他是一位杰出的诗人、剧作家、翻译家，也是一位始终如一、经常从事地下活动的波兰革命者。1861年，他被捕后流放，健康状况急剧恶化。和他的独子——小说家康拉德一样，阿波罗·科热尼奥夫斯基非常崇拜莎士比亚，并翻译过他的作品。摘自康拉德的作者注：

“Race” here means being Polish. We can credit Conrad for an astonishing detachment throughout Under Western Eyes, though there is always an undercurrent of repressed outrage. “Family” refers to Conrad’s father, Apollo Korzeniowski (1820–69), a distinguished poet and dramatist, as well as a translator, and a consistent, frequently underground revolutionary for the Polish cause. Arrested in 1861, he was sent into exile, which destroyed his health. Like his only child, the novelist, Apollo Korzeniowski greatly admired Shakespeare and translated him. From Conrad’s author’s note:

拉祖莫夫受到了同情。他为何不值得同情呢？他只是个普通的年轻人，工作能力强，志向也合乎情理。他良心尚可。如果说他有什么不寻常之处，那也只是他对自身处境的敏感。由于他并非孤儿，所以他比任何人都更强烈地感受到自己是俄罗斯人——否则他就什么都不是。他把整个俄罗斯视为自己的遗产，这完全合情合理。那片混沌之地沸腾着的罪恶和牺牲，其血腥的徒劳将他吞噬，将他压垮。但我认为，即便他心神不宁，也从未变成怪物。这里没有人被描绘成怪物——无论是头脑简单的特克拉，还是固执己见的索菲娅·安东诺夫娜。彼得·伊万诺维奇和德·S夫人则成了众矢之的。他们是阴森丛林中的猿猴，他们的恶行也正是他们应得的下场。至于尼基塔——绰号“死神”——他是恐怖主义荒野中的完美之花。在与他打交道的过程中，最令我感到困扰的不是他的残暴，而是他的平庸。

Razumov is treated sympathetically. Why should he not be? He is an ordinary young man, with a healthy capacity for work and sane ambitions. He has an average conscience. If he is slightly abnormal it is only in his sensitiveness to his position. Being nobody’s child he feels rather more keenly than another would that he is a Russian—or he is nothing. He is perfectly right in looking on all Russia as his heritage. The sanguinary futility of the crimes and the sacrifices seething in that amorphous mass envelops and crushes him. But I don’t think that in his distraction he is ever monstrous. Nobody is exhibited as a monster here—neither the simple-minded Tekla nor the wrong-headed Sophia Antonovna. Peter Ivanovitch and Madame de S. are fair game. They are the apes of a sinister jungle and are treated as their grimaces deserve. As to Nikita—nicknamed Necator—he is the perfect flower of the terroristic wilderness. What troubled me most in dealing with him was not his monstrosity but his banality.

康拉德的语气在此处稍作犹豫，随后又恢复了冷漠疏离。我不喜欢拉祖莫夫，也无法相信康拉德会喜欢他。拉祖莫夫的确是一位贵族的私生子，而这位贵族几乎不承认他的身份。当然，拉祖莫夫也并非十恶不赦。德·S夫人是彼得·伊万诺维奇的富裕赞助人，而彼得·伊万诺维奇的原型显然是米哈伊尔·巴枯宁，这位臭名昭著的激进分子、反犹主义者和暴力分子，同时也是无政府工团主义的主要理论家。尼基塔残暴无情，他是一名沙皇的双重间谍，他弄破了拉祖莫夫的耳膜，使他失聪。之后，拉祖莫夫被电车撞倒，身受重伤。他之所以能活下来，全靠特克拉毕生照顾他。一些评论家指出，康拉德在这里预示了汉娜·阿伦特关于“平庸之恶”的观点。

Conrad’s tone here hesitates before going back to detachment. I do not like Razumov and cannot believe Conrad did, either. It is true that Razumov is the bastard son of a nobleman who only barely acknowledges him. Granted also that Razumov is never monstrous. Madame de S. is the wealthy patroness of Peter Ivanovitch, who clearly is based upon Mikhail Bakunin, a notorious firebrand, anti-Semitic and violent, who was the major anarcho-syndicalist theorist. Nikita is brutal, a tsarist double agent who destroys Razumov’s eardrums, rendering him deaf. Subsequently, Razumov is run over by a tram and severely crippled. He survives only because Tekla devotes her life to taking care of him. Several critics have noted Conrad’s prolepsis of Hannah Arendt’s idea of the banality of evil.

最令人恐惧的反思（我这里仅代表我个人）是，这些人并非例外，而是普遍现象——他们所处地域、所处时代、所处种族的常态。专制统治的残暴和愚蠢，摒弃一切法律，实际上建立在彻底的道德无政府主义之上，这引发了同样愚蠢和残暴的回应：一种纯粹的乌托邦式革命主义，它不惜一切手段进行破坏，并异想天开地认为，任何既定的人类制度垮台后，必然会带来人心的根本转变。这些人看不到，他们所能做的仅仅是改变名称而已。压迫者和被压迫者都是俄罗斯人；世界再次直面那句谚语的真谛：虎纹难改，豹斑难改。

The most terrifying reflection (I am speaking now for myself) is that all these people are not the product of the exceptional but of the general—of the normality of their place, and time, and race. The ferocity and imbecility of an autocratic rule rejecting all legality and in fact basing itself upon complete moral anarchism provokes the no less imbecile and atrocious answer of a purely Utopian revolutionism encompassing destruction by the first means to hand, in the strange conviction that a fundamental change of hearts must follow the downfall of any given human institutions. These people are unable to see that all they can effect is merely a change of names. The oppressors and the oppressed are all Russians together; and the world is brought once more face to face with the truth of the saying that the tiger cannot change his stripes nor the leopard his spots.

在某些方面，2018 年的这种趋势比 1920 年更为强烈。康拉德希望我们记住《耶利米书》13:23，在《詹姆斯国王钦定版圣经》中是这样写的：“古实人岂能改变肤色呢？豹岂能改变斑点呢？你们习惯作恶，若能如此，也可以行善。” 在普京时代，除了认同康拉德对俄罗斯一切事物的怀疑态度，我们还能做什么呢？然而，尽管康拉德厌恶陀思妥耶夫斯基，但《罪与罚》显然为拉祖莫夫的处境提供了蓝本。拉斯科尔尼科夫最终意识到，他杀害两位老妇人就是在谋杀自己；拉祖莫夫则明白，他背叛哈尔金就是把自己出卖给了国家。

The surge of this is in some ways stronger in 2018 than it was in 1920. Conrad wants us to remember Jeremiah 13:23, which in the King James Version reads: “Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil.” In the age of Putin, what can we do except agree with Conrad’s skepticism as to all things Russian? And yet, despite his loathing for Dostoevsky, clearly Crime and Punishment serves as a model for Razumov’s situation. Raskolnikov comes to realize that by butchering the two old women he has murdered himself; Razumov sees that in betraying Haldin he has sold himself to the state.

在《西方目光下》中，我们还能找到陀思妥耶夫斯基和托尔斯泰的痕迹。它们为何存在？似乎是刻意为之。康拉德与屠格涅夫或亨利·詹姆斯一样，都具有文明的修养。他骨子里是个波兰人，无法原谅俄罗斯，但他像他的父亲一样，从莎士比亚那里领悟到，人物塑造超越了道德评判。或许，在康拉德的作品中，典故的使用成为了一种赎罪的方式。

There are other traces of Dostoevsky and also of Tolstoy in Under Western Eyes. Why are they there? They seem deliberate. Conrad was as civilized as Turgenev or Henry James. Polish at the core, he could not forgive Russia but had learned from Shakespeare, as his father had, that the creation of character transcended moral judgment. It may be that in Conrad allusiveness becomes a form of atonement.

我常常想，如果《在西方的目光下》像《秘密特工》一样采用全知视角叙述，会不会更加出色。马洛无法融入俄国革命流亡者的日内瓦生活，但那位不知名的老语言教师却无法让我相信他那西方的视角是可靠的。他似乎对娜塔莉娅·维克托罗夫娜·哈尔金情有独钟，却又缺乏足够的自信去明智地引导她。马洛从康拉德的框架中脱颖而出；而那位语言教师则显得茫然无措，无所适从。

I wonder if Under Western Eyes would not have been an even stronger work if, like The Secret Agent, it had had an omniscient narrator. Marlow could not fit in the Geneva of Russian revolutionary exiles, but the unnamed, elderly teacher of languages does not persuade me that his Western eyes are reliable. He seems to be all but in love with Natalia Victorovna Haldin yet lacks the confidence to guide her wisely. Marlow emerges from the matrix of Conrad; the language teacher is drearily adrift.

但每当我回想起康拉德在创作《西方之眼》时所经历的痛苦，我便感到惭愧。叶芝曾祈求那些沐浴在上帝圣火中的智者成为他灵魂的吟唱导师。作为一位博采众长的神秘主义者，叶芝将上帝与死亡等同起来。约瑟夫·康拉德始终保持怀疑态度，他曾在1902年写给爱德华·加内特的信中提到：“我从十四岁起就一直厌恶基督教，厌恶它的教义、仪式和节日。”正是这种质疑精神伴随康拉德直至生命的尽头。

But then I am chastened by thinking back to Conrad’s torment as he wrote Under Western Eyes. W. B. Yeats called upon sages standing in God’s holy fire to be the singing masters of his soul. An eclectic occultist, Yeats equated God and death. Joseph Conrad remained a skeptic, famously writing to Edward Garnett in 1902: “I always, from the age of fourteen, disliked the Christian religion, its doctrines, ceremonies and festivals.” That questioning spirit saw Conrad through to the end.

第32章

CHAPTER 32

礁石（1912）

The Reef (1912)

E ·迪思· W·哈顿

EDITH WHARTON

如果你有阅读和重读的狂热，你会收获意想不到的惊喜。我原本打算写一篇关于伊迪丝·华顿三部无可争议的杰作之一的简短评论：《欢乐之家》、《乡村习俗》和《纯真年代》。我曾多次重读这三部作品，并就它们以及《伊桑·弗洛姆》都写过评论。我的朋友R·W·B·刘易斯（1917-2002）曾撰写过华顿的巨著传记，并编辑过她的多卷作品集。2000年，他力荐我阅读《礁石》。我花了十八年时间才听从刘易斯的建议，如今终于读完了《礁石》的两遍。

IF YOU SUFFER from the rage for reading and rereading, you are rewarded by lucky surprises. I intended to write this brief commentary upon one of three indubitable masterpieces by Edith Wharton: The House of Mirth, The Custom of the Country, The Age of Innocence. I had reread them several times and written about all of them, as well as about Ethan Frome. My friend R. W. B. Lewis (1917–2002), who wrote a large biography of Wharton, and edited several volumes of her work, in the year 2000 urged me to read The Reef. I have taken eighteen years to follow Dick’s advice and have just completed two readings of The Reef.

这是一部曲折离奇、令人不安的小说，与伊迪丝·华顿的性生活有着错综复杂的关系。1907年，45岁的华顿与42岁的莫顿·富勒顿相识。富勒顿是一位美国记者，也是个声名远扬的情场高手，他雌雄莫辨，最引人注目的是，他让伊迪丝·华顿和亨利·詹姆斯都体验到了人生中的第一次性经历。他的魅力之一在于能够暗示乱伦，而乱伦正是华顿和亨利·詹姆斯内心深处压抑而强大的性心理因素。华顿幼年时曾与父亲，或许还有哥哥有过乱伦关系。有人推测，亨利·詹姆斯同性恋倾向的根源可能在于他早年对哥哥——哲学家兼心理学家威廉·詹姆斯——的爱慕。显而易见的是，富勒顿解放了亨利·詹姆斯，使他得以发展出许多后来的同性恋关系，并给予了伊迪丝·沃顿在她与爱德华·沃顿无性的婚姻中未能获得的感官上的满足。

It is a sinuous and disturbing novel, with a complex relation to Wharton’s erotic life. She met Morton Fullerton in 1907, when she was forty-five and he was forty-two. Fullerton, an American journalist, was a fabled seducer, androgynous, whose major distinction was that he gave both Edith Wharton and Henry James their first full sexual experience. Part of his charm was an ability to insinuate incest, a repressed and powerful element in the psychosexuality of both Wharton and Henry James. Wharton when very young had an incestuous relationship to her father and perhaps to her brother. Some have speculated that the basis for Henry James’s homoeroticism might be found in his early love for his brother, the philosopher and psychologist William James. What is clear is that Fullerton liberated Henry James into many subsequent homosexual relationships, and gave to Edith Wharton the sensual culmination she had not found in her sexless marriage to Edward Wharton.

在她与富勒顿恋情最热烈的1909年创作的充满惠特曼风格的情色诗作《终点》（Terminus）中，沃顿展现了她诗歌中其他作品所无法比拟的力量。她和亨利·詹姆斯都对沃尔特·惠特曼抱有极大的敬意，两人都准确地认为惠特曼是美国最伟大的诗人。沃顿曾动情地描述过，在一个夜晚，在她位于坦格伍德附近的庄园“芒特”（Mount），亨利·詹姆斯低声吟诵着惠特曼的诗句。她回忆说，我们都“如痴如醉”，詹姆斯“沉浸在一种内敛的狂喜之中”。真希望当时能有录音。

In her highly Whitmanian erotic poem “Terminus,” written in 1909, at the apex of her affair with Fullerton, Wharton achieves a power unmatched elsewhere in her verse. She and Henry James shared an ecstatic appreciation of Walt Whitman. Both accurately regarded him as the greatest of American poets. There is a moving description by Wharton of Henry James crooning Whitman aloud on an evening at the Mount, her estate near Tanglewood. She remarked that we all “sat rapt” as James chanted on “in a mood of subdued ecstasy.” One could wish for a recording of that.

对沃顿而言，沃尔特·惠特曼既是诗人，也是先知，是激情生活的伟大解放者，正如他对D·H·劳伦斯、哈特·克莱恩、洛尔卡、路易斯·塞尔努达、佩索阿、奥克塔维奥·帕斯、聂鲁达、博尔赫斯以及其他众多作家一样。将沃尔特·惠特曼——一位不拘一格的美国人——与沃顿和詹姆斯这两位文学巨匠并置，别有一番奇特的魅力。惠特曼和梭罗相聚甚欢，这位美国吟游诗人还留下了他拜访拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生的记录，其中最后一次拜访时，诗人特意调整了椅子的位置，以便能静静地欣赏这位已步入暮年的先知慈祥和蔼的面容。

For Wharton, Walt Whitman was as much a prophet as a poet, and a great liberator of the passional life, as he was for D. H. Lawrence, Hart Crane, Lorca, Luis Cernuda, Pessoa, Octavio Paz, Neruda, Borges and so many more. There is a weird charm in juxtaposing Walt Whitman, one of the roughs, an American, and the literary mandarins Wharton and James. Whitman and Thoreau met to their mutual delight, and the American Bard left us accounts of his visits to Ralph Waldo Emerson, including a final one during which the poet stationed his chair so that he could look on the benignly amiable countenance of the Seer in his senility.

《礁石》是一部情节错综复杂、跌宕起伏的小说，展现了沃顿驾驭对话的高超技巧，以及她在情感描写方面近乎智慧的洞察力。亨利·詹姆斯对这部作品的喜爱程度远胜于她的其他作品，也就不难理解了。尽管沃顿对詹姆斯晚期的作品褒贬不一，但《金碗》（1904）的影响却贯穿了整部《礁石》。

The Reef is an intricate, surging narrative that shows Wharton to be a master of dialogue and something close to a wisdom writer in matters of the heart. It is not surprising that Henry James preferred it to all her other work. Though Wharton professed mixed reactions to the Master’s late phase, the influence of The Golden Bowl (1904) pervades The Reef.

《礁石》的核心人物是安娜·利斯，一位年近四十的美国寡妇，与她二十三岁的继子欧文·利斯和九岁的女儿艾菲住在法国乡村庄园吉夫雷。她已故的丈夫弗雷泽·利斯是一位富有的业余爱好者，他致力于收集古董鼻烟盒，或许也热衷于风流韵事。

The central consciousness of The Reef is that of Anna Leath, an American woman in her late thirties, widowed and living in Givré, a rural estate in France, with her twenty-three-year-old stepson, Owen Leath, and her nine-year-old daughter, Effie. Fraser Leath, her late husband, was a wealthy dilettante who devoted himself to collecting antique snuffboxes and possibly to the usual philandering.

另外两个重要人物分别是驻伦敦的美国外交官乔治·达罗（可能比安娜小一两岁）和一位命运多舛、略显不幸的美国年轻女子索菲·维纳，她梦想在巴黎成为一名演员。达罗和索菲在巴黎有过一段短暂的恋情；这段恋情对达罗来说无关紧要，但索菲却始终无法释怀。机缘巧合之下，索菲成了艾菲的住家家庭教师，欧文·利斯爱上了她。

The two other consequential characters are George Darrow, an American diplomat stationed in London, who may be a year or two younger than Anna, and Sophy Viner, a poignant and rather luckless American young woman, who hopes to become an actress in Paris. Darrow and Sophy have a brief affair in Paris; it meant little enough to him, but Sophy never gets beyond it. Circumstances make Sophy a live-in tutor for Effie, and Owen Leath falls in love with her.

乔治·达罗是这部小说中最具美感的谜团。他固然令人钦佩，但略显肤浅，不过他对安娜真挚的爱——这份爱可以追溯到她婚前——却始终如一。伊迪丝·华顿着重刻画了安娜对其他人的复杂感受，包括她的继子索菲·维纳，尤其是她深爱却又心存疑虑的达罗。索菲与达罗短暂的婚外情曝光后，如同暗礁一般，几乎彻底摧毁了她期盼已久的第二次婚姻。

George Darrow is the aesthetic enigma of the novel. He is admirable enough but a touch shallow, though his authentic love for Anna, which goes back to before her marriage, is enduring. Edith Wharton invests herself in Anna’s perplexed awareness of other people, including her stepson, Sophy Viner, and most of all Darrow, whom she loves but distrusts. The revelation of the brief affair of Sophy and Darrow becomes the reef that virtually wrecks her possibility of long-delayed fulfillment in a second marriage.

沃顿对安娜内心世界的跌宕起伏刻画得淋漓尽致，令人叹为观止。人们不禁会想，安娜在多大程度上是这位小说家的化身。上天赐予伊迪丝·纽博尔德·琼斯一切天赋——如魔力般的冲动、过人的智慧、丰富的想象力——唯独缺少美貌。她称沃尔特·范·伦斯勒·贝里为“我一生的挚爱”，但这位国际律师兼外交官只给了她友谊，正如他对待亨利·詹姆斯和马塞尔·普鲁斯特一样。自童年之后，她唯一的爱人似乎只有富勒顿。

It is extraordinary how Wharton is able to play out the vicissitudes of Anna’s heart. One wonders to what extent Anna is a surrogate for the novelist. The gods gave Edith Newbold Jones every gift—daemonic drive, intellect, imaginative capaciousness—except beauty. She called Walter Van Rensselaer Berry “the love of my life,” but that international lawyer and diplomat gave her only friendship, as he did to Henry James and Marcel Proust. Her only lover, after her childhood, seems to have been Fullerton.

沃顿主要创作阶段的所有女性主人公都美艳动人。人们会想起《欢乐之家》中的莉莉·巴特，她命运多舛，时运不济，最终在二十九岁时服毒自杀。她被旧纽约的社交圈所束缚，又囊中羞涩，迫切需要嫁入豪门，获得显赫的社会地位。尽管她魅力四射、心地善良、令人向往，却始终未婚，还背负着沉重的债务，其中一些是因为在桥牌游戏中输得太多。她的真爱是一位名叫劳伦斯·塞尔登的年轻律师，他在旧纽约游刃有余，却囊中羞涩。莉莉和塞尔登的爱情最终以塞尔登在她临终前为她哀悼而告终。

All of the women protagonists in Wharton’s major phase are beautiful. One thinks of Lily Bart in The House of Mirth, whose ill luck and bad timing compel her, at twenty-nine, to kill herself by an overdose of chloral. Imprisoned by the social world of Old New York, and with inadequate means, she desperately needs a marriage into money and good social standing. Despite her charm, goodness, and desirability, she remains unmarried with many debts, some by losing large sums at bridge games. Her true love is a young lawyer, Lawrence Selden, who moves easily through Old New York but lacks money. The only culmination of the love between Lily and Selden is when he grieves for her over her deathbed.

我非常欣赏珍妮特·马尔科姆，无论作为作家还是作为一个人，但她对沃顿的评价却让我困惑：“她的作品弥漫着深深的悲观主义和同样根深蒂固的厌女症。”悲观主义的确深不可测，但为什么要把沃顿称为厌女者呢？《乡俗》中那个性欲旺盛、吞噬丈夫的女主角昂丁·斯普拉格，恰恰印证了马尔科姆的观点，然而昂丁本身却是一个空洞的恶魔，在沃顿笔下独树一帜。反英雄昂丁展现了沃顿作为戏仿作家的野蛮天才，她或许是纳撒尼尔·韦斯特和托马斯·品钦的先驱。

I am a fierce admirer of Janet Malcolm, as writer and as person, but it puzzles me when she says of Wharton, “Her books are pervaded by a deep pessimism and an equally profound misogyny.” The pessimism is an abyss, but why term Wharton a misogynist? Undine Spragg, sexual magnet and devourer of husbands, the monstrous protagonist of The Custom of the Country, vindicates Malcolm, yet Undine is a vacuous fiend unique in Wharton. The anti-heroine Undine manifests Wharton’s savage genius as a parodist, unlikely ancestor of Nathanael West and Thomas Pynchon.

在《纯真年代》中，艾伦·奥伦斯卡和梅·韦兰各有千秋，都令人钦佩，尽管她们都无法与纽兰·阿彻相提并论。阿彻的形象，如同《礁石》中的乔治·达罗一样，或许是以沃尔特·贝瑞为原型塑造的。然而，马尔科姆一如既往地洞察到了沃顿意识深处某种至关重要却又阴暗的东西。伊迪丝·琼斯·沃顿渴望被男人爱慕，至多也只希望得到足够杰出的女性的尊重。称沃顿为势利眼是荒谬的，完全没有必要；她完全符合萨克雷《势利眼大全》中的不止一种类型。她明显受到了萨克雷的影响：昂丁·斯普拉格戏仿了《名利场》中才华横溢的贝基·夏普，尽管这种戏仿反而让我越来越怀念贝基·夏普。

In The Age of Innocence, Ellen Olenska and May Welland are in their different ways admirable, even if neither is truly a match for Newland Archer, who, like George Darrow in The Reef, may be modeled on Walter Berry. And yet Malcolm, as always, is on to something vital and dark in the recesses of Wharton’s consciousness. Edith Jones Wharton wants to be loved by men and at most respected by women of sufficient eminence. It is absurdly unnecessary to term Wharton a snob; she would fit more than one category of Thackeray’s Book of Snobs. She has overt debts to Thackeray: Undine Spragg parodies the marvelous Becky Sharp of Vanity Fair, though the effect on me makes me miss Becky Sharp more and more.

沃顿作品中充斥着令人厌烦的反犹主义。然而，她并非美国小说史上唯一犯下这种错误的人：薇拉·凯瑟、F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德、欧内斯特·海明威，以及犹太裔反犹主义者纳撒尼尔·韦斯特，都是其中的佼佼者。凯瑟的一位女同性恋情人被一位犹太小提琴家夺走，她在其作品中不断进行报复。而对于沃顿来说，这仅仅是老纽约的遗风。

Wharton’s tedious anti-Semitism is everywhere in her work. Still, she is hardly unique in that blot on the American novel: Willa Cather, F. Scott Fitzgerald, Ernest Hemingway, and the Jewish anti-Semite Nathanael West are among many other offenders. Cather had lost one of her lesbian lovers to a Jewish violinist and revenged herself throughout her writings. With Wharton, it is merely the heritage of Old New York.

伊迪丝·华顿和亨利·詹姆斯之间的友谊长久而深厚，却也因文学上的焦虑而令人烦恼。华顿厌倦了被称作“女版亨利·詹姆斯”，而比她年长近二十岁的詹姆斯，有时却被她旺盛的精力吓得精疲力竭，甚至一度称她为自己的“毁灭天使”。华顿总是精力充沛，远非自然之力所能及。比较他们各自的鬼故事，可以看出詹姆斯在自然与超自然的交界处笔触柔和，而华顿即使在强调沉默时，也依然狂野而充满魔性。多年来，她每年都会在万圣节之夜守夜，缅怀逝去的挚爱，沉思自己的孤独。她最后创作的故事完成于1937年2月——在她75岁去世前六个月——主人公是萨拉·克莱伯恩，一位富有的老妇人，除了众多仆人之外，她独自生活。十月下旬一个寒冷的夜晚，萨拉·克莱伯恩遇到一个陌生的女人朝她家走来，说想见见她家的一个女孩。萨拉扭伤了脚踝，卧床不起，仆人留下了些食物在她身边。第二天早上醒来，她发现家里空无一人，只好一瘸一拐地四处走动，照顾自己。一年后，这一切再次发生，那个陌生的女人再次出现，萨拉终于明白了发生了什么。这是否是孤独的老妇人伊迪丝·华顿对死亡的恐惧的寓言，我们不得而知，但这个故事的叙述手法堪称精妙绝伦。

The friendship between Edith Wharton and Henry James was prolonged, deeply felt, yet vexing because of literary anxieties. Wharton was weary of being termed a female Henry James, while James, almost twenty years older than Wharton, was at times terrified and exhausted by her energy, to the point where he once referred to her as his “Angel of Devastation.” Wharton, always in overdrive, was rather more than a natural force. A comparison between their ghostly tales demonstrates that James is gentle at the borders between natural and preternatural, whereas Wharton is wild and daemonic even when she emphasizes silence. For many years she kept an annual vigil on All Souls’ Night, recalling her beloved dead and musing on her loneliness. The last story she wrote, concluded in February 1937—six months before her death at the age of seventy-five—has as its protagonist Sara Clayburn, a wealthy old lady living alone except for a houseful of servants. On a chilly late-October evening, she meets an unknown woman walking toward her house who says she wishes to see one of the girls. Sara Clayburn injures her ankle and takes to her bed, with food left nearby by a servant. In the morning, she wakes to find the house deserted and has to limp around to take care of herself. One year later, all this is repeated, with the strange woman reappearing, and Sara understands what is happening. Whether this is a parable of the lonely old Edith Wharton fearing death is unclear, yet the story is brilliantly narrated.

将沃顿的《礁石》与詹姆斯的《金碗》相提并论是不公平的。每次重读《金碗》，我的想法都会改变——或者更确切地说，是詹姆斯改变了我的想法。我对玛吉·弗弗和夏洛特·斯坦特的看法也时而变化，时而动摇。玛吉的耐心和婚姻之爱逐渐消磨了夏洛特对亚美利哥王子的执着热情。亚当·弗弗，一个只有女儿玛吉的鳏夫，听从了女儿的精明建议，向夏洛特求婚，夏洛特也接受了。然而，父女之间的联盟过于牢固，以至于夏洛特和亚美利哥重燃旧情。亨利·詹姆斯通过玛吉和夏洛特之间紧张的协议，解开了这两个难题，让亚当带着他的艺术收藏，以及夏洛特——他最重要的收获——回到了美国。

It would be unfair to contrast Wharton’s The Reef with James’s The Golden Bowl. Every time I go back to The Golden Bowl, I change my mind—or, rather, James changes it. My view both of Maggie Verver and of Charlotte Stant ebbs and flows. Maggie’s patience and marital love wear down Charlotte’s relentless passion for Prince Amerigo. Adam Verver, widower with only the single child, Maggie, yields to his daughter’s shrewd suggestion that he propose marriage to Charlotte, who accepts him. The daughter-father alliance abides too strenuously, so that Charlotte and Amerigo resume their affair. Henry James severs both knots by a tense accord between Maggie and Charlotte that sends Adam, his art collection, and Charlotte, his major acquisition, back to the United States.

伊迪丝·华顿曾说她觉得《金碗》 “难以卒读”。不过，或许她从中汲取了足够的养分，从而创作出了《礁石》，这部作品始终笼罩在詹姆斯笔下那段如梦似幻的婚姻故事的阴影之下。亨利·詹姆斯在给华顿的一封信中，既赞扬了这部小说及其作者，又含蓄地承认了自己的受其影响：

Edith Wharton stated that she found The Golden Bowl “unreadable.” Perhaps, though, she absorbed enough of it to help engender The Reef, which floats under the shadow of James’s daedal dance of marriages. Henry James, in a letter to Wharton, implicitly recognizes his parentage while complimenting the novel and its author:

《礁石》的品质以及两位主角之间难以言喻的纠葛给我留下了如此深刻的印象……以至于即使我嘴唇翕动，也忍不住要跟你细说几句……这两个人物都因其真实和公正而令人钦佩；那位女士美艳绝伦，她那细腻而又几乎难以区分的音符……以一种令人惊叹的微妙方式呈现。我不确定她的情感波动是否超出了我们的理解范围；然而，它们却被你如此精准地捕捉、感受、认知和展现，一切似乎都自然而然地发生。我略感遗憾或担忧的是，在序幕中，我们仿佛被带入了男主角的意识深处，而安娜（安娜这个名字真是恰如其分）出场后，我们几乎只能通过她的视角来看待他——这让我们不得不以不同的方式去关注他；然而，我认为这实际上是你方法的胜利，因为他始终保持着绝对一致的真实性，或许比其他任何方式都更能展现自我，而且他展现自我的方式没有任何虚假之处，一丝一毫都没有。它的美妙之处在于，就其本身而言，它是一部戏剧，而且在我看来，几乎达到了拉辛式的心理统一性、强度和优雅。安娜确实是拉辛式的……这就是为什么整件事，除了最肤浅的方式与它的环境和背景，以及任何决定性的或限定性的随行人员无关之外，没有任何关联，就以这种方式，以一种特定的、地域性的方式，发生在法国——这些非法国人仿佛“选择”将他们的故事公之于众……你拉辛式的灵感……绝对指定了一个模糊而优雅的法式柱廊或长廊，一条法国河流隐隐闪烁，作为你所要求的和谐背景。在这关键之处，你以你全部的真实，保留了一切：而且，为了加深和谐，凸显文学的韵味，你从未在某些精妙的瞬间、某些意象、类比、隐喻、某些银铃般的对应关系上超越自己……你身上曾经有一些细微的音符，如同乔治·艾略特那美好的善意指纹——那是她大量阅读这位杰出女性作品的回响，时隐时现。但如今，你就像一位失而复得的“古人”，她或许能从中读懂一些（尤其如果他是希腊人），而你的文风中也隐隐透露出一些微弱的反思。因为，亲爱的伊迪丝，你比他们所有人加起来都更强大、更坚定、更精妙；你走得更远，你说得更好。你唯一的缺点就是没有属于你自己的国家（比如我！ ）那种家的温馨、必然性、幸福的局限和富足的贫穷。这让你，正如你曾在某个时刻精辟地形容某人或某事时那样，变得哀婉动人（你对这个词的运用多么深刻、多么巧妙！）——也就是说，对于严肃的拉西尼主义者而言，的确如此——但这也让你（对于其他一切而言）更加孱弱于环绕着顶点城的沙漠之中。

（《亨利·詹姆斯书信集》，第二卷，珀西·卢博克编[1920]）

There remains with me so strongly the impression of [The Reef’s] quality and of the unspeakably fouillée nature of the situation between the two principals…that I can’t but babble of it a little to you even with these weak lips….Each of these two figures is admirable for truth and justesse; the woman an exquisite thing, and with her characteristic finest, scarce differentiated notes…sounded with a wonder of delicacy. I’m not sure her oscillations are not beyond our notation; yet they are so held in your hand, so felt and known and shown, and everything seems so to come of itself. I suffer or worry a little from the fact that in the Prologue, as it were, we are admitted so much into the consciousness of the man, and that after the introduction of Anna (Anna so perfectly named) we see him almost only as she sees him—which gives our attention a different sort of work to do; yet this is really, I think, but a triumph of your method, for he remains of an absolute consistent verity, showing himself in that way better perhaps than in any other, and without a false note imputable, not a shadow of one, to his manner of so projecting himself. The beauty of it is that it is, for all it is worth, a Drama, and almost, as it seems to me, of the psychologic Racinian unity, intensity and gracility. Anna is really of Racine…which is why the whole thing, unrelated and unreferred save in the most superficial way to its milieu and background, and to any determining or qualifying entourage, takes place comme cela, and in a specified, localised way, in France—these non-French people “electing,” as it were, to have their story out there….Your Racinian inspiration…absolutely prescribed a vague and elegant French colonnade or gallery, with a French river dimly gleaming through, as the harmonious fond you required. In the key of this, with all your reality, you have yet kept the whole thing: and, to deepen the harmony and accentuate the literary pitch, have never surpassed yourself for certain exquisite moments, certain images, analogies, metaphors, certain silver correspondences in your façon de dire….There used to be little notes in you that were like fine benevolent finger-marks of the good George Eliot—the echo of much reading of that excellent woman, here and there, that is, sounding through. But now you are like a lost and recovered “ancient” whom she might have got a reading of (especially were he a Greek) and of whom in her texture some weaker reflection were to show. For, dearest Edith, you are stronger and firmer and finer than all of them put together; you go further and you say mieux, and your only drawback is not having the homeliness and the inevitability and the happy limitation and the affluent poverty, of a Country of your Own (comme moi, par exemple!) It makes you, this does, as you exquisitely say of somebody or something at some moment, elegiac (what penetration, what delicacy in your use there of the term!)—makes you so, that is, for the Racinian-sérieux—but leaves you more in the desert (for everything else) that surrounds Apex City

(The Letters of Henry James, Vol. II, ed. Percy Lubbock [1920])

阿佩克斯城是昂迪娜·斯普拉格、她的父母以及她的第一任和最后一任丈夫埃尔默·莫法特的故乡，埃尔默·莫法特既是堪萨斯州的骄傲，也是华尔街的骄傲。我认为亨利·詹姆斯是《礁石》一书吸引到的最有价值的评论家。他敏锐地指出安娜的内心摇摆不定：“我不确定她的这种摇摆是否超出了我们的理解范围。”这正是安娜摇摆不定的意识的核心所在，它既将她吸引到乔治·达罗身边，又将她推离他。詹姆斯也帮助我们理解了沃顿笔下达罗的转变：从最初描绘他与索菲·维纳的婚外情，到“我们几乎只能通过安娜的视角来看待他——这让我们不得不以不同的方式去关注他；然而，我认为这实际上是你写作手法的胜利。”从某种意义上说，安娜对达罗的内化使我们失去了达罗的真实面貌，但詹姆斯再次准确地评价这是“你写作手法的胜利”。

Apex City is the origin of Undine Spragg, her parents, and of her both first and final spouse, Elmer Moffatt, pride both of Kansas and of Wall Street. I suggest that Henry James here is the most useful critic that The Reef has attracted. He acutely notes of Anna, “I’m not sure her oscillations are not beyond our notation.” That is the center of Anna’s vacillating consciousness, at once drawing her to George Darrow and spinning her away from him. James also helps us to appreciate Wharton’s movement from her initial depiction of Darrow in his affair with Sophy Viner to: “we see him almost only as she sees him—which gives our attention a different sort of work to do; yet this is really, I think, but a triumph of your method.” In a sense, we lose Darrow’s verity to Anna’s internalization of him, yet James is again accurate in judging this “a triumph of your method.”

尽管乔治·艾略特和詹姆斯本人都有先例，但这种方法实际上是沃顿新近发明的，这引出了一个微妙而令人信服的例子，即先驱者的回归，就像他们是我曾经称之为“亡灵节”（apophrades）的后代一样，在那个日子里，他们回到了他们以前的住所：

That the method, despite antecedents in George Eliot and in James himself, indeed is newly born in Wharton prompts a subtle and persuasive instance of that return of the precursors as if they were descendants that I once termed apophrades, the Athenian unlucky day of the dead, in which they returned to inhabit their former houses:

你身上曾经有一些细微的痕迹，像是乔治·艾略特那温柔而美好的指纹——那是她反复研读这位杰出女性作品的回响，时隐时现。但如今你却像是一位失而复得的“古人”，她或许能从中读懂些什么（尤其如果他是希腊人的话），而你身上也隐隐透露出一些对古人的反思。

There used to be little notes in you that were like fine benevolent finger-marks of the good George Eliot—the echo of much reading of that excellent woman, here and there, that is, sounding through. But now you are like a lost and recovered “ancient” whom she might have got a reading of (especially were he a Greek) and of whom in her texture some weaker reflection were to show.

在这句令人愉悦的赞誉中，沃顿仿佛孕育了（如果用“孕育”这个词恰当的话）乔治·艾略特和亨利·詹姆斯。然而，从审美角度来看，乔治·艾略特的道德光辉和亨利·詹姆斯的鲜活含蓄远胜沃顿的任何作品。如果将沃顿的所有小说汇集在一起​​，你会感受到比任何一部单作都更为深刻的印象。或许是因为我迟迟才读到《礁石》，才让我如此动容，尽管它比《欢乐之家》或《纯真年代》更让我回味无穷。我无法完全理解安娜对乔治·达罗的爱和求婚的无休止的犹豫、拒绝，以及最终欣然接受。这其中必定包含着比她对达罗和索菲·维纳短暂恋情的震惊，以及随后爆发的性嫉妒更深层次的原因。索菲和达罗都向她坦白了一切，对索菲来说，这的确是爱情；而对达罗来说，这既是出于善意，也是出于自我放纵。

In this charming compliment, Wharton has mothered (if that is the right word) George Eliot and Henry James. Aesthetic judgment, however, must admit that the moral splendor of George Eliot and the vibrant indirectness of Henry James far surpass anything in Wharton. If you mass all of Wharton’s fictions together, you get a larger impression than any single work provides. I may be moved by my own belatedness in coming upon The Reef, though it lingers in my speculations more even than The House of Mirth or The Age of Innocence. I cannot fully grasp Anna’s interminable hesitations, rejections, joyous reacceptances of George Darrow’s love and desire to marry her. Something more has to be involved than her conventional shock at the brief affair between Darrow and Sophy Viner, and her subsequent flarings of sexual jealousy. Both Sophy and Darrow have told her the full truth, that for Sophy it was indeed love, and for Darrow a mixed act of kindness and self-indulgence.

我无法妄称自己能完全理解安娜。她既是真正的瑰宝，又是一座迷宫。她是否像沃顿在叙事小说中允许的那样，是一幅接近自画像的形象？沃尔特·贝里对沃顿的爱恋含蓄内敛，他的阴影也笼罩着达罗，正如它笼罩着纽兰·阿彻和劳伦斯·塞尔登一样。

I cannot pretend to puzzle Anna out. She is somehow both true gold and a labyrinth. Is she as close to a self-portrait as Wharton would permit herself in a narrative fiction? The shadow of Walter Berry, whose love for Wharton declined sexual expression, falls over Darrow as it does over Newland Archer and Lawrence Selden.

在伊迪丝·华顿的作品中发现女权主义者，未免有些荒谬。然而，鲜有其他小说家能像她那样，如此淋漓尽致地展现父权制长期以来对女性性满足的双重标准。达罗从未想过，如果安娜在丈夫去世后有了外遇，他会作何反应。毫无疑问，他会逃之夭夭。安娜虽然也曾动摇，但最终没有选择离开。经过一番痛苦的挣扎，她似乎接受了嫁给乔治·达罗，但华顿并没有给出确切的答案。在《礁石》那诡异的结尾，安娜去找去了印度的索菲，却意外地遇到了索菲衣着邋遢的妹妹劳拉，劳拉的丈夫和情人络绎不绝。安娜震惊之余，离开了，大概是回到了达罗身边，准备迎接即将到来的婚姻。

It would be grotesque to find a feminist in Edith Wharton. And yet few other novelists so dramatize the double standard that patriarchy so long maintained against the sexual fulfillment of women. It does not occur to Darrow to think how he would react if Anna had gone through an affair after the death of her husband. Doubtless he would flee. Anna, though tempted, does not take flight. After much agony, she seems to accept marrying George Darrow, but Wharton gives us no certainty. In the weird final scene of The Reef, Anna goes in search of Sophy, who has departed for India, and finds instead the blowsy sister of Sophy, Laura, who has a steady succession of husbands and lovers. In some shock, Anna departs, presumably to go back to Darrow and her impending marriage.

在这段令人沮丧的插曲之后，我们很难预料接下来会发生什么。或许，身心俱疲的安娜会安于达罗，过上更好的生活。然而，疑云重重。沃顿拒绝告诉我们未来会怎样；或许她自己也不知道。这是沃顿笔下他们之间的最后一次对话：

It is unclear, after this depressing episode, what we are to assume will happen. Most likely, the emotionally exhausted Anna will be content with Darrow and live a better life. Yet there are too many shadows. Wharton declines to tell us what lies beyond; perhaps she does not know. This is the last exchange between them that Wharton gives us:

“安娜——安娜！”

“是的，我现在就想知道：想知道一切。也许那样我就能忘记。我早该让你告诉我。无论我们去哪里，我都觉得你和她在一起……我总觉得你们在一起。我想知道这一切是怎么开始的，你去了哪里，你为什么离开她……我再也无法忍受这种黑暗了！”

她不知道是什么引发了她如此激动的情绪爆发，但她已经感到轻松了许多，自由了许多，仿佛邪恶的魔咒终于被打破了。“我想知道一切，”她重复道，“这是唯一能让我忘记一切的方法。”

她停止说话后，达罗仍然站在原地，双臂抱在胸前，目光低垂，一动不动。她静静地等待着，目光始终停留在他的脸上。

你难道不打算告诉我吗？

“不。”

她顿时感到太阳穴发烫。“你不愿意？为什么不愿意？”

“如果我真的那样做了，你觉得你会忘记吗？”

“哦——”她呻吟了一声，转身背对他。

“你看，这不可能，”他继续说道，“我做了一件我厌恶的事，而你为了弥补，却要我再做一件。这能给你带来什么满足感？这只会让我们之间产生无法弥合的隔阂。”

她将手肘倚在壁炉架上，双手捂住脸。她感觉自己正在徒劳地抛弃最后一丝幸福的希望，却无能为力，什么也想不到，无法挽回。一个念头在她脑海中闪过：“如果我放弃他，我能获得平静吗？”她想起送走他之后那些日子的孤独寂寞，明白那希望终究是徒劳的。泪水涌上眼眶，缓缓地从指缝间滑落。

“再见，”她听到他说，然后他的脚步声转向了门口。

她试图抬起头，但绝望的重压让她无法动弹。她对自己说：“一切都结束了……他不会再来求我了……”她僵硬地站在那里，仿佛被催眠了一般，感知着命运般流逝的秒数，却感受不到。突然，束缚她的绳索仿佛断裂，她抬起头，看到他离去的背影。

“他是我的——他是我的！他谁也别想占！”他转过脸来看着她，眼神中流露出的神情驱散了她所有的恐惧。她不再明白自己刚才那声毫无防备的惊呼究竟是为何；而爱上他的那种人间甜蜜，再次成为这世间唯一真实的存在。

“Anna—Anna!”

“Yes; I want to know now: to know everything. Perhaps that will make me forget. I ought to have made you tell me before. Wherever we go, I imagine you’ve been there with her…I see you together. I want to know how it began, where you went, why you left her…I can’t go on in this darkness any longer!”

She did not know what had prompted her passionate outburst, but already she felt lighter, freer, as if at last the evil spell were broken. “I want to know everything,” she repeated. “It’s the only way to make me forget.”

After she had ceased speaking Darrow remained where he was, his arms folded, his eyes lowered, immovable. She waited, her gaze on his face.

“Aren’t you going to tell me?”

“No.”

The blood rushed to her temples. “You won’t? Why not?”

“If I did, do you suppose you’d forget that?”

“Oh—” she moaned, and turned away from him.

“You see it’s impossible,” he went on. “I’ve done a thing I loathe, and to atone for it you ask me to do another. What sort of satisfaction would that give you? It would put something irremediable between us.”

She leaned her elbow against the mantel-shelf and hid her face in her hands. She had the sense that she was vainly throwing away her last hope of happiness, yet she could do nothing, think of nothing, to save it. The conjecture flashed through her: “Should I be at peace if I gave him up?” and she remembered the desolation of the days after she had sent him away, and understood that that hope was vain. The tears welled through her lids and ran slowly down between her fingers.

“Good-bye,” she heard him say, and his footsteps turned to the door.

She tried to raise her head, but the weight of her despair bowed it down. She said to herself: “This is the end…he won’t try to appeal to me again…” and she remained in a sort of tranced rigidity, perceiving without feeling the fateful lapse of the seconds. Then the cords that bound her seemed to snap, and she lifted her head and saw him going.

“Why, he’s mine—he’s mine! He’s no one else’s!” His face was turned to her and the look in his eyes swept away all her terrors. She no longer understood what had prompted her senseless outcry; and the mortal sweetness of loving him became again the one real fact in the world.

这本小说笔力如此精湛，理应成为经典之作。然而，安娜的意识却像一个漩涡，恐惧终将重现。亨利·詹姆斯说得没错：安娜身上确实有几分拉辛笔下费德尔的影子。莉莉·巴特的命运太过悲惨，以至于称不上悲剧。安娜却始终摆脱不了悲剧的阴影。或许，这正是沃顿迈向伟大之作的门槛。

This is so powerfully wrought that it ought to be definitive. And yet the consciousness of Anna is a vortex. Terrors of the mind will return. Henry James was accurate: there is something of Racine’s Phèdre in Anna. Lily Bart’s fate was too pathetic to be tragic. Anna cannot shed a tragic aura. That may have been the threshold Wharton crossed into a touch of greatness.

第33章

CHAPTER 33

《虹》（1915）

The Rainbow (1915)

D · H ·劳伦斯​

D. H. LAWRENCE

大卫· H·埃伯特·劳伦斯因肺结核去世，享年四十四岁。他创作力惊人：十二部长篇小说，十几卷短篇小说集，以及大量诗集，其风格日臻成熟，从受托马斯·哈代的影响逐渐转向受沃尔特·惠特曼的影响。但这仅仅是劳伦斯创作才华的冰山一角。他是一位敏锐的文学评论家，一位生动传神的游记作家，一位辩论家（尽管他对弗洛伊德的理解大错特错），一位剧作家，一位笔耕不辍的书信作家，一位画家。七十多年来，我阅读他的作品，最令我珍视的是他的两部长篇小说：《虹》和《恋爱中的女人》（他原本打算将后者写成一部名为《姐妹》的长篇史诗）。同样重要的还有他的短篇小说（其中许多是中篇小说）和诗歌。如今，到了2018年，劳伦斯不再被尊为先知或精神导师。我年轻的时候，我这一代的很多男女都是劳伦斯主义者，但随着更激烈的女权主义的出现，这种风潮就消失了。

DAVID HERBERT LAWRENCE died of tuberculosis at the age of forty-four. He was amazingly prolific: a dozen novels, another dozen volumes of shorter fiction, many volumes of increasingly strong poetry that moved from the influence of Thomas Hardy to that of Walt Whitman. But that only begins to catalogue Lawrence’s fecundity. He was an incisive literary critic, an intensely vivid travel writer, a polemicist who argued against Freud while getting Freud quite wrong, a dramatist, an incessant letter writer, and a painter. After reading him for more than seventy years, I value him most for two great novels: The Rainbow and Women in Love, which he had intended to be one long saga to be called The Sisters. Of equal importance are his shorter fictions, many of them novellas, and his poetry. Now, in 2018, Lawrence is no longer esteemed as a prophet or a spiritual guide. When I was young, many women and men of my generation were Lawrentians, but that vogue expired when fiercer feminisms arrived.

劳伦斯援引了一位活生生的上帝：

Lawrence invoked a living God:

那么我必须知道这一点仍然

我已交托于未知的上帝之手。

他正在把我逼入绝境，直至他自己彻底毁灭。

让我以全新的面貌迎接新的一天，成为一个全新的人。

then I must know that still

I am in the hands of the unknown God,

he is breaking me down to his own oblivion

to send me forth on a new morning, a new man.

在赫尔曼·梅尔维尔、詹姆斯·乔伊斯、威廉·福克纳等人的作品中，优美的散文达到了崇高诗歌般的境界，但在劳伦斯的小说《虹》（1915）中达到了顶峰。在第一章中，《钦定版圣经》的韵律影响了劳伦斯对布朗温一家的描绘：

Heightened prose takes on the intensity of sublime poetry in Herman Melville, James Joyce, William Faulkner, and others, but achieves an apex in Lawrence’s novel The Rainbow (1915). In its first chapter, the rhythms of the King James Bible inform Lawrence’s vision of the Brangwens:

对男人们来说，大地翻腾，为他们开垦田地，微风吹拂，晒干湿漉漉的麦穗，让嫩嫩的玉米穗随风摇曳，这就足够了；他们帮母牛分娩，或从谷仓底下捉老鼠，或一巴掌拍断兔子的脊背，这就足够了。他们的血液里充满了温暖、繁衍、痛苦和死亡，与大地、天空、野兽和绿色植物有着如此多的交流与互动，以至于他们活得充实而饱满，感官得到充分的滋养，他们的脸庞总是迎着血液的热度，凝视着太阳，被生命的源泉所深深吸引，无法回头。

It was enough for the men, that the earth heaved and opened its furrow to them, that the wind blew to dry the wet wheat, and set the young ears of corn wheeling freshly round about; it was enough that they helped the cow in labour, or ferreted the rats from under the barn, or broke the back of a rabbit with a sharp knock of the hand. So much warmth and generating and pain and death did they know in their blood, earth and sky and beast and green plants, so much exchange and interchange they had with these, that they lived full and surcharged, their senses full fed, their faces always turned to the heat of the blood, staring into the sun, dazed with looking towards the source of generation, unable to turn round.

这些节奏在《彩虹》的最后一段中再次出现，乌苏拉在那里看到了幻象：

These cadences return in the final paragraph of The Rainbow, where Ursula has a vision:

彩虹屹立于大地之上。她知道，那些卑劣的人们，那些在世界腐败的表象下苟延残喘、形同陌路的人们，依然活着；彩虹由他们的鲜血铸成，将在他们的灵魂中颤动复苏；他们将褪去腐朽的角质外衣；崭新、洁净、赤裸的躯体将孕育新生，焕发新的生命，沐浴在光明、清风和天赐的甘霖之中。她从彩虹中看到了大地的新架构，旧日脆弱的房屋和工厂被扫除殆尽，世界在真理的鲜活织锦中重建，与浩瀚无垠的苍穹相得益彰。

And the rainbow stood on the earth. She knew that the sordid people who crept hard-scaled and separate on the face of the world’s corruption were living still, that the rainbow was arched in their blood and would quiver to life in their spirit, that they would cast off their horny covering of disintegration, that new, clean, naked bodies would issue to a new germination, to a new growth, rising to the light and the wind and the clean rain of heaven. She saw in the rainbow the earth’s new architecture, the old, brittle corruption of houses and factories swept away, the world built up in a living fabric of Truth, fitting to the over-arching heaven.

这种高度浪漫主义源于劳伦斯的非国教传统。《虹》之后，他的长篇小说数量锐减，这与他诗歌和各种长度的短篇小说数量不相上下。即使是《恋爱中的女人》（1920）也失去了《虹》中那种毫不妥协的激情。乌苏拉·布兰温在两部作品中都叫这个名字，但性格却截然不同。第一部中的乌苏拉更加热情奔放，更加坚定地追求完全属于自己的人生，并在各个方面寻求和实现自我价值。在一段炽热的女同性恋情之后，她与来自波兰的远房表兄安东·斯克雷本斯基——一位英国士兵——展开了一段波澜起伏的恋情。

This kind of High Romanticism stems from Lawrence’s Nonconformist heritage. After The Rainbow, his novels dwindle, unlike his poems and shorter fictions of all lengths. Even Women in Love (1920) falls away from the remorseless drive of The Rainbow. Ursula Brangwen bears the same name in both books yet scarcely is the same woman. The first Ursula is even more passionate and more determined to live a life altogether her own and to seek and find fulfillment in every sense. After an intense lesbian relationship, she undergoes a turbulent relationship with Anton Skrebensky, a remote cousin from Poland who has become an English soldier.

共进晚餐后，乌苏拉带着她的情人走向海边：

After dining together, Ursula leads her lover down to the sea:

她站在水边，站在波光粼粼的大海边缘，海浪拍打着她的脚。

“我想走，”她用坚定而有力的声音喊道，“我想走。”

他看到月光照在她脸上，她就像金属一样；他听到她那叮当作响、金属般的声音，在他听来就像是女妖的声音。

She stood on the edge of the water, at the edge of the solid, flashing body of the sea, and the wave rushed over her feet.

“I want to go,” she cried, in a strong, dominant voice. “I want to go.”

He saw the moonlight on her face, so she was like metal, he heard her ringing, metallic voice, like the voice of a harpy to him.

在古代神话中，哈耳庇厄是一种长着女人头的猛禽，这很难准确地描述热情似火的乌苏拉，但却揭示了斯克雷本斯基对自己能力不足的感受：

In ancient mythology a harpy is a predatory bird with the head of a woman, scarcely an accurate description of the passionate Ursula, but a revelation of Skrebensky’s sense of his own inadequacy:

她徘徊在水边，像个着了魔的怪物，他跟在她身后。他看到浪花翻滚，接着是坚硬明亮的海水拍打着她的脚踝，她伸出双臂保持平衡，他时刻都担心她会穿着这身衣服走进海里，然后被海水卷走。

但她转过身，走向了他。

“我想走，”她再次喊道，声音又高又尖，像海鸥的叫声。

“在哪儿？”他问。

“我不知道。”

She prowled, ranging on the edge of the water like a possessed creature, and he followed her. He saw the froth of the wave followed by the hard, bright water swirl over her feet and her ankles, she swung out her arms, to balance, he expected every moment to see her walk into the sea, dressed as she was, and be carried swimming out.

But she turned, she walked to him.

“I want to go,” she cried again, in the high, hard voice, like the scream of gulls.

“Where?” he asked.

“I don’t know.”

读者或许还记得， 《虹》的倒数第二章名为“狂喜的苦涩”。奇怪的是，这个乌苏拉与《恋爱中的女人》中的妹妹古德伦非常相似，却与后来的乌苏拉截然不同。她们都渴望打破一切束缚，却都无法在性交中找到自己渴望的化身：

The reader recalls that this next-to-the-last chapter of The Rainbow is called “The Bitterness of Ecstasy.” Strangely, this Ursula is very close to the younger sister, Gudrun, of Women in Love, and very different from that later Ursula. Each longs to break all bounds and fails to find in sexual intercourse her image for longing:

她抓住他的胳膊，紧紧地搂着他，就像抓住了俘虏一样，带着他沿着波光粼粼、令人眼花缭乱的水边走了一小段路。

就在那耀眼的光芒中，她猛地一把抓住他，力道之大，仿佛突然间拥有了毁灭的力量。她双臂紧紧环抱着他，将他牢牢搂在怀里，同时她的唇寻找着他的，一个猛烈、撕裂般、愈发浓烈的吻，直到他彻底无力招架，他的心在她那凶猛、尖嘴、妖女般的吻中恐惧得融化。海水再次冲刷着他们的脚，但她毫不在意。她似乎浑然不觉，仿佛要用她那尖嘴狠狠地咬住他的心。最后，她终于松开了他，看着他——看着他。他明白了她的意图。他牵起她的手，领着她穿过滩涂，回到沙丘上。她默默地走着。他感到自己即将面临生死考验。他领着她来到一个幽暗的洼地。

“不，就在这儿，”她说着，走到月光洒满的山坡上。她一动不动地躺着，睁大眼睛望着月亮。他径直走向她，没有丝毫铺垫。她紧紧地搂住他的胸口，那感觉令人胆寒。这场搏斗，这场为了达到目的的挣扎，是如此可怕。它持续了很久，直到他的灵魂都承受着巨大的痛苦，直到他彻底屈服，直到他像死了一样瘫倒在地，脸埋在沙子里，一半埋在她的头发里，一半埋在她的沙子里，一动不动，仿佛他将永远这样一动不动，被埋葬在黑暗中，被埋葬，他只想被埋葬在那美好的黑暗里，仅此而已，别无其他。

他仿佛昏厥过去，过了很久才回过神来。他感觉到她胸前一阵异样的起伏，便抬起头。月光下，她的脸庞像一幅画，双眼圆睁，目光僵硬。但就在这时，一滴泪珠缓缓从她的眼中滑落，在月光下闪闪发光，顺着脸颊滑落。

他感觉仿佛一把刀正插进他早已死去的身体里。他仰着头，绷紧神经，凝视着那张月光下如同金属般僵硬、纹丝不动的脸，凝视着那双空洞无神的眼睛，眼中缓缓涌起水珠，在闪烁的月光下颤动，然后盈满，溢出，缓缓流淌，如同承载着月光的泪珠，渗入黑暗，滴落在沙滩上。

他仿佛害怕般渐渐后退，后退——她一动不动。他瞥了她一眼——她依旧躺着。他能挣脱吗？他转过身，看到眼前开阔的沙滩，于是他纵身跃起，越走越远，离那可怕的身影越来越远。她躺在月光下的沙滩上，泪水在她静止的脸上汇聚，缓缓流淌。

他觉得，如果还要再见到她，就必须断骨断身，身躯粉碎，彻底消亡。而此刻，他至少还拥有自己鲜活身体的爱。他漫无目的地游荡了很久很久，直到大脑一片漆黑，疲惫不堪，昏睡过去。然后，他蜷缩在能找到的最深的黑暗中，在海草丛下，就这样毫无知觉地躺着。

她渐渐从剧烈的痉挛中挣脱出来，尽管每一次动作都伴随着剧烈的疼痛。她慢慢地将自己冰冷的尸体从沙滩上抬起，最终站了起来。现在，月亮对她来说已经消失了，大海也消失了。一切都已逝去。她拖着冰冷的尸体回到房子，回到自己的房间，然后一动不动地躺了下来。

And she seized hold of his arm, held him fast, as if captive, and walked him a little way by the edge of the dazzling, dazing water.

Then there in the great flare of light, she clinched hold of him, hard, as if suddenly she had the strength of destruction, she fastened her arms round him and tightened him in her grip, whilst her mouth sought his in a hard, rending, ever-increasing kiss, till his body was powerless in her grip, his heart melted in fear from the fierce, beaked, harpy’s kiss. The water washed again over their feet, but she took no notice. She seemed unaware, she seemed to be pressing in her beaked mouth till she had the heart of him. Then, at last, she drew away and looked at him—looked at him. He knew what she wanted. He took her by the hand and led her across the foreshore, back to the sandhills. She went silently. He felt as if the ordeal of proof was upon him, for life or death. He led her to a dark hollow.

“No, here,” she said, going out to the slope full under the moonshine. She lay motionless, with wide-open eyes looking at the moon. He came direct to her, without preliminaries. She held him pinned down at the chest, awful. The fight, the struggle for consummation was terrible. It lasted till it was agony to his soul, till he succumbed, till he gave way as if dead, lay with his face buried, partly in her hair, partly in the sand, motionless, as if he would be motionless now for ever, hidden away in the dark, buried, only buried, he only wanted to be buried in the goodly darkness, only that, and no more.

He seemed to swoon. It was a long time before he came to himself. He was aware of an unusual motion of her breast. He looked up. Her face lay like an image in the moonlight, the eyes wide open, rigid. But out of the eyes, slowly, there rolled a tear, that glittered in the moonlight as it ran down her cheek.

He felt as if as the knife were being pushed into his already dead body. With head strained back, he watched, drawn tense, for some minutes, watched the unaltering, rigid face like metal in the moonlight, the fixed, unseeing eye, in which slowly the water gathered, shook with glittering moonlight, then surcharged, brimmed over and ran trickling, a tear with its burden of moonlight, into the darkness, to fall in the sand.

He drew gradually away as if afraid, drew away—she did not move. He glanced at her—she lay the same. Could he break away? He turned, saw the open foreshore, clear in front of him, and he plunged away, on and on, ever farther from the horrible figure that lay stretched in the moonlight on the sands with the tears gathering and travelling on the motionless, eternal face.

He felt, if ever he must see her again, his bones must be broken, his body crushed, obliterated for ever. And as yet, he had the love of his own living body. He wandered on a long, long way, till his brain drew dark and he was unconscious with weariness. Then he curled in the deepest darkness he could find, under the sea-grass, and lay there without consciousness.

She broke from her tense cramp of agony gradually, though each movement was a goad of heavy pain. Gradually, she lifted her dead body from the sands, and rose at last. There was now no moon for her, no sea. All had passed away. She trailed her dead body to the house, to her room, where she lay down inert.

年轻的时候，我可以全神贯注地读这本书，而不会感到痛苦。如今我已年过八旬（正如我已故的朋友厄休拉·勒古恩教我称呼的那样），读这本书却感到无比痛苦，但其美学价值却无比卓越。劳伦斯预言了所谓的“头脑中的性欲”。威廉·布莱克或许会称之为“在比尤拉之夜虚幻的形体中，从腰间发出的理性”。作为劳伦斯的终身仰慕者，我更倾向于布莱克的说法。然而，《虹》却永远地揭示了莎士比亚、弥尔顿和托尔斯泰早已洞悉的真理：女性在性方面优于男性。亚当是上帝用红土塑造的最初形象。夏娃，从人类中被挖掘出来，却更加完美。

When I was much younger, I could read this intently without suffering it. In my High Eighties (as my late friend Ursula Le Guin taught me to call it), I find it exquisitely painful but aesthetically superb. Lawrence prophesied against what he called “sex in the head.” William Blake might have called this “Reasoning from the loins in the unreal forms of Beulah’s night.” A lifelong admirer of Lawrence, I go with Blake. And yet The Rainbow permanently illuminates what Shakespeare and Milton and Tolstoy understood too well: women are sexually superior to men. Adam was God’s initial molding out of the red clay. Eve, quarried out of the human, was better made.

第34章

CHAPTER 34

恋爱中的女人（1920）

Women in Love (1920)

D · H ·劳伦斯​

D. H. LAWRENCE

多年后重读《 恋爱中的女人》，我发现它与我记忆中的截然不同。几十年前，我对这本书了如指掌，甚至能预知许多段落和章节的内容，但那时我对劳伦斯的理解还停留在一种不确定的层面。如今，这本书显得更加奇特、丰富，也更具原创性。书中对意志的矛盾和存在的种种模式的刻画，笔触之犀利令人惊叹，因为如此复杂深刻的情感表达，在小说中可谓前所未有。

REREADING Women in Love after many years, I discover it to be strangely distant from what I had recalled. Several decades ago, I knew the book so fully that I anticipated many paragraphs, even chapters, but in those days I had a kind of provisional belief in Lawrence. The book now appears stranger and richer, more original than I had recalled. Ambivalences of the will, modes of being are represented by a sharpness that seems uncanny, since the power to suggest so many complex apprehensions could be judged without precedent in the novel.

劳伦斯在其创作巅峰时期令人惊叹，几乎展现了那些无法展现之物。《虹》和《恋爱中的女人》是他的杰作，其水准堪比他的许多诗歌和短篇小说。在男女之间永无休止的战争中，劳伦斯同时站在双方一边。他尤其擅长描绘恋人之间充满杀戮的争吵，例如在《恋爱中的女人》第二十三章“插曲”中，乌苏拉和伯金在劳伦斯所谓的“这片难忘的战场”上发生了一场激烈的冲突。

Lawrence on his heights astonishes, almost showing what cannot be shown. The Rainbow and Women in Love are his triumphs, equaled only by a number of his poems and by many of his short stories. In the endless war between men and women, Lawrence fights on both sides. He is superb at giving us really murderous lovers’ quarrels, as in Chapter 23, “Excurse,” of Women in Love, where Ursula and Birkin suffer one of their encounters upon what Lawrence calls “this memorable battlefield”:

“我嫉妒！我——嫉妒！你要是这么想就大错特错了。我一点也不嫉妒赫敏，她对我来说什么都不是，绝对不是！ ”乌苏拉打了个响指。“不，撒谎的是你。你必须像狗吃自己的呕吐物一样，回到过去。我恨的是赫敏所代表的一切。我恨透了它。那是谎言，那是虚假，那是死亡。但你想要它，你无法自拔，你无法控制自己。你属于那种陈旧、死亡的生活方式——那就回去吧。但别来找我，因为这与我无关。”

在强烈的情绪刺激下，她下了车，走到树篱边，无意识地摘了一些肉粉色的卫矛莓，其中一些已经裂开，露出了橙色的种子。

“啊，你真是个傻瓜！”他带着几分轻蔑，愤愤地喊道。

“没错，我就是。我真是个傻瓜。谢天谢地。我傻到根本上不了你的聪明才智。感谢上帝。你去找你的女人吧——去找她们吧——她们才是你这种类型——你身边总是跟着一群女人——以后也永远都会有。去找你的灵性新娘吧——但别再来找我了，因为我可不想要，谢谢。你还不满足，是吗？你的灵性新娘给不了你想要的，她们不够俗艳，不够肉欲，是吗？所以你来找我，把她们都当备胎！你会娶我，把我当成日常用品。但你还是会继续在背后找灵性新娘。我知道你那肮脏的小伎俩。”突然，她怒火中烧，疯狂地跺着脚，他吓得缩了一下，生怕她踢自己。“而且，我，我灵性不够，我没赫敏那么灵性——！”她眉头紧锁，双眼怒火中烧，如同老虎一般。“那就去找她，我就说一句，去找她，去找她。哈，她有灵性——灵性？她！她不过是个肮脏的唯物主义者。有灵性？她关心什么？她的灵性是什么？那是什么？”她的怒火仿佛灼烧着他的脸庞，他不由得缩了缩身子。 “我告诉你，那全是污秽，污秽，全是污秽。而你想要的正是这种污秽，你渴望它。灵性！她那霸凌、自负、肮脏的物质主义，也叫灵性？她是个卖鱼的，一个卖鱼的，她就是个彻头彻尾的物质主义者。一切都那么肮脏。到头来，她那所谓的社交热情又能给她带来什么？社交热情——她有什么社交热情？——给我看看！——在哪儿？她想要的是琐碎的、即时的权力，她想要的是自己是个伟大女人的幻觉，仅此而已。在她灵魂深处，她是个邪恶的无神论者，像污秽一样卑贱。这就是她最底层的样子。其他的一切都是伪装——但你却喜欢它。你喜欢这种虚假的灵性，它是你的精神食粮。为什么？因为底下的污秽。你以为我不知道你——还有她——的性生活有多么肮脏吗？——我知道。正是这种肮脏……”想要？你这个骗子。那就给你，给你。你真是个骗子。

她转过身去，断断续续地从篱笆上扯下卫矛的枝条，用颤抖的手指将它们固定在外套的胸前。

他默默地站在那里看着。看到她颤抖的、如此敏感的手指，他心中燃起一股奇妙的温柔；与此同时，他也充满了愤怒和冷酷。

“I jealous! I—jealous! You are mistaken if you think that. I’m not jealous in the least of Hermione, she is nothing to me, not that!” And Ursula snapped her fingers. “No, it’s you who are a liar. It’s you who must return, like a dog to his vomit. It is what Hermione stands for that I hate. I hate it. It is lies, it is false, it is death. But you want it, you can’t help it, you can’t help yourself. You belong to that old, deathly way of living—then go back to it. But don’t come to me, for I’ve nothing to do with it.”

And in the stress of her violent emotion, she got down from the car and went to the hedgerow, picking unconsciously some flesh-pink spindleberries, some of which were burst, showing their orange seeds.

“Ah, you are a fool,” he cried bitterly, with some contempt.

“Yes, I am. I am a fool. And thank God for it. I’m too big a fool to swallow your cleverness. God be praised. You go to your women—go to them—they are your sort—you’ve always had a string of them trailing after you—and you always will. Go to your spiritual brides—but don’t come to me as well, because I’m not having any, thank you. You’re not satisfied, are you? Your spiritual brides can’t give you what you want, they aren’t common and fleshy enough for you, aren’t they? So you come to me, and keep them in the background! You will marry me for daily use. But you’ll keep yourself well provided with spiritual brides in the background. I know your dirty little game.” Suddenly a flame ran over her, and she stamped her foot madly on the road, and he winced, afraid that she would strike him. “And, I, I’m not spiritual enough, I’m not as spiritual as that Hermione—!” Her brows knitted, her eyes blazed like a tiger’s. “Then go to her, that’s all I say, go to her, go. Ha, she spiritual—spiritual, she! A dirty materialist as she is. She spiritual? What does she care for, what is her spirituality? What is it?” Her fury seemed to blaze out and burn his face. He shrank a little. “I tell you it’s dirt, dirt, and nothing but dirt. And it’s dirt you want, you crave for it. Spiritual! Is that spiritual, her bullying, her conceit, her sordid materialism? She’s a fishwife, a fishwife, she is such a materialist. And all so sordid. What does she work out to, in the end, with all her social passion, as you call it. Social passion—what social passion has she?—show it me!—where is it? She wants petty, immediate power, she wants the illusion that she is a great woman, that is all. In her soul she’s a devilish unbeliever, common as dirt. That’s what she is at the bottom. And all the rest is pretence—but you love it. You love the sham spirituality, it’s your food. And why? Because of the dirt underneath. Do you think I don’t know the foulness of your sex life—and hers?—I do. And it’s that foulness you want, you liar. Then have it, have it. You’re such a liar.”

She turned away, spasmodically tearing the twigs of spindleberry from the hedge, and fastening them, with vibrating fingers, in the bosom of her coat.

He stood watching in silence. A wonderful tenderness burned in him at the sight of her quivering, so sensitive fingers: and at the same time he was full of rage and callousness.

这段战斗场景在乌苏拉无意识地采摘肉质饱满、果实破裂、种子外露的卫矛莓，以及她转身撕扯卫矛莓枝条并将其别在外套上的动作之间切换。伯金将这些卫矛莓解读为弗洛伊德所说的自身肉体自我的裸露肉体，在此遭受着如同酒神女祭司般的乌苏拉的鞭笞。仿佛伯金本人也被她的语言鞭笞，变成了一个游离于精神与肉体之间的边缘存在。伯金既感到排斥，又同时被某种神秘的吸引力所吸引，最终屈服于她的凶猛——与其说是嫉妒，不如说是女性对伯金劳伦斯式的、男性化的性爱理想化的抗议。乌苏拉最深切地反对的是，这种理想化既有缺陷又充满矛盾，因为它建立在一种错位的基督教新教之上，这种新教既渴望完全的结合，又无法容忍个体性的泯灭。伯金-劳伦斯身上带有新教上帝的印记，他总是暗暗地向乌苏拉宣告：“要像我一样，但千万别太像我！”这番告诫令她恼火不已。劳伦斯既是伯金又是乌苏拉，因此，作为一名小说家，他有一个奇特的特质：他总是让自己感到恼火。

This passage-at-arms moves between Ursula’s unconscious picking of the fleshly, burst spindleberries, open to their seeds, and her turning away, tearing the spindleberry twigs so as to fasten them in her coat. Birkin reads the spindleberries as the exposed flesh of what Freud called one’s own bodily ego, suffering here a sparagmos by a maenadlike Ursula. It is as though Birkin himself, lashed by her language, becomes a frontier being, caught between psyche and body. Repelled yet simultaneously drawn by a sort of orphic wonder, Birkin yields to her ferocity that is not so much jealousy as it is the woman’s protest against Birkin’s Lawrentian and male idealization of sexual love. What Ursula most deeply rejects is that the idealization is both flawed and ambivalent, because it is founded upon a displaced Protestantism that both craves total union and cannot abide such annihilation of individuality. Birkin-Lawrence has in him the taint of the Protestant God, and implicitly is always announcing to Ursula, “Be like me, but do not dare to be too like me!,” an injunction that infuriates her. As Lawrence is both Birkin and Ursula, he has the curious trait, for a novelist, of perpetually infuriating himself.

《恋爱中的女人》的核心难点在于劳伦斯内心清教徒式的意志与从雪莱、布莱克、托马斯·哈代和沃尔特·惠特曼那里汲取的浪漫主义情怀之间的冲突。这种自我分裂导致劳伦斯对西格蒙德·弗洛伊德的理解完全错误，以至于这位诗人先知断言，精神分析学的创始人想要消除一切禁忌。也就是说，他想把弗洛伊德变成萨德侯爵。

The central difficulty of Women in Love is Lawrence’s split between a Puritan will and a High Romantic sensibility quarried from Shelley, Blake, Thomas Hardy, and Walt Whitman. Division in the self compelled Lawrence to misunderstand totally Sigmund Freud, to the point where the poet-prophet asserted that the founder of psychoanalysis wished to cancel all inhibitions. That is to turn Freud into the Marquis de Sade.

《恋爱中的女人》中有五个关键人物：鲁珀特·伯金，显然是D·H·劳伦斯的化身；乌苏拉·布兰温，某种程度上是弗里达·冯·里希特霍芬的化身，她与劳伦斯私奔到欧洲大陆，当时她仍与劳伦斯的前任老师欧内斯特·威克利保持婚姻关系，留下了三个孩子；悲剧人物、与乌苏拉格格不入的实业家杰拉尔德·克里奇，一个愤世嫉俗的人；以及迷人的古德伦·布兰温，乌苏拉的妹妹。古德伦是一位雕塑家，一位美丽的虚无主义者，她只想了解他人，一旦了解了对方，便会失去兴趣。劳伦斯以新西兰短篇小说作家凯瑟琳·曼斯菲尔德为原型塑造了她，曼斯菲尔德于1923年因肺结核去世，年仅34岁。曼斯菲尔德曾与文学评论家约翰·米德尔顿·默里结婚、分居、离婚，之后又再婚，最终再次分居，而劳伦斯笔下的杰拉尔德·克里奇正是默里的化身。穆里曾一度是劳伦斯的门徒，但他背叛了劳伦斯，不仅与弗里达有染，还写了一本相当恶毒的书：《女人之子：D·H·劳伦斯的故事》（1931）。书中，劳伦斯被描绘成一个压抑的同性恋者，一个性欲过剩、总是过早射精的人，只能通过与弗里达的肛交来获得释放。这一切或许并非空穴来风，但穆里笔下的劳伦斯有时却令人反感。除了扮演杰拉尔德·克里奇之外，他还在奥尔德斯·赫胥黎的《针锋相对》（1928）中扮演了滑稽可笑的伯拉普一角。此外，还有赫敏·罗迪斯，伯金抛弃的情妇，是对奥托琳·莫雷尔夫人的辛辣讽刺。莫雷尔夫人是一位古怪而富有的贵妇，她资助作家和艺术家。她的丈夫是一名律师，他威胁要起诉劳伦斯，为了让他满意，做出了一些修改。

There are five crucial persons in Women in Love: Rupert Birkin, who clearly is D. H. Lawrence; Ursula Brangwen, a kind of vision of Frieda von Richthofen, who eloped to the Continent with Lawrence while she was still married to his former teacher, Ernest Weekley, leaving behind their three children. There are the tragic, hopelessly ill-matched Gerald Crich, industrialist and malcontent, and the fascinating Gudrun Brangwen, younger sister of Ursula. Gudrun is a sculptor, a beautiful nihilist who wishes only to know others, and loses interest once they are known. Lawrence modeled her on the New Zealand short-story writer Katherine Mansfield, who died of tuberculosis at the age of thirty-four in 1923. Mansfield was married, separated and divorced from, remarried, and separated again from the literary critic John Middleton Murry, whom Lawrence portrayed as Gerald Crich. For a time, Murry was Lawrence’s disciple, but betrayed him both by having an affair with Frieda and by writing a rather nasty book: Son of Woman: The Story of D. H. Lawrence (1931), in which Lawrence is exhibited as a repressed homosexual, a person so sexually overexcited that he always arrived too soon, as it were, and found release only by anal intercourse with Frieda. All this may well have been true, but Murry’s tonality is sometimes offensive. Aside from his appearance as Gerald Crich, there is a delightful travesty of him as one Burlap in Aldous Huxley’s Point Counter Point (1928). That leaves only Hermione Roddice, Birkin’s cast-off mistress, a fierce parody of Lady Ottoline Morrell, an eccentric and wealthy noblewoman who patronized writers and artists. Her husband, a lawyer, threatened to sue Lawrence, and a few changes were made to satisfy him.

或许，即使只是匆匆一瞥劳伦斯笔下的人物原型，也会产生误导。肯·罗素执导的精彩影片《恋爱中的女人》（1969）与原著小说惊人地契合，部分原因在于五位关键演员的精湛演技，尤其是格伦达·杰克逊饰演的古德伦。艾伦·贝茨饰演伯金/劳伦斯，他有时仿佛就是劳伦斯本人。奥利弗·里德阴郁深沉，将杰拉尔德·克里奇演绎得令人胆寒；珍妮·林登饰演的伯金与贝茨的形象相得益彰，既是爱人又是对手。埃莉诺·布朗饰演的赫敏也同样令人印象深刻，她始终游走在歇斯底里和愤怒的边缘。

It may be that even a brief glance at Lawrence’s models is misleading. Ken Russell’s wonderful film Women in Love (1969) is remarkably true to the novel, partly because the five crucial actors perform superbly, Glenda Jackson as Gudrun in particular. Birkin/Lawrence is played by Alan Bates, who at moments seems to be Lawrence. Oliver Reed, dark and saturnine, is threatening as Gerald Crich, while Jennie Linden is a fit lover/antagonist for Bates as Birkin. Not least in any sense is Eleanor Bron as Hermione, always on the verge of hysteria and fury.

当我筋疲力尽地翻阅《恋爱中的女人》时，我首先看到的是古德伦和杰拉尔德之间那场斯特林堡式的、以爱之死为主题的斗争。劳伦斯显然读过斯特林堡的作品，尽管他试图摆脱这种影响，但最终还是失败了。

When I turn over Women in Love in my exhausted moments after the endless exercise I have to perform to keep going in life, I see first the Strindbergian battle to the love-death between Gudrun and Gerald. Lawrence certainly had read Strindberg and could not ward off the influence, though he attempted to do so:

但我不想像高尔斯华绥、易卜生、斯特林堡或他们中的任何一位那样写作，即使我能做到。我们必须憎恨我们的前辈，才能摆脱他们的束缚。

（1913年致爱德华·加内特的信）

But I don’t want to write like Galsworthy nor Ibsen, nor Strindberg nor any of them, not even if I could. We have to hate our immediate predecessors, to get free from their authority.

(1913 letter to Edward Garnett)

斯特林堡于1900年创作了两部名为《死亡之舞》的戏剧。如果导演和演员演绎得当，它们对婚姻的可怕反抗至今仍令人震惊。斯特林堡娶了三位妻子；他显而易见的厌女症肆无忌惮，令人难以忍受。劳伦斯无论其缺点如何，都继承了男性小说家对女性充满爱意和深刻刻画的传统：从塞缪尔·理查森到詹姆斯·乔伊斯，莫不如此。

Strindberg wrote two plays called The Dance of Death, both in 1900. Properly directed and performed, they still shock with their dreadful recoil from marriage. Three wives endured Strindberg; his palpable misogyny was hectic and unchecked. Lawrence, whatever his flaws, is in the tradition of male novelists who lovingly and profoundly portrayed women: from Samuel Richardson to James Joyce.

乌苏拉和伯金的感情历经波折，最终走向真挚的结合。两个坚强的灵魂彼此明白，谁也不应凌驾于对方之上。细心的读者会为这段善意结合的爱情而欣喜，尽管他们各自都有局限。乌苏拉渴望一个欲望实现的乐园，而伯金虽然对自己充满怀疑（尽管他对乌苏拉充满信心），但他深知所有的乐园终将逝去。

The relationship between Ursula and Birkin, after many vicissitudes, culminates in an authentic marriage between two strong souls who recognize that neither must subsume the other. Joy, in the alert reader, celebrates this union between benign wills, each with its own limitations. Ursula wants a kind of paradise of achieved desire, while Birkin distrusts himself, though not her, and knows that all paradises are lost.

劳伦斯试图在杰拉尔德和古德伦痛苦挣扎中，平衡这种务实整体性的和谐与不和谐以及日益加剧的危险——最终令人麻木的、无法调和的冲突。小说以斯特林堡式的死亡之舞结尾，杰拉尔德漫步到冰天雪地的荒野，在那里冻死了自己。值得注意的是，这与其说是自杀，不如说是古德伦谋杀了她的爱人。

Lawrence attempts to balance the harmonics of this pragmatic wholeness against the discord and mounting danger of the frenetic and finally numbing clash of irreconcilables in the agon of Gerald and Gudrun. When the novel concludes in a Strindbergian dance of death, Gerald wanders off into a landscape of snow and ice and welcomes his death there by freezing.
