Since Joyce works toward a three-in-one of Shakespeare, Leopold Bloom, and James Joyce, he, too, would achieve aesthetic perfection on this account:

男人不能让他高兴，女人也不能，斯蒂芬说。他离开人世多年后，回到了他出生的那片土地，他一直都在那里，从男人到男孩，默默地见证着一切。在那里，他的人生旅程结束了，他种下了他的桑树。然后，他死了。一切结束了。掘墓人埋葬了老哈姆雷特和小哈姆雷特。一位国王和一位王子最终在死亡中离世，伴随着背景音乐。尽管他被谋杀和背叛，所有脆弱而温柔的心都为他哭泣，无论是丹麦人还是都柏林人，为死者哀悼的，是他唯一一个他们拒绝离婚的丈夫。如果你喜欢尾声，请仔细阅读：繁荣的普洛斯彼罗，好人得到了回报；莉齐，爷爷的掌上明珠；还有里奇叔叔，坏人被诗意的正义带走，去了恶人该去的地方。厚重的帷幕落下。他在外部世界里找到了与他内心世界尽可能相似的现实。梅特林克说：如果苏格拉底今天出门，他会发现智者正坐在他家门口。如果犹大今晚出门，他的脚步将指向犹大。每个人的一生都是由无数个日子组成的，日复一日。我们行走于自身之中，遇见强盗、幽灵、巨人、老人、年轻人、妻子、寡妇、情同手足的人，但始终遇见的是我们自己。那位写下这世界剧本却写得拙劣的剧作家（他先赐予我们光明，两天后又赐予我们太阳），那位万物之主，被最罗马化的天主教徒称为“迪奥·博亚”（dio boia），刽子手之神，无疑在我们所有人之中包罗万象，既是马夫又是屠夫，如果不是在哈姆雷特预言的天堂法则中不再有婚姻，他也会是老鸨和戴绿帽者，这位荣耀之人，一位雌雄同体的天使，他自己就是自己的妻子。

Man delights him not nor woman neither, Stephen said. He returns after a life of absence to that spot of earth where he was born, where he has always been, man and boy, a silent witness and there, his journey of life ended, he plants his mulberrytree in the earth. Then dies. The motion is ended. Gravediggers bury Hamlet père and Hamlet fils. A king and a prince at last in death, with incidental music. And, what though murdered and betrayed, bewept by all frail tender hearts for, Dane or Dubliner, sorrow for the dead is the only husband from whom they refuse to be divorced. If you like the epilogue look long on it: prosperous Prospero, the good man rewarded, Lizzie, grandpa’s lump of love, and nuncle Richie, the bad man taken off by poetic justice to the place where the bad niggers go. Strong curtain. He found in the world without as actual what was in his world within as possible. Maeterlinck says: If Socrates leave his house today he will find the sage seated on his doorstep. If Judas go forth tonight it is to Judas his steps will tend. Every life is many days, day after day. We walk through ourselves, meeting robbers, ghosts, giants, old men, young men, wives, widows, brothers-in-love, but always meeting ourselves. The playwright who wrote the folio of this world and wrote it badly (He gave us light first and the sun two days later), the lord of things as they are whom the most Roman of catholics call dio boia, hangman god, is doubtless all in all in all of us, ostler and butcher, and would be bawd and cuckold too but that in the economy of heaven, foretold by Hamlet, there are no more marriages, glorified man, an androgynous angel, being a wife unto himself.

暂且不论这段文字语言的华丽（我们对乔伊斯的文风并不陌生），我被其中蕴含的所谓“高雅美学神智学”深深震撼。如同赫尔墨斯主义的神圣之人、布莱克的阿尔比恩或卡巴拉的亚当·卡德蒙，哈姆雷特的梦境颂扬了人性。从约翰·弥尔顿到厄休拉·勒奎恩，关于雌雄同体的天使的描述不胜枚举，但乔伊斯赋予了它一种全新的圣经韵律：“成为自己的妻子”。

Setting aside the splendor of this language (from Joyce we expect it), I am overwhelmed by what could be called the High Aesthetic Theosophy of the passage. Like the Hermetic divine man or Blake’s Albion or Kabbalah’s Adam Kadmon, Hamlet’s dream glorifies man. There are many accounts of androgynous angels, from John Milton to Ursula K. Le Guin, yet Joyce gives us a new Biblical cadence: “being a wife unto himself.”

《哈姆雷特王子》就像一个漩涡，将一切都卷了进去。我挣脱出来，终于从斯蒂芬和莎士比亚转向了利奥波德·布鲁姆和莎士比亚。这与其说是斯蒂芬的作品，不如说是波尔迪的作品。布鲁姆先生唯一能与之匹敌的，是都柏林这座城市本身，它充满活力，喧嚣嘈杂，市民争论不休，古老的阴影挥之不去。当我离开《尤利西斯》太久时，我很容易觉得波尔迪比他的作品更加宏大，就像《亨利四世》中的福斯塔夫无法被完全容纳一样。再次沉浸于《尤利西斯》之中，便能消除这种错觉。乔伊斯这部史诗的每一页、每一句话、每一个词组都超越了既定的尺度。

Prince Hamlet is a vortex that draws everything in. I tear myself away and finally move from Stephen and Shakespeare to Leopold Bloom and Shakespeare. It is much more Poldy’s book than it is Stephen’s. Mr. Bloom’s only rival is Dublin itself, alive with sound, a contentious citizenry, and ancient shadows. When I’ve been away from Ulysses for too long, I am liable to believe that Poldy is larger than his book, as Falstaff is not to be contained by the Henry IV plays. Immersing myself again in Ulysses dispels that illusion. Every page, every sentence, every phrase of Joyce’s epic overflows the measure.

然而，波尔迪（我不得不沿用这个名字，因为我不过是个逊色的布鲁姆）却始终充满活力。我再次陷入对他的犹太身份的困惑，而乔伊斯却对此深信不疑。你或许会说，根据《塔木德》，莫莉·布鲁姆比波尔迪更像犹太人，因为她有个西班牙犹太母亲。但这说不通。她身上没有任何犹太特征。她是普世的。波尔迪才是谜。因为他认同他已故的父亲，所以他认为自己是犹太人。整个都柏林都这么认为。乔伊斯就是波尔迪，波尔迪就是莎士比亚：这就是《尤利西斯》的核心论点，最终比荷马和但丁更为重要。利奥波德·布鲁姆在寻找一个儿子，而这种寻找带有弥赛亚式的意味。他找到了斯蒂芬·迪达勒斯，但斯蒂芬始终无法真正满足他的需求，因为他既酗酒，又容易产生幻觉。

And yet Poldy (I have to keep to that name, since I am a lesser Bloom) is endlessly rammed with life. I return to my bafflement as to his Jewishness, upon which Joyce insists. You could argue that, according to Talmud, Molly Bloom is more Jewish than Poldy, because she had a Spanish Jewish mother. That will not work. There is nothing Jewish about her. She is universal. Poldy is the mystery. Since he identifies with his dead father, he thinks of himself as a Jew. All Dublin considers him such. Joyce is Poldy is Shakespeare: that is the argument of Ulysses, finally more central than Homer and Dante. Leopold Bloom is in search of a son, and this quest is Messianic. He finds Stephen Dedalus, who is never quite there since he is both alcoholic and given to authentic visions.

我并非在撰写一本关于《尤利西斯》的书；我不敢自称是乔伊斯研究专家。而且，在完成本书之前，我仍然打算谈谈《守灵夜》。因此，我将直接跳到第十二章：“独眼巨人”。这一章发生在下午五点，地点是都柏林的一家酒吧。波尔迪勇敢地与一个身材魁梧、令人厌恶的都柏林市民对峙，此人没有名字，残暴无礼，言语粗鲁。乔伊斯采用了一个性格单薄的叙述者，用都柏林方言讲述了波尔迪的这场搏斗。这位市民酗酒成性，预言爱尔兰的流亡者将会返回故土，加入反抗英国统治的起义。

I am not writing a book about Ulysses; I cannot pretend to be a Joyce scholar. And I still intend to say something about the Wake before I am done. Therefore, I will leap ahead to Episode 12: the “Cyclops,” set at 5:00 p.m. in a Dublin pub where Poldy courageously confronts a gigantic, nasty Dublin citizen, who is unnamed, brutal, and abusive. Joyce uses a narrator of little personality, who tells the story of Poldy’s agon in the Dublin vernacular. The citizen drinks heavily and predicts a return to Ireland of its émigrés to join in rebellion against the English.

“——完全正确，”布鲁姆说。“但我的重点是……”

“—Perfectly true, says Bloom. But my point was…”

 

他说，迫害，纵观世界历史，到处都是迫害，它加剧了各国之间的民族仇恨。

约翰·怀斯问道：“但是你知道一个国家意味着什么吗？”

“是的，”布鲁姆说。

“那是什么？”约翰·怀斯问道。

“一个国家？”布鲁姆说，“一个国家是指居住在同一地方的同一群人。”

“天哪，”内德笑着说，“如果真是这样，那我岂不成了一个国家了？因为我在同一个地方住了五年了。”

所以，大家都嘲笑布鲁姆，而他却试图撇清关系：

——或者居住在不同的地方。

乔说：“我的情况就是这样。”

“请问，你们是哪个国家？”这位公民问道。

布鲁姆说：“爱尔兰。我出生在这里。爱尔兰。”

那名市民什么也没说，只是清了清喉咙里的唾液，然后，他竟然把一只红岸牡蛎吐到了角落里。

—Persecution, says he, all the history of the world is full of it. Perpetuating national hatred among nations.

—But do you know what a nation means? says John Wyse.

—Yes, says Bloom.

—What is it? says John Wyse.

—A nation? says Bloom. A nation is the same people living in the same place.

—By God, then, says Ned, laughing, if that’s so I’m a nation for I’m living in the same place for the past five years.

So of course everyone had the laugh at Bloom and says he, trying to muck out of it:

—Or also living in different places.

—That covers my case, says Joe.

—What is your nation if I may ask? says the citizen.

—Ireland, says Bloom. I was born here. Ireland.

The citizen said nothing only cleared the spit out of his gullet and, gob, he spat a Red bank oyster out of him right in the corner.

· · ·

“您说的是新耶路撒冷吗？”市民问道。

布鲁姆说：“我指的是不公正。”

约翰·怀斯说：“没错。那就像个男人一样，用力量反抗它。”

这就是年鉴照片的风格。一颗软头子弹正等着他。一个老胖子硬生生地站在那里，面对着枪口。他那张大嘴巴，要是穿上护士围裙，肯定能撑得住一把扫帚。然后，他突然倒下了，身体扭曲成完全相反的模样，像一块湿抹布一样软绵绵的。

但他说道，这一切都无济于事。暴力、仇恨、历史，所有这一切，都不是男人和女人该有的生活，只有侮辱和仇恨。人人都知道，真正的生活恰恰相反。

—Are you talking about the new Jerusalem? says the citizen.

—I’m talking about injustice, says Bloom.

—Right, says John Wyse. Stand up to it then with force like men.

That’s an almanac picture for you. Mark for a softnosed bullet. Old lardyface standing up to the business end of a gun. Gob, he’d adorn a sweepingbrush, so he would, if he only had a nurse’s apron on him. And then he collapses all of a sudden, twisting around all the opposite, as limp as a wet rag.

—But it’s no use, says he. Force, hatred, history, all that. That’s not life for men and women, insult and hatred. And everybody knows that it’s the very opposite of that that is really life.

詹姆斯·乔伊斯，这位伟大的艺术家，此时也陷入了困境。波尔迪为他代言，然而艺术家应该超脱尘世，效仿荷马和莎士比亚，而非但丁。当布卢姆先生回到酒馆时，独眼巨人的出现加剧了这场争论：

James Joyce, great artist as he is, nevertheless is beset at this point. Poldy speaks for him, yet the artist should be disengaged, on the model of Homer and Shakespeare rather than that of Dante. When Mr. Bloom returns to the tavern, the citizen Cyclops heightens the contest:

但天哪，我正要放下啤酒杯，就看见那市民站起来，蹒跚地走向门口，他得了水肿，气喘吁吁，嘴里用爱尔兰语咒骂着克伦威尔的诅咒、钟声、书籍和蜡烛，还不停地吐着口水。乔和小阿尔夫围在他身边，像个小妖精一样试图安抚他。

“别管我，”他说。

他跑到门口，他们抓住他，他放声大哭：

—为以色列欢呼三声！

哎呀，看在老天的份上，赶紧坐下，别在公共场合出丑。我的天，总有些傻瓜为了鸡毛蒜皮的小事大吵大闹。老兄，你这样下去，肚子里的啤酒都会变酸的，真的。

全国的流浪汉和妓女都围在门口，马丁叫马车夫往前开，市民们嚎啕大哭，阿尔夫和乔冲他喊叫，他趾高气扬地谈论犹太人，游手好闲的人要求他发表演讲，杰克·鲍尔试图让他坐在车上，捂住他流血的下巴，一个眼睛上蒙着眼罩的游手好闲的人开始唱《如果月亮上的人是犹太人，犹太人，犹太人》，一个妓女从她嘴里喊道：

—哎呀，先生！您的裤子拉链没拉好，先生！

他说：

门德尔松是犹太人，马克思、梅尔卡丹特和斯宾诺莎也是犹太人。救世主是犹太人，他的父亲也是犹太人。你们的上帝。

“他没有父亲，”马丁说。“就这样吧。继续往前开。”

“谁的神？”市民问道。

“嗯，他叔叔是犹太人，”他说。“你们的上帝是犹太人。基督和我一样，也是犹太人。”

市民戈布猛地冲回了商店。

他说：“以耶稣的名义发誓，我要打爆那个该死的犹太人的头，他竟然敢用圣名说话！”

耶稣作证，我一定要把他钉在十字架上。把那盒饼干拿来。

But begob I was just lowering the heel of the pint when I saw the citizen getting up to waddle to the door, puffing and blowing with the dropsy, and he cursing the curse of Cromwell on him, bell, book and candle in Irish, spitting and spatting out of him and Joe and little Alf round him like a leprechaun trying to peacify him.

—Let me alone, says he.

And begob he got as far as the door and they holding him and he bawls out of him:

—Three cheers for Israel!

Arrah, sit down on the parliamentary side of your arse for Christ’ sake and don’t be making a public exhibition of yourself. Jesus, there’s always some bloody clown or other kicking up a bloody murder about bloody nothing. Gob, it’d turn the porter sour in your guts, so it would.

And all the ragamuffins and sluts of the nation round the door and Martin telling the jarvey to drive ahead and the citizen bawling and Alf and Joe at him to whisht and he on his high horse about the jews and the loafers calling for a speech and Jack Power trying to get him to sit down on the car and hold his bloody jaw and a loafer with a patch over his eye starts singing If the man in the moon was a jew, jew, jew and a slut shouts out of her:

—Eh, mister! Your fly is open, mister!

And says he:

—Mendelssohn was a jew and Karl Marx and Mercadante and Spinoza. And the Saviour was a jew and his father was a jew. Your God.

—He had no father, says Martin. That’ll do now. Drive ahead.

—Whose God? says the citizen.

—Well, his uncle was a jew, says he. Your God was a jew. Christ was a jew like me.

Gob, the citizen made a plunge back into the shop.

—By Jesus, says he, I’ll brain that bloody jewman for using the holy name.

By Jesus, I’ll crucify him so I will. Give us that biscuitbox here.

乔伊斯的论述很微妙，而波尔迪的说法并不完全准确。如果他所说的门德尔松指的是作曲家费利克斯·门德尔松（很可能如此），而不是费利克斯的祖父、十八世纪犹太启蒙运动的先驱摩西·门德尔松，那么他就忘记了或者根本不知道这位作曲家在七岁受洗成为新教徒之前，并没有宗教信仰。卡尔·马克思本人是反犹主义者，但他八岁时受洗成为路德教徒。萨维里奥·梅尔卡丹特是一位意大利非犹太人，曾以其歌剧而闻名。或许波尔迪把他和贾科莫·梅耶贝尔混淆了，后者是一位犹太裔歌剧作曲家。至于伟大的巴鲁赫·斯宾诺莎，他被阿姆斯特丹的犹太社群逐出了教籍。人们普遍认为耶稣基督是犹太人，他的父亲耶和华是犹太人的上帝。布鲁姆先生提出的一个有趣的观点——即使耶稣没有父亲，他的叔叔仍然是犹太人——也颇具魅力。

Joyce is subtle and Poldy is not totally accurate. If by Mendelssohn he means the composer Felix, as probably he does, rather than Felix’s grandfather Moses Mendelssohn, the eighteenth-century pioneer of Jewish Enlightenment, then he forgets or does not know that the composer was brought up without religion until he was baptized a Protestant at the age of seven. Karl Marx, himself anti-Semitic, was baptized a Lutheran at the age of eight. Saverio Mercadante was an Italian Gentile once famous for his operas. Perhaps Poldy is confusing him with Giacomo Meyerbeer, an operatic composer who was Jewish. As for the great Baruch Spinoza, he was excommunicated by the Jewish community of Amsterdam. It is generally agreed that Jesus Christ was Jewish and that his father, Yahweh, was the God of the Jews. Mr. Bloom’s interesting notion that, if Jesus had no father, nevertheless his uncle was Jewish, has its own charm.

愤怒的市民徒劳地扔出饼干盒，因为波尔迪和律师JJ·奥莫洛伊乘车逃走了。乔伊斯像荷马或莎士比亚一样思想多元，他试图摆脱与布卢姆先生过于紧密的联系：

The furious citizen flings his biscuit tin in vain, since Poldy and the lawyer J. J. O’Molloy make their escape by motor vehicle. Joyce is as many-minded as Homer or indeed Shakespeare as he seeks to extricate himself from too close an identification with Mr. Bloom:

忽然，他们周围出现了耀眼的光芒，他们看见祂所乘坐的战车升天。他们看见祂坐在战车上，身披荣光，衣着如同太阳般明亮，如同月亮般皎洁，威严无比，以至于他们不敢直视祂。这时，天上传来一个声音呼喊：“以利亚！以利亚！”祂大声回应：“阿爸！主啊！”他们看见祂，就是布鲁姆之子以利亚，在天使云的簇拥下，以四十五度角从小绿街多诺霍家上空升起，如同利箭射出，升入荣光之中。

When, lo, there came about them all a great brightness and they beheld the chariot wherein He stood ascend to heaven. And they beheld Him in the chariot, clothed upon in the glory of the brightness, having raiment as of the sun, fair as the moon and terrible that for awe they durst not look upon Him. And there came a voice out of heaven, calling: Elijah! Elijah! And He answered with a main cry: Abba! Adonai! And they beheld Him even Him, ben Bloom Elijah, amid clouds of angels ascend to the glory of the brightness at an angle of fortyfive degrees over Donohoe’s in Little Green street like a shot off a shovel.

这段文字如同爆炸般爆发，从“明亮”过渡到颇具贝克特风格的后半句，发生了彻底的改变。我想到的是塞缪尔·贝克特那部精彩绝伦的小说《墨菲》（1938），这部小说既是对乔伊斯的致敬，也是对贝克特本人的一次预告。据我所知，这是乔伊斯唯一欣赏的贝克特作品，但后来，当贝克特明智地拒绝了乔伊斯女儿露西娅对他的爱慕之情时，两人的关系便恶化了。露西娅当时被认为患有精神疾病，尽管她的病情至今仍有争议。

This explosion of a paragraph undergoes utter change with the transition from “brightness” to the rather Beckett-like remainder of the sentence. I am thinking of the Samuel Beckett of the marvelous Murphy (1938), a novel at once an homage to Joyce and an annunciation for Beckett. As far as I know, it was the only work by Beckett that Joyce admired, but, then, their relations were soured when Beckett wisely did not encourage the passion for him of Joyce’s daughter, Lucia, who was supposed to be mentally ill, though the nature of her illness remains in dispute.

《尤利西斯》浩瀚深邃，以至于我不得不采取一种近乎极简的叙述方式，这与原著的精神相悖。我选择先跟随布鲁姆和斯蒂芬的视角，进入“瑟茜”篇章中夜城的冒险，然后再阅读由莫莉·布鲁姆讲述的“佩内洛普”篇章。这样应该能让我简要地了解守夜之夜的种种细节。

So vast and deep is Ulysses that I am constrained to a somewhat desperate economy, which is contrary to the spirit of the book. I choose to follow Bloom and Stephen into their descent into Nighttown in the “Circe” episode, and only then go on to the “Penelope” episode, spoken by Molly Bloom. That should allow me a brief entry into the night of the Wake.

我先从一段美好却又复杂的回忆说起，那是1959年秋天，我和妻子在伦敦观看了玛乔丽·巴肯廷改编、伯吉斯·梅雷迪思执导的《夜城尤利西斯》。泽罗·莫斯特尔饰演利奥波德·布卢姆，他踮着脚尖翩翩起舞，有时仿佛在空中飞翔。我本该无比欣喜，因为我曾与泽罗相识，也因此与波尔迪融为一体。然而，我当时正长着一颗阻生智齿，疼痛难忍。第二天就拔掉了，但我清楚地记得，当大部分演员都指着泽罗，齐声喊道：“犹豫不决时，就去迫害布卢姆吧！”话音未落，一阵剧痛便猛然袭来。我当时既欣喜若狂又痛苦不堪，只能安慰自己，想起詹姆斯·乔伊斯生前饱受各种疾病的折磨，尤其是他的眼疾。

I begin with a wonderful but mixed memory from the autumn of 1959, when, with my wife, I attended in London a performance of Ulysses in Nighttown, adapted by Marjorie Barkentin and directed by Burgess Meredith. Zero Mostel was Leopold Bloom, dancing his way through the part on his toes, sometimes seeming airborne. I would have been gloriously happy, identifying myself with Zero, whom I had met, and thus with Poldy, except that I had an impacted wisdom tooth, which was exquisitely painful. It was drawn the next day, but I distinctly recall that when most of the cast pointed to Zero and cried out, “When in doubt persecute Bloom,” a shocking pain suddenly shot up. I was caught between ecstasy and suffering and consoled myself by remembering how many ailments James Joyce had to suffer, particularly with his eyes.

由于饮食习惯极其怪异，莫斯特尔六十二岁便去世了，比詹姆斯·乔伊斯只多活了三年。尽管他完全是犹太人，与爱尔兰毫无关系，但对我而言，他仍然是波尔迪的清晰形象。米洛·奥谢和斯蒂芬·雷都曾在银幕上扮演过布鲁姆先生。奥谢演得相当不错，但雷的表演令人愉悦。然而，将《尤利西斯》搬上舞台或银幕，总会损失太多东西。这部作品是复调的，它超越了视觉的局限，追求一种自莎士比亚以来无人能及的听觉体验。

Because of a lunatic diet, Mostel died at sixty-two, giving him just three more years than James Joyce. He remains for me a clear image of Poldy, even though he was wholly Jewish and in no way Irish. Milo O’Shea and Stephen Rea have both acted Mr. Bloom on the screen. O’Shea was quite good, but Rea was delightful. Still, too much is lost when you transfer Ulysses either to stage or to screen. It is polyphonic and transgresses the limits of the visible in favor of an audibility unmatched since Shakespeare.

让我们进入《喀耳刻》的场景，波尔迪蹒跚地寻找着醉酒的斯蒂芬。突然，幻象将他淹没：

Let us break into “Circe” with Poldy trudging along in search of the intoxicated Stephen. Phantasmagoria suddenly overwhelms him:

（寻回犬走近，鼻子贴着地面嗅探。一个四仰八叉的身影打了个喷嚏。一个佝偻着背、蓄着胡须的身影出现，身穿锡安长老的长袍，头戴饰有紫红色流苏的烟帽。一副角状眼镜垂在鼻翼上。憔悴的脸上布满了黄色的毒液痕迹。）

(The retriever approaches sniffing, nose to the ground. A sprawled form sneezes. A stooped bearded figure appears garbed in the long caftan of an elder in Zion and a smokingcap with magenta tassels. Horned spectacles hang down at the wings of the nose. Yellow poison streaks are on the drawn face.)

鲁道夫：今天又浪费了半克朗。我早就告诉过你，千万别跟醉醺醺的异教徒走。所以你一分钱也赚不到。

RUDOLPH: Second halfcrown waste money today. I told you not go with drunken goy ever. So you catch no money.

布鲁姆：（ 把脚趾和蹄子藏在背后，垂头丧气地摸了摸脚肉，感觉又冷又热）是的，我知道，爸爸。

BLOOM: (Hides the crubeen and trotter behind his back and, crestfallen, feels warm and cold feetmeat) Ja, ich weiss, papachi.

鲁道夫：你在这地方干什么？你没有心肠吗？（他用无力的秃鹫爪子摸了摸布鲁姆沉默的脸。）你不是我的儿子利奥波德吗？利奥波德的孙子？你不是我亲爱的儿子利奥波德吗？你离开了你父亲的家，离开了你祖先亚伯拉罕和雅各的神？

RUDOLPH: What you making down this place? Have you no soul? (With feeble vulture talons he feels the silent face of Bloom.) Are you not my son Leopold, the grandson of Leopold? Are you not my dear son Leopold who left the house of his father and left the god of his fathers Abraham and Jacob?

布鲁姆：（ 谨慎地）我想是的，父亲。莫森塔尔。他只剩下这些了。

BLOOM: (With precaution) I suppose so, father. Mosenthal. All that’s left of him.

鲁道夫：（ 严厉地）他们花光了你的钱，晚上把你醉得像条狗一样带回家。你管他们叫什么？流氓？

RUDOLPH: (Severely) One night they bring you home drunk as dog after spend your good money. What you call them running chaps?

布鲁姆：（ 身着青年时期剪裁合身的蓝色牛津西装，内搭白色马甲，肩部较窄，头戴棕色阿尔卑斯山帽，佩戴男士纯银沃特伯里无钥匙怀表和带有印章的双马鞍阿尔伯特马具，身上一侧沾满了凝固的泥浆）猎犬，父亲​​。仅此一次。

BLOOM: (In youth’s smart blue Oxford suit with white vestslips, narrowshouldered, in brown Alpine hat, wearing gent’s sterling silver waterbury keyless watch and double curb Albert with seal attached, one side of him coated with stiffening mud) Harriers, father. Only that once.

鲁道夫：就一次！浑身泥泞，手都割破了，下巴也打不开。他们把你弄得一团糟，利奥波德莱本。你看着他们。

RUDOLPH: Once! Mud head to foot. Cut your hand open. Lockjaw. They make you kaputt, Leopoldleben. You watch them chaps.

布鲁姆：（ 虚弱地）他们向我发起短跑挑战。赛道很泥泞。我滑倒了。

BLOOM: (Weakly) They challenged me to a sprint. It was muddy. I slipped.

鲁道夫：（ 轻蔑地）真可怜！给你可怜的母亲戴上这么漂亮的眼镜！

RUDOLPH: (With contempt) Goim nachez! Nice spectacles for your poor mother!

布鲁姆：妈妈！

BLOOM: Mamma!

艾伦·布鲁姆：（ 她头戴哑剧女主角的系带软帽，身穿特旺基寡妇的衬裙和裙撑，羊腿袖衬衫后背系着纽扣，戴着灰色手套和浮雕胸针，辫子用发网束着，出现在楼梯栏杆上方，手里拿着一根倾斜的烛台，发出尖锐的惊恐叫喊。）哦，蒙福的救世主，他们对他做了什么！我的嗅盐！（她掀起裙摆，翻遍条纹浅色衬裙的口袋。一个小瓶、一枚羔羊经、一个干瘪的土豆和一个赛璐珞娃娃掉了出来。）圣母玛利亚圣心，你究竟在哪里？

ELLEN BLOOM: (In pantomime dame’s stringed mobcap, widow Twankey’s crinoline and bustle, blouse with muttonleg sleeves buttoned behind, grey mittens and cameo brooch, her plaited hair in a crispine net, appears over the staircase banisters, a slanted candlestick in her hand, and cries out in shrill alarm.) O blessed Redeemer, what have they done to him! My smelling salts! (She hauls up a reef of skirt and ransacks the pouch of her striped blay petticoat. A phial, an Agnus Dei, a shrivelled potato and a celluloid doll fall out.) Sacred Heart of Mary, where were you at all at all?

波尔迪的“莫森塔尔。他仅存的一切”指的是十九世纪剧作家所罗门·莫森塔尔及其剧作《被遗弃的利亚》（1886）。乔伊斯出色地描绘了波尔迪·布鲁姆谨慎的父亲鲁道夫·维拉格-布鲁姆的意第绪语-英语混杂的语言，以及他母亲艾伦带有更多爱尔兰口音的哀叹。

Poldy’s “Mosenthal. All that’s left of him” refers to Salomon Mosenthal, a nineteenth-century dramatist, and to his play Leah: The Forsaken (1886). Joyce does remarkably well at rendering the Yiddish-English of Poldy Bloom’s prudential father, Rudolph Virag-Bloom, and of his mother, Ellen’s, more Irish-inflected lament.

随着事态愈演愈烈，布卢姆被公开审判，被指控行为不检、挑衅，并引诱各阶层女性对他进行性骚扰或更露骨的虐恋行为。高潮部分是几位衣着考究的上流社会女士对他的谴责：

In a mounting crescendo, Bloom is put on public trial, accused of nuisances, provocations, and invitations to women of all stations to misbehave with him either sexually or more explicitly sadomasochistically. The grand climax is the denunciations by very well-upholstered ladies of society:

贝灵厄姆夫人：他用好几份笔迹，对我极尽溢美之词，称我为身披皮草的维纳斯，并声称对我被冻死的马车夫帕尔默深表同情。与此同时，他又嫉妒帕尔默的耳罩和羊毛皮，以及他站在我身后，身着我的制服，佩戴着饰有贝灵厄姆家族纹章（黑色底，金色鹿头）的盾形纹章时，能如此近距离地接近我。他近乎夸张地赞美我的下半身，赞美我穿着紧身丝袜、丰满的小腿，并热情洋溢地赞美我其他用无价蕾丝制成的“珍宝”，他说他可以凭空变出这些。他敦促我（声称他觉得敦促我是他毕生的使命）玷污婚姻，尽早犯下通奸之罪。

MRS BELLINGHAM: He addressed me in several handwritings with fulsome compliments as a Venus in furs and alleged profound pity for my frostbound coachman Palmer while in the same breath he expressed himself as envious of his earflaps and fleecy sheepskins and of his fortunate proximity to my person, when standing behind my chair wearing my livery and the armorial bearings of the Bellingham escutcheon garnished sable, a buck’s head couped or. He lauded almost extravagantly my nether extremities, my swelling calves in silk hose drawn up to the limit, and eulogised glowingly my other hidden treasures in priceless lace which, he said, he could conjure up. He urged me (Stating that he felt it his mission in life to urge me.) to defile the marriage bed, to commit adultery at the earliest possible opportunity.

尊敬的默文·塔尔博伊斯夫人：（ 身着亚马逊女战士服饰，头戴安全帽，脚蹬带马刺的军靴，身穿朱红色背心，戴着饰有编织鼓纹的浅褐色火枪手手套，长长的拖尾高高扬起，手里拿着一根猎鞭，不停地抽打着自己的伤口）还有我。因为他在凤凰公园的马球场上看到了我，当时正在观看全爱尔兰队对阵爱尔兰其他地区的比赛。我知道，当我看到因尼斯基林队的斯洛格·丹尼希队长骑着他心爱的矮种马“半人马”赢得最后一节比赛时，我的眼睛闪闪发光。这个平民唐璜躲在出租车后面观察我，然后用双层信封寄给我一张下流的照片，就像巴黎林荫大道上夜幕降临后出售的那种照片一样，是对任何一位女士的侮辱。我至今还保留着它。画中是一位半裸的少女，柔弱而美丽（他郑重地向我保证，这是他的妻子，是他从自然中挑选出来的），正与一位肌肉发达的斗牛士——显然是个流氓——进行着不正当的性行为。他怂恿我效仿，放荡不羁，与驻军的军官们寻欢作乐。他恳求我以不堪入目的方式玷污他的信，让他受到应有的惩罚，骑在他身上，鞭打他，狠狠地抽打他一顿。

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: (In amazon costume, hard hat, jackboots cockspurred, vermilion waistcoat, fawn musketeer gauntlets with braided drums, long train held up and hunting crop with which she strikes her welt constantly) Also me. Because he saw me on the polo ground of the Phoenix park at the match All Ireland versus the Rest of Ireland. My eyes, I know, shone divinely as I watched Captain Slogger Dennehy of the Inniskillings win the final chukkar on his darling cob Centaur. This plebeian Don Juan observed me from behind a hackney car and sent me in double envelopes an obscene photograph, such as are sold after dark on Paris boulevards, insulting to any lady. I have it still. It represents a partially nude señorita, frail and lovely (his wife, as he solemnly assured me, taken by him from nature), practising illicit intercourse with a muscular torero, evidently a blackguard. He urged me to do likewise, to misbehave, to sin with officers of the garrison. He implored me to soil his letter in an unspeakable manner, to chastise him as he richly deserves, to bestride and ride him, to give him a most vicious horsewhipping.

耶尔弗顿·巴里夫人：我也是。

MRS YELVERTON BARRY: Me too.

（几位德高望重的都柏林女士举着从布鲁姆那里收到的不雅信件。）

(Several highly respectable Dublin ladies hold up improper letters received from Bloom.)

尊敬的默文·塔尔博伊斯夫人：（ 突然怒不可遏，跺着叮当作响的马刺）我发誓，我一定要这么做！只要我还能站在他面前，我就要鞭打这个胆小鬼！我要把他活活剥皮！

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: (Stamps her jingling spurs in a sudden paroxysm of fury) I will, by the God above me. I’ll scourge the pigeonlivered cur as long as I can stand over him. I’ll flay him alive.

布鲁姆：（ 闭上眼睛，期待地瑟瑟发抖）这里？（他扭动着身子。）又来了！（他喘着粗气，畏缩着。）我喜欢这种危险。

BLOOM: (His eyes closing, quails expectantly) Here? (He squirms.) Again! (He pants cringing.) I love the danger.

尊敬的默文·塔尔博伊斯夫人：正是如此！我会让你尝尝苦头。我会让你跳杰克·拉顿的舞来偿还。

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: Very much so! I’ll make it hot for you. I’ll make you dance Jack Latten for that.

贝灵厄姆夫人：把这暴发户的裤子擦干净！在上面写上星条旗！

MRS BELLINGHAM: Tan his breech well, the upstart! Write the stars and stripes on it!

耶尔弗顿·巴里夫人：太丢人了！他没有任何借口！他可是个已婚男人！

MRS YELVERTON BARRY: Disgraceful! There’s no excuse for him! A married man!

布鲁姆：这些人啊。我指的只是打屁股这个想法。一种温暖的、酥麻的、没有渗出的快感。精细的鞭打，以促进血液循环。

BLOOM: All these people. I meant only the spanking idea. A warm tingling glow without effusion. Refined birching to stimulate the circulation.

尊敬的默文·塔尔博伊斯夫人：（ 轻蔑地笑着）哦，是吗，我的好伙计？好吧，我的天哪，你现在就要大吃一惊了，相信我，你会尝到此生最惨痛的教训。你激起了我内心沉睡的母老虎的怒火。

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: (Laughs derisively) O, did you, my fine fellow? Well, by the living God, you’ll get the surprise of your life now, believe me, the most unmerciful hiding a man ever bargained for. You have lashed the dormant tigress in my nature into fury.

贝灵厄姆太太：（ 恶狠狠地摇晃着她的手筒和眼镜）让他变得聪明点，亲爱的汉娜。给他吃生姜。把那条杂种狗打得半死。用九尾鞭。阉了他。把他活活解剖。

MRS BELLINGHAM: (Shakes her muff and quizzing-glasses vindictively) Make him smart, Hanna dear. Give him ginger. Thrash the mongrel within an inch of his life. The cat-o’-nine-tails. Geld him. Vivisect him.

布鲁姆：（ 颤抖着，蜷缩着身子，双手合十，一副垂头丧气的样子）哦，冷！哦，瑟瑟发抖！你那如仙女般甜美的容颜啊。忘掉吧，原谅吧。命运使然。就这一次吧。（他抬起另一边脸颊。）

BLOOM: (Shuddering, shrinking, joins his hands: with hangdog mien) O cold! O shivery! It was your ambrosial beauty. Forget, forgive. Kismet. Let me off this once. (He offers the other cheek.)

耶尔弗顿·巴里夫人：（ 严厉地）塔尔博伊斯夫人，无论如何都不要这样做！他应该被狠狠地教训一顿！

MRS YELVERTON BARRY: (Severely) Don’t do so on any account, Mrs Talboys! He should be soundly trounced!

尊敬的默文·塔尔博伊斯夫人：（ 猛地解开手套扣子）我绝不会那样做。你这头猪，从你出生起就是！竟敢跟我说话！我要在大街上把他打得遍体鳞伤。我要用马刺狠狠地扎他，直到他的脚趾头。他可是个出了名的戴绿帽的家伙。（她狠狠地挥舞着猎鞭。）立刻把他的裤子脱下来。过来，​​先生！快！准备好了吗？

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: (Unbuttoning her gauntlet violently) I’ll do no such thing. Pigdog and always was ever since he was pupped! To dare address me! I’ll flog him black and blue in the public streets. I’ll dig my spurs in him up to the rowel. He is a wellknown cuckold. (She swishes her huntingcrop savagely in the air.) Take down his trousers without loss of time. Come here, sir! Quick! Ready?

布鲁姆：（ 颤抖着，开始服从）天气一直很暖和。

BLOOM: (Trembling, beginning to obey) The weather has been so warm.

这股强劲的合唱声，成了我们当代“#MeToo”运动中一种颇为特殊的变体。利奥波德·冯·萨克-马索克（Leopold von Sacher-Masoch）于1895年去世，享年59岁。这位加利西亚贵族如今为人所知，是因为他那部略显逊色的长篇小说《穿裘皮的维纳斯》（Venus in Furs，1870）。正是这部小说，让他获得了“受虐狂”（masochism）一词的“永垂不朽”，即通过痛苦获得性快感。我们有理由推测，乔伊斯给利奥波德·布鲁姆（Leopold Bloom）取名“布卢姆”（Bloom），正是源于萨克-马索克。除了性方面的怪癖之外，萨克-马索克本人是一位和蔼的社会思想家和积极的亲犹主义者。

This robust chorus becomes a rather specialized variety of our contemporary “MeToo” pastime. Leopold von Sacher-Masoch, who died at fifty-nine in 1895, was a Galician nobleman remembered now for his rather inadequate novel Venus in Furs (1870), that gives him the dubious immortality of the word “masochism,” or experiencing sexual pleasure through pain. It is reasonable to assume that Joyce gave Leopold Bloom his first name from Sacher-Masoch, who, aside from his sexual vagaries, was a benign social thinker and active philo-Semite.

尽管波尔迪的一些令人愉悦的“罪过”源自乔伊斯，但我无法在诺拉·巴纳克尔和詹姆斯·乔伊斯之间长久而幸福的关系中找到任何虐恋的迹象。乔伊斯为何如此渴望在波尔迪的性心理中根植受虐倾向？这种倾向体现在她对莫莉·布卢姆不忠行为的默许上，尤其是对布莱兹·博伊兰的恶劣行径。最终，这种倾向在波尔迪对妓女情妇贝拉/贝洛·科恩的臣服中达到了令人毛骨悚然的极致。

Though some of Poldy’s amiable sins derive from Joyce, I can find no evidence of sadomasochism in the long and happy relationship between Nora Barnacle and James Joyce. Why did Joyce desire so deeply ingrained an element of masochism in Poldy’s psychosexuality? It manifests itself in the acquiescence to Molly Bloom’s infidelities, particularly with the egregious Blazes Boylan. Ultimately, it achieves a horrifying splendor in Poldy’s submission to the whore mistress Bella/Bello Cohen.

贝灵厄姆夫人、尊敬的默文·塔尔博伊斯夫人和耶尔弗顿·巴里夫人组成的庞大队伍，由尊敬的默文·塔尔博伊斯夫人领衔，她宣称我们可怜的波尔迪“唤醒了我内心沉睡的母老虎”。幸亏有“喀耳刻”的狂热举动——一场盛大的游行——才救了他。整个都柏林都沉浸在疯狂的游行队伍中，直到最后，波尔迪被加冕为爱尔兰的统治者。

That grand phalanx of Mrs. Bellingham, the Honourable Mrs. Mervin Talboys, and Mrs. Yelverton Barry is properly headed by the Honourable Mrs. Mervin Talboys, who proclaims that our poor Poldy has “lashed the dormant tigress in my nature into fury.” He is saved by the delirious movement of “Circe”: a pageant and a parade. All of Dublin whirls by in a mad procession until, at last, Poldy is crowned as ruler of Ireland:

唐郡和康纳郡主教：我在此向你们隆重介绍你们无可争议的皇帝、总统、国王兼主席，这片土地上最沉稳、最强大、最威严的统治者。上帝保佑利奥波德一世！

THE BISHOP OF DOWN AND CONNOR: I here present your undoubted emperor president and king chairman, the most serene and potent and very puissant ruler of this realm. God save Leopold the First!

全体：上帝保佑利奥波德一世！

ALL: God save Leopold the First!

布鲁姆：（ 身穿达尔马提卡长袍和紫色斗篷，庄严地对唐郡和康纳郡的主教说）谢谢您，尊敬的主教。

BLOOM: (In dalmatic and purple mantle, to the bishop of Down and Connor, with dignity) Thanks, somewhat eminent sir.

阿马大主教威廉：（ 身着紫色领巾，头戴铲形帽。）您是否愿尽您所能，在爱尔兰及其附属领土的所有判决中，使法律和仁慈得以执行？

WILLIAM, ARCHBISHOP OF ARMAGH: (In purple stock and shovel hat.) Will you to your power cause law and mercy to be executed in all your judgments in Ireland and territories thereunto belonging?

布鲁姆：（ 右手放在睾丸上，咒骂）愿造物主惩罚我。我保证会做到这一切。

BLOOM: (Placing his right hand on his testicles, swears) So may the Creator deal with me. All this I promise to do.

阿马大主教迈克尔：（ 将一罐发油倒在布鲁姆的头上）Gaudium magnum annuntio vobis. Habemus carneficem. Leopold, Patrick, Andrew, David, George, be thou onainted!

MICHAEL, ARCHBISHOP OF ARMAGH: (Pours a cruse of hairoil over Bloom’s head) Gaudium magnum annuntio vobis. Habemus carneficem. Leopold, Patrick, Andrew, David, George, be thou anointed!

（布鲁姆披上金丝斗篷，戴上红宝石戒指。他登上命运之石。二十八位贵族代表同时戴上他们的王冠。基督教堂、圣帕特里克教堂、圣乔治教堂和同性恋聚集地马拉海德教堂响起欢庆的钟声。米鲁斯集市的烟花从四面八方升起，呈现出象征男性生殖器的烟火图案。贵族们依次上前行礼，屈膝行礼。）

(Bloom assumes a mantle of cloth of gold and puts on a ruby ring. He ascends and stands on the stone of destiny. The representative peers put on at the same time their twentyeight crowns. Joybells ring in Christ church, Saint Patrick’s, George’s and gay Malahide. Mirus bazaar fireworks go up from all sides with symbolical phallopyrotechnic designs. The peers do homage, one by one, approaching and genuflecting.)

贵族们：我愿成为你们的臣子，以生命和肢体来崇拜你们。

THE PEERS: I do become your liege man of life and limb to earthly worship.

（布鲁姆举起右手，手上闪耀着光之山钻石的光芒。他的坐骑嘶鸣一声。瞬间，四周一片寂静。洲际和星际无线电发射器已准备就绪，等待接收信息。）

(Bloom holds up his right hand on which sparkles the Koh-i-Noor diamond. His palfrey neighs. Immediate silence. Wireless intercontinental and interplanetary transmitters are set for reception of message.)

布鲁姆：我的臣民们！我们在此提名我们忠实的坐骑科普拉·费利克斯为世袭大维齐尔，并宣布我们今天已与前妻断绝关系，并将我们的王室之手授予了夜之光辉——塞勒涅公主。

BLOOM: My subjects! We hereby nominate our faithful charger Copula Felix hereditary Grand Vizier and announce that we have this day repudiated our former spouse and have bestowed our royal hand upon the princess Selene, the splendour of night.

（布鲁姆的前贵庶配偶被匆匆送上黑玛利亚号。身着月蓝色长袍、头戴银色新月的塞勒涅公主从由两名巨人抬着的轿子上走下。人群中爆发出一阵欢呼声。）

(The former morganatic spouse of Bloom is hastily removed in the Black Maria. The princess Selene, in moonblue robes, a silver crescent on her head, descends from a Sedan chair, borne by two giants. An outburst of cheering.)

约翰·霍华德·帕内尔：（ 举起皇家旗帜）杰出的布鲁姆！我那著名兄长的继承人！

JOHN HOWARD PARNELL: (Raises the royal standard.) Illustrious Bloom! Successor to my famous brother!

布鲁姆：（ 拥抱约翰·霍华德·帕内尔）约翰，我们衷心感谢你，欢迎你来到绿色的爱尔兰，我们共同祖先的应许之地。

BLOOM: (Embraces John Howard Parnell) We thank you from our heart, John, for this right royal welcome to green Erin, the promised land of our common ancestors.

（他被授予城市自由权，并以宪章的形式呈现。都柏林的钥匙交叉放在一个深红色的垫子上，被交给了他。他向众人展示了他穿着的绿色袜子。）

(The freedom of the city is presented to him embodied in a charter. The keys of Dublin, crossed on a crimson cushion, are given to him. He shows all that he is wearing green socks.)

汤姆·克南：您当之无愧，法官大人。

TOM KERNAN: You deserve it, your honour.

布鲁姆：二十年前的今天，我们在莱迪史密斯击败了世仇。我们的榴弹炮和骆驼式旋回炮猛烈轰击他们的防线，取得了显著成效。向前推进了半里格！他们冲锋！一切都完了！我们投降吗？不！我们迎头痛击！看！我们冲锋！我们的轻骑兵向左翼展开，横扫普列夫纳高地，高呼着“真正的萨巴奥特”，用马刀将萨拉森炮兵全部斩杀。

BLOOM: On this day twenty years ago we overcame the hereditary enemy at Ladysmith. Our howitzers and camel swivel guns played on his lines with telling effect. Half a league onward! They charge! All is lost now! Do we yield? No! We drive them headlong! Lo! We charge! Deploying to the left our light horse swept across the heights of Plevna and, uttering their warcry Bonafide Sabaoth, sabred the Saracen gunners to a man.

弗里曼排字工的礼拜堂：听！听！

THE CHAPEL OF FREEMAN TYPESETTERS: Hear! Hear!

约翰·怀斯·诺兰：这就是那个逃脱的男人——詹姆斯·斯蒂芬斯。

JOHN WYSE NOLAN: There’s the man that got away James Stephens.

一个身穿蓝色外套的小学生：好样的！

A BLUECOAT SCHOOLBOY: Bravo!

一位老居民：先生，您是国家的骄傲，您就是这样的人。

AN OLD RESIDENT: You’re a credit to your country, sir, that’s what you are.

一位苹果女：他正是爱尔兰想要的那种男人。

AN APPLEWOMAN: He’s a man like Ireland wants.

布鲁姆：我亲爱的子民们，一个新时代即将到来。我，布鲁姆，郑重地告诉你们，它现在就近在眼前。是的，凭着布鲁姆的誓言，你们不久将进入那座即将诞生的黄金之城，未来新爱尔兰的布鲁姆城。

BLOOM: My beloved subjects, a new era is about to dawn. I, Bloom, tell you verily it is even now at hand. Yea, on the word of a Bloom, ye shall ere long enter into the golden city which is to be, the new Bloomusalem in the Nova Hibernia of the future.

（来自爱尔兰各郡的三十二名佩戴玫瑰花结的工人，在建筑商德万的指导下，建造了新的布鲁姆萨勒姆。这是一座宏伟的建筑，拥有水晶屋顶，外形像一个巨大的猪肾，内有四万个房间。在扩建过程中，一些建筑物和纪念碑被拆除。政府办公室临时搬迁到铁路棚。许多房屋被夷为平地。居民们被安置在木桶和箱子里，所有容器都用红色标记着字母：L.B.。几个穷人从梯子上摔了下来。都柏林城墙的一部分，挤满了忠实的参观者，坍塌了。）

(Thirtytwo workmen, wearing rosettes, from all the counties of Ireland, under the guidance of Derwan the builder, construct the new Bloomusalem. It is a colossal edifice with crystal roof, built in the shape of a huge pork kidney, containing forty thousand rooms. In the course of its extension several buildings and monuments are demolished. Government offices are temporarily transferred to railway sheds. Numerous houses are razed to the ground. The inhabitants are lodged in barrels and boxes, all marked in red with the letters: L. B. Several paupers fall from a ladder. A part of the walls of Dublin, crowded with loyal sightseers, collapses.)

观光客们：（ 垂死）Morituri te salutant.（他们死了。）

THE SIGHTSEERS: (Dying) Morituri te salutant. (They die.)

（一个身穿棕色雨衣的男人从活板门里跳了出来。他用一根细长的手指着布鲁姆。）

(A man in a brown macintosh springs up through a trapdoor. He points an elongated finger at Bloom.)

穿麦金托什外套的男人：别相信他说的任何一个字。那个人是利奥波德·麦金托什，臭名昭著的纵火犯。他的真名叫希金斯。

THE MAN IN THE MACINTOSH: Don’t you believe a word he says. That man is Leopold M’Intosh, the notorious fireraiser. His real name is Higgins.

布鲁姆：毙了他！该死的基督徒！麦金托什就这么算了！

BLOOM: Shoot him! Dog of a christian! So much for M’Intosh!

（一声炮响。穿雨衣的男人消失了。布鲁姆挥舞着权杖击落罂粟花。许多权势显赫的敌人、牧场主、议员、常设委员会成员当场死亡。布鲁姆的保镖分发濯足节钱币、纪念奖章、五饼二鱼、禁酒徽章、昂贵的亨利·克莱雪茄、免费的牛骨熬汤、用金线扎紧的密封信封里的橡胶防腐剂、奶油糖、菠萝糖、三角帽形状的情书、成衣、蟾蜍洞粥、杰斯消毒液、购物券、40天的赎罪券、假币、奶猪香肠、剧院通行证、所有电车线路的季票、匈牙利皇家和特权彩票的优惠券、便士晚餐计数器、廉价的世界报纸重印版……）十二本最烂的书：《青蛙和弗里茨》（政治）、《照顾婴儿》（儿童读物）、《7先令6便士的50道菜》（烹饪）、《耶稣是太阳神话吗？》（历史）、《驱除痛苦》（医学）、《婴儿宇宙纲要》（宇宙学）、《让我们一起欢笑》（滑稽）、《拉票员手册》（新闻）、《母亲助手的情书》（情色）、《太空名人录》（星象）、《触动我们心灵的歌曲》（旋律）、《潘尼怀斯致富之道》（节俭）。人群熙熙攘攘，争先恐后。女人们挤上前去，想要摸摸布鲁姆长袍的下摆。格温多琳·杜贝达特女士冲过人群，跳上他的马，在热烈的欢呼声中亲吻了他的双颊。有人用镁光手电筒拍了张照片。婴儿和哺乳期的婴儿被抱了起来。

(A cannonshot. The man in the macintosh disappears. Bloom with his sceptre strikes down poppies. The instantaneous deaths of many powerful enemies, graziers, members of parliament, members of standing committees, are reported. Bloom’s bodyguard distribute Maundy money, commemoration medals, loaves and fishes, temperance badges, expensive Henry Clay cigars, free cowbones for soup, rubber preservatives in sealed envelopes tied with gold thread, butter scotch, pineapple rock, billets doux in the form of cocked hats, readymade suits, porringers of toad in the hole, bottles of Jeyes’ Fluid, purchase stamps, 40 days’ indulgences, spurious coins, dairyfed pork sausages, theatre passes, season tickets available for all tramlines, coupons of the royal and privileged Hungarian lottery, penny dinner counters, cheap reprints of the World’s Twelve Worst Books: Froggy And Fritz (politic), Care of the Baby (infantilic), 50 Meals for 7/6 (culinic), Was Jesus a Sun Myth? (historic), Expel that Pain (medic), Infant’s Compendium of the Universe (cosmic), Let’s All Chortle (hilaric), Canvasser’s Vade Mecum (journalic), Loveletters of Mother Assistant (erotic), Who’s Who in Space (astric), Songs that Reached Our Heart (melodic), Pennywise’s Way to Wealth (parsimonic). A general rush and scramble. Women press forward to touch the hem of Bloom’s robe. The lady Gwendolen Dubedat bursts through the throng, leaps on his horse and kisses him on both cheeks amid great acclamation. A magnesium flashlight photograph is taken. Babes and sucklings are held up.)

女人们：小爸爸！小爸爸！

THE WOMEN: Little father! Little father!

婴儿和哺乳期婴儿：

THE BABES AND SUCKLINGS:

拍手欢呼直到波尔迪回家，

Clap clap hands till Poldy comes home,

他口袋里装着蛋糕，都是给Leo一个人准备的。

Cakes in his pocket for Leo alone.

这场精彩绝伦的庆典中最耀眼的亮点，莫过于波尔迪对新布鲁姆萨勒姆的构想。唯一令我困惑的一句话是：“这就是那个与我擦肩而过的人——詹姆斯·斯蒂芬斯。”乔伊斯和詹姆斯·斯蒂芬斯之间有着一段奇特而长久的友谊，部分原因在于他们误以为彼此是同一天出生的。我想，任何读过詹姆斯·斯蒂芬斯的诗歌和他最著名的小说《金罐》（1912）的人，都不会认为，如果乔伊斯没有活到那一天，斯蒂芬斯或许就能完成《守灵夜》。然而，随着眼疾加重，乔伊斯创作的痛苦也与日俱增，这件事便成了他挥之不去的执念。不过，与这句惊世骇俗的宣言相比，这只是个微不足道的细节：

The glorious center of this bravura celebration is Poldy’s vision of the new Bloomusalem. The only sentence that baffles me remains, “There’s the man that got away James Stephens.” Joyce and James Stephens had a curious and long-enduring friendship, partly founded on the mistaken notion that they had been born on the same day. I do not think that anyone who has read James Stephens’s poetry and his best-known novel, The Crock of Gold (1912), could think that Stephens might have finished the Wake had Joyce not lived to do so. Yet that became an obsession of Joyce as his eye troubles increased the painful labors of composition. Still, that is a minor detail compared with this marvelous proclamation:

布鲁姆：我亲爱的子民们，一个新时代即将到来。我，布鲁姆，郑重地告诉你们，它现在就近在眼前。是的，凭着布鲁姆的誓言，你们不久将进入那座即将诞生的黄金之城，未来新爱尔兰的布鲁姆城。

BLOOM: My beloved subjects, a new era is about to dawn. I, Bloom, tell you verily it is even now at hand. Yea, on the word of a Bloom, ye shall ere long enter into the golden city which is to be, the new Bloomusalem in the Nova Hibernia of the future.

如今的读者或许更愿意居住在新都柏林（Bloomusalem），而非新耶路撒冷。我自上世纪八十年代中期以来就没去过都柏林，但上次去的时候，却失望地发现，曾经构成叶芝和乔伊斯笔下都柏林一部分的乔治亚式房屋和广场已不复存在。此后，人们发起了一场保护这些遗迹的运动。然而，我自1985年以来就没去过耶路撒冷，而且从我在那里的朋友那里得知，我恐怕认不出那里的大部分地方了。

These days readers might well prefer to live in the new Bloomusalem rather than the new Jerusalem. I have not been in Dublin since the mid-1980s but was dismayed, during my final visit, not to find so many Georgian houses and squares that had been part of the Dublin of Yeats and Joyce. Since then there has been a movement to preserve what still was there. But, then, I have not been in Jerusalem since 1985, and from my friends there I gather I would not recognize most of it.

新的布鲁姆萨勒姆以惊人的速度消散了：

The new Bloomusalem vaporizes with startling rapidity:

莱内汉：抄袭者！打倒布鲁姆！

LENEHAN: Plagiarist! Down with Bloom!

蒙面女先知：（ 热情洋溢地）我是布鲁姆的粉丝，我为此感到无比自豪。尽管如此，我仍然相信他。我愿意为他付出生命，他是地球上最幽默的人。

THE VEILED SIBYL: (Enthusiastically) I’m a Bloomite and I glory in it. I believe in him in spite of all. I’d give my life for him, the funniest man on earth.

布鲁姆：（ 向旁观者眨眼）我敢打赌她是个漂亮姑娘。

BLOOM: (Winks at the bystanders) I bet she’s a bonny lassie.

西奥多·普雷福伊：（ 戴着渔夫帽，穿着油布夹克）他利用机械装置来破坏自然的神圣目标。

THEODORE PUREFOY: (In fishingcap and oilskin jacket) He employs a mechanical device to frustrate the sacred ends of nature.

蒙面女先知：（ 自刎）我的英雄神！（她死了。）

THE VEILED SIBYL: (Stabs herself) My hero god! (She dies.)

（许多极具魅力和热情的女性也会选择自杀，例如刺伤、溺水、饮用氢氰酸、乌头、砒霜、割腕、绝食、跳入压路机下、从纳尔逊纪念柱顶端跳入吉尼斯啤酒厂的大桶中、将头伸入煤气炉窒息而死、用时尚的吊袜带上吊、从不同楼层的窗户跳下。）

(Many most attractive and enthusiastic women also commit suicide by stabbing, drowning, drinking prussic acid, aconite, arsenic, opening their veins, refusing food, casting themselves under steamrollers, from the top of Nelson’s Pillar, into the great vat of Guinness’s brewery, asphyxiating themselves by placing their heads in gasovens, hanging themselves in stylish garters, leaping from windows of different storeys.)

亚历山大·J·道伊：（ 激烈地）各位基督徒同胞和反布鲁姆派，这个叫布鲁姆的人简直是地狱的化身，是基督徒的耻辱。他自幼就是个放荡不羁的恶魔，这只门德斯的臭山羊早熟地显露出孩童般的放荡不羁，让人想起平原上的城市，以及他那放荡不羁的祖母。这个卑鄙的伪君子，浑身散发着恶名，就是《启示录》里提到的白牛。他是红衣女人的崇拜者，阴谋诡计是他呼吸的空气。火刑柱和沸油锅是为他准备的。卡利班！

ALEXANDER J. DOWIE: (Violently) Fellowchristians and antiBloomites, the man called Bloom is from the roots of hell, a disgrace to christian men. A fiendish libertine from his earliest years this stinking goat of Mendes gave precocious signs of infantile debauchery, recalling the cities of the plain, with a dissolute granddam. This vile hypocrite, bronzed with infamy, is the white bull mentioned in the Apocalypse. A worshipper of the Scarlet Woman, intrigue is the very breath of his nostrils. The stake faggots and the caldron of boiling oil are for him. Caliban!

亚历山大·J·道伊，这位令人愉悦的美国福音传教士，几乎什么都说不准。《圣约翰启示录》里根本没有提到白牛。当然，书中确实有那个风情万种的巴比伦娼妓，但何必再把老掉牙的卡利班扯进来呢？乔伊斯对神秘学的偏爱无疑促使道伊编造了“门德斯的臭山羊”这个说法，而这个说法源自埃利法斯·莱维·扎赫德，一位职业神秘主义者，真名是阿方斯·路易·康斯坦，他是内瓦尔和年轻的戈蒂埃的朋友。埃利法斯·莱维虚构了门德斯的山羊，据说这只山羊曾与古埃及那间茅屋里的女祭司们交媾。

Alexander J. Dowie, delightful American evangelist, cannot get much right. There is no white bull mentioned in the Revelation of Saint John the Divine. There is of course that splendid damozel the Whore of Babylon, but why drag in the much-tried Caliban? Joyce’s proclivity for esoterica doubtless prompts Dowie’s “stinking goat of Mendes,” derived from Éliphas Lévi Zahed, a professional mystifier whose name was Alphonse Louis Constant and who was a friend of Nerval and the young Gautier. Éliphas Lévi concocted the goat of Mendes, who supposedly copulated with the priestesses in that ancient Egyptian hovel.

暴民：把他吊死！烤死他！他跟帕内尔一样坏！狐狸先生！

THE MOB: Lynch him! Roast him! He’s as bad as Parnell was. Mr Fox!

（格罗根太太朝布鲁姆扔靴子。多塞特街上街和下街的几位店主扔出一些几乎没有商业价值的物品，比如火腿骨、炼乳罐头、卖不出去的卷心菜、隔夜面包、羊尾巴和零碎的肥肉。）

(Mother Grogan throws her boot at Bloom. Several shopkeepers from upper and lower Dorset street throw objects of little or no commercial value, hambones, condensed milk tins, unsaleable cabbage, stale bread, sheep’s tails, odd pieces of fat.)

布鲁姆：（ 兴奋地）这简直是仲夏夜的疯狂，又有人在开什么可怕的玩笑。老天作证，我清白得像未晒过的雪！是我哥哥亨利干的。他跟我长得一模一样。他住在海豚谷仓2号。诽谤，这条毒蛇，冤枉了我。同胞们，请出面为我作证。我请我的老朋友，性学专家马拉奇·穆里根医生来为我提供医学证词。

BLOOM: (Excitedly) This is midsummer madness, some ghastly joke again. By heaven, I am guiltless as the unsunned snow! It was my brother Henry. He is my double. He lives in number 2 Dolphin’s Barn. Slander, the viper, has wrongfully accused me. Fellowcountrymen, sgenl inn ban bata coisde gan capall. I call on my old friend, Dr Malachi Mulligan, sex specialist, to give medical testimony on my behalf.

穆里根医生：（ 身穿紧身短上衣，额头上戴着绿色摩托车护目镜）布鲁姆医生性取向异常，且为双性恋。他最近从尤斯塔斯医生为精神错乱绅士设立的私人精神病院逃了出来。他患有先天性癫痫，这是由于长期卧床不起造成的，而癫痫是其放纵欲望的后果。他的祖先中发现了象皮病的痕迹。他有明显的慢性暴露癖症状，并且可能存在双手灵巧性。他因自慰而过早秃顶，因此变得异常理想主义，曾经是个浪荡子，现在改邪归正，并且戴着金属假牙。由于家庭情结，他暂时失去了记忆，我认为他受到的伤害比他加害的要多。我已对他进行了阴道检查，并在对5427根肛门、腋窝、胸毛和阴毛进行酸性测试后，宣布他仍是处男。

DR MULLIGAN: (In motor jerkin, green motorgoggles on his brow) Dr Bloom is bisexually abnormal. He has recently escaped from Dr Eustace’s private asylum for demented gentlemen. Born out of bedlock hereditary epilepsy is present, the consequence of unbridled lust. Traces of elephantiasis have been discovered among his ascendants. There are marked symptoms of chronic exhibitionism. Ambidexterity is also latent. He is prematurely bald from selfabuse, perversely idealistic in consequence, a reformed rake, and has metal teeth. In consequence of a family complex he has temporarily lost his memory and I believe him to be more sinned against than sinning. I have made a pervaginal examination and, after application of the acid test to 5427 anal, axillary, pectoral and pubic hairs, I declare him to be virgo intacta.

乔伊斯在戈加蒂身上找到了他真正的“黑兽”，并将其发挥到了极致。都柏林暴民企图私刑处死波尔迪，并将他与堕落的查尔斯·斯图尔特·帕内尔联系起来。帕内尔45岁时死于凯瑟琳·奥谢的怀中，两人曾长期保持着婚外情。在这段情事中，他曾用“狐狸先生”作为化名与奥谢通信。帕内尔被罗马天主教会开除，最终耻辱地死去，尽管他长期以来一直是爱尔兰争取摆脱英国统治的领袖。

Having found in Gogarty his true black beast, Joyce exploits him to the limit. The Dublin mob seeking to lynch Poldy associates him with the fallen Charles Stewart Parnell, who died at forty-five in the arms of Katharine O’Shea, with whom he had enjoyed a long adulterous relationship. During the romance, he had used “Mr. Fox” as one pseudonym in his correspondence with her. Cast out by the Roman Catholic Church, Parnell died in disgrace, though he had long been the leader in the Irish struggle for emancipation from England.

戈加蒂，也就是巴克·穆里根，一如既往地滑稽可笑。乔伊斯虽然深受戈加蒂之苦，却依然凭借其艺术才华赋予穆里根永生。巴克的言辞虽略显浮夸，却也气势磅礴：他拥有伟大的福斯塔夫那般滔滔不绝的热情，尽管巴克并非约翰爵士。或许更接近巴克的是帕努尔格，尽管拉伯雷《魔笛》第三卷和第四卷中的这位伟大的恶魔，虽然精明放荡，却是个懦夫，而戈加蒂——至少在这一点上——行动上却十分勇敢。

Gogarty, that is to say Buck Mulligan, is as funny as ever. Joyce, who had suffered much from Gogarty, nevertheless was artist enough to endow Mulligan with eternal life. Buck’s rhetoric, though pompous, is orotund: it has the rolling gusto of the great Falstaff, though Buck is no Sir John. Closer perhaps is Panurge, though that great Daemon in Books Three and Four of Rabelais, while shrewd and licentious, is a coward, whereas Gogarty—to grant him that much—was courageous in action.

盛大的游行继续进行，波尔迪再次表现出弥赛亚式的献祭姿态：

The pageant swirls on, and Poldy again manifests Messianic gestures towards oblation:

一个声音：布鲁姆，你是约瑟之子还是大卫之子？

A VOICE: Bloom, are you the Messiah ben Joseph or ben David?

布鲁姆：（ 阴沉地）你说得对。

BLOOM: (Darkly) You have said it.

巴兹兄弟：那就跟查尔斯神父一样行个奇迹吧。

BROTHER BUZZ: Then perform a miracle like Father Charles.

BANTAM LYONS：预测谁将赢得圣莱杰锦标赛。

BANTAM LYONS: Prophesy who will win the Saint Leger.

（布鲁姆走在网子上，用左耳捂住左眼，穿过几堵墙，爬上纳尔逊纪念柱，用眼皮挂在顶端边缘，吃了十二打牡蛎（包括壳），治愈了几个受国王诅咒的人，收缩面部表情，使自己看起来像许多历史人物，如比肯斯菲尔德勋爵、拜伦勋爵、沃特·泰勒、埃及的摩西、摩西·迈蒙尼德、摩西·门德尔松、亨利·欧文、里普·凡·温克尔、科苏特、让·雅克·卢梭、利奥波德·罗斯柴尔德男爵、鲁滨逊·克鲁索、夏洛克·福尔摩斯、巴斯德，同时将两只脚转向不同的方向，命令潮水退去，伸出小指遮蔽了太阳。）

(Bloom walks on a net, covers his left eye with his left ear, passes through several walls, climbs Nelson’s Pillar, hangs from the top ledge by his eyelids, eats twelve dozen oysters (shells included), heals several sufferers from king’s evil, contracts his face so as to resemble many historical personages, Lord Beaconsfield, Lord Byron, Wat Tyler, Moses of Egypt, Moses Maimonides, Moses Mendelssohn, Henry Irving, Rip van Winkle, Kossuth, Jean Jacques Rousseau, Baron Leopold Rothschild, Robinson Crusoe, Sherlock Holmes, Pasteur, turns each foot simultaneously in different directions, bids the tide turn back, eclipses the sun by extending his little finger.)

布里尼，教皇努西奥：（ 身着教皇祖阿夫制服，钢制胸甲作为胸板、臂甲、腿甲、大腿甲，留着夸张的胡须，头戴棕色纸质主教冠。）Leopoldi autem generatio.摩西生诺亚，诺亚生太监，太监生奥哈洛兰，奥哈洛兰生古根海姆，古根海姆生阿根达斯，阿根达斯生内泰姆，内泰姆生勒赫希，勒赫希生耶苏伦，耶苏伦生麦凯，麦凯生奥斯特罗洛普斯基，奥斯特罗洛普斯基生斯梅尔多兹，斯梅尔多兹生魏斯，魏斯生施瓦茨，施瓦茨生阿德里亚诺波利，阿德里亚诺波利生阿兰胡埃斯，阿兰胡埃斯生莱维·劳森，莱维·劳森生伊查布多诺索尔，伊查布多诺索尔生奥唐奈尔·马格努斯，奥唐奈尔·马格努斯生克里斯特鲍姆，克里斯特鲍姆生本·迈蒙，本·迈蒙生达斯蒂Rhodes 和 Dusty Rhodes 生了 Benamor，Benamor 生了 Jones-Smith，Jones-Smith 生了 Savorgnanovich，Savorgnanovich 生了 Jasperstone，Jasperstone 生了 Vingtetunieme，Vingtetunieme 生了 Szombathely，Szombathely 生了 Virag，Virag 生了 Bloom et vocabitur nomen eius Emmanuel.

BRINI, PAPAL NUNCIO: (In papal zouave’s uniform, steel cuirasses as breastplate, armplates, thighplates, legplates, large profane moustaches and brown paper mitre.) Leopoldi autem generatio. Moses begat Noah and Noah begat Eunuch and Eunuch begat O’Halloran and O’Halloran begat Guggenheim and Guggenheim begat Agendath and Agendath begat Netaim and Netaim begat Le Hirsch and Le Hirsch begat Jesurum and Jesurum begat MacKay and MacKay begat Ostrolopsky and Ostrolopsky begat Smerdoz and Smerdoz begat Weiss and Weiss begat Schwarz and Schwarz begat Adrianopoli and Adrianopoli begat Aranjuez and Aranjuez begat Lewy Lawson and Lewy Lawson begat Ichabudonosor and Ichabudonosor begat O’Donnell Magnus and O’Donnell Magnus begat Christbaum and Christbaum begat ben Maimun and ben Maimun begat Dusty Rhodes and Dusty Rhodes begat Benamor and Benamor begat Jones-Smith and Jones-Smith begat Savorgnanovich and Savorgnanovich begat Jasperstone and Jasperstone begat Vingtetunieme and Vingtetunieme begat Szombathely and Szombathely begat Virag and Virag begat Bloom et vocabitur nomen eius Emmanuel.

死手：（ 在墙上写字）布鲁姆是条鳕鱼。

A DEADHAND: (Writes on the wall) Bloom is a cod.

螃蟹：（ 身穿丛林强盗的装备）你在基尔巴拉克后面的牛栏里做了什么？

CRAB: (In bushranger’s kit) What did you do in the cattlecreep behind Kilbarrack?

女婴：（ 摇晃拨浪鼓）在巴利博桥下呢？

A FEMALE INFANT: (Shakes a rattle) And under Ballybough bridge?

冬青树：在魔鬼谷里呢？

A HOLLYBUSH: And in the devil’s glen?

布鲁姆：（ 脸颊绯红，从额头到脚趾都红透了，左眼流下三滴眼泪）饶了我的过去吧。

BLOOM: (Blushes furiously all over from frons to nates, three tears falling from his left eye) Spare my past.

被驱逐的爱尔兰佃户们：（ 身穿紧身衣、及膝短裤，手持唐尼布鲁克公平的棍棒）用鞭子抽他！

THE IRISH EVICTED TENANTS: (In bodycoats, kneebreeches, with Donnybrook fair shillelaghs) Sjambok him!

（长着驴耳朵的布鲁姆双臂交叉，双脚伸出，坐在示众台上。他吹着《唐璜》的口哨，唱着一首塞纳尔·特科舞曲。阿尔塔纳的孤儿们手拉手，围着他嬉戏。监狱门救济院的女孩们也手拉手，朝相反的方向嬉戏。）

(Bloom with asses’ ears seats himself in the pillory with crossed arms, his feet protruding. He whistles Don Giovanni, a cenar teco. Artane orphans, joining hands, caper round him. Girls of the Prison Gate Mission, joining hands, caper round in the opposite direction.)

阿坦孤儿：

THE ARTANE ORPHANS:

你这头猪，你这头猪，你这条肮脏的狗！

You hig, you hog, you dirty dog!

你以为女士们都喜欢你！

You think the ladies love you!

监狱门卫：

THE PRISON GATE GIRLS:

如果你看到凯

If you see Kay

告诉他他可以

Tell him he may

茶会见。

See you in tea

替我告诉他。

Tell him from me.

号手：（ 身穿以弗得，头戴猎帽，宣告）他必将百姓的罪孽带给旷野中的邪灵阿撒泻勒和夜魔莉莉丝。他们必用石头打死他，玷污他，是的，所有来自阿根达·尼泰姆和米斯莱姆（含的地）的人都必如此。

HORNBLOWER: (In ephod and huntingcap, announces) And he shall carry the sins of the people to Azazel, the spirit which is in the wilderness, and to Lilith, the nighthag. And they shall stone him and defile him, yea, all from Agendath Netaim and from Mizraim, the land of Ham.

（众人向布卢姆投掷轻柔的哑剧石块。许多正经的旅行者和流浪狗靠近他，对他进行侮辱。马斯蒂安斯基和西特龙身穿长袍，留着长长的鬓角，向布卢姆摇晃着胡须。）

(All the people cast soft pantomime stones at Bloom. Many bonafide travellers and ownerless dogs come near him and defile him. Mastiansky and Citron approach in gaberdines, wearing long earlocks. They wag their beards at Bloom.)

马斯蒂安斯基和西特龙：贝利亚！伊斯特拉的莱姆莱因，假弥赛亚！阿布拉菲亚！悔改！

MASTIANSKY AND CITRON: Belial! Laemlein of Istria, the false Messiah! Abulafia! Recant!

古代犹太末世神学中描绘了两位弥赛亚。第一位是约瑟之子弥赛亚，他的作用是为大卫家的真正弥赛亚的到来做铺垫。第一位弥赛亚在召集被掳的犹太人并收复耶路撒冷后，注定会在战场上阵亡；而第二位弥赛亚将带来新天新地。当波尔迪意味深长地说出“你说得对”时，乔伊斯暗示了路加福音23:3，耶稣在那里巧妙地回答“你说得对”，从而避免了祭司们指责他自称为基督君王或大卫家的弥赛亚。

Ancient Jewish apocalyptic theology features two Messiahs. The first is the Messiah ben Joseph whose function is to prelude the coming of the true Messiah of the House of David. Whereas the first Messiah, after ingathering the exiles and retaking Jerusalem, is destined to be slain in battle, the second will bring about a new heaven and earth. When Poldy darkly says, “You have said it,” Joyce implies Luke 23:3, where Jesus avoids the indictment of the priests that he calls himself Christ a King or the Messiah of the House of David, by subtly answering, “Thou sayest it.”

利奥波德·布鲁姆的内涵总是远超我的理解范围。尤利西斯或奥德修斯的故事包罗万象，但最终却不如波尔迪完整。但丁笔下的尤利西斯，后来又成为丁尼生笔下的尤利西斯，更像是诗人但丁，而非朝圣者但丁。在《地狱篇》第二十六歌中，尤利西斯与狄俄墨得斯共用双焰，向朝圣者讲述他最后一次超越诸神界限的旅程。但丁的反应是沉默。这暗示着他意识到尤利西斯的胆识与他自己从地狱到炼狱再到天堂的雄心壮志之间的相似之处。

There is always more to Leopold Bloom than I can hope to understand. Ulysses or Odysseus is more than comprehensive but finally less complete than Poldy. Dante’s Ulysses, who becomes Tennyson’s, is like Dante the Poet rather than Dante the Pilgrim. When Ulysses speaks to the Pilgrim out of the double flame he shares with Diomed in Canto 26 of Inferno, he tells the story of his last voyage beyond the limits set by the gods. Dante’s reaction is silence. The implication is that he recognizes the affinity between the audacity of Ulysses and his own ambitious voyage from Inferno to Purgatorio to Paradiso.

尽管但丁可能将神学家的寓言与诗人的寓言融合在一起，但他自视为至高无上的诗人，甚至超越了他敬爱的父亲维吉尔。他将弗洛拉的约阿希姆置于天堂之中，尽管托马斯·阿奎那驳斥了约阿希姆遗赠给方济各会的《永恒福音》 。但丁将他的《神曲》视为第三约，它完善了旧约和新约，并印证了约阿希姆关于精神第三时代的预言，取代了圣父时代和圣子时代。

Though Dante may fuse the allegory of the theologians with the allegory of the poets, he thinks of himself as the supreme poet, transcending even his beloved father Virgil. He places Joachim of Flora in Paradise even though Thomas Aquinas refuted The Everlasting Gospel, which Joachim bequeathed to the Franciscans. Dante thought of his Commedia as a Third Testament, completing the Old and the New, and confirming Joachim’s prophecy of the Third Age of the Spirit, replacing the Ages of the Father and the Son.

约阿希姆的《灵性时代》影响了英国革命时期那些激进的教派分子，他们起初效忠克伦威尔，后来却抗议任何限制他们获得“内在之光”的措施。这些革命者——狂热派、掘地派、穆格尔顿派、平等派——正是约翰·弥尔顿最终形成其复杂而独特的宗教立场的根基所在。这条脉络从弥尔顿延续到威廉·布莱克，后者创作了另一部“永恒福音”，并在其插图中对但丁和弥尔顿都提出了批评。

Joachim’s Age of the Spirit contaminated the radical sectaries of the English Revolution who fought on the side of Cromwell but then protested any restrictions on their access to the Inner Light. These revolutionaries—Ranters, Diggers, Muggletonians, Levellers—were the matrix from which John Milton evolved his highly intricate and personal final religious stance. The line goes from Milton to William Blake, who wrote another “Everlasting Gospel” and who criticized both Dante and Milton in his illustrations to them.

詹姆斯·乔伊斯似乎无所不知，如同他之前的莎士比亚一样，将但丁和布莱克的思想转化成了《尤利西斯》和《芬尼根守灵夜》中反弥赛亚的漩涡。看到波尔迪被指控冒充弥赛亚，真是令人感到亵渎的乐趣。难道这不远不止于此吗？既然乔伊斯、波尔迪和莎士比亚构成了一个新的三位一体，或者说三位一体，莎士比亚是圣父，詹姆斯·乔伊斯是圣子，那么波尔迪或许真的预示着灵性时代的到来。

James Joyce, who somehow seems to have known everything, like Shakespeare before him, transmuted Dante and Blake into the anti-Messianic vortices of Ulysses and the Wake. It is blasphemous fun to behold Poldy accused of Messianic imposture. Is it not more than that? Since Joyce, Poldy, Shakespeare form a new Trinity or three-in-one, and Shakespeare is God the Father, James Joyce the Son, then Poldy may indeed be an omen of Advent for the approach of the Age of the Spirit.

在疯狂欢呼、极富创意的“begats”歌声之后，各种侮辱和谩骂如潮水般涌向波尔迪。其中最引人注目的是，马斯蒂安斯基和西特龙公开指责布鲁姆是假弥赛亚亚伯拉罕·阿布拉菲亚。在阿布拉菲亚离奇的一生中最精彩的时刻，这位自称卡巴拉先知的阿布拉菲亚于1280年抵达罗马，并宣布他将在犹太新年前一天前来劝说教皇尼古拉三世皈依真正的犹太教。当时教皇尼古拉三世正在苏里亚诺，他欣然下令，一旦阿布拉菲亚抵达该城，就立即将其烧死。然而，阿布拉菲亚依然向苏里亚诺进发，那里的内门已经为他准备好了火刑柱。奇迹发生了！当毫不畏惧的阿布拉菲亚穿过外门时，他被告知教皇已于前夜因中风猝然离世。在罗马被监禁一个月后，先知诗人亚伯拉罕·阿布拉菲亚前往西西里岛，在那里他宣称自己是弥赛亚。

After the insanely jubilant and inventive chant of “begats,” various insults and enunciations are hurled at Poldy. Most significantly, Mastiansky and Citron denounce Bloom as the false Messiah Abraham Abulafia. In the most colorful moment of his bizarre career, the prophetic Kabbalist Abulafia arrived in Rome in 1280 and announced that he had come to convert Pope Nicholas III to the true faith of Judaism the day before the Jewish New Year. At that time Pope Nicholas was in Suriano and cheerfully ordered the burning of the Jewish fanatic as soon as he reached that town. Nevertheless, Abulafia marched on Suriano, where a stake had been prepared for him at the inner gate. Miracle! As the unshrinking Abulafia went through the outer gate, he was told that the Pope had died suddenly the night before, of a stroke. After weathering a month’s imprisonment in Rome, the prophetic poet Abraham Abulafia went on to Sicily, where he proclaimed himself to be the Messiah.

我回到被戴绿帽的波尔迪那里，再通过他回到莎士比亚那里：

I return to Poldy the cuckold and by way of him to Shakespeare:

玛丽昂：让他看看，这个皮条客！皮条客！让他自食其果！我要写信给一个有势力的妓女或者长胡子的巴托洛蒙娜，让她在他身上弄出一英寸厚的鞭痕，让他给我带回一张签名盖章的收据。

MARION: Let him look, the pishogue! Pimp! And scourge himself! I’ll write to a powerful prostitute or Bartholomona, the bearded woman, to raise weals out on him an inch thick and make him bring me back a signed and stamped receipt.

博伊兰：（抱紧自己）我再也撑不住了。（他迈着僵硬的骑兵式步伐离开。）

BOYLAN: (Clasps himself.) Here, I can’t hold this little lot much longer. (He strides off on stiff cavalry legs.)

贝拉：（ 笑）嗬嗬嗬。

BELLA: (Laughing) Ho ho ho ho.

博伊兰：（ 越过肩膀对布鲁姆说）你可以盯着钥匙孔自慰，而我只要进去几次就行了。

BOYLAN: (To Bloom, over his shoulder) You can apply your eye to the keyhole and play with yourself while I just go through her a few times.

布鲁姆：谢谢您，先生。好的，先生。我可以带两个哥们儿来见证一下，顺便拍张照片吗？（他拿着一个药膏罐）凡士林，先生？橙花油……？温水……？

BLOOM: Thank you, sir. I will, sir. May I bring two men chums to witness the deed and take a snapshot? (He holds an ointment jar) Vaseline, sir? Orangeflower…? Lukewarm water…?

凯蒂：（ 从沙发上）告诉我们，弗洛里。告诉我们。什么事？

KITTY: (From the sofa) Tell us, Florry. Tell us. What.

（弗洛里在她耳边低语。低语的爱语发出轻柔的拍唇声，噼里啪啦，噗噗作响。）

(Florry whispers to her. Whispering lovewords murmur liplapping loudly, poppysmic plopslop.)

米娜·肯尼迪：（ 她仰起眼睛）哦，那一定像天竺葵和甜美桃子的香味！哦，他简直把她的一切都迷得神魂颠倒！黏在一起！满是吻痕！

MINA KENNEDY: (Her eyes upturned) O, it must be like the scent of geraniums and lovely peaches! O, he simply idolises every bit of her! Stuck together! Covered with kisses!

莉迪亚·杜斯：（ 张开嘴）嗯嗯。哦，他抱着她在房间里转来转去！骑着公马。在巴黎和纽约都能听到。就像满嘴草莓奶油一样。

LYDIA DOUCE: (Her mouth opening) Yumyum. O, he’s carrying her round the room doing it! Ride a cock horse. You could hear them in Paris and New York. Like mouthfuls of strawberries and cream.

凯蒂：（ 笑着）嘻嘻嘻。

KITTY: (Laughing) Hee hee hee.

博伊兰的声音：（ 甜美而沙哑，从他胃底深处传来）啊！Gooblazeqruk brukarchkrasht！

BOYLAN’S VOICE: (Sweetly, hoarsely, in the pit of his stomach) Ah! Gooblazeqruk brukarchkrasht!

玛丽昂的声音：（ 沙哑而甜美地，从喉咙深处升起）哦！ Weeshwashtkissimapooisthnapoohuck！

MARION’S VOICE: (Hoarsely, sweetly, rising to her throat) O! Weeshwashtkissimapooisthnapoohuck!

布鲁姆：（ 双眼瞳孔狂跳，双手抱胸）快！快躲！快！干掉她！再来！开枪！

BLOOM: (His eyes wildly dilated, clasps himself) Show! Hide! Show! Plough her! More! Shoot!

贝拉、佐伊、弗洛里、基蒂：嗬嗬！哈哈！嘻嘻！

BELLA, ZOE, FLORRY, KITTY: Ho ho! Ha ha! Hee hee!

林奇：（ 指着）大自然的镜子。（他大笑。）哈哈哈哈哈哈！

LYNCH: (Points) The mirror up to nature. (He laughs.) Hu hu hu hu hu!

（斯蒂芬和布鲁姆凝视着镜子。镜子里映出威廉·莎士比亚的脸，他没有胡须，面部僵硬，仿佛面部麻痹，镜子里倒映着大厅里驯鹿角帽架的影像。）

(Stephen and Bloom gaze in the mirror. The face of William Shakespeare, beardless, appears there, rigid in facial paralysis, crowned by the reflection of the reindeer antlered hatrack in the hall.)

莎士比亚：（ 用庄严的腹语）大笑暴露了空虚的心灵。（对布卢姆说）你以为你隐形了？睁大眼睛。（他发出黑阉鸡般的笑声。）伊阿戈戈！我的老伙计星期四早上笑得多么难受啊。伊阿戈戈戈！

SHAKESPEARE: (In dignified ventriloquy) ’Tis the loud laugh bespeaks the vacant mind. (To Bloom) Thou thoughtest as how thou wastest invisible. Gaze. (He crows with a black capon’s laugh.) Iagogo! How my Oldfellow chokit his Thursdaymornun. Iagogogo!

布鲁姆：（ 对着三个妓女露出黄牙般的笑容）我什么时候才能听到笑话？

BLOOM: (Smiles yellowly at the three whores) When will I hear the joke?

佐伊：在你结过两次婚、丧过一次丧偶之前。

ZOE: Before you’re twice married and once a widower.

布鲁姆：疏忽是可以被容忍的。即使是伟大的拿破仑，在他死后人们也曾测量过他的皮下尺寸……

BLOOM: Lapses are condoned. Even the great Napoleon when measurements were taken next the skin after his death…

（迪格纳姆太太，一位寡妇，鼻子上翘，脸颊因临终前的呓语、泪水和图尼的黄褐色雪利酒而泛红，她穿着丧服匆匆走过，帽子歪戴，一边往脸颊、嘴唇和鼻子上抹胭脂和粉，一边用钢笔驱赶着她的孩子们。裙下露出她已故丈夫的日常裤子和卷边靴，靴筒很大，是8字形的。她拿着一份苏格兰寡妇保险单和一把大篷伞，孩子们在伞下奔跑：帕齐单脚跳着，衣领松松垮垮，手里拿着一捆猪排；弗雷迪呜咽着；苏西张着嘴，像条哭闹的鳕鱼；爱丽丝正费力地抱着婴儿。她给孩子们系好袖子，飘带在空中飘扬。）

(Mrs Dignam, widow woman, her snubnose and cheeks flushed with deathtalk, tears and Tunney’s tawny sherry, hurries by in her weeds, her bonnet awry, rouging and powdering her cheeks, lips and nose, a pen chivvying her brood of cygnets. Beneath her skirt appear her late husband’s everyday trousers and turnedup boots, large eights. She holds a Scottish widow’s insurance policy and a large marquee umbrella under which her brood run with her, Patsy hopping on one shod foot, his collar loose, a hank of porksteaks dangling, Freddy whimpering, Susy with a crying cod’s mouth, Alice struggling with the baby. She cuffs them on, her streamers flaunting aloft.)

弗雷迪：啊，妈，你拖着我一起走！

FREDDY: Ah, ma, you’re dragging me along!

SUSY：妈妈，牛肉茶要溢出来了！

SUSY: Mamma, the beeftea is fizzing over!

莎士比亚：（ 带着麻痹般的愤怒） Weda seca whokilla farst。

SHAKESPEARE: (With paralytic rage) Weda seca whokilla farst.

（马丁·坎宁安蓄着胡须，他的脸庞酷似莎士比亚无须的脸。帐篷的遮阳伞摇摇晃晃，孩子们纷纷跑到一边。伞下出现了坎宁安夫人，她戴着“风流寡妇”的帽子，身穿和服。她侧身而行，鞠躬致意，翩翩起舞，宛如日本舞者。）

(The face of Martin Cunningham, bearded, refeatures Shakespeare’s beardless face. The marquee umbrella sways drunkenly, the children run aside. Under the umbrella appears Mrs Cunningham in Merry Widow hat and kimono gown. She glides sidling and bowing, twirling japanesily.)

坎宁安夫人：（ 唱歌）

MRS CUNNINGHAM: (Sings)

他们称我为亚洲的瑰宝！

And they call me the jewel of Asia!

马丁·坎宁安：（ 面无表情地凝视着她）太棒了！真是个可怕的恶魔！

MARTIN CUNNINGHAM: (Gazes on her, impassive) Immense! Most bloody awful demirep!

斯蒂芬： Et exaltabuntur cornua iusti.女王们与获奖公牛交媾。记住帕西法厄，我的祖父为了满足她的欲望，建造了第一个忏悔室。不要忘记格里塞尔·史蒂文斯夫人，还有兰伯特家族的那些卑鄙的后裔。诺亚喝醉了酒。他的方舟敞开着。

STEPHEN: Et exaltabuntur cornua iusti. Queens lay with prize bulls. Remember Pasiphae for whose lust my grandoldgrossfather made the first confessionbox. Forget not Madam Grissel Steevens nor the suine scions of the house of Lambert. And Noah was drunk with wine. And his ark was open.

贝拉：这里可不是这样。你来错店了。

BELLA: None of that here. Come to the wrong shop.

在原本应该是彻底堕落的时刻，波尔迪却透过钥匙孔偷窥布莱兹·博伊兰与莫莉交媾，以此取乐。一群妓女哄堂大笑，斯蒂芬醉醺醺的同伴林奇指着镜子，笑着引用《哈姆雷特》中的名言：“照镜子，看清自然。” 随后，神秘的景象出现了。斯蒂芬和布卢姆——詹姆斯·乔伊斯笔下的人物——凝视着镜子，映出的却是莎士比亚的脸，他没有胡须，面部僵硬，仿佛面部瘫痪，而戴绿帽者的形象则是由帽架上的驯鹿角构成。这位吟游诗人以和蔼的尊严，用奥利弗·戈德史密斯的诗作《荒村》中的一句误引来责备愚昧的林奇：“大笑暴露了空虚的心灵。” 他对波尔迪说：“你以为你隐形了？” 这对偷窥狂来说，算是温和的责备。但随后，莎士比亚又对波尔迪强调：“看。”他带着悲剧演员那种阴郁的笑声，仿佛在嘲讽被戴绿帽的遭遇，警告波尔迪：“伊阿戈戈！我的老伙计星期四早上都吓得魂飞魄散了。伊阿戈戈！”波尔迪不太可能把莫莉当成苔丝狄蒙娜，但这并非莎士比亚的本意。斯蒂芬生于星期四；他和波尔迪融为一体，莎士比亚化身为哈姆雷特父亲的亡灵，警告这个融合体不要将哈姆雷特与奥赛罗混为一谈，否则莫莉就会变成格特鲁德、苔丝狄蒙娜和斯蒂芬已故母亲的复杂混合体。

In what ought to be a moment of total degradation, Poldy pleasures himself by watching through a keyhole the plowing of Molly by Blazes Boylan. To a chorus of laughing whores, Stephen’s intoxicated companion Lynch points to a mirror and laughingly quotes Hamlet: “The mirror up to nature.” Then mystery intervenes. Stephen and Bloom, components of James Joyce, gaze in the mirror and their reflection is the face of Shakespeare, beardless, rigid in facial paralysis, with the image of the cuckold formed by the reindeer antlers of a hat rack. With amiable dignity, the Bard reproves the mindless Lynch by misquoting Oliver Goldsmith’s poem “The Deserted Village”: “ ’Tis the loud laugh bespeaks the vacant mind.” To Poldy he says, “Thou thoughtest as how thou wastest invisible,” a mild reproof to a Peeping Tom. But then Shakespeare emphasizes to Poldy: “Gaze.” With the dark laughter of the tragedian of supposed cuckoldry, he warns Poldy, “Iagogo! How my Oldfellow chokit his Thursdaymornun. Iagogo!” Poldy is hardly likely to treat Molly as Desdemona, but that is not Shakespeare’s point. Stephen was born on a Thursday; he and Poldy fuse, Shakespeare is the ghost of Hamlet’s father warning the composite figure not to meld Hamlet with Othello, which would make Molly into a complex mix of Gertrude, Desdemona, and Stephen’s dead mother.

但为什么莎士比亚的形象被扭曲成无须胡须、面容僵硬、如同阉鸡一般？我认为，作为先驱的莎士比亚是在嘲讽他的追随者布鲁姆/乔伊斯/斯蒂芬，以此表达：“你们试图在我身上看到自己，但当你们凝视镜子时，看到的却是你们的本来面目；你们没有胡须，所以缺乏我的力量；你们面容僵硬，所以没有我温柔的容颜。” 随后，莎士比亚在《守灵夜》的预言中补充道：“ Weda seca whokilla farst”，这句话改编自《贡扎戈之死 》，由哈姆雷特王子修订，原句为“没有人娶过第二个，除非他杀过第一个”。斯蒂芬引用了《武加大译本》中的诗篇75:10：“义人的角必被高举。”他接着讲到帕西法厄与一头获奖公牛交配，还玩起了诺亚方舟和摩西约柜的文字游戏。贝拉对“他的方舟是开着的”这句话的回应是生硬而又出奇地充满美德的：“这里可不是闹着玩的。你来错地方了。”

But why is the image of Shakespeare so transmuted that he is beardless, a frozen face, and a capon? I think that Shakespeare as precursor mocks his disciple Bloom/Joyce/Stephen so as to say, “You are trying to see yourself in me, but, staring in the mirror, you behold what you are; being beardless, you lack my potency, and, being rigid in facial paralysis, you are void of my gentle countenance.” Shakespeare then adds, in a prophecy of the Wake, “Weda seca whokilla farst,” which reworks “None wed the second but who kill’d the first,” taken from The Murder of Gonzago, as revised by Prince Hamlet. Stephen quotes from Psalm 75:10 in the Vulgate: “And the horns of the righteous shall be exalted.” He goes on to the copulation of Pasiphaë with a prize bull, and to a wordplay on Noah’s Ark and the Ark of the Covenant of Moses. Bella’s response to “his Ark was open” is a brusque and strangely virtuous “None of that here. Come to the wrong shop.”

《瑟茜》的危机源于斯蒂芬母亲的幻影出现：

The crisis of “Circe” comes with the apparition of Stephen’s mother:

斯蒂芬：嚯！

STEPHEN: Ho!

（斯蒂芬的母亲骨瘦如柴，身着麻风病人般的灰色长袍，头戴褪色的橙花花环，披着破烂的婚纱，从地板下狰狞地升起。她面容憔悴，鼻子已然消失，脸上长满了坟墓上的霉菌，呈现出绿色。她的头发稀疏而稀疏。她用那布满青筋的空洞眼窝盯着斯蒂芬，张开没有牙齿的嘴，无声地吐出一个字。一群贞女和忏悔者无声地吟唱着。）

(Stephen’s mother, emaciated, rises stark through the floor in leper grey with a wreath of faded orange blossoms and a torn bridal veil, her face worn and noseless, green with grave mould. Her hair is scant and lank. She fixes her bluecircled hollow eyesockets on Stephen and opens her toothless mouth uttering a silent word. A choir of virgins and confessors sing voicelessly.)

合唱团：

THE CHOIR:

Liliata rutilantium 忏悔室…

Liliata rutilantium te confessorum…

Iubilantium te virginum…

Iubilantium te virginum…

（巴克·穆里根身穿紫红色和黄色相间的丑角服，头戴饰有卷曲铃铛的小丑帽，站在塔顶上，目瞪口呆地望着她，手里拿着一块冒着烟的涂了黄油的切开的烤饼。）

(From the top of a tower Buck Mulligan, in particoloured jester’s dress of puce and yellow and clown’s cap with curling bell, stands gaping at her, a smoking buttered split scone in his hand)

巴克·穆里根：她死得真惨！太可惜了！穆里根见到了这位悲痛欲绝的母亲。（他抬起头）反复无常的马拉基！

BUCK MULLIGAN: She’s beastly dead. The pity of it! Mulligan meets the afflicted mother. (He upturns his eyes) Mercurial Malachi!

母亲：（ 带着死亡般的疯狂微笑）我曾经是美丽的梅·古尔丁。我已经死了。

THE MOTHER: (With the subtle smile of death’s madness) I was once the beautiful May Goulding. I am dead.

斯蒂芬：（ 惊恐万分）狐猴，你是谁？这又是什么妖魔鬼怪的伎俩？

STEPHEN: (Horrorstruck) Lemur, who are you? What bogeyman’s trick is this?

巴克·穆里根：（ 摇晃着他的卷发帽）真是讽刺！金奇杀了她那狗崽子。她死了。（融化的黄油泪水从他眼中滴落到烤饼上。）我们伟大的慈母！ Epi oinopa ponton。

BUCK MULLIGAN: (Shakes his curling capbel) The mockery of it! Kinch killed her dogsbody bitchbody. She kicked the bucket. (Tears of molten butter fall from his eyes into the scone.) Our great sweet mother! Epi oinopa ponton.

母亲：（ 走近他，轻轻地向他吹着沾湿的灰烬气息）每个人都要经历这一切，斯蒂芬。世界上女人比男人多得多。你也一样。时候到了。

THE MOTHER: (Comes nearer, breathing upon him softly her breath of wetted ashes) All must go through it, Stephen. More women than men in the world. You too. Time will come.

斯蒂芬：（ 因恐惧、悔恨和惊恐而哽咽）他们说我杀了你，母亲。他冒犯了你的名誉。是癌症害死了你，不是我。命运。

STEPHEN: (Choking with fright, remorse and horror) They said I killed you, mother. He offended your memory. Cancer did it, not I. Destiny.

母亲：（ 一股绿色的胆汁从她嘴角流出）你曾为我唱过那首歌。爱情苦涩的奥秘。

THE MOTHER: (A green rill of bile trickling from a side of her mouth) You sang that song to me. Love’s bitter mystery.

斯蒂芬：（ 急切地）母亲，如果你知道的话，告诉我那个词。那个所有人都知道的词。

STEPHEN: (Eagerly) Tell me the word, mother, if you know now. The word known to all men.

母亲：那天晚上你和帕迪·李在达尔基跳上火车时，是谁救了你？当你孤身一人，在陌生人中伤心难过时，是谁怜悯你？祈祷的力量无所不能。为受苦的灵魂祈祷，请参考乌尔苏拉修女会的祈祷文，并可获得四十天的宽恕。斯蒂芬，悔改吧。

THE MOTHER: Who saved you the night you jumped into the train at Dalkey with Paddy Lee? Who had pity for you when you were sad among the strangers? Prayer is all powerful. Prayer for the suffering souls in the Ursuline manual, and forty days’ indulgence. Repent, Stephen.

斯蒂芬：食尸鬼！鬣狗！

STEPHEN: The ghoul! Hyena!

母亲：我在另一个世界为你祈祷。让迪莉每天晚上在你脑力劳动后给你煮米饭。我爱你，我的儿子，我的长子，从你还在我腹中的时候起，我就一直爱你。

THE MOTHER: I pray for you in my other world. Get Dilly to make you that boiled rice every night after your brain work. Years and years I loved you, O, my son, my firstborn, when you lay in my womb.

佐伊：（ 用电扇给自己扇风）我要融化了！

ZOE: (Fanning herself with the grate fan) I’m melting!

弗洛里：（ 指着斯蒂芬）看！他是白人。

FLORRY: (Points to Stephen) Look! He’s white.

布鲁姆：（ 走到窗边，把窗户开得更大）吉迪。

BLOOM: (Goes to the window to open it more) Giddy.

母亲：（ 眼神充满怒火）忏悔吧！哦，地狱之火！

THE MOTHER: (With smouldering eyes) Repent! O, the fire of hell!

斯蒂芬：（ 喘息）食尸鬼！生的头颅和血淋淋的骨头！

STEPHEN: (Panting) The corpsechewer! Raw head and bloody bones!

母亲：（ 她的脸越来越近，吐出一口灰）当心！（她缓缓抬起她那焦黑枯槁的右臂，伸出一根手指，指向斯蒂芬的胸口）当心上帝之手！（一只绿色的螃蟹，长着恶毒的红眼睛，咧着嘴，将爪子深深地插入斯蒂芬的心脏）

THE MOTHER: (Her face drawing near and nearer, sending out an ashen breath) Beware! (She raises her blackened, withered right arm slowly towards Stephen’s breast with outstretched finger) Beware God’s hand! (A green crab with malignant red eyes sticks deep its grinning claws in Stephen’s heart)

斯蒂芬：（ 怒火中烧）该死！（他的面容变得憔悴、灰白、苍老）

STEPHEN: (Strangled with rage) Shite! (His features grow drawn and grey and old)

布鲁姆：（ 在窗边）什么？

BLOOM: (At the window) What?

斯蒂芬： 啊，不，举例来说！理性的想象力！要么全盘接受，要么全盘否定。Non serviam！

STEPHEN: Ah non, par exemple! The intellectual imagination! With me all or not at all. Non serviam!

弗洛里：给他点凉水。等等。（她冲了出去）

FLORRY: Give him some cold water. Wait. (She rushes out)

母亲：（ 双手缓缓绞着，绝望地呻吟着）耶稣圣心啊，怜悯他吧！救他脱离地狱，神圣的圣心啊！

THE MOTHER: (Wrings her hands slowly, moaning desperately) O Sacred Heart of Jesus, have mercy on him! Save him from hell, O Divine Sacred Heart!

斯蒂芬：不！不！不！你们都来摧毁我的意志吧！我会让你们都臣服于我！

STEPHEN: No! No! No! Break my spirit, all of you, if you can! I’ll bring you all to heel!

母亲：（ 在临终的痛苦呻吟中）主啊，为了我，求你怜悯司提反！我在髑髅地山上因爱、悲伤和痛苦而死时，我的痛苦是无法言喻的。

THE MOTHER: (In the agony of her deathrattle) Have mercy on Stephen, Lord, for my sake! Inexpressible was my anguish when expiring with love, grief and agony on Mount Calvary.

斯蒂芬： 什么也没有！

STEPHEN: Nothung!

（他双手高举白蜡木，砸碎了吊灯。时间最后的炽烈火焰跃起，随之而来的是一片黑暗，空间尽毁，玻璃破碎，砖石坍塌。）

(He lifts his ashplant high with both hands and smashes the chandelier. Time’s livid final flame leaps and, in the following darkness, ruin of all space, shattered glass and toppling masonry)

燃气喷射器：噗噗！

THE GASJET: Pwfungg!

垂死的母亲、悲痛欲绝的斯蒂芬和最后化身为浮夸的巴克·穆里根之间的互动堪称精妙。我始终不明白为何这段文字会令我如此痛苦。它与我记忆中早已离世的母亲如此遥远，以至于我不得不反思自己对这位接受过耶稣会教育、并对此做出如此强烈反抗的作家的情感理解是否有限。或许应该将其解读为一场戏仿的末日预言，因为斯蒂芬的灰烬植物仅仅撕掉了廉价吊灯上的纸，波尔迪为此给了贝拉一先令，然而舞台指示却几乎是布莱克式的：“时间的最后火焰猛烈跃起，随之而来的是黑暗，所有空间的毁灭，破碎的玻璃和倾倒的砖石。”我们仿佛置身于《四佐阿之夜》的第九夜，只是煤气喷射器发出一声无力的“噗！”打破了这幻象。

The interplay between the deathly mother, the stricken Stephen, and the flamboyant Buck Mulligan in his final manifestation is masterly. I have never understood why this passage hurts me. It is so remote from my memories of my long-ago departed mother that I have to reflect on the limits of my emotional understanding of an author who had a Jesuit education, against which he reacted so formidably. Perhaps it should be read as a mock apocalypse, since Stephen’s ashplant merely tears the paper off the cheap chandelier, for which Poldy gives Bella one shilling, and yet the stage directions are almost Blakean: “Time’s livid final flame leaps and, in the following darkness, ruin of all space, shattered glass and toppling masonry.” We could be in Night the Ninth of The Four Zoas, except that the gasjet punctures illusion with a limp “Pwfungg!”

斯蒂芬：（ 转身）嗯？（他起身离开）为什么我不能和他说话，或者和任何一个在这扁平的橘子上直立行走的人说话？（他指着）如果我看到他的眼睛，我并不害怕和什么人说话。保持垂直。

STEPHEN: (Turns) Eh? (He disengages himself) Why should I not speak to him or to any human being who walks upright upon this oblate orange? (He points his finger) I’m not afraid of what I can talk to if I see his eye. Retaining the perpendicular.

（他踉跄后退了一步）

(He staggers a pace back)

布鲁姆：（ 扶着他）保留你自己的。

BLOOM: (Propping him) Retain your own.

斯蒂芬：（ 空洞地笑了笑）我的重心偏移了。我忘了诀窍。我们找个地方坐下来好好谈谈吧。生存斗争是存在的法则，但是那些人类的仁慈主义者，尤其是沙皇和英国国王，发明了仲裁。（他敲了敲额头）但是在这里，我必须杀死牧师和国王。

STEPHEN: (Laughs emptily) My centre of gravity is displaced. I have forgotten the trick. Let us sit down somewhere and discuss. Struggle for life is the law of existence but but human philirenists, notably the tsar and the king of England, have invented arbitration. (He taps his brow) But in here it is I must kill the priest and the king.

比迪·克拉普：你听到教授说什么了吗？他可是大学里的教授。

BIDDY THE CLAP: Did you hear what the professor said? He’s a professor out of the college.

贱人凯特：我听到了。

CUNTY KATE: I did. I heard that.

BIDDY THE CLAP：他用词如此精妙，表达如此清晰。

BIDDY THE CLAP: He expresses himself with such marked refinement of phraseology.

泼妇凯特：没错。而且言辞如此一针见血。

CUNTY KATE: Indeed, yes. And at the same time with such apposite trenchancy.

卡尔列兵：（ 挣脱束缚，走上前）你们在说什么关于我国王的事？

PRIVATE CARR: (Pulls himself free and comes forward) What’s that you’re saying about my king?

斯蒂芬拍了拍额头，宣布道：“但在这里，我必须杀死祭司和国王。”这番话再次展现了布莱克式的风格。这让我们感到振奋，但士兵们和斯蒂芬一样醉醺醺的，年轻的诗人被一击打倒在地。

It is again very Blakean that Stephen taps his forehead and announces: “But in here it is I must kill the priest and the king.” That cheers us, but the soldiers are as drunk as Stephen is, and the young poet is felled by a blow:

布鲁姆：（ 越过斯蒂芬的肩膀）是的，去吧。你看他根本做不到。

BLOOM: (Over Stephen’s shoulder) Yes, go. You see he’s incapable.

卡尔下士：（ 挣脱束缚）我要羞辱他。

PRIVATE CARR: (Breaks loose) I’ll insult him.

（他冲向斯蒂芬，伸出双拳，一拳打在他的脸上。斯蒂芬踉跄了一下，倒地不起，晕头转向。他趴在地上，脸朝天，帽子滚到墙上。布鲁姆跟过去，捡起了帽子。）

(He rushes towards Stephen, fists outstretched, and strikes him in the face. Stephen totters, collapses, falls, stunned. He lies prone, his face to the sky, his hat rolling to the wall. Bloom follows and picks it up.)

无论我重读多少遍《尤利西斯》，每当看到躺着的斯蒂芬引发布卢姆对他失散的儿子鲁迪的幻觉时，我总是感到震惊：

No matter how often I reread Ulysses, I am always startled when the recumbent Stephen provokes Bloom’s vision of his lost son, Rudy:

（他伸展双臂，再次叹了口气，蜷缩起身子。布鲁姆拿着帽子和梣树，直立着身子。远处传来狗吠声。布鲁姆握紧又放松梣树的手。他低头看着斯蒂芬的脸和身形。）

(He stretches out his arms, sighs again and curls his body. Bloom holding his hat and ashplant stands erect. A dog barks in the distance. Bloom tightens and loosens his grip on the ashplant. He looks down on Stephen’s face and form.)

布鲁姆：（ 与夜交流）这张脸让我想起他可怜的母亲。在阴凉的树林里。深邃的白色胸膛。弗格森，我想我抓住了。一个女孩。一个了不起的女孩。对他来说，这是最好的事……（他低声说。） ……我发誓，我将永远致敬，永远隐藏，永不泄露，任何部分，任何艺术……（他低声说。）在粗糙的海沙上……离岸边一截缆绳……潮起潮落的地方……

BLOOM: (Communes with the night) Face reminds me of his poor mother. In the shady wood. The deep white breast. Ferguson, I think I caught. A girl. Some girl. Best thing could happen him…(He murmurs.)…swear that I will always hail, ever conceal, never reveal, any part or parts, art or arts…(He murmurs.) in the rough sands of the sea…a cabletow’s length from the shore…where the tide ebbs…and flows…

（他沉默不语，若有所思，警觉地站在那里，手指放在嘴唇上，摆出一副神秘主人的姿态。黑暗的墙边缓缓浮现出一个身影，一个十一岁的精灵男孩，一个被掳走的换子，身穿伊顿公学的西装，脚蹬水晶鞋，头戴一顶小小的青铜头盔，手里拿着一本书。他从右往左无声地阅读着，脸上带着微笑，轻轻地亲吻着书页。）

(Silent, thoughtful, alert, he stands on guard, his fingers at his lips in the attitude of secret master. Against the dark wall a figure appears slowly, a fairy boy of eleven, a changeling, kidnapped, dressed in an Eton suit with glass shoes and a little bronze helmet, holding a book in his hand. He reads from right to left inaudibly, smiling, kissing the page.)

布鲁姆：（ 惊叹不已，低声喊道）鲁迪！

BLOOM: (Wonderstruck, calls inaudibly) Rudy!

鲁迪：（ 目光空洞地凝视着布鲁姆，继续读书、亲吻、微笑。他有着一张精致的淡紫色脸庞。他的西装上镶嵌着钻石和红宝石纽扣。他空着的左手拿着一根细长的象牙手杖，上面系着一个紫色的蝴蝶结。一只白色的小羊羔从他的马甲口袋里探出头来。）

RUDY: (Gazes unseeing into Bloom’s eyes and goes on reading, kissing, smiling. He has a delicate mauve face. On his suit he has diamond and ruby buttons. In his free left hand he holds a slim ivory cane with a violet bowknot. A white lambkin peeps out of his waistcoat pocket.)

波尔迪并未察觉斯蒂芬正在低声吟诵叶芝的诗句，他被迫重复了部分共济会的沉默誓言，随后他看到了一个换子鲁迪，虽然他11岁就夭折了，如今却已11岁，身着仙女装束，显然正在阅读《托拉》或《塔木德》，因为他从右向左翻阅，“无声地微笑着，亲吻着书页”。他认不出自己的父亲，而父亲则悲痛地回忆起，婴儿被埋葬在一条白色的羊羔皮里。

Uncomprehending that Stephen is murmuring a Yeatsian lyric, Poldy is prompted to repeat part of his Masonic oath of silence and then beholds a changeling Rudy, now eleven years though he died at eleven days, in fairy garb and evidently reading Torah or Talmud, since he goes from right to left, “inaudibly, smiling, kissing the page.” He does not recognize his father, who remembers heartbreakingly that the infant had been buried in a white lambkin.

尽管《尤利西斯》又延续了三集，最终​​以莫莉热情洋溢的独白达到高潮，但对我而言，鲁迪的幻象——与斯蒂芬母亲的幻影形成对比——才是故事的终点。波尔迪想要斯蒂芬生个儿子，却未能如愿。斯蒂芬保持着原样，因此“犹太希腊人”并没有变成“希腊犹太人”。利奥波德·布卢姆回到了他不忠的妻子佩内洛普身边，并安然入睡，枕着她。莫莉的长篇独白值得所有赞誉，结尾处反复出现的“是的”的合唱更是精彩绝伦。

Though Ulysses goes on for three more episodes, culminating in Molly’s rapturous monologue, for me the vision of Rudy, which counters the apparition of Stephen’s mother, is a destination attained. Poldy wants a son in Stephen but will not find one. Stephen goes forth unaltered, so that jewgreek does not become greekjew. Leopold Bloom returns to his unfaithful Penelope and falls asleep cheerfully enough, resting upon her. Molly’s long soliloquy deserves all the admiration it has been accorded and ends quite gloriously with its repeated chorus of “yes,” one after another.

我并未读过所有关于《芬尼根守灵夜》的评论文章，但我从约翰·毕肖普1986年出版的《乔伊斯的黑暗之书：芬尼根守灵夜》一书中获益良多。我记得当时在伦敦买到这本书，连续几天一口气读完，反复阅读。在过去的三十年里，我多次重读此书，每次都觉得它依然充满新鲜感。

I have not read all the critical studies of Finnegans Wake, but I have learned most from Joyce’s Book of the Dark: Finnegans Wake by John Bishop (1986). I recall purchasing it in London and reading it straight through and back again for several days. During the last thirty years, I have made a number of returns to it and have found it perpetually fresh.

约翰·毕肖普教导我们接受《芬尼根守灵夜》的晦涩之处是刻意为之且不可避免的。乔伊斯决心创作《夜与梦》这部史诗巨著。《尤利西斯》的曙光已然消逝。如同西格蒙德·弗洛伊德一般，乔伊斯也在书写他的《梦之书》。我只正式研读过一次《芬尼根守灵夜》，那是在一个学年里，我参加了桑顿·怀尔德在他位于哈姆登迪普伍德路50号的家中举办的《芬尼根守灵夜》研讨会，那里可以俯瞰纽黑文。当时我是耶鲁大学的研究生，但怀尔德的研讨会与耶鲁大学无关，需要邀请才能参加。我们大多时候都在聆听，因为这位剧作家对乔伊斯作品的深入研究令人印象深刻。后来，在剑桥大学彭布罗克学院，我的导师兼好友是马修·J·C·霍加特，他既研究歌曲，也研究莎士比亚在《芬尼根守灵夜》中无处不在的影响。

John Bishop teaches us to accept that the obscurities of the Wake are deliberate and inevitable. Joyce sets himself to write the epic of Night and Dream. The daylight of Ulysses is gone. Like Sigmund Freud, Joyce writes his Dream Book. I have studied the Wake formally only once, throughout an academic year when I took part in Thornton Wilder’s seminar on the Wake, conducted in his house at 50 Deepwood Drive in Hamden, overlooking New Haven. I was a graduate student at Yale, but Wilder’s seminar was independent of Yale, and you joined by invitation. Mostly we listened, as the dramatist’s immersion in Joyce was impressive. Later, at Pembroke College, Cambridge, my tutor and friend was Matthew J. C. Hodgart, who wrote both on song and on Shakespeare’s endless presence in the Wake.

在《守灵夜》第一卷第七章中，笔杆子谢姆是詹姆斯·乔伊斯创作时的原型。但他是一位生活在莎士比亚阴影下的作家：

Shem the Penman, in Book 1, Chapter 7, of the Wake, is the author James Joyce at work. But he is the author working under the shadow of Shakespeare:

除了疯人院的人，谁会相信这种事呢？无论是尼禄还是诺布基森斯特本人，这两个纯洁的小天使，都从未像这个精神和道德都有缺陷的人（或许是出于他最卑微的虚荣心）那样，对自己的怪诞壮举抱有如此扭曲的看法。据说，有一次，他喝得酩酊大醉，在一家吉普赛酒吧的门廊里，对着一个后来私下里和他一起在卡维哈兹酒吧里厮混的家伙——他的孪生兄弟戴维·布朗-诺兰（这个自称贝斯格勒特的家伙）——说着“咕噜咕噜”而不是“咕噜咕噜”。（他总是亵渎神明，比利，他会试着，老贝利，然后付给这个男人，他那四种汤的信徒，每个内克斯茅斯的姑娘，博利，就像彗星上有尾巴一样确定，就像……）斯托里克四十岁了，他喜欢待在那里，倾听，只有二十分钟，恶霸，他的《幻想民谣》，后来被命名为《酒、女人和水钟，或一个家伙疯了时如何装腔作势》，作者是谢姆斯·德·拉·普卢姆大师（Maistre Sheames de la Plume），一些极其可怕的东西，就像一面杀人的镜子），他承认（老天！）没有其他沙格斯皮克，其他沙基斯比尔德，要么与他的极地安迪西斯完全不同，要么看起来就像他喜欢或猜测的一样，就像他自己一样，然后，欢迎快车、鸭子和暴徒，尽管他像个兔子男孩罗杰一样被卢姆德拉姆茶馆里所有的狮子围攻，因为他是一个失言的语言带着 ruvidubb shortartempa，坏 cad dad fad sad mad nad vanhaty bear，因果关系的 consciquenchers 在 postposition 中预烦扰十字军，scruff，scruffer，scrufferumurraimost 等等，如果 reams 坚持理性，他的 lanka-livline 持续下去，他会把 alley english spooker，multapho-niaksically spuking，从 erse 的脸上擦掉。

But would anyone, short of a madhouse, believe it? Neither of those clean little cherubum, Nero or Nobookisonester himself, ever nursed such a spoiled opinion of his monstrous marvellosity as did this mental and moral defective (here perhaps at the vanessance of his lownest) who was known to grognt rather than gunnard upon one occasion, while drinking heavily of spirits to that interlocutor a latere and private privysuckatary he used to pal around with, in the kavehazs, one Davy Browne-Nowlan, his heavenlaid twin, (this hambone dogpoet pseudoed himself under the hangname he gave himself of Bethgelert) in the porchway of a gipsy’s bar (Shem always blaspheming, so holy writ, Billy, he would try, old Belly, and pay this one manjack congregant of his four soups every lass of nexmouth, Bolly, so sure as thair’s a tail on a commet, as a taste for storik’s fortytooth, that is to stay, to listen out, ony twenny minnies moe, Bully, his Ballade Imaginaire which was to be dubbed Wine, Woman and Waterclocks, or How a Guy Finks and Fawkes When He Is Going Batty, by Maistre Sheames de la Plume, some most dreadful stuff in a murderous mirrorhand) that he was avoopf (parn me!) aware of no other shaggspick, other Shakhisbeard, either prexactly unlike his polar andthisishis or procisely the seem as woops (parn!) as what he fancied or guessed the sames as he was himself and that, greet scoot, duckings and thuggery, though he was foxed fux to fux like a bunnyboy rodger with all the teashop lionses of Lumdrum hivanhoesed up gagainst him, being a lapsis linquo with a ruvidubb shortartempa, bad cad dad fad sad mad nad vanhaty bear, the consciquenchers of casuality prepestered crusswords in postposition, scruff, scruffer, scrufferumurraimost andallthatsortofthing, if reams stood to reason and his lanka-livline lasted he would wipe alley english spooker, multapho-niaksically spuking, off the face of the erse.

我不想逐句逐字地解读这段文字，因为这样的译者比比皆是。顺其自然，大声吟诵，最重要的东西自然会显现。沙格斯皮克和沙基斯比尔德让我们回到那面映照自然的镜子，斯蒂芬和布卢姆在镜子中看到一个没有胡须的莎士比亚凝视着他们，从而宣告了他的优先地位和他的延续。然而，谢姆的自负依然占据上风。乔伊斯不会改写莎士比亚，尽管他无法停止借鉴他的作品。

I do not want to try to decipher this phrase by phrase, word by word, as there are a plenitude of such translators. Go with the drift, chanting this aloud, and what matters most will reveal itself to you. Shaggspick and Shakhisbeard return us to the mirror up to nature in which Stephen and Bloom beheld a beardless Shakespeare staring out at them and thus proclaiming his priority and his continuance.
