And copied out what I could read

In that religious gloom;

Found many a famous man there;

But fame and virtue rot.

Draw round, beloved and bitter men,

Draw round and raise a shout;

罗杰·凯斯门特的鬼魂

The ghost of Roger Casement

正在猛烈敲门。

Is beating on the door.

我发现，理解塞巴尔德作品的一个难点在于，他的结尾即是他的开始。以下是《土星之环》的结尾：

I find that one of my problems in absorbing Sebald is that in his end is his beginning. Here is the close of The Rings of Saturn:

因此，帝国食品和农业部长、劳工部长、林业部长和航空部长启动了一项养蚕计划，开启了德国养蚕业的新纪元。位于柏林的帝国养蚕协会是帝国德国小型动物饲养者联合会的成员组织，而后者又隶属于帝国农业委员会。该协会的任务是提高现有养蚕作坊的产量，在报刊、电影院和广播中宣传养蚕业，建立示范养蚕场用于教学，在地方、地区和区域层面组织咨询机构为所有养蚕户提供支持，提供桑树，并在闲置土地、居民区、墓地、路边、铁路路堤和帝国高速公路沿线种植数百万棵桑树。据教育手册F213/1939的作者兰格教授所述，养蚕业在德国的意义不仅在于避免从国外进口丝绸，从而减轻外汇储备的压力，更在于丝绸在空战时代初期以及构建自给自足的国防经济中的重要性。因此，学校应当激发德国青年对养蚕的兴趣，但并非像腓特烈大帝时期那样强制推行。相反，应该鼓励教职工和学生自发地从事养蚕业。兰格教授建议，学校可以在这方面发挥开拓作用。可以在校园周围种植桑树，并在校舍内养蚕。毕竟，教授补充道，除了其无可置疑的实用价值之外，蚕也是课堂上近乎理想的教具。几乎可以免费获得任意数量的蚕，它们性情温顺，无需笼子或饲养箱，而且在其进化的各个阶段都适合进行各种实验（称重、测量等等）。它们可以用来展示昆虫解剖结构和特征、昆虫驯化、退化突变，以及育种者为监测生产力和进行选育而采取的必要措施，包括为防止种族退化而进行的灭绝。——在影片中，我们看到一位丝工接收了由位于策勒的中央帝国蚕业研究所送来的蚕卵，并将它们放入无菌托盘中。我们看到了蚕卵孵化、喂养饥饿的毛虫、清理蚕框、吐丝，以及最后的杀死过程。与过去常用的做法不同，这次不是将蚕茧放在阳光下或高温烤箱中烘烤，而是将它们悬挂在沸腾的大锅上方。茧被摊放在浅篮子里，必须在上升的蒸汽中保持三个小时以上。当一批动物被宰杀完毕后，就轮到下一批，如此反复，直到整个宰杀过程结束。

今天，当我结束这些笔记时，是1995年4月13日。今天是圣周四，纪念基督为门徒洗脚的节日，也是圣阿加顿、圣卡普斯、圣帕皮卢斯和圣赫尔门吉尔德的瞻礼日。397年前的今天，亨利四世颁布了南特敕令；253年前，亨德尔的《弥赛亚》在都柏林首演；223年前，沃伦·黑斯廷斯被任命为孟加拉总督；113年前，反犹联盟在普鲁士成立；74年前，发生了阿姆利则惨案，戴尔将军下令军队向聚集在贾利安瓦拉巴格广场的一万五千名叛乱民众开枪，以儆效尤。很可能有些受害者从事蚕丝养殖业，当时蚕丝养殖业在阿姆利则地区乃至整个印度都处于起步阶段，尽管基础非常简陋。

五十年前的今天，英国报纸报道说，策勒城已被攻陷，德军正从沿多瑙河谷推进的红军手中仓皇撤退。最后，1995年4月13日，圣周四，也是克拉拉的父亲在被送往科堡医院后不久去世的日子。如今，当我写下这些文字，再次回想起我们的历史——这不过是一部漫长的灾难史——我突然想到，在过去，对于上流社会的女士来说，表达深切悲痛的唯一恰当方式，就是身着厚重的黑色丝绸塔夫绸或黑色绉绸长袍。例如，在维多利亚女王的葬礼上，据说泰克公爵夫人身着一件令人叹为观止的礼服亮相，当时的时尚杂志将其描述为一件飘逸的面纱礼服，全部由黑色曼图亚丝绸制成。诺里奇丝绸织造商 Willett & Nephew 在公司永久关闭之前，专门为此次场合制作了一件长达约 60 步的曼图亚丝绸，以展示他们在制作丧服丝绸方面无与伦比的技艺。丝绸商人的儿子托马斯·布朗爵士或许对这些事情很有眼光，他在《伪科学大全》的一段文字中写道：“我再也找不到任何资料表明，在他那个时代的荷兰，如果有人去世，人们习惯于在所有镜子和所有描绘风景、人物或田野果实的画布上挂上黑色的丧葬丝带，这样灵魂在离开身体时，就不会在最后的旅程中被自身的倒影或对即将永远失去的土地的最后瞥见所干扰。

Hence the Reich ministers of food and agriculture, of labour, of forestry and of aviation had launched a sericulture programme, inaugurating a new era of silk cultivation in Germany. The Reich Association of Silkworm Breeders in Berlin, a constituent group within the Reich Federation of German Breeders of Small Animals, which in turn was affiliated to the Reich Agricultural Commission, saw its task as increasing production in every existing workshop, advertising silk cultivation in the press, in the cinema and on radio, establishing model rearing units for educational purposes, organizing advisory bodies at local, district and regional level to support all silk-growers, providing mulberry trees, and planting them by the million on unutilized land, in residential areas and cemeteries, by roadsides, on railway embankments and along the Reich’s autobahns. According to Professor Lange, the author of educational pamphlet F213/1939, the significance of silk cultivation in Germany lay not only in obviating the need to buy from abroad, and so easing the pressure on foreign currency reserves, but also in the importance silk would have in the dawning era of aerial warfare and hence in the formation of a self-sufficient economy of national defence. For that reason, it was desirable that schools should interest the youth of Germany in silk cultivation, although not under compulsion, as in the days of Frederick the Great. Rather, the teaching staff and pupils should be motivated to practise sericulture of their own accord. Schools might do pioneering work in this sector, suggested Professor Lange. Schoolyards might have mulberries planted along their perimeters, and silkworms could be reared in the school buildings. After all, the Professor added, quite apart from their indubitable utility value, silkworms afforded an almost ideal object lesson for the classroom. Any number could be had for virtually nothing, they were perfectly docile and needed neither cages nor compounds, and they were suitable for a variety of experiments (weighing, measuring and so forth) at every stage in their evolution. They could be used to illustrate the structure and distinctive features of insect anatomy, insect domestication, retrogressive mutations, and the essential measures which are taken by breeders to monitor productivity and selection, including extermination to preempt racial degeneration.—In the film, we see a silk-worker receiving eggs despatched by the Central Reich Institute of Sericulture in Celle, and depositing them in sterile trays. We see the hatching, the feeding of the ravenous caterpillars, the cleaning out of the frames, the spinning of the silken thread, and finally the killing, accomplished in this case not by putting the cocoons out in the sun or in a hot oven, as was often the practice in the past, but by suspending them over a boiling cauldron. The cocoons, spread out on shallow baskets, have to be kept in the rising steam for upwards of three hours, and when a batch is done, it is the next one’s turn, and so on until the entire killing business is completed.

Today, as I bring these notes to a conclusion, is the 13th of April 1995. It is Maundy Thursday, the feast day on which Christ’s washing of the disciples’ feet is remembered, and also the feast day of Saints Agathon, Carpus, Papylus and Hermengild. On this very day three hundred and ninety-seven years ago, Henry IV promulgated the Edict of Nantes; Handel’s Messiah was first performed two hundred and fifty-three years ago, in Dublin; Warren Hastings was appointed Governor-General of Bengal two hundred and twenty-three years ago; the Anti-Semitic League was founded in Prussia one hundred and thirteen years ago; and, seventy-four years ago, the Amritsar massacre occurred, when General Dyer ordered his troops to fire on a rebellious crowd of fifteen thousand that had gathered in Jallianwala Bagh square, to set an example. Quite possibly some of the victims were employed in silk cultivation, which was developing at that time, on the simplest of foundations, in the Amritsar region and indeed throughout India.

Fifty years ago to the day, British newspapers reported that the city of Celle had been taken and that German forces were in the headlong retreat from the Red Army, which was advancing up the Danube valley. And finally, Maundy Thursday, the 13th of April 1995, was also the day on which Clara’s father, shortly after being taken to hospital in Coburg, departed this life. Now, as I write, and think once more of our history, which is but a long account of calamities, it occurs to me that at one time the only acceptable expression of profound grief, for ladies of the upper classes, was to wear heavy robes of black silk taffeta or black crêpe de chine. Thus at Queen Victoria’s funeral, for example, the Duchess of Teck allegedly made her appearance in what contemporary fashion magazines described as a breathtaking gown with billowing veils, all of black Mantua silk of which the Norwich silk weavers Willett & Nephew, just before the firm closed down for good, had created, uniquely for this occasion, and in order to demonstrate their unsurpassed skills in the manufacture of mourning silks, a length of some sixty paces. And Sir Thomas Browne, who was the son of a silk merchant and may well have had an eye for these things, remarks in a passage of the Pseudodoxia Epidemica that I can no longer find that in the Holland of his time it was customary, in a home where there had been a death, to drape black mourning ribbons over all the mirrors and all canvasses depicting landscapes or people or the fruits of the field, so that the soul, as it left the body, would not be distracted on its final journey, either by a reflection of itself or by a last glimpse of the land now being lost for ever.

这段文字中的每一句话，甚至每一个短语，都承载着灾难性的负担，但其中有一句话是塞巴尔德所有作品的母题：

Every sentence, indeed every phrase, in this passage carries a catastrophic burden but one sentence is the matrix of everything that Sebald wrote:

它们可以用来说明昆虫解剖结构和独特特征、昆虫驯化、退化突变，以及育种者为监测生产力和选择而采取的基本措施，包括为防止种族退化而进行的灭绝。

They could be used to illustrate the structure and distinctive features of insect anatomy, insect domestication, retrogressive mutations, and the essential measures which are taken by breeders to monitor productivity and selection, including extermination to preempt racial degeneration.

我从未见过塞巴尔德，但我记得从1955年到20世纪90年代末，我曾在英国和美国与他的朋友迈克尔·汉堡有过几次交谈。之后我们失去了联系，他于2007年在萨福克郡的家中去世。我欣赏汉堡自己的诗作以及他的译作，其中包括塞巴尔德和保罗·策兰的作品。我们从未讨论过塞巴尔德，但我记得曾仔细聆听汉堡朗诵策兰的诗，先是德语朗诵，然后是他自己引人入胜的译本。策兰49岁时投塞纳河自尽，带走了他那几乎无法估量的诗歌天赋。和卡夫卡一样，策兰用德语写作，仿佛在用希伯来语写作。当我读完《土星之环》时，策兰的形象萦绕在我的脑海中。

I never met Sebald, but I recall conversations with his friend Michael Hamburger in both England and the United States at various times from 1955 through the late 1990s. After that we lost touch, and he died in 2007 at his home in Suffolk. I admired Hamburger’s own poems as well as his translations, which included Sebald and Paul Celan. We never discussed Sebald, but I remember listening to Hamburger closely as he recited Celan, first in German and then in Hamburger’s own arresting versions. Celan drowned himself in the Seine at the age of forty-nine, taking with him a poetic gift almost incommensurable. Like Kafka, Celan writes German as if he is writing in Hebrew. Celan’s image haunts me as I conclude The Rings of Saturn.

第四十八章

CHAPTER 48

数字之书（2015）

Book of Numbers (2015)

J OSHUA C OHEN

JOSHUA COHEN

刚满三十八岁的约书亚·科恩是一位小说家，他有一种既迷人又注定失败的天赋，能唤起那些名声显赫的散文家们模棱两可的言论。我对这些矛盾的回响无法产生热情，不过，我对美国年轻一代小说家的了解确实有限。除了科恩之外，我还欣赏威廉·吉拉尔迪和内尔·弗罗伊登伯格等人的作品。

A NOVELIST WHO HAS just turned thirty-eight, Joshua Cohen has a charmed and doomed gift for evoking equivocal emanations from excessively eminent essayists. I cannot exert enthusiasm for these ambivalent echoing reverberations, but, then, I do not possess extensive erudition on the question of our younger American novelists. In addition to Cohen, I admire William Giraldi and Nell Freudenberger, among others.

我赞同威廉·吉拉尔迪对美国人胆识的赞扬。约书亚·科恩的胆识远超常人，而且无疑会一直如此。胆识若要成为一种审美价值，就必须获得真正的自由。

I agree with William Giraldi’s exaltation of American audacity. Joshua Cohen is audacious beyond audacity and doubtless will remain so. In order to become an aesthetic value, audacity must acquire authentic freedom.

我的学生安德鲁·福特在他的著作《荷马：昔日的诗歌》（1992）中，思考了《伊利亚特》和《奥德赛》与那些如今已失传的早期史诗之间的竞争。争夺首要地位的竞争，是古希腊文化的中心。品达与赫西俄德和荷马展开较量，雅典的悲剧作家们也彼此挑战。约书亚·科恩作为小说家，肩负着双重重担。一方面，他要与更早的托马斯·品钦——《拍卖第49批》、 《万有引力之虹》和 《梅森与迪克森》的作者——竞争。更令人不安的是，他继承了犹太裔美国小说的传统：纳撒尼尔·韦斯特的《寂寞芳心小姐》（1933）；亨利·罗斯的《称之为睡眠》（1934）；伯纳德·马拉默德的《助手》（1957）；索尔·贝娄的《洪堡的礼物》（1975）。辛西娅·奥齐克的《斯德哥尔摩的弥赛亚》（1987 年）；菲利普·罗斯的《安息日剧院》（1995 年）。

My former student Andrew Ford, in his book Homer: The Poetry of the Past (1992), mulls over the contest that Iliad and Odyssey had to conduct with prior epics now lost to us. Agon, the competition for the foremost place, is the center of ancient Greek culture. Pindar strives with Hesiod and with Homer, and the Athenian tragedians challenge one another. Joshua Cohen has a double burden as a novelist. On the one side, he contends with the earlier Thomas Pynchon, the maker of The Crying of Lot 49, Gravity’s Rainbow, Mason & Dixon. More darkly, he is the inheritor of the Jewish American novel: Nathanael West’s Miss Lonelyhearts (1933); Henry Roth’s Call It Sleep (1934); Bernard Malamud’s The Assistant (1957); Saul Bellow’s Humboldt’s Gift (1975); Cynthia Ozick’s The Messiah of Stockholm (1987); Philip Roth’s Sabbath’s Theater (1995).

按照约书亚·科恩的风格，我将以《民数记》的结尾作为我的起点：

As befits Joshua Cohen, I will take the end of Book of Numbers as my beginning:

据称，11月19日或20日，一具尸体在印度瓦拉纳西的恒河中被打捞上来。地点就在玛尼卡尼卡河坛下游不远处，那里是主要的火葬场，一具具燃烧的尸体从河岸倾泻而下，但触底后却不会溅起水花，因为河底的一切都已化为灰烬，只见成群的苍蝇在水面上飞舞。

我只能推测，印度当局通常不会费心处理一个漂浮的尸体，但他显然是白人，或者说他剩下的部分是白人。其他或同一批印度当局展现出令人印象深刻的行动特权，下令进行尸检，确定死因是意外/自杀，并下令进行DNA检测，将结果和报告都抄送给了美国国务院，结果显示基因标记与校长相符。萨里·阿普特·勒·瓦伊请求归还遗体，但遗体损毁严重，如同鳄鱼撕咬一般，最终被火化，并非在玛尼卡尼卡火葬场，而是在另一处火葬场。目前还没有遗体的照片或视频流出，就像丢失的胰腺一样。

事情又回到了莫伊时代——但因为PBS播完没有莉莎贝丝的赛斯节目后我就关掉了电视，所以我只能从《阿斯伯里公园新闻报》、《新泽西犹太新闻》以及妈妈还订阅的那些非园艺类的杂刊（虽然送报一直不太准时）的零碎片段中拼凑出这件事。还有家里的调制解调器，自从我搬来就坏了——妈妈甚至都不记得它是什么时候坏的。

我没法去Wawa便利店，也不能让妈妈替我去，所以我戒了酒，也戒了烟，大概是这样吧。我在阁楼里找了点事做，整理一下传家宝。突然间，家里所有重物都得搬走。直到冬令时来临，暴风雪预警发布，草坪上的遮荫物才被撤走。

卡尔给我打了电话留言，但我还没回复他。芬恩也给我打了电话留言，说他会考虑重印我的书，让我保持联系。

我没有去过。我从未发表过声明——我只是写了文章。

想想看：十二个莫伊闯入了校长在四合院举行的“冥想纪念会”，其中四个人合法地名叫毗湿奴，还有一个人甚至名叫毗湿奴·费尔南德斯。库伦·德·格罗夫和奥玛·奥奎因朗读了《西藏度亡经》中的一段经文：“空不能伤空，无质不能伤无质。”

由于事先在百慕大有安排，以及提前退休并享有检控豁免权，科里·迪内罗维茨未能出席。

大约在同一时间，皮尤研究中心进行了一项民意调查，询问美国民众，政府的在线监控举措是否合理（62%），是否不合理（28%），只有 10% 的人尚未决定。

到了12月，果阿邦维尔纳工业区的排水涵洞里又发现了一具泛白的尸体。发现尸体的男孩竟然认出了尸体，并将照片和视频发布到了网上。据信，这些照片和视频相当逼真：尸体是校长，已经开始腐烂。之后发生了一些事，比如男孩的父亲在没有联系任何人的情况下，甚至可能对儿子的所作所为毫不知情，试图出售尸体。但他被抓住了。或者，从他手中买下尸体并联系了萨里·阿普特·勒·瓦伊的人被抓住了，尸体被扣押了，或者其他什么情况，但据小报报道，尸体在检验前就丢失了。随后，在开罗、里斯本、纳布卢斯郊外的基夫勒·哈里斯（巴勒斯坦领土）等地也发现了尸体。各种传闻层出不穷，甚至在巴西也出现了活人目击事件。校长则成了芬兰一家迪斯科舞厅里的过客。时光飞逝，我四十岁了。一个孩子在石川县金泽市出生，他的灵魂被认为是他的。

A body was hauled out of the river Ganges, Varanasi, India, 11/19 or 20, apparently. This was just downstream from the Manikarnika Ghat, the main crematorium ghat, a perpetual stream of burning bodies plunging down the stairs but not plashing at bottom because by the bottom all was ash, a cloud of flies scattering across the waters.

I can only assume that the Indian authorities wouldn’t ordinarily bother with a floater, but he was white, or what was left of him was white, apparently. Other or the same Indian authorities, evincing impressive operational prerogative, ordered an autopsy that determined the COD as accidental/suicide, ordered a DNA test and copied both the results and report to the US State Department, which matched the genetic markers as being Principal’s. Sari Apt Le Vay petitioned for the body’s return, but it was in such a bitten crocodilian or ultimately imaginary condition that it was cremated, not at the Manikarnika but in a facility. No pics or vids of the body exist or have—like a missing pancreas—leaked yet.

It was Moe all over again—but because I switched off the TV after PBS had on Seth without Lisabeth, I can only piece this together from scrap bits of the Asbury Park Press, the NJ Jewish News, and whatever general interest nonpotting rags Moms still subscribes to, though delivery’s been iffy. And the house modem, which has been broken since I got here—Moms doesn’t even remember it breaking.

I couldn’t go to Wawa and couldn’t have Moms go for me, so I quit drinking, quit smoking, I guess. I made myself useful in the attic department, heirloom rearrangements. Suddenly everything heavy in the house had to be moved. The coverage didn’t leave the lawn until purdah season’s winter storm advisory.

Cal called and left a msg, and I still haven’t gotten back to him. Finn called and left a msg saying he’d consider a reprint of my book, be sure to be in touch.

I haven’t been. I never made a statement—I wrote.

Consider this: A dozen Moes crashed Principal’s “medimorial” (meditation memorial) held at the Tetplex, four of them legally named Vishnu, and one even named Vishnu Fernandes. Cullen de Groeve and Owmar O’Quinn read a selection from the Tibetan Book of the Dead: “Void cannot injure void, the qualityless cannot injure the qualityless.”

Kori Dienerowitz did not attend due to a prior commitment in Bermuda, a premature retirement with prosecutorial immunity.

A Pew Research poll, of around this date, queried a responsible sampling of Americans as to whether their government’s online surveillance initiatives were justified (62%)? or unjustified (28%)? with only 10% undecided.

Into December, another whitish body washed up in a drainage culvert at the Verna Industrial Estate, Goa, and the boy who found it, shockingly recognizing his find, posted the pics and vids online, which were reasonably convincing, according to the convinced: Principal, already decaying. Anyway, something happened next like the boy’s father without contacting anyone, perhaps without even being privy to his son’s exploits, tried selling the body. But he was caught. Or the guy who’d bought it from him and contacted Sari Apt Le Vay was caught, the body taken into custody or whatever, but lost before tests, according to the tabloids. Subsequent corpses turned up in Cairo, Lisbon, Kifl Haris outside Nablus (Palestinian Territories). The great wheel turned and memed. Live in the flesh spottings in Brazil were a thing. Principal was a wayfarer in a Finnish disco. The wheel was turning me 40. A child was born in Kanazawa, Ishikawa, whose soul was recognized as his.

这位负责人是另一位约书亚·科恩，他是Tetration公司的创始人兼高管，这家公司从一家初创公司发展成为互联网、计算机、智能手机和政府监控领域的科技巨头。他聘请了我们这位约书亚·科恩（大家都叫他乔什）为他代笔撰写自传。乔什带着些许苦涩（虽然情有可原），却又带着一种不准确的预言感，喜欢自称“一个失败的小说家”。

Principal is the other Joshua Cohen, founder and high satrap of Tetration, the ultimate startup turned tech titan of the Internet, computers, smartphones, and government surveillance. He has hired our Joshua Cohen, familiarly Josh, to ghostwrite his autobiography. Josh, with somewhat justified bitterness but with an inaccurate sense of prophecy, likes to refer to himself as “a failed novelist.”

—

要想公正地评价约书亚·科恩，就必须从他作品的艰涩性说起。他是一位晦涩难懂的作家，而且很可能在未来的作品中更加晦涩难懂。如今的读者往往避之不及，因为他们很容易被各种事物分散注意力。“屏幕时代”正在威胁着小说艺术的存续。约书亚·科恩是一位雄心勃勃的小说家。他内心深处的渴望是超越他的前辈，无论是犹太人还是非犹太人。《数字之书》本身就足够晦涩难懂，因此不得不依靠虚构的技巧来抚慰读者艰难的阅读体验。

If you are to do critical justice to Joshua Cohen, you have to begin with the necessity of difficulty. He is a difficult writer and is likely to become even more difficult. These days readers shun difficulty, because they are so desperately distracted. The Age of the Screen jeopardizes the art of the novel. Joshua Cohen is an immensely ambitious novelist. His innermost desire is to transcend his precursors, Jewish and Gentile. Book of Numbers is difficult enough and has to call upon invention to palliate readers having an arduous experience.

当我重读《民数记》时，我想起了我与已故的威廉·加迪斯的私人交情，以及1955年第一次阅读《辨认录》时那不可思议的经历。约书亚·科恩博览群书，而且都是阅读原文，他无疑也了解《辨认录》。去年我重读了《辨认录》，起初我努力抗拒沉浸其中，但最终还是屈服了。它与《克莱门汀辨认录》有关，后者是一部存疑的公元三世纪作品。表面上，《克莱门汀辨认录》反对诺斯替教，但它却奇特地推崇撒玛利亚的西蒙·马格斯这位传奇人物。西蒙·马格斯是公元一世纪一位著名的江湖骗子和奇迹创造者，他声称自己与神合一，并与推罗的一位妓女结为伴侣。西蒙宣称她是特洛伊的海伦的转世，是上帝思想中堕落的元素。由于克莱门汀教义是基督教的，西蒙·马格斯被宣称为所有诺斯替主义的创始人。在与圣彼得的悬浮术比赛中，西蒙坠落身亡。

When I reread Book of Numbers I remember my personal acquaintance with the late William Gaddis and the uncanny experience of first reading The Recognitions in 1955. Since Joshua Cohen has read everything, and in the original languages, doubtless he knows The Recognitions. I reread The Recognitions last year and was again a reader who fought against immersion but gradually yielded to it. It is linked to the Clementine Recognitions, a work dubiously ascribed to the third century of the Common Era. Ostensibly set against the Gnostics, the Clementine Recognitions curiously exalt the marvelous figure of Simon Magus of Samaria, a first-century C.E. grand charlatan and miracle worker who asserted an identity with the divine, and who matched himself with a whore of Tyre. Simon declared her the reincarnation of Helen of Troy, and the fallen element in God’s thought. Since the Clementine Recognitions are Christian, Simon Magus is declared the founder of all Gnosticism. In a levitation contest with Saint Peter, Simon plunges to his death.

约书亚·科恩并非诺斯替教徒，而更接近于一位正统的犹太人。他内心深处信赖耶和华与犹太民族之间的盟约。他没有丝毫幻想，因为他深知犹太历史的全部沉重。然而，每当他研读圣贤的著作，无论是古代的、哈西德派的还是现代的，总会流露出一丝淡淡的惆怅。我自己也意识到，当我这样做时，我所研究的不过是怀旧之情，仅此而已。耶和华已经背弃了盟约，我又有什么资格去拾起这破碎的碎片呢？小说家、诗人或剧作家或许可以做到，但世俗的圣经诠释者却无能为力。约书亚·科恩和哈罗德·布鲁姆都喜欢引用塔尔丰拉比的话：“你无需完成这项工作，但你也不能放弃它。”约书亚·科恩试图完成这项工作。而我，很久以前就放弃了。

Joshua Cohen is no Gnostic but something close to a normative Jew. Implicitly he trusts in the Covenant between Yahweh and the Jewish people. He has no illusions, because he knows the full burden of Jewish history. Yet there is a wistful quality whenever he turns to the Sages, whether ancient, Hasidic, or modern. I myself am aware that when I do so, I am studying the nostalgias and little more. Yahweh broke the Covenant, and who am I to gather the shards? A novelist, poet, or dramatist might do it, but not a secular exegete. Both Joshua Cohen and Harold Bloom are addicted to quoting Rabbi Tarfon: “You are not required to complete the work, but neither are you free to desist from it.” Joshua Cohen is trying to complete the work. Long ago I desisted from it.

犹太教的信任和犹太身份的容器已经破碎。格尔松·肖勒姆（1897-1982）——在他生命的最后一年零八个月里，我曾与他相处许多小时，认真聆听他的教诲——会否认这种说法。然而，肖勒姆伪装成一位卡巴拉历史学者，实际上却是一位先知，一位回归阿摩司和弥迦时代的先知。约书亚·科恩没有如此崇高的抱负，但他同样渴望看到破碎的容器得以修复。

The vessels of Judaic trust and of Jewish identity have broken. Gershom Scholem (1897–1982), to whom I listened attentively during many hours we spent together in the last year and eight months of his life, would have denied that sentence. And yet Scholem, who masked as a historical scholar of Kabbalah, truly was a navi, a throwback to Amos and Micah. Joshua Cohen has no such exalted ambition, yet he also wants to see the broken vessels mended.

约书亚·科恩的一大雄心壮志是与幽灵展开一场搏斗。他为犹太传统中所有逝去的事物——语言、信任、仁慈——而感到忧虑。他的哀叹也延伸至爱默生和沃尔特·惠特曼的超凡境界，这些境界已然失落。修补（Tikkun），即修复破碎的器皿，是他最深切的渴望。他满怀希望地认为，他的作品将成为修补的工具。我不能忽略他最近的小说《移动的国王》（2017），因为这部小说也试图进行修补。对约书亚·科恩而言，这意味着在修补口传律法和被其所淹没之间找到一种微妙的平衡。我冒昧地引用他好心寄给我的一封信中的一段话：

One of Joshua Cohen’s dazzling ambitions is to conduct an agon with phantoms. He is haunted by all the losses in Jewish tradition—of language, trust, benignity. His lamentation extends also to the transcendence of Emerson and of Walt Whitman, which is lost to us. Tikkun, the mending of the broken vessels, is his deepest desire. His exorbitant hope is that his books will be the mending. I must not neglect his recent novel, Moving Kings (2017), since that attempts tikkun. For Joshua Cohen, that is to achieve a perilous balance between mending the Oral Law or being overwhelmed by it. I take the liberty of quoting from a letter he kindly sent me:

《移动的国王》第一部分是我对罗斯/马拉默德/贝娄的致敬——大卫·金是他们时代的产物，而非我这个时代的产物。第二部分是我对以色列小说的致敬——以色列小说的创作初衷是在一片新的土地上创造一种新的语言，但又不断地与《塔纳赫》（希伯来圣经）相联系，并时而沉浸于这种张力之中，时而又对其保持警惕。第三部分是我试图将两者融合的尝试，但出人意料的是，我部分地借用了一位对两者都抱有怀疑的黑人穆斯林的视角。

我认为，这最好地概括了我对“疗愈的统一性”的态度：一个破碎的传统本身永远无法恢复完整，但它的碎片只能与另一个破碎的传统碎片结合起来，形成一个全新的、前所未有的整体，而将这个整体维系在一起的人，对这种行为本身感到怀疑甚至羞愧，但却无能为力——历史上也无能为力——去做其他任何事情。

我认为这种束缚是永恒的，并且会不断延续——正如我在《移动的君王》一书中写道： “追随一颗星辰的难处在于，你该止步于何处？很难说它何时会告诉你放下重担。因为一颗星辰似乎总是凌驾于一切之上，它似乎总是一道难以逾越的障碍。你所能做的就是不断追随，直到你被它蒙蔽。”

The first section of Moving Kings is my homage to Roth/Malamud/Bellow—David King is a creature of their times, not of mine. The second section is my homage to the Israeli novel—written with the impulse to create a new language in a new land, but constantly recalled to the Tanach, and alternately reveling in and wary of that tension. The third section is my attempt to unite the two, but perversely to do it partially in the voice of a black Muslim who mistrusts both.

This, I think, is the best summation of my attitude toward the “unity” of healing: A broken tradition can never be made whole again in and of itself, but rather its pieces can only be combined with the pieces of another broken tradition, into a new and never-before-imagined whole, bound together by someone suspicious of and even ashamed by the very activity but unable—historically unable—to do anything else.

This binding I take to be perpetual, and perpetualizing—as I write in Moving Kings, “The thing about following a star is where do you stop? Hard to tell where it’s telling you to lay down your burden. Because a star can always seem to be above everything, it can always seem a block beyond. All you can do is follow until you’ve fooled yourself.”

我无法企及那种紧迫感，但它却深深地打动了我。然而，科恩对“四重奏”（Tetration）的描述如此巧妙，以至于可以被解读为一种戏谑的英雄式嬉戏。从某种意义上说，《数字之书》（Book of Numbers）就像一枚射向互联网的导弹，而从另一个角度来看，它又大胆地试图占据那片空旷的海洋。与菲利普·罗斯及其众多先驱不同，他们沉溺于双重身份的纠缠，约书亚·科恩则在互联网的深渊中寻找另一个自我。或许科恩真正的先驱是赫尔曼·梅尔维尔，他曾在抄写员的办公室和捕鲸船上探寻暧昧之处。一种愿意接受困境的耐心可以支撑到美好的时光再次到来——如果真的会到来的话。这或许就是约书亚·科恩能够如此危险地吸收困扰我的东西的原因：

I cannot hope to achieve that urgency but it moves me almost beyond measure. Yet so ingenious is Cohen’s account of Tetration that it can be read as mock-heroic frolic. In one way, Book of Numbers is a missile launched against the Internet, yet in another, it boldly attempts to appropriate that vacant ocean. Unlike Philip Roth and his many precursors, for whom doubling hooked identities, Joshua Cohen seeks his other self in the abyss of the Internet. It may be that Cohen’s true forerunner is Herman Melville, who sought out the ambiguities in scriveners’ offices and on whalers. A patience willing to accept a bad time can prevail until the good time comes again, if ever it can. That may be why Joshua Cohen can so perilously absorb what bedevils me:

基本上，Kor召集了一次视频会议，没有邀请我们，却邀请了Moe。这是我们第一次得知此事。显然，Moe一直以为这次会议的目的是审查他关于DCent的计划，对他来说，这计划至关重要。换作其他人，肯定会对这种不提前通知的做法感到不满，但他早已做好了准备。他从出生起就被设定好了目标。他的第一世。正因如此，他才忍受了服务器的种种问题和Tetplex的延迟，正因如此，他才在每一次业力的延宕中，不断地修炼、封印、焊接，承受着痛苦，无数次的轮回，如同逆行转世一般，直到肉身放下自我。一切的存在都只是为了这一刻的动员，为了他修行的觉知显现，为了他的目标，为了这场幻灯片演示。

Moe 完成演讲后，Kor 鼓掌表示，他们暂且搁置 DCent 法案的缺失问题，留待以后讨论。目前，Moe 必须专注于一个叫做 Sapp 的东西。

相反，他必须把它改造成一个 STrapp 系统，使其具备搜索功能。这就是全部目标。在这方面，科尔是最终的决定者。

莫伊一开始说不出话来。

凯纳表示，这样做的理由是出于营收考虑。校外服务器可以等，但存储设备却不能等。它对千年虫问题非常敏感。而千年虫问题本身就非常敏感。

达斯汀说，等待是服务员的工作。

这项决定并非像委托生产的产品那样，而是自然而然形成的。

莫伊用印地语大喊大叫，如果你还记得《摩诃婆罗多》或《罗摩衍那》，就会知道弓弦断裂、箭矢呼啸着划破空气，就像罗摩神杀死猴王一样，莫伊就是用这种声音逃离了会议。

Basically, Kor had called a VC meeting, had not invited us but had invited Moe. This was the first we had been informed about any of this. Apparently, Moe had been under the impression that the purpose of the meeting was to examine his plans for the DCent, which, for him, was culminant. Anyone else would have resented the lack of notice, but he was primed. He had been primed since birth. His first birth. This was why he had endured the quibbly servers and Tetplex delays, this was what he had been mounting and sealing and soldering and suffering for through every karmic deferral, countless reincarnations counted as like retroincarnations until the bodies released their egos. All existence had been just a mobilization for this, the mindful manifestation of his sadhana, his purpose, this slideshow presentation.

After Moe finished presenting Kor applauded and said they were tabling on the absence of table the DCent for later. For now Moe had to focus on this thing called a Sapp.

Rather, he had to turn it into a STrapp. To make it searchcapable. That was the agenda in its entirety. In this, Kor was the decider.

Moe was speechless initially.

The rationale was revenue, Keiner said. An outcampus server could wait, but a tetrating storage device could not. It was y2K sensitive. And y2K was sensitive.

Waiting, Dustin said, is what servers do.

The decision, not as like the commissioned product, made itself.

Moe yelled in Hindi, and if you recall your Mahabharata or Ramayana, how the bowstring is said to snap and the arrow is said to wail through the air as like the god Rama slays the king of the monkeys, that was the yell with which Moe fled the meeting.

约书亚·科恩教会了我们如何区分“莫伊”（Moe）和“科尔”（Kor），然而，其中的乐趣远不止于此。这位小说家的耳朵早已吸收了我们当下生活中那些令人窒息的术语。我们当下的气候，其诗篇何在？爱默生式的自由又在何方？为何沃尔特·惠特曼要吟唱那些构成他自身一部分的事物，那些过去和未来的世界，死亡与白昼？这就是口头传统的全部遗存吗？硅谷是否就是死亡阴影笼罩的山谷？

Joshua Cohen has taught us how to distinguish between Moe and Kor, yet the fun of this transcends the distinction. The novelist’s accumulative ear has absorbed the soul-killing jargon of how we live now. Where are the poems of our climate? Where is Emersonian freedom? Why did Walt Whitman sing and chant the things that are part of him, the worlds that were and will be, death and day? Is this all that is left of the Oral Tradition? Is Silicon Valley the Valley of the Shadow of Death?

后记

AFTERWORD

换子疑云

The Changeling

昨晚的梦里，我独自一人坐在长桌旁。房间里没有其他人，但一个声音却语气严厉地不断质问我。

IN LAST NIGHT’S DREAM, I sat alone at a long table. There was no one else in the room, but a voice rather harshly kept questioning me.

你相信死人复活吗？

Do you believe in the resurrection of the dead?

我琢磨着该如何回答“你”的哪个部分。我小时候是个正统的阿什肯纳兹犹太人，母亲虔诚至极，父亲却对这种“愚昧”漠不关心。我的四个哥哥姐姐也都是正统派，但到了十四岁，我开始敬仰以利沙·本·阿布亚，而教我《塔木德》的那些人却视他为恶人。

I wondered which part of the “you” ought to reply. As a child I was an Orthodox Ashkenazi Jew raised by an intensely religious mother and a father indifferent to such “foolishness.” My four older siblings remained Orthodox, but by the age of fourteen I venerated Elisha ben Abuya, who was regarded as a villain by the men who taught me Talmud:

关于以利沙观点的最古老、最引人注目的记载见于以下巴莱塔（Ḥ ag. 14b；Yer. ii. 1）：

“四位智者进入了天堂——本·阿扎伊、本·佐玛、阿赫尔和阿基巴。本·阿扎伊看了之后就死了；本·佐玛疯了；阿赫尔毁掉了植物；只有阿基巴毫发无损地出来了。”

（进入天堂的四人）

The oldest and most striking reference to the views of Elisha is found in the following baraita (Ḥag. 14b; Yer. ii. 1):

“Four [sages] entered paradise—Ben ‘Azzai, Ben Zoma, Aḥer, and Akiba. Ben ‘Azzai looked and died; Ben Zoma went mad; Aḥer destroyed the plants; Akiba alone came out unhurt.”

(The Four Who Entered Paradise)

毫无疑问，“四人”前往天堂的旅程，如同以诺（在基督教之前的《以诺书》中）以及许多其他虔诚之人的升天一样，应当按字面意义而非寓意理解。这种对巴莱塔的理解得到了“进入天堂”这一短语的支持，因为“进入伊甸园”（נכנס לג״ע ）是一个常见的表达方式（Derek Ere ẓ Zu ṭ a i.; Ab. R. N. xxv.）。这意味着以利沙如同保罗一样，在一次狂喜中看到了天堂的内部景象——然而，以利沙的这种景象却导致他摧毁了天园中的植物。

There can be no doubt that the journey of the “four” to paradise, like the ascension of Enoch (in the pre-Christian books of Enoch) and of so many other pious men, is to be taken literally and not allegorically. This conception of the baraita is supported by the use of the phrase (“entered paradise”), since נכנס לג״ע (“entered the Garden of Eden” = paradise) was a common expression (Derek Ereẓ Zuṭa i.; Ab. R. N. xxv.). It means that Elisha, like Paul, in a moment of ecstasy beheld the interior of heaven—in the former’s case, however, with the effect that he destroyed the plants of the heavenly garden.

我引用了《犹太百科全书》中的这段话，该书谨慎地避免对以利沙·本·阿布亚的任何单一判决表示支持。 “ ḥ er ”意为“他者”或“陌生人”，是莫西姆（minim）或诺斯替异端之一。他被拉比阿基瓦的门徒诽谤，他们完全错误地指控他是罗马的合作者。他真正的罪过是，在一次异象中，他进入了天庭，发现两位神坐在宝座上，一位是耶和华，另一位是梅塔特隆，一位曾是天使以诺的神。

I have quoted this from The Jewish Encyclopedia, which is careful not to endorse any single judgment of Elisha ben Abuya. Aḥer means “the Other” or “the Stranger,” one of the minim or Gnostic heretics. He was slandered by the disciples of Rabbi Akiva, who denounced him, quite falsely, as a Roman collaborator. His true offense was that in a vision he entered the Heavenly Court and found two Gods sitting on thrones, Yahweh and Metatron, an angel who had been Enoch:

以诺与神同行，神将他取去，他就不在了。

（创世记 5:24，英王钦定本）

And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.

(Genesis 5:24, KJV)

即使在我还是个孩子的时候，我就很钦佩阿赫尔“拔除幼苗”的做法，在我三十多年教学生涯中，我一直都在践行这一理念。

Even as a boy I admired Aḥer for the way in which he had “torn up the young shoots,” an endeavor I have followed in my two-thirds of a century as a teacher.

如同以利沙·本·阿布亚一样，我相信卡巴拉式的死者复活。我们这些未能充分发挥自身潜能的人，将会在那些努力做得更好的人身上重生。我们当中，又有谁真正成为了自己应该成为的一切呢？

Like Elisha ben Abuya, I believe in what became a Kabbalist version of the resurrection of the dead. Those of us who have failed to realize all of our potential will be reborn in others who will try to do better. Who among us has become everything she or he ought to have been?

当你临终之时，你会吟诵莎士比亚以及你最爱的其他诗人的作品：弥尔顿、布莱克、雪莱、惠特曼、华莱士·史蒂文斯、哈特·克莱恩等等。那么，你为何在八十八岁高龄，却要写一本关于小说的书，以便在离世前重读呢？

When you are dying you will recite Shakespeare and the other poets you have loved best: Milton, Blake, Shelley, Walt Whitman, Wallace Stevens, Hart Crane, and many more. Why at eighty-eight are you writing a book about novels to reread ere you vanish?

孩提时代，我如饥似渴地阅读小说和短篇故事，但与阅读诗歌或戏剧截然不同。我早期的那点鉴赏力都倾注在了对诗歌的理解上。我过去是，现在仍然是散文小说的懵懂读者。大约十岁的时候，我爱上了托马斯·哈代的《林中居民》中的玛蒂·索斯。当她剪掉自己美丽的长发时，我感动得热泪盈眶。读《还乡》时，我被托马斯·哈代笔下的“夜之女王”尤斯塔西亚·维深深吸引。即便到了耄耋之年，我对这些的喜爱也几乎未曾改变。

As a child, I read novels and short stories incessantly but in a very different spirit from reading poetry or drama. What early sophistication I had went into the apprehension of poetry. I was and remain a naïve reader of prose fiction. At ten or so, I fell in love with Marty South in Thomas Hardy’s The Woodlanders. When she cuts off her long and beautiful hair, I was moved to tears. When I read The Return of the Native, I was captivated by Eustacia Vye, Thomas Hardy’s Queen of the Night. In that way, I have scarcely changed in extreme old age.

我最亲密的朋友都已离世。我迫切需要结识新的朋友。我的学生们都很优秀，但他们还很年轻。本书献给厄休拉·勒奎恩，我们素未谋面，却已成为挚友。在她生命的最后两个月里，我们互通了无数封邮件。但她也已离世。我重读小说，是为了寻找那些依然健在的老朋友，也是为了结识新的朋友。

My closest friends have all died. I desperately need new ones. My students are remarkable people but very young. Ursula Le Guin, to whom this book is dedicated, became a dear friend without our ever meeting, since we exchanged a multitude of e-mails in the last two months of her life. But she, too, is gone. I go back to reread novels to find old friends still living and to make new ones.

那难道不只是另一种错觉吗？查尔斯·狄更斯58岁去世时，你认为他在临终前是否感受到了他笔下所有人物的存在？

Is that not merely another illusion? When Charles Dickens died at fifty-eight, do you think in his final stroke he somehow felt the presence of all the people he had created?

彼得·阿克罗伊德在他那本精彩的传记中，用这个推测深深吸引了我。不过，阿克罗伊德本人也是一位优秀的小说家。我一直信奉维科的格言：“你只了解你自己创造的东西。”我无法像华莱士·史蒂文斯的创作者那样了解他的《一个特定人物的成长历程》，也永远无法像狄更斯那样，从内到外地了解他的《荒凉山庄》或《我们共同的朋友》。作为一名莎士比亚和诗歌教师，我努力深入理解《李尔王》或《秋日的曙光》，但我始终无法达到我所渴望的深度。对于散文小说，我的期望则更为谦逊。我向来不热衷于情节或社会历史，但我试图将自己代入到人物之中，这是一种徒劳的尝试，却又令我无法抗拒。

Peter Ackroyd, in his marvelous biography, charms me with that surmise. But, then, Ackroyd is himself a good novelist. I have always believed in Vico’s adage: “You only know what you yourself have made.” I cannot know Wallace Stevens’s “The Course of a Particular” as its creator knew it, and I will never know Bleak House or Our Mutual Friend as Dickens must have known it, from the inside out. As a teacher of Shakespeare and the poets, I endeavor to get as far inside King Lear or The Auroras of Autumn as I can, yet I cannot get as far inward as I desire. With prose fiction, my hope is more modest. Never fond of plot or of social history, I attempt to place myself within the characters, a vain drive yet for me inescapable.

我刚入康奈尔大学读大一时，在弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫开设的欧洲小说课程的第一堂课上，我中途离场了。当时，我只读过他的《塞巴斯蒂安·奈特的真实生活》（1941）和刚出版英文版的《弯曲的辛尼斯特》（1947）。我的导师M·H·艾布拉姆斯对我的生活和创作产生了深远的影响，他与纳博科夫是朋友，力劝我选修这门课。我记得纳博科夫一开始就对果戈理和简·奥斯汀进行了贬低性的比较，还说女人根本不会写作。十七岁的我，胆子大到直接离开了教室。纳博科夫和他的妻子薇拉都看到了这一幕。那天晚上，我接到了纳博科夫夫人的电话，她邀请我第二天下午去她位于伊萨卡东州街957号的家中喝茶，并委婉地告诉我，她丈夫很不高兴，打算下午茶后和我下棋，好好“教训”我一顿。

When I was a Cornell freshman, I walked out of Vladimir Nabokov’s initial lecture in a course on the European novel. At that time, I had read only The Real Life of Sebastian Knight (1941) and Bend Sinister (1947), which had just come out in English. My adviser M. H. Abrams, a permanent influence on my life and work, was a friend of Nabokov and urged me to take the course. I recall that Nabokov began by unfavorably comparing Gogol and Jane Austen. He added that women just could not write. At seventeen, I was brash enough to walk out. This was observed by Nabokov and by his wife, Vera. That evening, I received a phone call from Mrs. Nabokov, inviting me to tea at their house at 957 East State Street, Ithaca, the next afternoon and gently telling me that her husband was displeased and intended to destroy me in a chess match after tea.

我当时只是个业余棋手，也知道纳博科夫以创作国际象棋谜题而闻名。我忐忑不安地去了康奈尔图书馆，借了何塞·卡帕布兰卡的《国际象棋基础》。凭借记忆，我背诵了五六个例局。第二天下午，在一个温暖的九月天，我们在户外享用下午茶。纳博科夫全程一言不发。下午茶后，纳博科夫夫人收拾好一切，这位小说家领我来到一副摆放在树荫下的华丽大棋盘前。我从未见过如此精美的棋子，不禁惊叹不已。纳博科夫默默地示意我先走，于是我开始下卡帕布兰卡最喜欢的一盘棋。我拖延了主人大约八步，期间他一脸困惑。突然，他恍然大悟，大声说道：“你这小家伙，竟然把卡帕布兰卡的棋谱都背下来了！”他得意洋洋地说：“现在我只需四步就能把你打败。” 他果然做到了。他一言不发，走回了家。我也走回了家。

I was only an amateur chess player and knew Nabokov’s reputation as a composer of chess problems. In some terror, I went over to the Cornell library and took out José Capablanca’s Chess Fundamentals. Relying on memory, I ingested five or six sample games. After tea the next afternoon, which was outdoors on a balmy September day, during which Nabokov did not speak at all, Mrs. Nabokov cleared everything away and the novelist led me over to a very ornate and large chessboard, placed in the shade of a tree. I had never seen such beautiful chessmen, and I was awed. Silently, Nabokov graciously indicated I had the first move, and I commenced one of Capablanca’s favorite games. I held my host off for about eight moves, during which he looked perplexed. Suddenly his face cleared and he cried out, “You young rascal, you have memorized Capablanca!” With great relish he said, “Now I will destroy you in just four moves.” He did exactly that. Without a word, he walked back into his house. I walked home.

后来，我编辑了两卷关于纳博科夫的论文集，但我完全不记得内容了。我对《洛丽塔》的感受很复杂，但我非常喜欢《微暗的火》和一篇名为《范恩姐妹》的短篇小说。有时我仍然觉得他的作品难以卒读。他的矫揉造作、语言炫耀和虚荣心无处不在。纳博科夫对果戈理情有独钟，我也一样，但只有《爱达，或热情：一部家族编年史》（1969）的作者才能真正戏仿果戈理那种纯粹的魔幻主义。我的一位挚友，也是我在剑桥大学彭布罗克学院的导师马修·J·C·霍加特（1916-1996），在《纽约书评》上发表了一篇关于《爱达》的精彩评论文章。1967-1968年，我们和家人一起在康奈尔人文社团待了一年。马修把他的书稿给了我，我读的时候感觉很不自在。我们争论这本书，马修虽然承认其中有些过激之处，却对它的巧妙构思和天马行空的典故运用赞叹不已。霍加特本人是《芬尼根守灵夜》的狂热研究者（我也曾试图效仿他），但他最终还是被纳博科夫那种严谨而又惊世骇俗的风格所折服。

In later years, I edited two volumes of essays on Nabokov, which I do not remember at all. I had a mixed reaction to Lolita but greatly enjoyed Pale Fire and one short story called “The Vane Sisters.” Sometimes I still find him unreadable. His preciosity, linguistic exhibitionism, vanity shine through everywhere. Nabokov had a passion for Gogol, which I share, but Gogol’s authentic daemonism could only be parodied by the author of Ada, or Ardor: A Family Chronicle (1969). One of my closest friends, who had been my tutor at Pembroke College, Cambridge, Matthew J. C. Hodgart (1916–96), wrote a sparkling essay on Ada in The New York Review of Books. In 1967–68, we and our families spent a year together at the Cornell Society for the Humanities. Matthew gave me his review copy, and I read it with considerable discomfort. We argued the book, but Matthew, while granting excesses, was delighted by its ingenuity and mad allusiveness. Himself an enthusiastic scholar of Finnegans Wake, which I tried to be in his wake, Hodgart yielded to Nabokov’s disciplined outrageousness.

在沉浸于其他创作爱好之余，W·G·塞巴尔德也对纳博科夫颇有研究。在《移民》一书中，纳博科夫的身影如蝴蝶网般轻盈地穿梭其间，为四篇阴郁的故事注入了一丝温暖的曙光。纳博科夫的回忆录《说吧，记忆》（1951）与塞巴尔德笔下包罗万象的《爱达》或《热情》融为一体。

W. G. Sebald cultivated Nabokov amid his other creative obsessions. All through The Emigrants, the figure of Nabokov flits with a butterfly net, endearingly bestowing a touch of cheer to the four dismal narratives. Speak, Memory (1951), Nabokov’s memoir, fuses with Ada, or Ardor, in Sebald’s capacious reflections.

在我的教学生涯中，我一直向学生们指出，一部文学作品可能在美学上取得了巨大成功，但未必讨人喜欢。塞巴尔德是一位各方面都令人喜爱的作家，即使他的作品有时会让我感到悲伤。我无法忍受纳博科夫。这是我个人的评价，与他无关。我原以为任何有鉴赏力的人都不会不喜欢简·奥斯汀，但我的偶像拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生却在1861年的日记中对她不屑一顾：

Throughout my teaching career, I have suggested to my students that a literary work can be an aesthetic triumph and yet not very likable. Sebald is a writer likable in every way, even when he saddens me. I cannot abide Nabokov. That is a judgment upon me and not on him. I would have thought that no one of sensibility could dislike Jane Austen, but my hero Ralph Waldo Emerson dismissed her in his journal from 1861:

我实在不明白为什么人们对奥斯汀小姐的小说评价如此之高。在我看来，她的小说庸俗不堪，艺术创意匮乏，囿于英国社会那些令人作呕的习俗，既缺乏才华，又缺乏智慧，更缺乏对世事的了解。生活从未如此狭隘压抑……书中人物唯一值得关注的，似乎只有一件事：他（或她）有没有钱结婚……？……自杀都比这体面。

I am at a loss to understand why people hold Miss Austen’s novels at so high a rate, which seem to me vulgar in tone, sterile in artistic invention, imprisoned in their wretched conventions of English society, without genius, wit, or knowledge of the world. Never was life so pinched and narrow….All that interests in any character [is this]: has he (or she) the money to marry with…?…Suicide is more respectable.

爱默生不太喜欢小说：在他1842年的日记中，他贬低了他的散步伙伴纳撒尼尔·霍桑的小说：

Emerson did not much like novels: in his journal from 1842, he dismissed those by his walking companion Nathaniel Hawthorne:

纳撒尼尔·霍桑作为作家的声誉是一件令人欣慰的事，因为他的作品没有任何实际用途，而这恰恰是对他本人的一种褒奖。

Nathaniel Hawthorne’s reputation as a writer is a very pleasing fact, because his writing is not good for anything, and this is a tribute to the man.

永远不应忘记，爱默生凭借非凡的敏锐洞察力，在收到沃尔特·惠特曼寄来的第一部《草叶集》（1855年）后，做出了精彩的回应：

It should never be forgotten that Emerson, in an extraordinary act of immediate critical perception, received in the mail from Walt Whitman the first Leaves of Grass (1855) and responded magnificently:

尊敬的先生-

我并非对《草叶集》这部杰作的价值视而不见。我认为它是美国迄今为止贡献的最杰出的智慧和才华之作。阅读它令我十分愉悦，正如强大的力​​量带来快乐。它满足了我一直以来对西方人那种看似贫瘠吝啬的性格的渴望——仿佛过多的辛劳，或者说过多的温情，就使我们西方人的才智变得臃肿而吝啬。

我由衷地赞赏你自由而勇敢的思想。我为此感到无比欣慰。我发现你言辞优美，表达得淋漓尽致，这才是它应有的样子。我看到了你那令人钦佩的勇气，而这种勇气唯有广阔的视野才能激发。

我祝贺你开启了一段辉煌的职业生涯，但如此卓越的开端，想必背后有着漫长的积累。我揉了揉眼睛，想确认这道阳光并非幻觉；但这本书所传递出的坚实信息，却令人确信无疑。它具备最宝贵的品质，那就是鼓舞人心、激励士气。

直到昨晚我在报纸上看到这本书的广告，才知道这个名字真实存在，而且邮局也收不到。我很想见见我的恩人，甚至很想放下手头的工作，亲自去纽约拜访您，向您致以我的敬意。

RW EMERSON。

DEAR SIR—

I am not blind to the worth of the wonderful gift of “LEAVES OF GRASS.” I find it the most extraordinary piece of wit and wisdom that America has yet contributed. I am very happy in reading it, as great power makes us happy. It meets the demand I am always making of what seemed the sterile and stingy nature, as if too much handiwork, or too much lymph in the temperament, were making our western wits fat and mean.

I give you joy of your free and brave thought. I have great joy in it. I find incomparable things said incomparably well, as they must be. I find the courage of treatment which so delights us, and which large perception only can inspire.

I greet you at the beginning of a great career, which yet must have had a long foreground somewhere, for such a start. I rubbed my eyes a little, to see if this sunbeam were no illusion; but the solid sense of the book is a sober certainty. It has the best merits, namely, of fortifying and encouraging.

I did not know until I last night saw the book advertised in a newspaper that I could trust the name as real and available for a post-office. I wish to see my benefactor, and have felt much like striking my tasks and visiting New York to pay you my respects.

R. W. EMERSON.

我无比热爱沃尔特·惠特曼，但我常常想，如果当初我第一次读到《草叶集》，会作何感想。当我重读、教授、撰写关于莎士比亚或弥尔顿的文章时，我有时会不自觉地借鉴浩瀚的评注传统。阅读，就如同与文学或人生中所有先驱的幽灵相遇。几乎每晚我都会梦见已故的朋友，有时还会将他们与虚构人物混淆。

I love Walt Whitman with a passion beyond bounds, and yet I wonder how I would have reacted to a first reading of Leaves of Grass. When I reread, teach, write about Shakespeare or Milton, I build, sometimes involuntarily, on immense traditions of commentary. To read is to encounter ghosts of all the forerunners in literature or life. Almost every night I dream about departed friends, sometimes mixing them up with fictive characters.

几天前，在我八十八岁生日前夕，我梦见了换子。在我朋友约翰·克劳利的《小小大人》里，仙子们绑架了苏菲的女儿莉拉克，把她带到了仙子族的老妇人安德希尔夫人那里。一个假莉拉克取代了人类的孩子，最终爆炸了。我不记得自己梦到过约翰·克劳利，但我确实梦到过他笔下的某些人物，比如莉拉克、安德希尔夫人和鳟鱼爷爷。就在我写下这些文字的时候，一个风趣幽默的年轻人闯了进来，我们聊起了雅里的“超形而上学”，也就是想象解决方案的科学。我的朋友罗杰·沙塔克向我介绍了雅里，他用一句雅里的信条深深吸引了我：“超形而上学是我们刚刚发明的一门科学，而且我们迫切需要它。”这位年轻人大约十年前曾上过我的课，一门是关于《暴风雨》，另一门是关于哈特·克莱恩。他想和我谈谈我那部古老的论著《影响的焦虑》（1973），我写这本书的目的是为了对“形而上学”做出贡献，如果可能的话，也为了对犹太教的对立生命论传统做出贡献，这一传统可以追溯到《塔纳赫》及其注释家。我很高兴能听他谈谈，因为我已经几十年没看过这本书了，恐怕我现在不会完全认同书中的观点了。

A few nights ago, on the eve of my eighty-eighth birthday, I dreamed about changelings. In my friend John Crowley’s Little, Big, the fairies kidnap Lilac, Sophie’s daughter, and carry the child off to Mrs. Underhill, the grande dame of the faerie folk. A false Lilac replaces the human child, and in time it explodes. I cannot recall ever dreaming about John Crowley, but I do about some of his characters, like Lilac, Mrs. Underhill, and Grandfather Trout. As I was writing these sentences, a charmingly wild young man burst in, and we discoursed about Jarry’s ’Pataphysics, or the science of imaginary solutions. I was introduced to Jarry by my friend Roger Shattuck, who charmed me by uttering Jarry’s credo: “ ’Pataphysics is a science which we have only just invented and for which there is a crying need.” The young man had attended classes by me about a decade ago, one on The Tempest and the other on Hart Crane. He wanted to talk about my ancient treatise The Anxiety of Influence (1973), which I intended as a contribution to ’Pataphysics and, if possible, to the tradition of Jewish antithetical vitalism that goes back to Tanakh and its exegetes. I was glad to listen to him, because I have not looked at the book for some decades and fear I would no longer totally agree with it.

关于作者的说明

A NOTE ABOUT THE AUTHOR

哈罗德·布鲁姆生前居住在纽黑文，曾任耶鲁大学斯特林人文讲席教授。此前，他曾任哈佛大学查尔斯·艾略特·诺顿讲席教授。他著述颇丰，出版了四十余部著作，包括《记忆的附身》（Possessed by Memory）、《影响的焦虑》（The Anxiety of Influence）、《莎士比亚：人的发明》（Shakespeare: The Invention of the Human）、《西方经典》（The Western Canon）、《美国宗教》（The American Religion）以及《恶魔知晓：文学的伟大与美国的崇高》（The Daemon Knows: Literary Greatness and the American Sublime）。他是麦克阿瑟奖获得者、美国艺术与文学院院士，并荣获众多奖项和荣誉学位，其中包括美国艺术与文学院颁发的文学与评论金奖、加泰罗尼亚国际奖以及墨西哥阿方索·雷耶斯国际奖。他一直居住在纽黑文，直至2019年10月14日逝世，享年八十九岁。

Harold Bloom lived in New Haven and was a Sterling Professor of Humanities at Yale University. Before that, he was Charles Eliot Norton Professor at Harvard. His more than forty books include Possessed by Memory, The Anxiety of Influence, Shakespeare: The Invention of the Human, The Western Canon, The American Religion, and The Daemon Knows: Literary Greatness and the American Sublime. He was a MacArthur Fellow, a member of the American Academy of Arts and Letters, and the recipient of many awards and honorary degrees, including the American Academy of Arts and Letters’ Gold Medal for Belles Lettres and Criticism, the Catalonia International Prize, and Mexico’s Alfonso Reyes International Prize. He lived in New Haven until his death on October 14, 2019, at the age of eighty-nine.
